title: Trump’s approval rating hits new low amid growing support for Democrats — poll
body:
WAHINGTON, October 18. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has hit a record low, with popular support for Democrats growing fast two weeks ahead of the midterm elections, according to an opinion poll conducted by The Washington Post, the ABC television channel, and the French pollster Ipsos.
According to the poll results, Trump’s approval stands at 33%, or 4 p.p. down on July and 8 p.p. down on October 2025.
In the race for control of the House of Representatives, Democrats are 8 p.p. ahead of Republicans, compared to 3 p.p. in July. Respondents stated that their dissatisfaction with Republicans stems primarily from Trump’s actions, as well as from rising inflation in the country caused by the war with Iran. Specifically, 72% of those surveyed believe the country is moving in the wrong direction, which is 5 p.p. higher than in April.
The poll also revealed that, for the first time in more than a decade, Democrats are perceived as more reliable when it comes to addressing economic issues. The approval rating for Trump’s economic policies fell to 28%, down from 33% in July. Economic problems faced by many Americans are so severe that 48% of survey respondents reported that their financial situation had worsened since Trump returned to the White House in 2025. This is the highest figure among all presidents recorded in WP and ABC polls since 1986. In addition, 65% of respondents believe that the war with Iran was a mistake.
According to the newspaper, the survey has revealed that Republicans "are on the defensive in these final weeks, even in areas where they have traditionally held a strong advantage." However, "Republicans still enjoy an overall lead in money to pour into political advertising that they hope will hold back the Democratic tide," it noted, adding that the voter turnout at midterms is typically lower than that at presidential elections and it will be more difficult for Republicans to mobilizer their supporters. This said, the newspaper anticipates that Democrats will be able to regain control of the House.
The poll was conducted from October 9 through 13 among 2,545 adult respondents.
he US midterm congressional elections will take place on November 3. In these elections, 33 of the 100 members of the Senate and all 435 members of the House of Representatives will be up for re-election. Republicans currently control both chambers of Congress.

title: Lagos Task Force detains dismissed operative over alleged extortion
body: The Lagos State Environmental and Special Offences Enforcement Unit (Task Force) has detained a dismissed operative for alleged impersonation and extortion of motorists and traders. The chairman of task force, CSP Adetayo Akerele, disclosed this in a statement signed by the agency’s spokesperson, Mr Abdulraheem Gbadeyan on Sunday in Lagos. Akerele said that the suspect was detained at Oshodi bus-stop following the circulation of a viral video of his apprehension. The chairman said that the suspect, a former paramilitary operative, was dismissed several months ago over alleged misconduct, including theft, use of a fake identity card, extortion of motorists and traders, and indiscipline. “The suspect continued to pose as a serving task force official after his dismissal. “Operatives accosted the suspect for questioning, but he allegedly rejected the invitation and resisted arrest before being apprehended through tactical coordination and minimal force. “The suspect no longer had any affiliation with the agency, ” he said. The task force boss said the alleged impersonation could mislead the public and undermine confidence in legitimate law enforcement activities. “The arrest underscored the agency’s determination to prevent dismissed personnel and other unauthorised individuals from exploiting its identity and authority for unlawful purposes, ” he said. According to him, the suspect will be arraigned in court on Monday, after completion of investiation. He urged residents to verify the identities of individuals claiming to be task force officials and report suspicious activities through appropriate channels. Akerele also urged journalists to verify allegations and obtain responses from relevant parties before publication to promote balanced and responsible reporting. He reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to protecting residents and preventing the abuse of its name and authority. title: MOVIE REVIEW: Agbara Nla remake casts old spell on new generation
body:
A particular kind of fear only a classic Nollywood villain from the late 1990s can inspire: the kind that makes an audience laugh nervously, whisper prayers in fear, and still refuse to look away.
More than three decades after he first embodied Isawuru, the veteran Christian filmmaker Mike Bamiloye returns as the terrifying antagonist of a story that once helped define an era of Nigerian gospel filmmaking.
Yet the most remarkable thing about this remake is not simply that Mr Bamiloye has revisited one of his most recognisable roles. It is that a film built around spiritual warfare, demonic oppression and the supremacy of God’s power has become one of Nollywood’s biggest non-December releases.
Directed by Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and his brother, Joshua “Jay Mikee” Bamiloye, the film opened nationwide on 1 October, Nigeria’s Independence Day. PREMIUM TIMES reported that it generated approximately ₦71.4 million from preview screenings and another ₦99.2 million during its opening weekend, bringing its opening-frame total to about ₦170.6 million. It recorded the biggest non-December opening for a Nigerian film and the strongest opening for a faith-based Nollywood production. It has grossed ₦307.2 million so far.
But does the film’s success translate into an equally convincing cinematic experience? And more importantly, what is the secret behind the film’s success? Is it just nostalgia?
To appreciate the ambition behind Agbara Nla: The Return, it helps to understand what the original meant to Nigerian audiences.
The first ‘Agbara Nla’ premiered in 1993 as a Mount Zion Film Productions television serial written by Mike Bamiloye. Its English-language adaptation, ‘The Ultimate Power’, followed in 1994, helping the story reach audiences beyond Yoruba-speaking communities. The production became one of Mount Zion’s defining works and helped establish the ministry’s reputation for bringing Christian teachings to the screen.
The story itself had an extraordinary journey. Bamiloye has recalled that the original production idea dates to 1987, when a project initially titled ‘Agbara To Ju Agbara Lo’ was filmed but abandoned after the cameraman reportedly disappeared with the tapes. The project revived in 1993, after Mount Zion had gained filmmaking experience, and eventually reached television audiences across western Nigeria.
The village of Muwonleru lives under the oppressive influence of Isawuru, a feared occult figure whose power extends beyond ordinary fear and superstition.
Isawuru challenges Oba Adetunji, the village king, demanding that he bow to him and pay homage as his predecessors allegedly did. When the king refuses, Isawuru makes good on his threat, destroying the royal household and beheading the monarch.
Before his death, however, the king writes to his cousin, Kola, who lives in Ibadan. The letter becomes a call to take the Christian message to a community held captive by spiritual oppression.
Kola and Bose, played by Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and Aanu Kolade Abiodun, initially evade the assignment. Kola receives a promotion that transfers him to Lagos, which he sees as an escape from the daunting mission.
The responsibility eventually falls to Olaboye and his wife, Olatomi, played by Philip Olubakin and Remilekun Mosiko. The couple must leave behind the comfort of urban life to confront the forces terrorising Muwonleru.
Olaboye’s journey to the mission is strengthened by his encounter with Engineer Ojo, whose family has experienced what the film presents as a miraculous birth after more than two decades of childlessness. The encounter helps persuade Olaboye to accept the assignment.
What follows is a familiar but compelling Mount Zion confrontation between light and darkness, featuring marine spirits, forest witches, occult rituals, and a succession of encounters designed to establish the film’s central question: whose power is truly greater?
The most immediately satisfying element of Agbara Nla: The Return is its central performance.
As Isawuru, Mike Bamiloye doesn’t merely reprise an iconic character; he seems to understand exactly why the character endured in the original movie. Beyond the costume’s intimidating presence, Mr Bamiloye animates the persona that gives Isawuru his well-earned reputation, giving the villain a presence that endures even when he is not the centre of the action.
There is also an unexpectedly entertaining quality to his wickedness. Isawuru seems to relish his own reputation, and Bamiloye plays that relish with a conviction that invites nervous laughter from the audience.
Aanu Kolade Abiodun also makes a strong impression as Bose. Her performance gives the character a relatable personality. Even after she is possessed following her ill-fated friendship with Paulina, she convincingly depicts both fierce horror and vulnerable pity.
The plot is straightforward in its moral architecture. Evil is real, spiritual warfare has real consequences, and faith demands more than personal conviction; it requires obedience and sacrifice.
The more interesting conflict, however, is not simply between Isawuru and the Christian protagonists. It is between the desire for personal comfort and the responsibility to confront a community’s suffering. Kola’s reluctance gives the story a human side that occasionally feels more relatable than its supernatural spectacle.
The film’s production design and costumes show an understanding that remaking a classic doesn’t mean reproducing every visual limitation of the original. Isawuru’s appearance, the forest coven, the marine queen, and the redesigned Ologosodudu evoke the visual imagination of older Nigerian supernatural films while benefiting from a more ambitious production.
The film also shows an appealing willingness to retain the narrative associated with Mount Zion’s earlier productions. Rather than disguising the film’s origins, the directors build on them, preserving the heightened performances and dramatic confrontations that made the original distinctive.
The commercial success of Agbara Nla: The Return is more than a flattering statistic. It challenges assumptions about when Nigerian audiences will turn out for local films and what kinds of stories they are willing to pay to see.
For years, December has been a key period for Nollywood releases, benefiting from holiday travel, family gatherings, and increased cinema attendance. Against that backdrop, the remake’s October opening stands out.
Agbara Nla: The Return shows that nostalgia, faith, and theatrical spectacle combine to create commercial power.
However, for all its strengths, Agbara Nla: The Return is not immune to the weaknesses of the tradition from which it emerges.
Its runtime, estimated at between two hours and 40 minutes and three hours, is a substantial demand on the audience. The chapter-like structure provides some relief, but the film occasionally confuses duration with dramatic depth.
Certain sequences linger longer than necessary, particularly when the narrative pauses to underline a spiritual lesson that the preceding action has already communicated.
The film has a clear theological framework, and its resolution should be judged partly within that framework. But audiences unfamiliar with Mount Zion’s storytelling conventions may find the conclusion less dramatically persuasive than the preceding conflict.
Agbara Nla: The Return does not treat the supernatural as a metaphor to be explained away; it takes the existence of spiritual forces as a premise of its story and builds its drama around the consequences of that belief.
For audiences who share its theological assumptions, this approach may heighten their appreciation of the film. For others, some of its claims and dramatic choices may invite scepticism or discomfort. This matters because the film is not simply trying to entertain a general cinema audience. It is also engaging viewers whose religious convictions shape how they interpret the actions on screen.
These shortcomings do not erase its achievement. Agbara Nla: The Return has made an old story feel relevant again, even if it occasionally takes longer than necessary to make its point.
Overall, Agbara Nla: The Return shows that, beyond nostalgia, a good story that resonates with audiences still finds relevance when told with an understanding of the trends of the time.
Agbara Nla: The Return is showing in Cinemas Nationwide

title: NPP holds national thanksgiving service in Goaso after successful internal elections
body: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has held a national thanksgiving service at the Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church in Goaso in the Ahafo Region to express gratitude to God following what it described as successful elections of its executives and flagbearer. The service formed part of the party’s efforts to seek divine guidance, protection and wisdom as it prepares for the 2028 general elections. Addressing the congregation, NPP General Secretary Justin Frimpong Kodua said the party considered it important to hold a thanksgiving service with members of the SDA Church, who observe their day of worship on Saturdays, to thank God for the peaceful conduct of its internal elections. Read also: Here are NPP’s newly elected executives He said the party was also seeking God’s direction and protection as it works towards its goal of winning the 2028 general elections. Meanwhile, the party’s National Chairman, John Boadu, said NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia would address concerns among SDA members relating to elections held on Saturdays if elected president in 2028. According to him, Dr Bawumia would speak on the matter at the appropriate time and explain the steps he intends to take. The Presiding Superintendent and President of the SDA Church, Jonathan Owusu, urged the NPP to prioritise unity and teamwork as it prepares for the next general elections. He commended the party for organising the thanksgiving service following its internal elections, describing the gesture as a positive sign of unity, and encouraged its members to work together towards their electoral goal.

title: Mysterious explosion hits Baghdad, injuring soldiers from Iranian-backed militias in Iraq
body: A mysterious explosion has struck an ammunition depot of the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) in Baghdad.The PMF is an umbrella group of several Iranian-backed militias in Iraq. The Iraqi military and government are investigating the blast that took place on Saturday. Five members of the PMF were wounded in the explosion.“The explosion of a cache of damaged ammunition inside one of [the PMF's] headquarters east of the canal in the capital, Baghdad, has been brought under control ... The final toll of the incident resulted in minor injuries to five personnel,” the PMF said.Iraq's state media said that the PMF said on Saturday that “preliminary investigations into an explosion at one of its headquarters in eastern Baghdad indicate it was caused by an internal malfunction, with no evidence of an external attack.”This indicates that Iraq is trying to downplay the idea that a munition struck this site because the Iraqi narrative is that this was an accident.Explosion was the result of internal malfunction, not a targeted attackA statement from the PMF, received by the state Iraqi News Agency (INA), noted that “preliminary investigations by the Ministry of Interior's forensic evidence unit indicate that the explosion at one of the PMF's headquarters was the result of an internal malfunction, and there is no indication of any external targeting.”Iraq's prime minister has ordered an investigation into the incident. The Iraqi Security Media Cell stated that “the Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali Falih al-Zaidi, has directed the formation of an investigative committee to determine the circumstances of the explosion.” The Iraqi Security Media Cell, an official government account, also said that the prime minister “emphasized the urgency of completing the investigation work to determine the precise causes of the incident, while taking all necessary safety measures and procedures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents in the future.”Explosion viewed with suspicion in IraqSome will view the explosion as suspicious. This is because it is not the first of its kind. There have been explosions at arms depots in Iraq before. This has also happened in Syria. Is it all accidents, local people ask? They wonder whether something may be behind the explosions.Iranian-backed militias have become a powerful force in Iraq over the last two decades, playing a role in the country's security and politics.Many of the groups, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, and the Badr Organization, have longstanding ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).The Badr Organization was founded in Iran in the 1980s, while Kataib Hezbollah emerged around 2007, and Asaib Ahl al-Haq in 2006. These groups expanded their influence after the 2003 US invasion of Iraq, with some attacking American forces.A turning point came in June 2014, when Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani issued a fatwa calling on Iraqis to defend the country against ISIS. The mobilization helped create the PMF, known as Hashd al-Shaabi.Although the PMF includes numerous factions, Iranian-backed groups became the leaders within its ranks. The PMF was subsequently incorporated into Iraq's official security structure. Many of the networks have been sanctioned by the US as terrorist groups. They increased their attacks on US forces in Iraq in 2019 and 2020.In 2019, a series of explosions rocked PMF weapons depots across Iraq. The militias blamed some incidents on Israeli and American airstrikes.The explosions highlighted concerns about militia stockpiles and Iranian weapons transfers. It was reported in 2018 and 2019 that Iran had moved ballistic missiles to the militias.Following October 7, Iranian-backed factions launched numerous drone and rocket attacks against US forces in Iraq and Syria. Operating under the Islamic Resistance in Iraq umbrella, they also claimed attacks targeting Israel throughout 2023 and 2024.The militias have remained a challenge for Baghdad. In 2026, Iraq's prime minister pledged to bring weapons under state control.Iraq later revised the September 30 disarmament deadline, with several powerful factions refusing to surrender their arsenals. Baghdad claims it will rein in the militias by June 2027.

title: Photos: CIMG awards honour marketing excellence at Labadi Beach Hotel
body: The Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), held its 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, recognising individuals and organisations for their achievements in marketing and business performance. Among the major award recipients, Salem Kalmoni, Managing Director of Japan Motors, was named Marketing Man of the Year, while Abena Amoah, Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange, received the Marketing Woman of the Year award. Mavis Frimpong of Consolidated Bank Ghana Limited was named Marketing Practitioner of the Year, and Thomasina Tetey of MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company received the Marketing Student of the Year award. The ceremony also saw MyJoyOnline inducted into the CIMG Hall of Fame after winning the Marketing-Oriented Online News Portal of the Year award for five consecutive years. The recognition highlighted the platform’s work in digital journalism and audience engagement. title: Yemen warns shareholders of Aramco oil company
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Yemeni Armed Forces have issues a new warning calling on Saudi non-military people to stay away from Saudi oil facilities and sell Aramco oil company's shares on the stock markets.
A Yemeni military source issued a warning about the security situation in Saudi Arabia and called on employees and citizens to stay away from the country's oil facilities and advised Aramco shareholders to sell their shares before it is too late.
The source from the Yemeni Armed Forces issued the warning in an interview with local Saba News Agency.

title: Iran attacks Komala Kurdish opposition group in Iraq amid increased regional tensions
body: The Komala group said that it was attacked overnight in the Kurdistan Region of northern Iraq.Komala is a Kurdish Iranian opposition group. It has been attacked many times since February 2026. Now it is under attack again.Many of these Kurdish Iranian opposition groups are concerned that Iran will now escalate attacks in the wake of the US leaving Iraq on September 30.Since the US left, there have been several attacks on these groups, including attacks on the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (PDKI) in Koya and Khabat near Erbil.Komala said overnight on Saturday, “Moments ago, one of the bases of the Komala Party of Iranian Kurdistan in the Khalifan region was once again targeted in a drone strike. Fortunately, no casualties have been reported.”Rudaw said that “two drones launched from Iran struck a base belonging to the Iranian Kurdish opposition group Komala in Balisan, Erbil province, on Saturday night, an official from the group and a security source told Rudaw English.” Rudaw is a local major Kurdish media outlet based in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG).Rudaw noted that Ali Ranjbari, head of Komala's relations, “confirmed the attack, saying there were no casualties, but buildings were damaged. He said one drone struck the base, while the other hit a guard post. Separately, a security source in the Kurdistan Region confirmed the attack to Rudaw English, while Iran's semi-official Mehr News Agency also reported the drone strikes.”There have been more than 1,000 attacks on the KRG since February 28. Many of the Kurdish groups have said that they have been targeted hundreds of times each.Rudaw provided important context, noting that “the latest strike comes amid rising tensions between Tehran and Washington in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian forces have stepped up pressure on commercial shipping, targeting more than a dozen vessels over the past two weeks.”This means that Iran appears to be increasing raids in the Kurdish region of Iran. The Kurdish region of Iran is in northwestern Iran and borders the Kurdish areas of northern Iraq. Iran has been cracking down on Kurdish activism amid concerns there could be an uprising. Early in the conflict with Iran, in March 2026, there were reports that the US was supporting Kurdish groups in Iran.Despite reports of US aid, no rebellion among Kurds against IranHowever, a rebellion did not happen. PDKI has said recently that it is not sending its Peshmerga fighters into Iran.The KRG President Nechirvan Barzani also condemned the Kurdish groups recently for behaving irresponsibly. What he implies is that they have brought the attacks on the KRG.Rudaw said that “in western Iran, clashes between the IRGC and fighters from the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) have escalated in the Shaho mountain range in the Hawraman region over the past few days, with Iranian forces deploying heavy weaponry and drones to bombard areas where Kurdish militants maintain positions.”Rudaw added that “the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) reported that Iranian forces had continued shelling and drone attacks in the Shaho mountains, including areas around Daleh Marz village in Sarvabad county.Witnesses told the rights group that several explosions caused by suicide drones were heard in the Daleh Marz and Bareza Lang areas, while Iranian reconnaissance drones flew over the mountains.”What might happen next? Iranian Kurdish opposition groups have maintained bases in the Kurdistan Region of northern Iraq for decades, having fled repression and conflict with the Islamic Republic. These groups include the (PDKI), Komala, the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), PJAK, and the Organization of Iranian Kurdistan Struggle (Khabat).This matters because these groups began to coordinate more in late 2025 and then formed an alliance in January and February 2026. However, they have been cautious about an uprising. Nevertheless, they know tensions with Iran in the region are increasing. Iran may also feel freer to operate in Iraq.The roots of Kurdish groups' presence in Iraq date to the aftermath of Iran's 1979 Islamic Revolution. Kurdish opposition groups clashed with the new Islamic Republic, which sought to consolidate control over Kurdish areas of western Iran.During the Iran-Iraq War and subsequent years, many Kurdish fighters and political activists crossed into northern Iraq. They established camps, political headquarters, and residential compounds, particularly around Erbil, Koya, and Sulaymaniyah.The establishment of the autonomous Kurdistan Region after 1991 provided these groups with a relatively secure base. However, Iran continued pursuing them across the border, including through assassinations, artillery attacks, and airstrikes.Iran increasing use of missiles, drones against Kurdish oppositionOver the last decade, Tehran has increasingly employed ballistic missiles and drones against Iranian Kurdish opposition groups. In September 2018, Iranian missiles struck PDKI headquarters near Koya, killing senior party members and others. Iran launched another major wave of strikes in 2022, following protests sparked by the death of Mahsa Amini in Iranian custody.In 2023, Baghdad and Tehran reached a security agreement intended to disarm Iranian Kurdish groups and relocate them away from the border.As noted above, the attacks escalated dramatically after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026. More than 1,000 drone and missile attacks have targeted the Kurdistan Region since February 28, according to Kurdistan Regional Government figures.This regional total includes attacks on Kurdish opposition camps, diplomatic facilities and infrastructure, rather than exclusively on Iranian Kurdish groups.The continuing strikes highlight the vulnerability of Iranian Kurdish opposition organizations and the challenges facing the Kurdistan Regional Government as it seeks to balance relations with Tehran while protecting refugees living on its territory.This means that any increase in clashes with groups such as PJAK will be watched closely. The messaging from Erbil, as well as groups such as PDKI, shows that the KRG is worried about escalation.

title: 2027: Defeating Tinubu in 12 states is wishful thinking – Lagos APC tells Makinde
body: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has dismissed the claim by Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s campaign organisation that it will defeat President Bola Tinubu in 12 states in the 2027 presidential election. APC described the declaration as grandiose, wishful thinking and political bravado without electoral evidence. Lagos APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, reacting to the claim said participation in an election is not a guarantee of victory. According to him, “Governor Makinde and his campaign team appear to have mistaken the privilege of participating in an election for the guarantee of victory. In the Olympics, participation is celebrated, but no athlete earns a gold medal merely for showing up at the starting line,” the Lagos APC said. The party said the 2027 presidential election is not a theatrical performance rewarded for loudest declarations, noting that it demands national reach, organisational depth, credible structures and capacity to mobilise voters across the federation. “On these fundamental indices, Makinde’s boast raises more questions about the foundations of his confidence than it offers evidence of his electoral strength. Where is the demonstrable national structure? What coalition of enduring value has he assembled?” APC queried. It said Makinde should be more concerned about political crises within his own political family in Oyo State and his unravelling relationships with erstwhile allies, rather than projecting national invincibility. “A politician who has yet to convincingly demonstrate enduring cohesion within his immediate political environment should be cautious about presenting himself as the architect of a nationwide electoral upset,” it said. The party said President Tinubu brings decades of political experience, formidable national network and proven capacity for coalition-building to the 2027 contest, attributes which cannot be wished away by announcing a dozen states. It added that Nigerians will judge platforms on ideas, records and vision, stressing that opposition must do more than announce states it intends to win. “Makinde’s declaration sounds less like a carefully reasoned electoral forecast and more like an attempt to manufacture momentum through headline-grabbing bravado. It is political confidence without sufficiently demonstrated evidence,” the party said. The Lagos APC advised Makinde to spend less time counting imaginary victories and more time examining political turbulence around him, noting that ballot presence does not equal mandate. “After all, in the ultimate reckoning of democracy, the electorate awards the medals, not campaign organisations intoxicated by their own declarations,” Oladejo said. The post 2027: Defeating Tinubu in 12 states is wishful thinking – Lagos APC tells Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tensions continue to mount in Lebanon as Hezbollah challenges Beirut’s authority
body: Tensions between the Lebanese government and Hezbollah have escalated following the Iran-backed terrorist group's recent attempt to obstruct an Internal Security Forces (ISF) operation to inspect a warehouse storing unregulated cancer drugs, according to Lebanese media reports and officials.Hezbollah supporters also protested the seizure of explosives allegedly being trafficked into southern Beirut by the group.Armed men affiliated with Hezbollah surrounded a judicial police patrol vehicle in the Galerie Semaan area on the outskirts of Beirut's southern suburbs after the ISF arrived to raid warehouses suspected of storing unlicensed cancer medications. The armed men withdrew after the Lebanese military arrived at the scene.نفّذت وحدات من الجيش في مدينة بيروت والضاحية الجنوبية تدابير لحفظ الأمن، شملت تسيير دوريات مؤللة وراجلة وإقامة حواجز ظرفية، لملاحقة المطلوبين والمخلين بالأمن. #الجيش_اللبناني #LebaneseArmy https://t.co/2aEJrTWegg https://t.co/h77BkYgHbl— الجيش اللبناني (@LebarmyOfficial) October 17, 2026Hezbollah's political wing subsequently condemned the security forces for carrying out the operation in the area, which it described as being outside its Shi'ite stronghold, “without observing the mechanism agreed upon between Hezbollah and the security services.”According to MTV Lebanon, the ISF acted on the orders of Lebanese Prosecutor-General Ahmad Rami al-Hajj, following a referral from Public Health Minister Rakan Nasser al-Din, who insisted the medications be seized over the risk of spoilage and their failure to meet health standards.Former parliamentarian Wahbi Qatisha, a retired Lebanese Army brigadier-general, told Al Hadath that the medications seized during the operation last week were counterfeit Iranian drugs. He alleged that the trafficking operation was overseen by the son of Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem, a claim repeated by an anonymous source to Alhurra.Reports: Unregulated Iranian, Syrian medications have long entered LebanonThere have long been reports of unregulated Iranian and Syrian medications entering Lebanon. In September, the Lebanese Health Ministry sent samples of suspected counterfeit cancer drugs to France for testing.In 2021, Al Arabiya published an exposé on Iranian medications approved by the Health Ministry despite concerns about a lack of appropriate testing. At the time of the exposé, hospitals reportedly refused to prescribe the Iranian-manufactured drug Lenoma, which former Lebanese health minister Hamad Hassan pushed through despite significant opposition. Hassan was nominated and backed by Hezbollah for the role.مسيرات أمنية مسلّحة لحزب الله جالت في بيروت، رفضاً للتحقيق بشأن شحنة المتفجرات المضبوطة وفقاً لمصادر الحدث https://t.co/OLrfwsxZIQ— الحدث اللبناني (@Alhadath_Leb) October 17, 2026Gen. Ashraf Rifi, a former director of Lebanon's ISF, told Alhurra that the raid on Hezbollah's counterfeit medication warehouse could be a signal that Beirut is changing its approach to dealing with Hezbollah.Notably, the incident came shortly after the Lebanese military seized at least 500 kg. of explosives from Hezbollah-affiliated individuals en route to Beirut.The explosives contained metal balls and shards designed to maximize damage in an explosion. They were reportedly intended for an assassination attempt on Lebanese soil.Hezbollah has reportedly continued to demand the release of the two individuals arrested in connection with the shipment and the return of the seized materials.According to the independent news source This Is Beirut, armed Hezbollah security patrols have openly roamed the streets of Beirut in what has been interpreted as a rejection of the seizure.However, the Lebanese military reported that army units had implemented security measures in Beirut and the southern suburbs, including deploying motorized and foot patrols and establishing temporary checkpoints “to pursue wanted individuals and those disrupting security.”Unconfirmed reports of minor clashes between Hezbollah, Lebanese armed forcesThere are also unverified reports of minor clashes between Hezbollah-affiliated individuals and members of the Lebanese Armed Forces, though officials have not confirmed such reports. الجيش اللبناني يقوم بتطويق المصلى التابع لحزب الله في السعديات  معلومات أولية وقوع إصابات في صفوف أبناء العرب وبعد الإصابات وصفت بالخطيرة https://t.co/n07jztxGRX— LebyNews (@lebynews) October 17, 2026Lebanon's Grand Jaafari Mufti Sheikh Ahmad Qabalan stated during his sermon on Friday that Beirut's actions against Hezbollah were a threat to Lebanese sovereignty and should be seen as in favor of Israel.Qabalan said that Beirut's legitimacy had derived from the legitimacy of the “resistance” and claimed that the security establishment was supporting the “American-Zionist project.”

title: Poland, Bulgaria, now Lithuania: Russia’s suspected arson campaign reaches a third Starlink site serving Ukraine
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Someone tried to set fire overnight to a Lithuanian company that stores Starlink communication equipment, but tipped-off guards foiled the attempt, Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said . He linked the attack to Russia’s hybrid war against Europe. It is the third suspected sabotage of Starlink infrastructure in Europe in under a month. Russia keeps attacking Ukraine at the front and from the air while running a sabotage campaign behind the lines in Europe, which ISW has linked into one pattern. Starlink keeps Ukraine’s drone units and front-line troops connected, and Poland pays for much of that service. Fuel canisters and a control unit The attack came just after midnight, the prime minister wrote. Security services had warned the company about possible attacks, security was stepped up, and the attempt failed. The company provides connectivity through nine Starlink satellite antennas used by Ukraine, Sinkevičius told Lithuanian public radio LRT. At almost 2 a.m., intruders tried to burn the antennas and their control unit, leaving behind incendiary liquid in canisters of 3 to 10 liters. “It is obvious that this is part of Russia’s hybrid war with elements of sabotage,” he said, adding that the client was likely “the Russian side.” He said he believes the people involved, and how many there were, are known, but gave no details, citing the investigation. Police Commissioner General Arūnas Paulauskas said no suspects had been detained, any damage was minimal, and the company kept working. A pretrial investigation is under way. Explore further New Starlink restrictions disrupt Ukrainian drone missions. Kyiv adviser says move is tied to “political situation” A drone the same morning Hours later, an object that apparently entered from Poland crossed northern Lithuania, and NATO jets failed to identify it, Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said . Possible fragments were found in the Pasvalys district near the Latvian border. Latvia’s military said the object may have blown itself up on a course toward Latvia. Sinkevičius said the sabotage version had to be checked for the drone too. He called the National Security Commission for Monday, 19 October, to examine both incidents and consider giving services more powers to neutralize drones. The third Starlink site In September, a fire destroyed the distribution panel at a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska, Poland. Germany detained two Turkish nationals on 12 October, and Warsaw blamed Russian intelligence. In Bulgaria, masked intruders burned 11 of 17 Starlink antennas near Sofia. title: Ukraine Peace Prospects – Q&A
body:
Q? Do you think the Trump–Putin “deal” will see diesel and global energy prices fall?
Answer - No. I don’t see Russia as having much spare diesel capacity to export. Recent Ukrainian deep-strike drone attacks have been successful, forcing shortages at home and forcing the Russian authorities to impose an export ban. I do not expect Ukraine’s deep-strike drone attacks to stop, as they are having an effect. Why would Ukraine stop?
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Answer - I assume that someone in the US administration understands the Russian economy and has told Trump my answer to the first point above. If that is the case, then I think Trump’s messaging around the Russian diesel deal is more to create a scapegoat for the fact that energy prices have remained elevated after Trump’s Iran war. He is seeking to portray Zelensky as the recalcitrant party and responsible for higher global energy prices - even though the evidence still suggests that the biggest driver of higher global energy prices is the Iran war, not the war in Ukraine. Clearly, Trump is trying to change the pitch around midterms, which look increasingly difficult for Trump and the GOP.
Q? Is there an actual energy deal behind the scenes?
Answer - No. Neither the Russian nor Ukrainian side seems to know of any behind-the-scenes deal. One is tempted to think that Trump is making this up as he goes along. Trump seems to think that just by him saying something makes it happen. That’s not the case with Putin and Zelensky. I think Putin and Zelensky have other interests and drivers.
Answer - I think Putin has zero interest in accepting any energy deal right now. His agenda will be focused on the French elections in May 2027, and he will be eager to escalate until then and through the winter. The aim will be to cripple the Ukrainian economy and increase the costs to Europe of supporting Ukraine, to the point that in mid 2027 Europe will have to decide whether and how it continues to support Ukraine.
Putin will offer Trump warm words but deliver nothing. He will take any concessions from Trump, and expect and demand more. The more he holds out for more, the weaker Trump and the Western alliance look. He likely sees Trump as increasingly desperate and incoherent, and he will exploit this by stringing Trump along and, in doing so, further pushing Europe away from the U.S.
Answer - Very likely; actually, he is already doing that. The question is how far he will go in risking a kinetic attack on NATO. As the US backstop for Europe is threadbare, few people trust that Trump would commit US forces to defend Europe. The question is whether this an opportunity that Putin can resist - to test, and diminish NATO’s article 5, while the opportunity is there. Expect more Russian cyberattacks, drone strikes, attacks on European critical infrastructure, assassination attempts against Western industrials, and election meddling, et al.
Q ? Will Ukraine agree to an energy deal?
Answer - Only if Russia agrees, which it is unlikely to do. With that in mind, Ukraine has an interest in continuing to hit Russian energy sector assets - in order to bring the war to Russia. And increasingly it has the autonomous capability to do so.
Q? Will Europe pull the plug on support for Ukraine, if demanded by Trump as the price for a Ukraine peace deal?
Answer - Not for a bad deal. Europe increasingly realizes that a) Russia is an existential threat; b) the US backstop to Europe is no longer there; c) European security depends on Ukraine surviving as long as possible against Russia to allow time for Europe to develop an independent defense capability from the US. When push comes to shove, Europe will choose Ukraine over the US.
See the original in the author’s @tashecon blog here.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.

title: Ukraine retook Kolodiazi north of Lyman as its drones hit 200-plus Russian vehicles in Operation Vivaldi’s last phase, Ukrainian drone officer says
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukrainian infantry encircled and retook the village of Kolodiazi north of Lyman without getting drawn into street fighting, while a drone battalion kept the sky above them shut, the battalion’s chief of staff told Suspilne on 18 October. The village fell during the fourth and final phase of Operation Vivaldi, Ukraine’s counteroffensive in northern Donetsk Oblast. For years now, Russia has aimed to seize Lyman and cross the Siverskyi Donets River. It needs this area to encircle Ukraine’s fortress belt of Donetsk Oblast cities from the northwest, ISW assesses . Vivaldi’s four phases retook 277 km² and 16 settlements on that approach, and a veteran of the operation has said Ukraine’s assault troops suffered more than ten times fewer casualties than Russian forces doing it. Drones over the infantry The 60th Mechanized Brigade fought in all four phases of Vivaldi and took Kolodiazi in the last one, said the chief of staff of the brigade’s Fatum unmanned systems battalion, callsign Krash. “Our task, as an unmanned systems battalion, was to escort and ‘close’ the air in front of our infantry to make it impossible for the enemy to hit it. To suppress all the firing assets possible,” he said. The brigade’s 3rd Mechanized Battalion, the main striking force, encircled Kolodiazi and retook it without getting drawn into street fighting, Krash said. The 1st Mechanized Battalion kept Russian reinforcements out of the area, while drone crews suppressed artillery, hit supply runs, and worked against Russian drone operators. Explore further Vivaldi counteroffensive advanced after Ukraine took Russia’s drones out of the fight, ISW assesses 500 troops and 200-plus vehicles The drone battalion killed or wounded about 500 Russian troops during the fourth phase and struck Russian armored vehicles, trucks, and motorbikes, its chief of staff said. “More than two hundred pieces of various equipment: Grad and Uragan multiple rocket launchers, various armored vehicles, tanks, armored combat vehicles. Most of all motorbikes and quad bikes, there the count runs into the hundreds. This is our enemy’s main logistics tool,” he said. Lyman sector now. Map: ISW Ghost villages The villages retaken in northern Donetsk Oblast are nearly empty of civilians, Krash said. “It’s very typical for de-occupied settlements: these are ghost towns. You can see right away where the occupier stepped. All the settlements are under the control of the Third Army Corps, our forces stand there and prevent enemy infiltration. But civilian life in these towns is either absent or very scarce,” he said. Third Army Corps commander Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi reported Kolodiazi’s liberation, along with Zelena Dolyna and Lypove, when he summed up Vivaldi’s fourth phase, which secured 101 km². title: 2027: We’ll repay good deeds with votes, Jigawa APC chairman says
body: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The All Progressives Congress (APC) Chairman in Ringim Local Government Area of Jigawa State, Bashir Danmalam, has pledged to mobilise massive votes for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi and other party candidates in the 2027 general elections. Danmalam made the pledge on Saturday during an APC stakeholders’ meeting in Ringim, saying residents would reciprocate what he described as the benefits of the APC-led administrations by voting overwhelmingly for the party. He said the developmental projects and political opportunities provided by the administrations had given the people of the area reasons to support the party in the forthcoming elections. “We don’t have enough words to express our gratitude to Governor Umar Namadi and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for what they have done for us. The best way to appreciate them is to vote for the APC again in 2027,” he said. Danmalam said the Namadi administration had addressed several challenges that had affected the local government for decades, particularly unreliable electricity supply. He said connecting Ringim to the Gagarawa electricity grid had brought relief to residents who had endured unstable power supply for more than 30 years. “This administration has solved many serious challenges facing our people for several years, including connecting Ringim to the Gagarawa grid for steady electricity supply, solarising water schemes to improve water availability and providing access to quality education,” he said. The APC chairman also commended the governor for rehabilitating the Ringim General Hospital, constructing a new specialist hospital and providing free drugs to pregnant women and children. He described the appointment of three commissioners from Ringim, overseeing Special Duties, Agriculture and Power, as an unprecedented political opportunity for the area. Danmalam added that more than 30 other political appointments had been given to indigenes of the local government under the present administration. “I don’t think we have ever enjoyed these kinds of privileges in the history of Ringim Local Government Area. The governor has given us more than we expected,” he said. He urged residents, party members and supporters to demonstrate their appreciation by voting for all APC candidates, from the presidency to the State House of Assembly. Danmalam expressed confidence that Ringim would be among the first local government areas in Jigawa State to deliver substantial votes for the ruling party. “By the grace of God, Ringim will be the first local government to deliver victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi and all other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections,” he said. The post 2027: We’ll repay good deeds with votes, Jigawa APC chairman says appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia, Saudi Arabia note importance of international navigation safety — Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 18. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud have noted the importance of ensuring the safety of navigation and passage of ships through all international waterways, said the Russian Foreign Ministry after a meeting of the parties on the sidelines of a ministerial meeting of the strategic dialogue Russia - the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Persian Gulf.
"The current topics on the international and Middle Eastern agenda, including the situation in the Persian Gulf zone, were discussed. The ministers expressed concern about the tension in the south of the Arabian peninsula and in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait. Both sides noted the importance of ensuring the safety of navigation and the unhindered passage of ships through all international waterways," it said in a statement.

title: Settlement expansion, Jewish terror pose severe risk to Israel’s economy, senior economists warn
body: West Bank settlement expansion and rising Jewish terror against Palestinians could expose Israel to sweeping international sanctions, deepen its economic isolation, and drive up the cost of living for all Israelis, a group of 61 senior economists warned in a letter published on Sunday."The damage to Israel's economy could increase by orders of magnitude if such measures spread from a handful of countries to a significant portion of Europe and extend beyond the settlements to the Israeli economy as a whole," the letter read."The expansion of settlements in the West Bank and the failure to prevent Jewish violence and terrorism against Palestinians are causing diplomatic damage to Israel, contributing to its international isolation, and carrying a high economic cost that will ultimately be borne by every resident of the country."This damage must be prevented now, while there is still time," the economists added, noting that the momentum is building in the international sanctions movement."There are currently approximately 100 sanctions imposed by more than 50 countries," they said. "Financial measures and restrictions on arms transactions feature prominently among them."UN blacklist of settlement-linked companies expanding, economists warnThe letter further called attention to the expansion of the United Nations' blacklist of companies linked to Israeli settlements, which as of now "includes 214 companies from 11 countries, most of them Israeli, including all Israeli banks and Tnuva.""These measures add to an atmosphere of boycotts that is already harming Israeli academia, including fields essential to the high-tech industry," the economists said.The sanctions and boycotts further harm Israel's defense industry and cultural sphere, according to the letter, citing the INS Drakon submarine's delivery delays and artists refusing to perform in Israel.Nearly one in three Israeli students considering leaving over living costsThe economists' letter comes amid revelations that nearly one in three Israeli students is considering leaving the country due to the high cost of living, according to a survey by the National Union of Israeli Students.The survey found that the average Israeli student's monthly expenses have reached NIS 6,907, with nearly half of them relying on financial assistance from their parents.Avihai Chiim contributed to this report.

title: Court orders man to sweep mosque for stealing streetlights in Kano
body: A Kano Islamic court has ordered a youth, Ahmad Salisu Sheka, to sweep Murtala Mohammed Friday Mosque and attend all five daily obligatory prayers in congregation. The Upper Sharia Court sitting at Hausawa, Filin Hockey, Kano, presided over by Dr Bello Musa Khalid, convicted Sheka after he pleaded guilty to charges of conspiracy and theft. Following his plea, the court established his guilt through his confession before sentencing him to sweep the mosque and attend the five daily prayers in congregation. The court also ordered him to pay compensation before handing him over to a correctional facility official, Habib H. Habib, for the execution of the sentence. Man allegedly stabbed to death in Kano Mining Marshals deny involvement in operation linked to miners’ deaths Reports indicated that Sheka was arrested alongside his friend over the alleged theft of streetlights in the Sallare neighbourhood. However, his accomplice reportedly escaped from those who apprehended them.

title: Edo tanker explosion: NUPENG grieves over loss of lives, calls for sweeping safety reforms
body: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers, NUPENG, has expressed profound sorrow over the deadly tanker explosion at Oluku, along the Benin-Lagos Highway in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of Edo State, raising fresh concerns over road safety, deteriorating highway conditions and the persistent dangers associated with scooping spilled fuel at accident scenes. The union, in a condolence message to Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, and the people of Oluku community, called for sustained preventive measures to avert similar tragedies, stressing the need for improved road infrastructure, heightened public awareness and stronger collaboration among government agencies and other stakeholders to protect lives and property. In a statement signed by its Acting General Secretary, Comrade Otite Onohwohwo, NUPENG said: “The Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers, NUPENG, is profoundly saddened by the tragic tanker explosion that occurred at Oluku along the Benin-Lagos Highway, Ovia North East Local Government Area, Edo State, on Thursday, 15th October 2026. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to His Excellency, Governor Monday Okpebholo, and to the people of Oluku community in Ovia North East Local Government Area, Edo State. “The loss of lives, the injuries sustained, and the destruction of properties in this incident have left our Union’s leadership and membership in a state of collective mourning. We offer our full solidarity to the affected families and communities, and we pray for the repose of the souls of the departed and the swift healing of the injured. “In line with our role as a responsible organization, NUPENG reaffirms its dedication to supporting the Edo State Government and all stakeholders in implementing effective preventive measures. “We emphasize that this disaster underscores the critical necessity for immediate and sustained action to address the deteriorating state of key roadways, especially in Edo State and across the nation as a whole. “It is disheartening that such fatal events continue to occur despite our ongoing collaborative efforts with safety agencies to educate the public on the dangers of interfering with accident scenes through the scooping of spilled fuel and other flammable substances. “NUPENG salutes the efforts of first responders and medical personnel for their prompt intervention. “NUPENG remains steadfast in its pursuit of a safer transportation ecosystem and calls upon all Nigerians to prioritize safety and maintain vigilance. A concerted effort is essential to eradicate these preventable tragedies. “Our solidarity remains constant, for the Union makes us strong!” The post Edo tanker explosion: NUPENG grieves over loss of lives, calls for sweeping safety reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Immigration ruined France, it must close its borders urgently — Trump
body:
WASHINGTON, October 18. /TASS/. The high level of immigration has led to the destruction of France, and it needs to close the borders as soon as possible, US President Donald Trump.
"France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country. Close the borders and take control of the situation, before it's too late!" he wrote on Truth Social.
On October 17, mass demonstrations were held in Paris and throughout France against rising fuel prices and declining purchasing power. According to the organizers, 800,000 people participated, while the Interior Ministry counted 550,000. In some cities, the protests erupted into riots and clashes with the police. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 1,800 people were detained and vowed to continue to prosecute all those who participated in riots and ransacking.

title: Pope Addresses Crowd In Vatican After Cancer Surgery
body: Pope Leo XIV addressed thousands of people in St Peter’s Square on Sunday, smiling and saying he would resume work “gradually” in his first major public appearance since undergoing lung cancer surgery. The 71-year-old pope had part of his right lung removed in the surgery on Tuesday at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and he was discharged on Saturday. “I would like to thank all the people who have been praying for me in these days,” the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics told the crowd. “Having overcome this delicate phase, as you know I will now gradually resume my activities,” said the pope, who looked well and spoke normally. People listen to Pope Leo XIV in St. Peter’s square during the Angelus prayer, a day after his return to The Vatican following a surgery to remove a cancerous tumour in his right lung, on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Tiziana FABI / AFP) A chorus of “Viva il papa!” (Hooray for the pope!) had reverberated across the square as he appeared at the window of his Apostolic Palace for his traditional Angelus prayer and address. People in the square welcomed the pope’s speedy return. Christopher Butler, 68, a parish priest from Leeds in northern England called Leo a “great shepherd for the Catholic Church”. “I’m concerned he needs to take time to make a full recovery but he’s obviously a very resilient man and keen to return to work, to lead the Church and to be a world leader,” Butler said. Soledad Espinosa, 59, from Ecuador, said she was happy to hear that the pope would be allowed by his doctors to visit Latin America next month. Nuns wait in St Peter’s Square before the Angelus prayer, a day after Pope Leo XIV returns to the Vatican following surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Andreas SOLARO / AFP) “We are all hoping for his recovery and that he has gotten through the situation well. We know that he is ok and we’re pleased,” she said. Norma Grasso, 76, from Argentina, said: “We are waiting for him”. Following the surgery, there had been doubts about a planned papal voyage scheduled for November 6-17, to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where Leo spent two decades as a missionary. But his surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, told Vatican News he believed there were “no clinical reasons why the trip should not go ahead”. ‘Absolutely satisfactory’ The pope’s discharge on Saturday capped days of uncertainty that rattled the Vatican and the world’s Catholics, less than two years into the Chicago-born pope’s papacy. Pope Leo XIV addresses the crowd from the window of the apostolic palace overlooking St. Peter’s square during the Angelus prayer a day after his return to The Vatican following a surgery to remove a cancerous tumour in his right lung, on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Tiziana FABI / AFP) Margaritora said Leo was in “absolutely satisfactory clinical condition,” estimating another ten days before he is fully recovered. Margaritora told Vatican News that Leo’s tumour had been discovered by chance, during a routine abdominal X-ray that captured the “little spot” at the base of his right lung. While calling the lung operation “routine”, he saluted the pope’s commitment to his recovery, saying he “really put his heart and soul into it, like the most motivated patients”. “His determination to achieve a very quick and very effective recovery from every point of view was really commendable,” Margaritora said. The results of tests to determine whether the cancer has spread are still pending. Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky. AFP The post Pope Addresses Crowd In Vatican After Cancer Surgery appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Strike: SSANU suspends two-week ultimatum
body: –Urges FG to reciprocate by releasing 2023 25%/35% salary award arrears, two months’ withheld salaries By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has announced the suspension of the two-week ultimatum issued to the Federal Government to release funds for the implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU Agreement. The suspension, according to a statement issued by the association’s National President, Comrade Mohamed Ibrahim, followed the approval and release of eight months’ arrears by the Federal Government on October 7, 2026. Recall that SSANU, at its 56th National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in the University of Uyo, resolved to issue a two-week ultimatum to the Federal Government to release funds for the implementation of the 2026 Agreement, failing which it would embark on a total and indefinite strike. The Federal Government promptly responded, within two days of the issuance of the ultimatum, by releasing funds for the payment of eight months’ arrears (January to August 2026). Consequently, arising from its National Administrative Committee (NAC) meeting, SSANU has withdrawn the ultimatum. In a statement titled, “Notification of the Suspension of the Two-Week Ultimatum Issued to the Federal Government,” the association stated that the decision reflected its commitment to constructive engagement, peaceful dialogue and the maintenance of cordial relations with the government. The statement read: “Following the two-week ultimatum issued to the Federal Government by the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), which commenced on October 5, 2026, and the subsequent approval and release of eight months’ arrears by the Federal Government on October 7, 2026, the National Administrative Committee (NAC), acting on behalf of the National Executive Council (NEC), wishes to formally inform and notify members of SSANU and the general public of its decision to suspend the ultimatum. “At its meeting, the NAC took cognisance of the Federal Government’s prompt release of funds for the payment of eight months’ arrears of CONTTA owed to SSANU members for the period of January to August 2026. “In recognition of this positive development, mutual understanding and good faith, the NAC, on behalf of the NEC, has resolved to suspend the intended industrial action. “This decision reflects the union’s commitment to constructive engagement, peaceful dialogue and the maintenance of cordial relations with the government, particularly in the interest of sustaining industrial harmony in our citadels of learning. “While acknowledging this development, the union urges the Federal Government to reciprocate this gesture by fulfilling all other outstanding demands, which include the release and payment of the one-year arrears of the 25% and 35% salary award of 2023 and the two months’ 2022 withheld salaries. “It also urges state governments that are yet to implement the 2026 signed agreement to pay other outstanding arrears to our members in state universities. “The union remains committed to dialogue but expects the government to demonstrate the same level of goodwill by taking concrete steps towards resolving all outstanding issues affecting our members across federal and state universities. “All NEC members are hereby notified of this decision and are encouraged to communicate the position of the NAC accordingly. We must continue to engage constructively with relevant stakeholders to preserve the peace in our citadels of learning, while remaining steadfast in the pursuit of the welfare and legitimate interests of our members. “Thank you for your continued commitment and solidarity.” The post Strike: SSANU suspends two-week ultimatum appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Blasts reported in separatist groups bases in Erbil
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Local media in Iraqi Kurdistan Region reported attacks on headquarters of anti-Iran separatist terrorists in Erbil province.
Local Iranian media cited sources in Iraqi Kurdistan region that explosions were heard in the Koyeh District in Erbil province in northern Iraq.
According to Sabireen News, which is close to resistance groups in Iraq, kamikaza drones targeted the headquarters of separatist terrorist groups in Koyeh.

title: 2027 Polls: Katsina governor seeks forgiveness, urges APC unity – News Agency of Nigeria
body:
Governor Dikko Radda of Katsina State has appealed to anyone offended by his administration’s decisions to forgive him, urging unity among All Progressives Congress (APC) members ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Mr Radda made the appeal on Saturday in Katsina while inaugurating the APC campaign council for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and himself.
“I have no grudge against anybody in the party, and I welcome everyone who wants to join the party,” he said.
The governor urged party members to close ranks, mobilise voters and intensify grassroots campaigns to secure victory for APC candidates.
He warned members against relying on the party’s popularity without actively campaigning for votes.
“The time to get into any seat of power by awuf has gone. Come out and campaign massively for votes,” he said.
Mr Radda said APC members must work collectively for Tinubu and all party candidates, from polling units and wards to local, state and federal levels.
He described every party member as an ambassador of Mr Tinubu and other APC candidates, urging them to demonstrate commitment to the party’s collective interests.
The governor expressed confidence in the APC’s electoral prospects in Katsina and across the country, urging members to remain focused on victory.
He thanked residents for their support and patience with his administration over the past three and a half years.
Mr Radda said his administration had recorded significant infrastructure development across the state’s 34 local government areas.
He also said the government consistently paid monthly allowances to APC officials at the state, local government, and ward levels.
According to him, the payments have helped sustain the party’s organisational structure.
Earlier, APC State Chairman, Bishir Gambo-Saulawa, commended Mr Radda for strengthening the party and supporting the construction of its newly completed state secretariat.
He described the secretariat, where the inauguration took place, as a distinctive facility.
Mr Gambo-Saulawa also said the party’s candidates in the state had been duly certified by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
He acknowledged former APC state chairman Sani Ali’s contributions to the secretariat, noting that Mr Ali initiated the project.
During the inauguration, Mr Radda appointed Mr Gambo-Saulawa as the deputy chairman of the campaign council.
Ahmed Dangiwa, an architect, was named Director-General, while Abdullahi Aliyu Turaji was appointed Secretary-General.
Alhaji Sani Aliyu was named the council’s organising secretary.
The Minister of Arts, Culture and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, also commended Mr Radda for the infrastructure development recorded in the state.
Ms Musawa said Mr Tinubu had directed her to work closely with the governor to promote the development of Katsina State.

title: Man allegedly stabbed to death in Kano
body: A Kano magistrate’s court has remanded a youth, Aliyu Nasir, for allegedly stabbing one Magaji Dalladi to death and causing grievous bodily harm to Aminu Nura. Nasir was arraigned before Magistrate Abdulaziz Mahmud of Magistrates’ Court No. 15, Nomansland, Kano, on charges of causing grievous bodily harm and murder. The prosecution counsel, Auwal Sani Dandago, presented the defendant before the court, which ordered his remand in a correctional facility until November 12, 2026, pending government advice. Nasir was accused of stabbing Magaji Dalladi and Aminu Nura, resulting in Dalladi’s death, while Nura is reportedly receiving treatment.
