title: Lagos water corporation serves only 1.03% of population — Official
body:
The Lagos Water Corporation (LWC) says its water network serves 34,424 registered households or an estimated 1.03 per cent of the state’s 20 million residents. The corporation, through the Deputy Director, Corporate Affairs and Brand Management, Rasaq Anifowoshe, disclosed this in an exclusive interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Lagos.
Mr Anifowoshe said this while responding to questions bordering on the LWC’s water coverage and expansion plans.
“Using an estimated average household size of six persons, the number of residents associated with these connections is 206,444, an equivalent to approximately 1.03 per cent of the state’s estimated population of 20 million,” he said.
Mr Anifowoshe disclosed that the corporation had an installed water production capacity of approximately 210 million gallons per day (MGD).
This, he said, was against an estimated state’s daily water demand of approximately 540 MGD, as stated in the Lagos State Water Supply Master Plan.
“A review of the corporation’s 2025 production records indicates an aggregate annual production of approximately 2,633.22 million gallons, equivalent to an average daily production of about 7.21 MGD.
“Based on these records, actual daily production is three per cent of the installed capacity,” he said.
NAN reports that the above figures highlight a substantial gap between installed capacity, actual output and estimated water demand across Lagos State.
Mr Anifowoshe identified ageing distribution pipelines, increasing demand arising from population growth and rapid urbanisation as well as the need to rehabilitate and expand existing water infrastructure as the major constraints.
NAN reports that these challenges affect the corporation’s ability to extend public water supply, particularly to communities relying on boreholes and private vendors.
Across Lagos, residents spend thousands of naira on alternative water sources as irregular public supply and inaccessible connections increase household costs.
Some Lagos residents interviewed by the NAN across Iponri, Oworonshoki, Costain, Apapa Road and Ebute Metta revealed concerns about unreliable supply, failed facilities and inadequate water pressure.
At the Iponri Housing Estate, Adebayo Solomon, said his household spent about N1,500 daily on vendor-supplied water, amounting to N45,000 monthly.
Mr Solomon said the expenditure would total approximately N547,500 if sustained throughout the year.
He said electricity shortages sometimes disrupted water availability, forcing his household to manage stored supplies or pay higher rates.
Mr Solomon said he would welcome an LWC connection if it provided regular supply and reduced dependence on vendors.
Another Iponri resident, Abdulkareem Ibrahim, said he relied on public boreholes provided by philanthropists because his community received no LWC supply.
“I depend on public water, the one provided by philanthropists. I fetch it in the morning or when I return from work at night,” he said.
Mr Ibrahim said the boreholes helped him avoid direct water expenses, although power interruptions sometimes disrupt pumping, forcing him to buy from vendors.
“I am just happy that we have water at all, all thanks to our magnanimous neighbours,” he said.
In Oworonshoki, Amanda Ogbodo, said she spent between N2,200 and N3,600 weekly on vendor-delivered borehole water.
Mrs Ogbodo said the expenditure amounts to between N8,800 and N14,400 over four weeks.
She said the LWC water had flowed more consistently in parts of her area over the preceding four months, mainly from Friday afternoons into Saturday.
However, she disclosed that homes on the higher ground remained underserved because of insufficient pressure, leaving residents on the lower ground better supplied.
She recalled that her business premises previously received LWC water, with eight or nine users contributing N10,000 monthly.
Mrs Ogbodo said supply stopped for about four years after a pipe broke and residents were told repairs were necessary.
She said water returned intermittently in 2025 but had only recently become more consistent.
“Electricity shortages over the preceding two weeks had also reduced availability and increased water costs.
“We plead with the government to help us run the pipe again and resume provision of constant water access,” she said.
At Costain, Eniola Adewale, said a truckload of water costs between N1,200 and N1,500, with vendors sometimes doubling prices during shortages.
She said her household relied on mobile vendors because the public facility was distant and supplied water irregularly.
Ms Adewale said she distrusted vendor-supplied water because its source was unknown, using sachet water for cooking instead.
Eunice David, a food vendor on Thomas Street, Costain, said she spent substantial amounts monthly pumping water for household use.
Mrs David said a public water facility previously serving her community had been non-functional for some time.
“We don’t know what to do again. We need help from the government,” she said, appealing for regular and affordable public water,” he said.
On Opeoluwa Street, Apapa Road, Garuba Alasan, said the public water facility had been non-functional for about 20 years.
“I have lived here for about 30 years, and in the past 20 years, I have used private water sources for my water needs,” he said.
At Vaughan Street in Costain, Anthony Olamide, a point-of-sale operator, said residents had an LWC connection, although supply depended largely on electricity.
Mr Olamide said residents contributed N1,000 monthly towards water supply, reducing alternative-water expenses when public water was available.
However, power outages stopped supply, sometimes forcing households to buy from vendors.
At Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction Ebute Metta, Esther Emokpaire said her household spent between N1,000 and N1,500 per truckload of vendor-supplied water.
She said the household usually purchased water every two days, with prices varying according to availability.
Mrs Emokpaire said vendors claimed the water was clean and treated, although her household had not verified its quality.
“There was a time when members of my household developed skin rashes after bathing with water purchased from vendors,” she said.
She added that shortages made water harder to obtain and sometimes prompted vendors to increase prices.
Residents’ accounts show how irregular supply, failed facilities and inadequate pressure leave households paying for alternatives, including in communities with existing public connections.
Their experiences raise questions about the reach of public water infrastructure, supply reliability and whether announced interventions are translating into improved access.
However, the Lagos State Government’s second-quarter 2026 budget implementation report showed that 36.2 per cent of the approved annual budget for improving 15 existing mini and micro waterworks had been spent by June 30.
The report also recorded expenditure equivalent to four per cent of the approved annual budget for the Adiyan Phase II Waterworks project.
These expenditure figures do not establish the projects’ physical completion status or how much water they currently supply.
Speaking on the corporation’s plan for increasing public water coverage across the state, Mr Anifowoshe disclosed plans of rehabilitation and upgrade of micro/mini treatment plants.
“This will make water accessible to over 5,616,000 households upon full rehabilitation, thereby fulfilling the mandate of the corporation to provide potable water to Lagosians,” he said.
He also identified extension of distribution network to increase access to potable water for Lagosians as another plan.
Meanwhile, the corporation has announced plans to rehabilitate Ojokoro Mini Waterworks and construct Lagos Island Micro Waterworks to improve public water supply.
Mr Anifowoshe also listed the rehabilitation and upgrading of micro and mini water treatment plants among the corporation’s planned interventions.
He said the intervention would make water accessible to more than 5.6 million households upon full rehabilitation.
He listed digitisation of the distribution network as another planned intervention to enable digital monitoring and remote management of underground pipes and other assets.
According to Anifowoshe, the initiative will help reduce water losses and non-revenue water.
He also disclosed plans to construct the Igbonla 100 MGD water treatment plant to boost supply along the Lekki-Epe corridor.
“This will increase the production capacity of the corporation to meet the demand for water in the Lekki-Epe corridor,” he said.
For residents who continue spending thousands of naira on alternative water sources, the impact of these interventions will ultimately depend on reliable supply, functioning facilities and wider household connections across Lagos State.

title: France Reeling From Cost-of-Living Riots as 1,800 Arrested
body:
France was reeling on Sunday from widespread damage caused by violent protests the day before that saw 1,800 people arrested, a historic town hall torched and widespread looting.
“It’s like we had a war,” a 78-year-old resident in central Paris, Mehmet Ozeden, told AFP amid burnt street barricades from the protests.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The convulsion raised the stakes for President Emmanuel Macron, who is in his final months in power before elections to replace him in six months’ time. It followed weeks of student protests that had also turned violent at times.
Macron was to address the nation Sunday evening at 6 p.m. GMT, his office said, after meeting key ministers.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 1,800 people were arrested over the protests and looting, with investigations under way “to identify the perpetrators of these acts so they can be brought to justice”.
Torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris scarred numerous streets in Paris, where officials said 557 people were in custody after a “record” number of arrests.
The capital experienced “a level of violence that we have never, I believe, seen before”, said Paris deputy mayor Lamia El Aaraje.
Hundreds of shops were looted in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, during the protests over the cost of living.
One person died during the main march in Paris, but officials said it was health-related and not linked to the protest violence.
Around 1,500 businesses were damaged, causing losses estimated in the hundreds of millions of euros, according to the Retail and Trade Federation.
One Paris resident, Anita Gras, out for a jog between the debris, said she saw young men loot a sports shoe retailer.
“They stayed until 1:00 am, we were afraid they were going to throw things at us,” she said.
“It’s appalling, terrifying -- groups of young people came here yesterday (Saturday), looting, smashing everything, with total impunity,” said another resident, 57-year-old Cecile Rogue, surveying a pile of charred bicycles.
The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire. The local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI it had been deliberately set by “a wild horde” and was only brought under control early Sunday.
The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, said “the chaos that reigned in the city for several hours was abominable”.
A tourist office in the centre of Lyon was set ablaze during the protests, which saw multiple clashes and looting.
Political recriminations have followed, with the government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen blaming ultra-left groups, while far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon accused authorities of inflaming tensions.
Paris’s Socialist deputy mayor El Aaraje accused Le Pen’s party of “acting like a pyromaniac firefighter”, using the protests to further her presidential ambitions.
US Vice President JD Vance also waded in, implying on X that the unrest was because France had “imported the third world”.
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu was to chair a crisis meeting of ministers at 0800 GMT on Monday, his office said. They were to look at the insurance and help for impacted shops as well as the prosecution of perpetrators of the violence.
In Paris, startled tourists were seen Saturday running with suitcases along streets filled with tear gas and protesters.
A Danish tourist, Soren Petersen, said it was “sad” to see damage to Paris buildings. “It is not a protest, it’s far beyond a normal protest,” he told AFP.
An American tourist, Jill Burns, said “we were scared”.
Around 500 police, firefighters and paramedics were hurt in the protests, the interior minister said.
The violence took place on the sidelines of nationwide protests that the interior ministry said were attended by 550,000 people. The CGT union said 800,000 people participated.
A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Etienne.
Analyst Mujtaba Rahman of the Eurasia Group think tank said on X that most of the demonstrations Saturday were peaceful, and “the violence came from a fringe of the ultra left” with looting “by opportunistic gangs from the poor suburbs”.
“All good news for Marine Le Pen,” he said.
France’s Yellow Vest movement, which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron’s government over planned fuel-tax hikes, had called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations.
The principal grievance was the cost of living, pushed up in part by the war in the Middle East, which has helped send inflation soaring in Europe as elsewhere.

title: NATO’s expansion has taught Russia not to be naive in relations with West — diplomat
body:
VIENNA, October 18. /TASS/. The failure of NATO leaders to honor their promises not to expand the alliance eastward has taught Russia not to be naive in its relations with the West, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the Vienna-based international organizations Mikhail Ulyanov said.
"These commitments were violated. Now NATO propagandists claim that leaders of the Alliance never promised to abandon eastward expansion. It was a painful, but useful lesson for Russia: don’t be naive when you deal with the West," he wrote on X.
As an example of such a pledge, the Russian diplomat cited a statement made by the then German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher back in 1990, where he said that NATO had no plans to expand its defense structures eastwards, including to the territory of the former German Democratic Republic.

title: EU To Offer €20m Defence Support For Nigerian Armed Forces
body: The European Union (EU) is planning to provide €20 million in defence assistance to the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) under the European Peace Facility. The proposed support was discussed when the Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, met with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, at Ship House in Abuja. In a statement on Saturday, the minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, said an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details of the assistance. The meeting also reviewed security cooperation between Nigeria and the EU, with Mignot commending Musa’s efforts to improve the country’s security situation. The ambassador also invited the minister to a meeting of defence ministers in Brussels later this year. The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, met with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, at Ship House in Abuja. Musa thanked the EU for its continued support and reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to protecting lives and promoting national development. He said relative peace was gradually returning to troubled parts of the country through the efforts of the armed forces and other security agencies, although kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities remained a challenge. The minister also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting the delivery of 10 attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other military equipment to strengthen security operations. On regional security, Musa identified the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, which supports more than 50 million people, as a potential source of instability. He said denying terrorists access to holding areas on the Lake Chad islands remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force. On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme, the minister stressed that the initiative should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel. Mignot also commended a recent conference of past and present MNJTF force commanders, attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission. The post EU To Offer €20m Defence Support For Nigerian Armed Forces appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Police arrest 95 suspected ‘Vikings’ cultists in Delta, recover five guns
body: The Delta State Police Command has arrested 95 suspected cultists and recovered five firearms, 12 live cartridges and seven expended cartridges during coordinated operations across four local government areas of the state. The operations, conducted on October 15, 2026, targeted suspected cultists in Asaba, Ika South, Ughelli South and Okpe local government areas, according to a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe, on Friday. The recovered firearms comprised two pump-action guns, one locally fabricated cut-to-size gun and two locally made pistols. The police said the operations involved operatives of the Department of Operations, Rapid Response Squad (RRS) and Command Anti-Cultism Unit (CACU), acting on intelligence about suspected cult activities. In Asaba, operatives raided a hotel along Abraka Road following intelligence that suspected members of the Supreme Vikings Confraternity (SVC), also known as Aro Bagger, had gathered for an alleged cult anniversary celebration. The operation led to the arrest of 67 suspects, comprising 55 males and 12 females. Police said they recovered two pump-action guns, one locally fabricated cut-to-size gun, 10 live cartridges, five expended cartridges, 11 caps bearing suspected cult insignia and two jackets bearing suspected cult branding. In a related operation in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area, RRS operatives arrested 15 additional suspects, comprising 14 males and one female, over suspected links to the same confraternity. The command also reported an operation at Jeremy Community in Ughelli South Local Government Area, where operatives of the Command Anti-Cultism Unit, Ovwian-Aladja Sector, working with a civilian anti-cult group, raided a suspected criminal hideout. Three suspects, identified as John Pius, 32; Oghene Ochuko, 28; and Akinbule Godstime, 24, were arrested, while others reportedly fled. The police said two locally made pistols, two live cartridges, two expended cartridges, two caps bearing suspected cult insignia and suspected charms were recovered during the operation. In another operation at Jeddo Community in Okpe Local Government Area, 10 additional male suspects were arrested over suspected cult activities. The command said all the suspects and recovered exhibits were in police custody, while investigations were ongoing. The Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, commended the operatives and directed area commanders, divisional police officers and tactical commanders to intensify operations against cult groups across the state. He warned that the command would not tolerate cult-related activities capable of threatening public peace and urged residents to provide credible information to assist the police in tackling crime. The post Police arrest 95 suspected ‘Vikings’ cultists in Delta, recover five guns appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Lithuania links attempted arson at Starlink equipment facility to Russia
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said this, according to LRT.
According to him, the relevant authorities warned the company in advance of possible attacks and strengthened security, preventing the attempted arson.
Sinkevičius believes Russia was likely behind the attempted arson at the Lithuanian facility where Starlink equipment is stored.
He said the Lithuanian authorities are monitoring the activities of hostile states “very closely” and taking measures to protect people and their property.
Later, speaking on LRT radio, Sinkevičius said similar or related incidents had already occurred abroad, including in Poland and Bulgaria. He linked the incident to Russia’s hybrid war against Europe.
“At around 02:00, there was an attempt to burn satellite antennas and a control unit. Incendiary liquids were found, along with containers ranging in capacity from three to 10 litres. The fact is that this was clearly an attempted act of sabotage or diversion, as we are seeing similar actions repeated across Europe. It is obvious that [...] this is part of Russia’s hybrid war, involving acts of sabotage,” the Prime Minister said on LRT radio.
“We will learn more about who ordered it, how everything happened and who was behind it. It is likely that it is already clear who commissioned it – it is the Russian side,” he added.
Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas also confirmed the information, but stressed that he could not provide further details at this time.
“We will learn more about who ordered it, how everything happened and who was behind it. It is likely that it is already clear who commissioned it – it is the Russian side,” he added.
Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas also confirmed the information but stressed that he could not yet provide further details.
“The incident has been brought under control and prevented, but it is also being investigated,” the minister told journalists on Sunday.
Jolita Orentaitė, head of the Communications Division at the Fire and Rescue Department (PAGD), told BNS that a pre-trial investigation had been launched into the incident.
The Prime Minister has convened a meeting of the National Security Commission for October 19 to discuss the attempted arson, as well as an incident involving a drone that crashed in northern Lithuania earlier on Sunday.
The commission will also consider expanding the powers of Lithuanian agencies to neutralize drones.
As reported by Ukrinform, last week Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said he had authorized the use of the military to reinforce security along the border with Russia’s Kaliningrad region.

title: Richard Branson Condemns Trump Policy on Russia, Urges European Aid
body:
British billionaire and Virgin Group founder Sir Richard Branson has condemned US President Donald Trump’s foreign policy approach toward Russia , warning that Washington’s diplomatic and economic accommodations to Vladimir Putin compromise Western security and undermine allied trust.
Writing on LinkedIn on Sunday, Oct. 18, Branson criticized recent White House decisions to ease energy sanctions on Moscow and restrict technical support to Kyiv, calling on European leaders to step forward and deliver decisive military and financial support to Ukraine.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“I never thought I’d have to say this in my lifetime, but it’s 2026, and unfortunately, nothing is the way it used to be,” Branson wrote.
“The Trump administration has become an enabler of autocrats and dictators, placing their personal whims ahead of the interests of the American people and the free world.”
The entrepreneur questioned the administration’s posture toward the Russian head of state, asking: “What is it about [Russian President Vladimir] Putin that makes President Trump fawn over him? How can America’s allies ever trust this administration again, when it is now turning against them in a time of war and suffering?”
BREAKING NEWS: Billionaire Sir Richard Branson launches a SCATHING attack on Trump and his disgusting coziness with Russian dictator Vladimir Putin. This is EXACTLY the kind of thing that gets under Trump’s skin... "I never thought I’d have to say this in my lifetime, but it’s… pic.twitter.com/d2drBRfTVX
Branson highlighted a series of recent policy shifts in Washington that have raised concerns among Ukraine’s allies, pointing specifically to the commercial diesel agreement between the US and Russia alongside restrictions affecting Ukrainian defense capabilities.
Under the commercial framework announced on Oct. 9 , Moscow agreed to deliver refined diesel onto global markets through 2027 to mitigate fuel benchmark inflation, supported by a US Treasury general license. Branson noted that facilitating fuel exports injects direct revenue into the Russian state budget during active military operations.
The Virgin Group founder also cited reports regarding technical and intelligence constraints imposed on Ukrainian forces, including delays in US early-warning missile tracking notifications and the throttling of SpaceX’s military-grade Starshield satellite network.
“The throttling of Starlink /Starshield and the inexplicable failure to provide advance warning of Russian missile launches have already led to the needless deaths of Ukrainian civilians,” Branson stated. “How much worse can it get?”
The criticism follows statements by President Volodymyr Zelensky disclosing that an artificial 161 km/h (100 mph) velocity cap placed on Starlink terminals operating inside Ukraine had impaired domestic interceptors targeting Russian turbojet-powered strike drones.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and President Trump have denied ordering deliberate operational curbs , with Rubio stating that Starshield remains a dedicated US military capability not currently accessible to Ukraine for deep strikes inside Russia.
With transatlantic relations strained by shifting policies in Washington ahead of the Nov. 3 US midterm elections , Branson urged European governments to overcome hesitation and assume greater leadership in European security.
“If one thing is clear, it’s that European leaders must move past the initial shock of Trump’s recent actions and step up,” Branson wrote. “This is as much about European freedom as it is about Ukraine’s sovereignty. Both are worth fighting for.”
The British business leader urged European capitals to explore all available mechanisms to support Ukraine’s defense, including the full mobilization of immobilized Russian state reserves and the transfer of advanced standoff weapon systems.
“Every option should now be on the table – from transferring frozen Russian assets to Ukraine, to delivering advanced weapons systems like the German Taurus ,” Branson emphasized. “We cannot allow the free world to be dismantled before our very eyes.”
The appeal arrives as EU leaders instructed the European Commission to draft proposals bridging Ukraine’s projected €70 billion ($79 billion) financial shortfall for 2027 , with discussions encompassing plans to leverage proceeds from roughly €210 billion in Russian sovereign assets immobilized in European financial depositories.

title: Several dead or injured in major fire at Canada military base
body: Several people have been killed or injured as a result of a large fire near a Canadian military base in Alberta, the nation’s defence minister has said. David McGuinty did not confirm the cause or the number of casualties, describing the situation as “very, very active and delicate”. The Canadian military and local authorities were managing the fire, he said. Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where the fire broke out, is one of the country’s busiest military training bases. Canadian TV network Global News reported that at least seven were killed and dozens more injured when a gas line or gas well was hit during a live-fire training exercise, citing unnamed military sources. Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney said that a “serious incident creating a major fire” had occurred, adding that his “thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected”. The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) said Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton had declared a code orange, a disaster response protocol for responding to a high-casualty incident. Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor there, told the broadcaster that the number of patients would otherwise “overwhelm” Edmonton’s healthcare facilities. “It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster.” After the fire erupted on Saturday, it “spread rapidly due to high winds” and tore through the fences of the base, the Municipal District of Wainwright said. The region experienced gusts of up to 100km/h (62mph), though local officials indicated fire crews had contained the blaze. The defence minister told reporters he “cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory”. It is unclear when the fire broke out, but the district first posted about the incident at about 17:30 local time (23:30 GMT). Local authorities have urged residents to avoid the area and give all emergency vehicles right of way. The mayor of the nearby town of Wainwright, Bruce Pugh, said it was a “heavy day” for his community. “We have neighbours who are either serving or former members of the Canadian Armed Forces. We’re integrated, our kids play in the same hockey teams, attend the same schools,” he told CBC. While details on the impact of the fire remain unclear, Pugh said he believed this would come to be the area’s largest-ever mass casualty event. Alberta’s Premier Danielle Smith said the “significant and tragic fire” was “affecting many of [the province’s] brave military personnel”. Neighbouring provinces have mobilised in support. Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said he had deployed resources to Alberta and was “ready to provide more if required”, while British Columbia Premier David Eby said his government had offered “all possible assistance”. Wainwright is the main base used by the Canadian military for live-fire training exercises, according to CBC, with about 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers on-site on a typical day.

title: Priest dies after statue of Jesus falls on him during mass livestream
body: A Catholic priest died after a cross fell on top of him while he was performing a mass in Ecuador, which was being livestreamed at the time. Footage shared widely on social media shows Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari, the parish priest of Perpetuo Socorro, addressing his congregation in Guayaquil on Saturday before the crucifix came tumbling down on top of him. The Archdiocese of Guayaquil on Sunday confirmed that Father Molinari had died in a post on social media which said: “We announce that our beloved Fr. Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari, CSsR., who served as parish priest of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in the Central Vicariate, has departed for the Father’s House to rejoice in His presence and glory.” “Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord. And let perpetual light shine upon him. May he rest in peace. Amen.”

title: 2027: Jigawa Fulani community endorses Tinubu, Namadi, commends livestock development initiatives
body:
The Fulani Community in Jigawa State has endorsed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi, and all aspirants seeking elective positions under the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The endorsement was announced during a community gathering organised under the leadership of Shehu Hadejia, at the Manpower Development Institute, Dutse, to appreciate the Jigawa State Government for its efforts to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders and its interventions to improve livestock development across the state.
Speaking at the event, the community leader, Shehu Hadejia, said the gathering was organised to acknowledge the government’s role in sustaining peaceful relations between farming and herding communities, as well as the establishment of the Ministry of Livestock Development.
He particularly commended the government for initiatives introduced through the ministry, including the gazetting of grazing reserves, animal vaccination programmes and other interventions aimed at improving livestock production and addressing the needs of herders.
Governor Namadi, in his remarks, described the gathering as an important event, saying that members of the Fulani community had come from different parts of the state to express appreciation to the government and declare their support for the president, the governor, and APC candidates.
“Today is also another important day for us. Today, the entire Fulani community in Jigawa State is here,” he said.
He further said that the gathering demonstrated the community’s position on the political developments ahead of the 2027 general elections.
“You can see the number of people who came from all over the state. And they were here to endorse Mr President, the Governor, and all the APC candidates in Jigawa State.”
The governor reiterated his administration’s efforts to address challenges facing livestock owners through the provision of grazing areas, watering stations, and the cultivation of alfalfa to provide feed for animals.
“We have provided watering stations in every location. We are also working to grow alfalfa so that there will be sufficient food for the animals.
“We are ready to provide feed. We are ready to provide water, hospitals, schools, and everything else for them.
Governor Namadi also stated that the state had invested about ₦3.1 billion in artificial insemination over the last two to three years to improve cattle breeds and increase milk production, and has been undertaking regular animal vaccination for the protection of livestock health.
He emphasised that peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders remained essential to sustaining the peace and stability enjoyed in Jigawa State, urging communities to continue cooperating with government and security agencies to identify and report individuals whose activities could threaten public peace.
Also speaking, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Mohammed, highlighted programmes and achievements recorded by the ministry within its relatively short period of establishment.
He listed the demarcation of additional grazing reserves, animal vaccination programmes and sensitisation campaigns promoting peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders among the ministry’s key interventions.

title: Moscow advises Latvian PM to turn on TV after words about visas for Russians
body:
MOSCOW, October 18. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova has advised Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, who called on the EU to stop issuing tourist visas to Russians, to turn on the TV and see who really threatens Europe.
"Turn on the TV for Kulbergs - it shows who not in the future, but in present, not hybrid, but primitive, not threatening, but smashing the EU - EU citizens," the diplomat wrote on Telegram.

title: SEHRB, Intersociety allege killings, torture in South-East
body: By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU — A coalition of human rights organisations has called for an independent investigation into alleged killings, torture, enforced disappearances, secret burials and deaths in custody linked to security operations in South-East Nigeria. The coalition, comprising the South-East Human Rights Bureau (SEHRB), Oganihu Igbo Development Foundation and the International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), also demanded a probe into reports of unidentified bodies in mortuaries in Imo State. Addressing a joint press conference in Enugu on Saturday, the organisations alleged that some detainees had been subjected to prolonged detention without access to their families and lawyers, as well as torture and other forms of inhuman treatment. They expressed concern that persons reportedly arrested in the South-East had been transferred to detention facilities outside the region, including Wawa Barracks in Niger State and custodial centres in Kuje and Suleja, without their families being adequately informed of their whereabouts. “Our position is clear: the State has a duty to protect citizens from violence, but security operations must themselves comply with the law. Fighting lawlessness cannot justify lawlessness by the State,” the coalition said. The organisations presented accounts from families whose relatives allegedly disappeared after being arrested by security operatives, with some reportedly remaining unaccounted for years after their arrest. One of the cases highlighted was that of Ozioma Elizabeth Onyeaka, a 35-year-old teacher from Anambra State, who reportedly disappeared for more than five years before her family learnt that she was alive and being detained at Wawa Barracks. The coalition also raised concerns over the case of Sunday Ifedi and his wife, Calista, who were reportedly arrested by operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) in Enugu in 2021 and transferred to Wawa Barracks. According to the organisations, Sunday regained his freedom after more than four years in detention, while Calista allegedly died in custody. The coalition said allegations attributed to Sunday and human rights activist Omoyele Sowore indicated that Calista was buried in a shallow grave at Wawa Barracks. It demanded an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding her reported death, the disclosure of relevant custody and medical records, and the identification of her burial location. The organisations said that if the allegations were established, her remains should be recovered and released to her family for a dignified burial. Another case cited was that of Esther Okwudili Egbom, who was reportedly arrested by DSS operatives during a night prayer programme in Aba, Abia State, in February 2025. Her daughter, Chiamaka, alleged that the operatives were searching for another person who had fled before their arrival but arrested her mother because she owned the ministry where the operation took place. The family reportedly had not seen Egbom since the incident. Chiamaka also alleged that her brother was beaten during the operation and subsequently died. The coalition demanded that the DSS account for Egbom’s whereabouts and investigate the circumstances surrounding the alleged death of her son. Other testimonies presented by the organisations included allegations of torture, prolonged detention and denial of family contact involving persons reportedly arrested in Owerri, Orlu and other parts of the South-East. The coalition said the allegations, if substantiated, could amount to serious violations of constitutional rights, the Anti-Torture Act 2017 and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations. Probe of unidentified bodies On reports of unidentified bodies in Imo State, the organisations called for independent forensic investigations to establish the identities of the deceased and determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths. They demanded the preservation of mortuary registers, police records, autopsy reports and other relevant evidence, as well as the use of DNA testing where necessary to identify the remains. The coalition urged the Federal Government, the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, military authorities, the Attorney-General of the Federation and the National Human Rights Commission to establish an independent investigative mechanism to examine the allegations of disappearances, torture and deaths in custody. It also called for a comprehensive audit of detention facilities to establish the identities and legal status of detainees, their custody histories and whether they had access to judicial safeguards. The organisations, however, condemned killings, abductions and other atrocities allegedly committed by armed separatist elements, criminal gangs and other non-state actors in the region. “There must be no hierarchy of victims,” they said, adding that civilians killed by armed criminals, persons unlawfully killed by security personnel, detainees who disappear in state custody, torture survivors and unidentified dead all deserved truth, justice and accountability. The coalition urged the National Assembly, the Nigerian Bar Association, civil society groups, religious and traditional leaders, and the media to support credible investigations into the allegations. “The missing must be accounted for. The detained must have access to justice. The dead must be identified and treated with dignity,” the organisations said. The post SEHRB, Intersociety allege killings, torture in South-East appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Abiodun mourns
body:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has expressed deep sorrow over the death of the Ogun State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, describing his passing as a painful loss to the Corps, the road safety community and the nation.
Governor Abiodun commiserated with the Corps Marshal and the national leadership of the FRSC in Abuja, the management, officers and men of the Corps across the country, as well as the family, friends and professional associates of the deceased.
The governor noted that the late Ogunjobi’s commitment to road safety administration, public enlightenment and stakeholder engagement reflects the importance of dedicated service to the protection of lives and property.
He observed that the late Sector Commander played an important role in promoting responsible road use, improving compliance with traffic regulations and advancing efforts to make Ogun State’s roads safer for motorists and other road users.
Governor Abiodun described the death as a painful loss, particularly at a time when the collective efforts of road safety officials remain critical to reducing road traffic crashes and protecting the lives of citizens.
While praying for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul, he urged his family, colleagues and associates to take solace in the worthy service he rendered to the nation.
He prayed that God would grant the bereaved family, the FRSC national leadership, officers and men of the Corps, and all those affected by the loss the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss.

title: Soldiers killed as military van runs into ISWAP landmine in Borno
body: A Nigerian army patrol vehicle hit a landmine planted by Islamic State group-aligned jihadists near the border with Cameroon, killing eight soldiers, defence sources told AFP Sunday. The attack happened in the northeastern state of Borno on Saturday, the same day the Nigerian Army Chief, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, was visiting the state capital, Maiduguri, over an attack on a base days earlier that killed 15 soldiers and five anti-jihadist militia members. Jihadist violence in Nigeria which erupted in 2009 has eased since its peak a decade ago, but violence has been on the rise in the last two years. In the latest attack, troops were inspecting anti-jihadist militia members who were clearing thickets along the highway outside the town of Gamboru when their vehicle rolled over the mine and exploded, killing all eight on board, the sources said. Wase mobilises stakeholders to tackle insecurity Corruption turning Nigerian courts to ‘market stalls’ – Retired Justice Augie The sources blamed the attack on Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), which is active in the area. Jihadists use thickets along the highway as cover to ambush troops and motorists. “All eight soldiers in the vehicle were killed in the explosion,” which happened in Kinuba village, 25 kilometres (15.5 miles) from Gamboru, a military officer in the region said. Ibrahim Liman, an anti-jihadist militia member assisting the military against jihadists, gave the same toll. “The explosive was planted on the dusty road and remotely detonated by a detonating cord,” Liman said. A militia member supervising the thicket clearing was injured by shrapnel, said Liman. ISWAP and rival jihadist group Boko Haram have increasingly resorted to planting mines on highways against military and civilian targets. The long jihadist conflict has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced around two million from their homes in Nigeria’s northeast. The violence has spread to neighbouring Niger, Chad and Cameroon, prompting a regional military coalition to fight the militants. (AFP) Editor’s note: This picture was used for illustration

title: Gov’t will not lower certification standards under One Million Coders Programme – Sam George
body: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George, says that the government will maintain international certification standards under the One Million Coders Programme (OMCP), even if the requirements make the training more demanding for beneficiaries. He explained that lowering the standards could undermine the international recognition of certificates earned by trainees and jeopardise remote employment opportunities being secured for graduates. Mr George made the remarks during an interaction with trainees as part of a monitoring tour of OMCP learning centres and rural telephony projects in the Volta Region. He was responding to concerns from a beneficiary training to become a cybersecurity expert, who said the course was too demanding. The Minister insisted that maintaining internationally recognised certification benchmarks was in the best interest of trainees, as the government sought to prepare them for opportunities beyond Ghana. He disclosed that the government was engaging Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) companies to create internship and remote employment opportunities for programme graduates. Among the companies involved is a Kenyan firm seeking to establish a centre in Ghana with plans to employ 5,000 people, he said. According to Mr George, the courses offered under the OMCP were deliberately selected to meet the skills requirements of such companies. He urged beneficiaries to progress beyond the beginner level to advanced training, noting that the job market increasingly required higher-level competencies. The Minister added that the training modules were self-paced and free, allowing participants to continue their studies outside the learning centres using their login credentials. He also encouraged trainees with general academic backgrounds to complete the specialised information and communications technology (ICT) versions of their courses to improve their readiness for the job market. As part of the tour, the Minister presented 200 Lenovo laptops to the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS) in Ho under the programme. The laptops feature Intel Core i5 processors, 16GB of RAM, 512GB solid-state drive storage and Windows 11 operating systems. Mr George said the donation was intended to equip future healthcare professionals with digital skills to complement their clinical training as the university expanded technology-based learning. “The medical field is changing very fast. Telemedicine is a big part of the world today, where you have doctors sitting in John Hopkins and carrying out surgery 7,000 miles across the ocean using robotic arms,” he said. He stressed the importance of combining clinical expertise with technological knowledge to keep pace with advances in medical practice. Vice-Chancellor of UHAS, Professor Lydia Aziato, expressed gratitude for the support, saying the selected OMCP learning pathways would complement the university’s professional health sciences training. She added that the courses would help students develop skills in digital literacy, data analytics and emerging technologies.

title: Jigawa Fulani community endorses Tinubu, Namadi, APC candidates
body: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Fulani community in Jigawa State has endorsed President Bola Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The endorsement was announced at a gathering held at the Manpower Development Institute, Dutse, where community members commended the state government for its efforts to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders. Speaking at the event, the community leader, Alhaji Shehu Hadejia, said the decision to support APC candidates was in recognition of the government’s efforts to address the challenges facing livestock farmers across the state. He particularly commended Namadi for establishing the Ministry of Livestock Development and introducing programmes aimed at improving livestock production and reducing conflicts between farmers and herders. According to him, the gazetting of grazing reserves, regular animal vaccination and other livestock development initiatives have helped improve the welfare of herders in the state. Responding, Namadi described the endorsement as a demonstration of the community’s confidence in his administration and the APC-led government. “Today is also another important day for us. Today, the entire Fulani community in Jigawa State is here,” the governor said. “You can see the number of people who came from all over the state. And they were here to endorse Mr President, the governor, and all the APC candidates in Jigawa State.” Namadi reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving livestock production through the provision of grazing reserves, watering stations and animal feed. He said the government was also promoting alfalfa cultivation to ensure adequate feed for livestock. “We are ready to provide feeds. We are ready to provide water, hospitals, schools, and everything else for them,” he said. The governor disclosed that his administration had invested about ₦3.1 billion in artificial insemination programmes over the past two to three years to improve cattle breeds and boost milk production. He added that the government had sustained regular animal vaccination programmes to protect livestock against diseases. Namadi also stressed the need for peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders, urging residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing information on individuals threatening peace in their communities. Earlier, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Mohammed, said the ministry had recorded significant achievements since its establishment. He listed the demarcation of additional grazing reserves, animal vaccination and public sensitisation on peaceful coexistence among measures introduced to strengthen livestock development in the state. title: The best gadget I bought this year is a milk frother
body:
Back in February, I went to Los Angeles to take in some art and stayed in Koreatown. Down the street from my hotel, there was this little coffee shop — Stagger — that is, I think, best known for its matcha, which is good. But the drink I unexpectedly found myself obsessed with was their cream top, an iced Americano with, yep, vanilla cream on top. When I got back to Oakland, I kept thinking about how badly I wanted one.
For more than 20 years, I’ve been drinking my coffee — iced or otherwise — black. Originally this was because I knew I could put black coffee that had cooled off in the microwave to reheat it without worrying that the milk in it would curdle. (Gross, I know.) Then, as I started drinking better coffee, it felt like the best way to appreciate the expensive beans I was buying.
So my attachment to the cream top surprised me. And then, when Oakland had a gnarly heat wave in March, I decided there was one way I’d tolerate it: fancy coffee drinks. I splashed out $14 for the Zulay Kitchen frother and I was off.
A handheld foamer looks and works kinda like an immersion blender. I pour milk into a glass, stick the frother in there, and then hold the power button until it reaches my preferred consistency. When the disposable batteries it uses are fresh, this takes about 30 seconds to a minute. As the batteries degrade, it takes longer; if I’m getting impatient about how long it’s taking me to make my frothy treats, it’s time to change the batteries. The frother also works to beat eggs, mix protein powder or creatine into a drink, and make hot chocolate. But by far it’s gotten the most use making my coffee drinks as I set out to make a cream top of my own.
[Image: Also I think it’s neat to watch the foam descend into the coffee. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/E16BF163-4057-4543-9FFE-E730462F0473_1_105_c.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
The cream top descended from the Einspänner, an espresso drink that’s named for a one-horse carriage. The original Viennese version used hot espresso, and the whipped cream on top served as a kind of insulation, which kept the drivers’ drinks hot for them when they were out in the cold. (Obviously, its popularity expanded beyond carriage drivers.) It isn’t clear to me how the Einspänner made it to South Korea, but it exploded in popularity there, with all kinds of variations, mostly iced. And then from South Korea, it made its way to the US, where the ground had already been cleared by Starbucks’ “cold foam” drinks.
The notable thing about the cream top, besides the addition of delicious fat and sugar to coffee, was that the cream wasn’t as light as latte foam, but wasn’t as heavy as ordinary whipped cream. It was melty and dripped slowly into the coffee.
My first experiments with my at-home cream top were pretty simple. I don’t have an espresso machine, but I do make concentrated cold brew in hot weather, which has a strong enough flavor to stand up against the foam. (Some recipes suggest powdered espresso if you don’t want to use concentrated cold brew.)
After I mastered the simple cream top, I began making forays into weirder breakfast treats, my favorite of which I… recreated from a Starbucks ad. It’s a cold brew with coconut ube cold foam, the top of which I dust with toasted coconut flakes. It is dank. (This is a recipe for a more sophisticated version than I make.) So when it was 90 degrees in Oakland for about two weeks running recently, this drink was how I consoled myself.
To be honest, I’m just recommending getting a frother. You can spend a lot on a milk frother and some people do. I relied on America’s Test Kitchen to steer me in the right direction — but outlets like Wirecutter and Bon Appétit have their own preferred options. This one is cheap and simple, and it’s been treating me right. I’m sure the Apple HomeView is nice, too, but in pleasure per dollar can it match a $14 cold foamer that takes AA batteries? I have my doubts.

title: Some ministers steal but aren’t arrested, while ‘fraud boys’ are – Shatta Wale criticises selective justice recounting EOCO saga
body: Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has criticised what he perceives as selective justice in Ghana, accusing authorities of targeting young people over fraud while ministers who allegedly steal public funds escape arrest. Speaking during his ShattaFest 2026 show at the Accra Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 17, the musician questioned why young people were being arrested for fraud while public officials accused of financial wrongdoing were seemingly not facing similar consequences. “Make I tell you, I get plenty fraud boys wey be my friends, but me, I no be snitch wey I go snitch anybody. The country no good, so if you go fraud, fraud. Ministers dey steal, they no dey catch them. Them dey steal our money, they no dey catch them, they dey catch young boys for Ghana,” he said. The artiste’s comments centred on what he considers an imbalance in the enforcement of laws against financial crimes, particularly the treatment of young people suspected of engaging in fraudulent activities compared with public officials accused of corruption. Shatta Wale also disclosed that he had several friends involved in fraud but insisted that he would not report them to the authorities. “Make I tell you, I get plenty fraud boys wey be my friends, but me, I no be snitch wey I go snitch anybody,” he said. He went on to cite the country’s economic difficulties as part of his argument, saying: “The country no good, so if you go fraud, fraud.” The musician subsequently accused ministers of stealing public funds without being arrested, contrasting their perceived treatment with that of young people who are apprehended over fraud-related offences. “Ministers dey steal, they no dey catch them. Them dey steal our money, they no dey catch them, they dey catch young boys for Ghana,” he added.

title: ‘Why airlines may not get cheaper jet fuel despite local production’
body: By Dickson Omobola Aviation fuel marketer, CITA Energies, has said jet fuel marketers may not be able to significantly reduce the price of Jet A1 supplied to the country’s airlines due to the single-source supply arrangement, pricing disparities and rising operational costs. This comes amid recent complaints by the country’s airlines over the high cost of aviation fuel, which accounts for at least 40 per cent of their operational expenses. The company said the reliance on a single supplier had limited competition among marketers, leaving little room for notable price differences despite efforts to offer airlines cheaper fuel. CITA Energies’ representatives spoke to newsmen on the sidelines of the company’s 20th anniversary celebration in Lagos. Chairman of CITA, Dr Thomas Ogungbagbe, said the pricing structure for locally supplied aviation fuel had created difficulties for marketers, particularly because of the mismatch between the global pricing formula and the pricing arrangement adopted by Dangote Refinery. Ogungbagbe said marketers operating under the global pricing formula used the average benchmark price for the preceding month, while Dangote’s pricing arrangement followed a different formula. He said: “We still have issues with pricing because we are priced on the global formula pricing, and the global formula pricing does not recognise individual countries. The contracts are signed, for example, on a month minus one basis, using the average of prices published daily during the preceding month. “This means that in October, we use the September average as our benchmark for selling. Meanwhile, in Dangote, it is BL plus five. So, you have a lot of mismatches, which means that once you load, five days may pass before you know the price. You can even be selling in Lagos without knowing the price at which you bought the product. That is the major gap. “Second, we have a premium that was introduced sometime around March by Dangote, which has not been removed. It is not in line with the global pricing formula. What that means is that we can only pass it on to customers, and that is why the airlines are making noise.” CITA chairman said Dangote Refinery had helped address aviation fuel scarcity in Nigeria, but maintained that pricing remained a major challenge for marketers. He said: “You can’t even get N1,900 per litre. Nigeria had never produced jet fuel. Even the refineries we had before never produced jet fuel. Basically, Dangote is the first one. Dangote, being the first, has also brought a lot of opportunities and challenges. The opportunity is that the problem of scarcity has been eradicate d. Availability is assured. “But the challenge is also in the pricing because, as I told you earlier, there is a nebulous premium that you pay on top of the average, which should not be there. That is why some people prefer to import, where they can get the real formula. We are still pleading with Dangote to help us remove this.” Also speaking, Acting Managing Director of CITA Energy, Titilayo Olaore, said marketers reviewed their costs weekly to determine how competitive they could be and how much relief they could offer airlines. She, however, said the current supply arrangement meant marketers were working with the same price, leaving little room for significant differences in the prices charged to airlines. Olaore said: “It is a dynamic industry, and we have a one-source justification hazard now, which has led us and every other stakeholder that supplies aviation fuel to the airlines to rely on one price. “With that price, we then build up whatever other costs come up along the way before we get to the airside. Every week, we look at our numbers. We try to work on how competitive we can be and how beneficial we can be to the airlines in terms of pricing, but we are working with one price. “The times when we could work with multiple options, maybe there would be a bit more flexibility. But the fact is that we all get from one source now, and our prices vary within a N5 differential between us and the next person. So, the flexibility is not there.” Meanwhile, CITA’s National Operations Manager, Dr Jeffrey Egbadon, lamented the international conflicts that had disrupted global supply chains, saying these were some factors responsible for the pressure on aviation fuel prices. Egbadon fingered tensions involving Iran, Israel and the United States, disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz and the Russia-Ukraine war as factors affecting the availability and movement of petroleum products. He said: “It has been challenging with aviation fuel, especially in terms of pricing. The war currently happening between Iran and Israel, as well as the tensions involving Israel and the United States, have also been a challenge because of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. “Recently, the war involving Yemen and Saudi Arabia has also shown that there have been a lot of blockages in the movement of products into Africa and through African waters. You can also see what is happening between Russia and Ukraine. That is another major factor. What we see today is that many of the countries that produce these products are engaged in one conflict or another.” The post ‘Why airlines may not get cheaper jet fuel despite local production’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Jigawa governor commissions ₦3.5bn asphalt and precast plant to boost indigenous constructions
body:
Jigawa State Governor, Umar Namadi has commissioned an industrial facility established by ALREN Construction Company comprising an asphalt plant, a concrete batching plant and a precast plant. The facility is located in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital.
The facility which represents an investment of approximately ₦3.5 billion, is expected to improve local access to construction materials, reduce sourcing challenges for contractors and stimulate economic activities across the state.
Speaking while opening the facility, the governor reaffirmed the Jigawa State Government’s commitment to strengthening indigenous contractors and expanding employment opportunities through private-sector investment.
Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Governor Namadi said the investment aligned with his administration’s 12-Point Agenda, particularly its focus on private-sector partnership, employment generation and economic expansion.
“One of our 12-Point Agenda is in action today in this place. That is a partnership with the private sector to generate employment and increase economic activities in Jigawa State,” he said.
The Governor said that the facilities would provide indigenous contractors, particularly small-scale operators, with easier access to asphalt and other essential construction materials without having to travel outside the state to procure them.
According to Governor Namadi, the availability of these materials within Jigawa would reduce operational difficulties for local contractors, strengthen their capacity to execute projects and support the growth of indigenous businesses in the construction industry.
“Our indigenous small contractors in Jigawa State will now have no reason to travel outside Jigawa State to get asphalt for the work they are doing.”
The governor described the investment as an example of how private-sector participation could complement government efforts to expand economic opportunities, strengthen local enterprises and create sustainable employment.
He said that the facilities had already employed 265 people, all of them indigenes of Jigawa State, adding that the company’s chairman had pledged to increase the workforce at the facilities to 500 by the first quarter of 2027.
Governor Namadi also stated that the employment generated by the investment would stimulate economic activities through workers’ earnings and contribute to government revenue.
He commended ALREN Construction Company for investing in Jigawa State and assured the company of the government’s continued cooperation and support.
“The Jigawa State Government will continue to work with you, because you are a very good partner to us.”
The governor further encouraged the company to explore investment opportunities in other sectors of the state’s economy, reiterating his administration’s commitment to maintaining an enabling environment for private businesses to thrive.
Speaking earlier, the Managing Director of ALREN Construction Company, Engr. Salim El Ters, said the investment was designed to strengthen the company’s operational capacity, support construction development and create employment opportunities.
“Our main concern today is to strengthen our capacity to support construction development and create valuable employment opportunities,” he said.
Engr. El Ters disclosed that the company planned to increase its overall workforce from 935 to approximately 1,170 employees, with about 30 per cent of the additional employees expected to be recruited from Jigawa State.
He expressed appreciation to the state government for its support and for creating an environment conducive to private-sector investment.

title: Lithuania foils arson attack on Starlink equipment, suspects Russian involvement
body:
Lithuanian authorities thwarted an attempted arson attack on a company storing Starlink satellite communications equipment overnight on Oct. 18, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said.
The attackers attempted to set fire to satellite antennas and a control unit. Investigators found incendiary liquids and containers with capacities ranging from three to 10 liters at the scene, Sinkevicius told Lithuania's national broadcaster LRT Radio .
"The authorities had warned the company of possible attacks, security had been stepped up, and the attempt failed," he later wrote in a Facebook post.
Sinkevicius described the incident as part of Russia's hybrid warfare campaign, pointing to similar suspected sabotage incidents across Europe , including in Poland and Bulgaria.
"We will learn more about who ordered it, how everything happened, and who was behind it. It is likely that it is already clear who commissioned it — the Russian side," he added.
A similar incident was reported in Poland on Sept. 23, when a fire broke out at a Starlink ground station in what may have been an attempt to disrupt its operations.
The suspected sabotage attempt in Lithuania came as a drone crashed and exploded in the country's north near the Latvian border on Oct. 18, damaging a passing car, Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania's National Crisis Management Center, told LRT Radio.
Authorities have yet to determine whether the drone carried explosives or what caused the blast, Sinkevicius told the broadcaster.
It remains unclear who the drone belonged to. Ukraine launched a large-scale attack on the Russian city of St. Petersburg overnight on Oct. 18, and similar drone incidents in the Baltic states have occurred during Ukrainian attacks on the city.
Sinkevicius said Lithuania's warning system had been activated but had not functioned perfectly, with reports received only from the Kaunas district.
The prime minister said he would convene the National Security Commission on Oct. 19 to discuss both incidents.

title: Built as a cheap Shahed lookalike, Russia’s Gerbera now flies with a 10-kg warhead and an incendiary bag
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia has started fitting its enlarged Gerbera-2 drones with a 10-kg warhead and an extra bag of incendiary mixture, Ukrainian military outlet Militarnyi reported on 18 October. The setup is designed to start a fire where the drone hits and is probably meant for attacks on critical infrastructure and warehouses, the outlet said. Russia’s industry makes about 3,000 jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones a month, Ukraine’s military intelligence has said , and Russian strikes have destroyed 2.1 million m² of Ukraine’s modern warehouse space since the full-scale invasion began. A cheap drone that carries fire adds one more threat for air defenses that already let nearly half of Russia’s jet-powered Shaheds through . A fire bag behind the warhead Ukrainian Telegram channel Polkovnyk HSh posted photos of the payload on 17 October. Gerbera-2 strike and reconnaissance drones had begun to appear with a 10-kg high-explosive fragmentation-incendiary warhead and an extra package of incendiary mixture, the channel wrote. They navigate with Kometa-M12, a 12-element antenna array designed to resist jamming, it added. title: The drones flew 1,000 km. St. Petersburg’s oil terminal, fuel depot, and a nearby data center were waiting at the end
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukrainian drones struck St. Petersburg’s oil terminal, a fuel depot, an Ozon distribution center, and a VK data center overnight, setting off fires across the city, monitoring channels reported. Russian outlet Meduza called it apparently the largest attack on the city and Leningrad Oblast since the war began. Russian officials acknowledged fires, damaged homes and substations, and power cuts. Russia keeps fighting along the front while bombarding Ukrainian cities and the grid behind it. Ukraine’s long-range drones, in turn, target the oil exports and logistics that fund and supply that war, and Russia’s Baltic oil ports have been hit repeatedly this year. St. Petersburg is a symbolic place: Russia’s so-called second capital and Putin’s hometown. Oil terminal and fuel depot on fire Ukrainian forces struck the Petersburg Oil Terminal with FP-1 drones, starting a fire, Ukrainian drone maker Fire Point said . The company described the terminal as one of the region’s largest, handling 12.5 million tonnes of petroleum products a year, including for export. Piter port and oil facility in one shot pic.twitter.com/KfptwkhsDS — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 18, 2026 St. Petersburg Governor Aleksandr Beglov acknowledged fires at the terminal and in four city districts, adding that Pulkovo airport had restricted flights. By morning, firefighters were still battling blazes at the terminal, the Ruchyi oil depot, and industrial warehouses in the Kolpinsky district, he wrote . He claimed one person was killed and five injured. Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported that the Ruchyi depot had been burning since the night. Ozon hub, VK data center, and a bridge An Ozon distribution center in Kolpinsky district caught fire after the attack, the company said, Russian independent outlet Astra reported . He acknowledged damage to the data center’s transformer equipment and warehouse complex, and minor damage to the Vostochnaya substation. Two other substations in Yanino went offline, cutting power to about 20,000 people, he said . Damaged VK data center building in Novosergiyevka, Leningrad Oblast, after a Ukrainian FP-1 drone strike, 18 October 2026. The channel also reported a fire near a Russian Aerospace Forces radar company outside the village of Kaporskoye. Smoke rising over St. Petersburg after the overnight drone attack, 18 October 2026. Photo: Astra To reach St. Petersburg, Ukrainian drones had to cover 1,000 km across four Russian regions guarded by air defenses and electronic warfare, said Serhii Beskrestnov, adviser to Ukraine’s president on defense technology. “And these are not cruise missiles with special systems, these are drones that fly at speeds of up to 200 km/h,” he wrote . title: APC Wins All 21 LG Chairmanship Seats, 239 Councillorships In Kogi
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has won all 21 local government chairmanship seats and 239 councillorship seats in the Kogi State local government election. The elections were conducted on Saturday by the Kogi State Independent Electoral Commission (KOSIEC). The results were announced by the Kogi State Independent Electoral Commission (KOSIEC) after the collation exercise at its headquarters in Lokoja. Declaring the results, KOSIEC Chairman, Mamman Nda-Eri, said the APC won all chairmanship and councillorship seats across the state’s 21 local government areas and 239 wards. He described the election as peaceful and credible, saying it was conducted in line with the electoral guidelines. He also commended security agencies, observers, journalists and voters for their orderly conduct. According to Nda-Eri, the conclusion of the polls marked the completion of the 13 activities outlined by the commission for the 2026 local government elections, which began almost a year ago. He added that Certificates of Return would be issued to the winners in due course. The outgoing chairmen and councillors, who were sworn in on October 23, 2024, are expected to leave office this month at the end of their two-year tenure, as stipulated by the state’s electoral law. It used to be so easy to get away with things in school. The teacher, after all, was always turned around writing at the chalkboard! But then came a bit of technology, previously mostly used for military purposes, called the overhead projector. It would change far more than just the disciplinary record of students everywhere.
In this episode of Version History , we tell the story of the overhead projector. David Pierce is joined by The Verge ’s Jake Kastrenakes and Stanford professor Antero Garcia to discuss how overhead projectors were developed, how they made their way into classrooms, and how they changed so much about the way kids learn. They also try to figure out why overhead projectors have mostly gone away, and whether the things that replaced them — from PowerPoint presentations to computer screens to those new-fangled smart boards — actually improved on the OHP.
This is the final episode of the fifth season of Version History , all about the most iconic school tech. Thanks so much for watching, listening, sending feedback, and everything else! Other than the OHP, we also spent this season looking at Oregon Trail , the original Chromebook , the One Laptop Per Child program, the LeapFrog LeapPad , and those ubiquitous Texas Instruments calculators . title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
body:
Pope Leo XIV appears at the window of his study in the Apostolic Palace overlooking St. Peter's Square at the Vatican for the traditional noon blessing after praying the Angelus, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, a day after he returned from the hospital, where he had lung cancer removed on Tuesday. Alessandra Tarantino/AP hide caption
VATICAN CITY — Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized for an operation to remove a malignant tumor, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.
The crowd erupted in cheers when the pontiff showed himself in the window overlooking the square, where a week ago on the same occasion of the traditional Angelus blessing he revealed that a nodule had been located on his lung, and that it would be surgically removed.
''Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God's help and your prayers," Leo said, his voice sounding strong four days after the lower lobe of his right lung was removed.
The pontiff said the experience of the last week "has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity." He told the faithful that he had ''truly felt your support,'' and expressed ''particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli hospital'' where he was treated.
The pope paused for a moment and waved to the crowd before retreating into his apartment in the Apostolic Palace.
A delegation from Africa in Rome for a congress danced and ululated after the pope's blessing.
''He was always in our prayers when he was sick, and we are happy to see him today,″ said Alain Kalembu of the Democratic Republic of Congo. ″This is an expression of our joy.″
The 71-year-old pontiff had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.
He told a reporter in English that he was doing ''much better'' as he drove away from Rome's Gemelli hospital to return to the Vatican, after a shorter hospital stay than had initially been anticipated.
"I don't believe it, because he was just operated on the other day," Cosimo Mastrocinque, a retired factory worker visiting the Vatican from the southern region of Puglia, said. "It is a miracle that he recovered already."
American tourists were especially eager to pray alongside the first pope born in the United States. Marla Marsala of Michigan was supposed to attend a Mass with the pope last week that was canceled due to his hospitalization.
''I am just happy that we are praying with him today instead of for him, like we were before,'' Marsala said. "It was a tough week for all of the people who love him, which are many. He seems like a very strong soul. So I think he will pull through and fight it, and succeed and keep doing the wonderful work he is doing.''
Claire Holland from Jacksonville, Florida, said she felt "very blessed" to be present for the pope's return to his flock.
"I'm so happy that he has recovered so quickly. I think there have been millions and millions of prayers. And he is a strong, determined man, and I am so happy that he is feeling well enough to do this," Holland said.
Leo's next major engagement is an ambitious Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, including a dozen flights and two helicopter rides to high altitudes. His surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora, told Vatican News on Saturday that "there are no clinical reasons why it should not take place."
"The Holy Father has put his heart and soul into his recovery," Margaritora told Vatican News, adding that he expected the pope to recover fully from surgery "in another 10 days or so."
Histological testing of the tumor and related lymph nodes was underway. The results, along with details of the tumor's molecular and genetic makeup, will help doctors determine whether the pope needs additional treatment. Options include chemotherapy, a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, or targeted oral therapy based on the tumor's genetic characteristics.
