title: Rainbow Coalition will fail in Kwara — Accord Party
body: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Accord Party in Kwara State has predicted that the Rainbow Coalition will fail to make the expected electoral impact in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, arguing that the alliance is driven more by elite political realignments than grassroots support. The party’s state publicity secretary, Olamilekan Esinrogunjo, stated this in a statement on the emerging political alignment made available to Vanguard on Sunday. He described the coalition as flawed, alleging that it lacked a clear governance agenda and was driven largely by personality clashes. Esinrogunjo also described the Rainbow Coalition as a credibility challenge because of what he called contradictions in its political positioning. He questioned the decision to oppose the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara while supporting President Bola Tinubu at the federal level, saying the arrangement could confuse voters and serve the interests of political elites rather than ordinary citizens. “ You cannot claim to be opposition in Kwara and, at the same time, ask the same people to support the APC at the presidential level. That contradiction is one of the fundamental problems of the Rainbow Coalition,” he said. The Accord Party spokesman also dismissed the suggestion that the movement of prominent politicians across party lines would automatically translate into electoral support. “They can make noise here and there. Politicians can move from one party to another, but votes do not move automatically with them. An alliance of politicians is not necessarily an alliance of voters,” he said. He further argued that the coalition’s reliance on political heavyweights and former officeholders to revive support for the Saraki political dynasty amounted to more political noise than electoral substance. According to him, the coalition had yet to establish a clear message capable of attracting ordinary voters across the state. “What is the Rainbow Coalition offering Kwarans beyond political realignment? Is it an opposition platform, a vehicle for supporting the President, a return to the defeated dynasty or simply an arrangement among politicians seeking new political opportunities?” he queried. Esinrogunjo said the 2027 elections would not be determined solely by defections, endorsements or alliances among political elites, but by the ability of parties to connect with voters and present credible programmes. He maintained that the Accord Party was offering an alternative across all levels of the elections, from the presidency to the state House of Assembly. “Kwara is not anybody’s political inheritance. The people own their votes, and they will decide who gets their mandate,” he said. The party spokesman insisted that Accord would continue to present itself as an opposition platform focused on policy, grassroots engagement and what he described as a “new direction” for the state. He urged voters to look beyond politicians’ movement between parties and assess political platforms based on their programmes, candidates, records and capacity to address the challenges facing the state. title: Borno loses billions in infrastructure to metal scavenging — Zulum
body: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Babagana Umara Zulum, has said the state has lost infrastructure, electrical materials and metals worth billions of naira to metal scavengers, known in Hausa as Ajakuta. Zulum said the losses, alongside other security concerns, informed the state government’s decision to ban scrap metal trading. The governor spoke at the weekend while addressing scrap metal operators, urging them to submit proposals on how they could continue their businesses without contributing to insecurity or damaging public infrastructure. He explained that the ban was imposed in the overall interest of the state and was not intended to deprive operators of their means of livelihood. Zulum said the government had no personal interest in shutting down their businesses, stressing that the restriction was aimed at protecting public assets and strengthening security. “It is deeply concerning to me if one person loses his livelihood for whatever reason in Borno. Believe me, there is nothing I stand to gain from banning scrap metal trade other than addressing the serious security concerns associated with your activities,” he said. The governor disclosed that the state government spent more than ₦3 billion to connect an electricity distribution line from Damaturu to Maiduguri, but the wires were subsequently lost to metal scavenging. “We spent more than ₦3 billion to connect an electricity distribution line from Damaturu to Maiduguri, but unfortunately, we lost all the wires to metal scavenging activities,” he said. Zulum also said hundreds of scavengers had been killed while searching for metals in villages that were not yet safe for civilian activities. He added that security intelligence available to the government indicated that insurgents were using scrap metal trading channels to sell looted metals. “We have security intelligence that even the insurgents use your platforms to sell looted metals. So, no responsible government will ignore such intelligence just to be politically correct,” the governor said. Despite the restriction, Zulum granted operators a waiver to evacuate stocks accumulated before the ban from designated locations. The measure, he said, was intended to ease the impact of the restriction on genuine operators while the government addressed the security and infrastructure concerns associated with the trade. The post Borno loses billions in infrastructure to metal scavenging — Zulum appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Governor donates ₦60m to Offa hospital project, awards scholarships to 50 students
body:
Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq has donated ₦50 million to an ongoing hospital project in Offa and awarded scholarships worth ₦10 million to 50 students of an Arabic institution in the community.
The governor made the donations during the Annual Maolud Nabiy celebration organised by the Chief Imam of Offa, Muyideen Hussein, in Offa, Kwara State.
The donations comprise ₦50 million for the hospital project and ₦200,000 each for 50 students, bringing the total support to ₦60 million.
Speaking at the event, Mr Hussein commended the governor for his support for the Offa community, his institution and the Adabiyyah movement.
The cleric said Governor AbdulRazaq’s interventions and projects in the community had strengthened residents’ appreciation of his administration.
“I am welcoming Your Excellency to Offa, your second home. We are pleased to receive you today. We welcome you, because you are a true philanthropist and a blessing to the Offa community,” he said.
Mr Hussein also expressed gratitude for the governor’s support for the hospital project, which is currently under construction, as well as his contributions to the institution and its students.
The Olofa of Offa, Oba Mufutau Gbadamosi, also thanked Mr AbdulRazaq for the donations and other forms of support to the Chief Imam and the people of Offa.
The monarch described the governor’s personal attendance at the celebration as a great honour to the community and prayed for his success in office and his political ambition.
The Maolud celebration brought together Islamic scholars, traditional rulers, political leaders and other stakeholders.
Among those present were the Khalifatul Adabiyyah, Sheikh Mustapha Al-Adabiy; the All Progressives Congress deputy governorship candidate, Seun Ogunniyi; the Chairman of Offa Local Government, Sulaiman Omituntun; Wahab Agbaje; and Hassan Oyeleke.
The event formed part of activities celebrating the birth of Prophet Muhammad and the religious institution’s contributions to Islamic learning.

title: France detains 1,800 after unrest as damage estimated at hundreds of millions of euros
body:
The Élysée Palace said this, according to Ukrinform, citing Le Figaro .
Around midnight the previous day, the Prime Minister warned of the serious consequences of the riots for the country and said he had instructed ministers to support business owners whose businesses had been affected.
“It cannot be that a minority smashes everything while the same people always end up paying,” he said, calling for an expedited review of a bill that would make those responsible for the destruction liable for the damages.
According to updated figures from the Interior Ministry, 1,800 people were detained across the country following Saturday’s protests.
“More than 600 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have so far been injured during this unrest. Unfortunately, these figures on those affected are only preliminary. The material damage is significant. Demonstrations are a fundamental right. Rioting through coordinated acts of violence is not,” Nunez wrote on X .
He again blamed far-left groups for the organized violence and said investigations were ongoing to identify those involved in the attacks and looting.
Meanwhile, Alexandre Bompard, President of the Trade and Distribution Federation and CEO of Carrefour, estimated that around 1,500 retail establishments had been directly affected, while the total damage to French retail amounted to several hundred million euros. He called for insurance compensation procedures to be expedited.
Stores were looted and damaged in Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Nantes and Nice, among other cities. Supermarkets, clothing stores, sports retailers, luxury goods stores and mobile phone shops were damaged.
The mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon asked Prime Minister Lecornu to meet with them at the beginning of the week due to the scale of the destruction and the seriousness of the situation. They want to establish how the events unfolded and what led to such consequences.
Public buildings also sustained significant damage. In Limoges, a fire destroyed a large part of the historic city hall.
In Saint-Étienne, a 17-year-old protester suffered a severe hand injury after a police grenade exploded. The investigation was assigned to the General Inspectorate of the National Police.
As reported, mass protests took place in France on October 17 over the rising cost of living, higher fuel prices and problems in education and public services. According to the Interior Ministry, 550,000 people took part, while organizers put the figure at 800,000. Most participants protested peacefully, but in several cities, some groups resorted to violence, arson and looting.

title: PREMIUM TIMES’ journalists, others named finalists of African Investigative Journalism Awards
body:
Two PREMIUM TIMES’ journalists who worked on a collaborative investigation that unravelled lead poisoning linked to battery recycling in Nigeria have been named among the three finalists for the 2026 African Investigative Journalist of the Year Awards .
The investigation was led by the editor of the Business and Economy desk of PREMIUM TIMES, Oladeinde Olawoyin, and an award-winning investigative reporter, Folashade Ogunrinde.
The Wits Centre for Journalism, supported by Absa Africa, is organising the award in its fourth year to recognise outstanding investigative reporting across Africa that reveals untold stories, holds the powerful to account, questions those in public life, and serves the public interest.
The 2026 African Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC), where the winner and runners-up will be announced at a gala ceremony on 11 November, is scheduled to be held from 10 to 12 November at the Edge Convention Centre in Nairobi, Kenya.
This year’s edition attracted over 200 entries across the continent, and the quality of investigative reporting made it challenging for the judges to select finalists.
“Judging these awards is never an easy process as there is so much valuable investigative journalism happening on our continent now,” said the convenor of judges, Gwen Lister.
He noted that judges had to assess the investigative work of shortlisted finalists against strict criteria, sparking vibrant debates and in-depth discussions on the merits and impact of the submissions.
“As judges, we all hope that striving for the prestigious title of African Investigative Journalist of the Year will spur on journalists across the continent to even greater heights,” Mr Lister added.
Dinesh Balliah, the director of the Wits Centre for Journalism, said the award reaffirmed journalism’s role in holding power to account in the context of a lack of resources, ongoing threats of violence and death and misinformation/disinformation.
“I wish we could recognise every one of the entrants through these awards, but it is impossible. The top three, though, represent all of these incredible journalists and their impactful work,” Mr Balliah said.
Daniel Munslow, managing executive of group communications at Absa Group, said the organisation recognises the critical role investigative journalism plays in strengthening transparency, accountability and public trust, which is why it celebrates some of the continent’s finest journalistic talent and the important work they do in bringing vital issues to light.
“The 2026 Absa African Investigative Journalist of the Year Award celebrates some of the continent’s finest journalistic talent and the important work they do in bringing vital issues to light.
“We are proud to support a platform that champions excellence in journalism and contributes to building more informed, resilient and prosperous societies across Africa,” Mr Munslow stated.
From a longlist of five, PREMIUM TIMES’ investigation, ‘Lead In Their Blood / Poor Oversight, Regulatory Failure Expose Nigerians to Slow Death from Battery Recycling’, by Mr Olawoyin and Ms Ogunrinde of PREMIUM TIMES with The Examination, Nigeria, was shortlisted alongside two other investigative reports.
They are ‘Your Eyes, Their Data’ by Naipanoi Lepapa, Kenya, in collaboration with Julia Lindblom of Göteborgs-Posten and Ahmed Abdigadir of Svenska Dagbladet, and ‘Nine Lives: King Cat and His Tender Empire’ by Jeff Wicks of News24, South Africa.
The investigation examined the health and environmental consequences of lead-acid battery recycling in parts of Africa, with PREMIUM TIMES reporting extensively from Ogijo, a community in Ogun State where several battery recycling factories operate.
The report found that residents and workers around the factories had been exposed to dangerous levels of lead pollution.
To provide scientific evidence for the investigation, the project commissioned independent blood lead testing for 70 residents, along with soil and air quality sampling around battery recycling plants in Ogun State.
Of the 70 people who volunteered for blood tests, seven out of every 10 recorded harmful levels of lead, according to the investigation. Every worker tested was also found to have been poisoned.
More than half of the children tested had lead levels high enough to cause lifelong brain damage, the investigation reported.
Soil and dust samples collected around the factories also showed extensive contamination, with some recording lead concentrations far above levels generally regarded as hazardous.
The investigation estimated that more than 20,000 people lived within a mile of the factories.
PREMIUM TIMES published its Nigerian investigation in two parts. The first report, “Lead In Their Blood: How Battery Recyclers Are Poisoning Nigerians,” documented the health risks faced by residents and workers in Ogijo.
The second, “Poor Oversight, Regulatory Failure Exposes Nigerians to Slow Death from Battery Recycling,” examined failures by regulatory authorities and the conditions that allowed the hazardous operations to continue.
The investigation also examined the international supply chain, tracing Nigeria’s recycled lead to overseas buyers and the global automotive industry.
The broader project found that recycled lead from Nigerian factories entered international supply chains used to produce car batteries.
It documented how one American battery manufacturer, East Penn Manufacturing, bought Nigerian lead through the global trading company Trafigura. Following the reporting, the company said it would stop importing the Nigerian lead and introduce additional scrutiny of its lead purchases.
Following the publication, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency shut down battery recycling facilities in Ogijo over environmental concerns.
The Ogun State Government also announced measures in response to the findings, including plans to test residents for lead exposure, while the House of Representatives called for an investigation into lead poisoning concerns in Ogijo and demanded an emergency response.
The state government and Lagos State Government also began a joint investigation into the pollution threat, while the Ogun government moved to suspend lead exports and shut affected battery recycling plants.
Nigerian authorities later moved to close factories linked to the US automotive industry amid the lead-poisoning investigation.
The reporting project has since been recognised for its depth and impact, winning PREMIUM TIMES’ standout report of 2025.
In September, it was named a finalist in two categories of the 2026 Online Journalism Awards in the United States.
The project has also received other international recognition, especially in the United States.
The project won the Selden Ring Award for Investigative Reporting from USC Annenberg and the John B. Oakes Award for environmental journalism.
It also won the Edward R. Murrow Awards for Investigative Reporting (Large Digital Organisation) and Best Video/Documentary about international affairs from the Overseas Press Club.
It won the Scripps Howard Journalism Awards, receiving both the Impact Award and the Excellence in Environmental Reporting Award.
In the Gerald Loeb Awards, it was named a finalist in the Video News category.
Mr Olawoyin, a multiple award-winning journalist, leads several projects at PREMIUM TIMES and mentors and supervises reporters.
Apart from his reporting of global economic issues across parts of Africa and the rest of the world, Mr Olawoyin’s reporting and research interests sit at the intersection of media framing and the impact of AI on the future of work, especially in the informal economy in Nigeria, sub-Saharan Africa, and the Global South.
Ms Ogunrinde is an award-winning investigative journalist recognised for her work in governance, accountability and inclusive development.

title: Russia’s Sporting Comeback Gathers Pace as Its War in Ukraine Grinds On
body:
It’s been over four and a half years since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Initially, Belarusian and Russian Olympic groups and sports teams were booted from international competition, although they were allowed to compete under a neutral flag. But financial interests have encouraged sporting organizations to reconsider these restrictions, despite Russia’s ongoing war in Ukraine. Many of the Russian athletes featured on the international stage have voiced support to the Russian military and its war in Ukraine.
To many Ukrainians, there is no good answer as to why Russian athletes should be allowed back into international competitions while Ukrainian cities are bombed daily and innocent civilians are being killed. In places such as Kherson , there is an active “human safari,” where Russian drone operators regularly hunt civilians. Videos of these attacks are often posted online, with children and elderly people among those targeted and killed. Most recently, a Russian strike on a bus in Kramatorsk killed 30 civilians.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to a BBC investigation, 13 of the athletes who competed under a neutral banner during the 2026 Winter Olympics, have engaged in pro-war activities. In turn, Ukraine asked the International Olympic Committee to reconsider the neutral status of Russian athletes.
British-Ukrainian sports journalist Andrew Todos, founder of Zorya Londonsk , warned that Russia is gradually being welcomed back into international sports.
“Despite Russia’s 12-year war against Ukraine, and now the fifth year of the full-scale invasion, with no letup in war crimes and killings, Russia is slowly edging back into world sporting competitions,” Todos said.
“A substantial number of sports have even permitted the return of the Russian flag and national colors, starting with the IOC,” he said. “This sets a dangerous precedent. Russia’s rehabilitation in the sporting sphere is happening in real time, despite there being no change in the country’s actions since the full-scale invasion began in 2022.”
In September, Russian hockey star Alexander Ovechkin appeared in a campaign advertisement for Putin-backed United Russia.
“During the summer off season he took part in the filming of a campaign video for Putin’s party United Russia ahead of the parliamentary elections,” said Todos. “When this video was released it created a large backlash amongst Ukrainian adjacent voices on social and traditional media.”
“I’m Russian, and I support my country,” Ovechkin said when asked about his decision to participate. Ovechkin, who has a long history of publicly supporting Putin, also referred to Putin as “my president” following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
“Many established hockey journalists were rather timid in their coverage of this subject. The Washington Capitals official statement also left a lot to be desired,” added Todos. “There have been no repercussions for the NHL’s all-time points scorer for supporting Putin and Russia’s war against Ukraine.” At the Washington Capitals’ home opener on Oct. 7, pro-Ukraine demonstrators gathered outside Capital One Arena to protest Ovechkin’s ties to Putin.
At Paris Saint-Germain, Ukrainian defender Illia Zabarnyi plays alongside Russian goalkeeper Matvey Safonov. Zabarnyi said he supports the complete isolation of Russian football and maintains no relationships with Russians, although he will interact professionally with Safonov as his teammate.
At Louisiana State University, the basketball program recruited Russian player Anna Minaeva while Ukrainian Kate Koval, whose father serves in the Ukrainian military, was already on the team. Coach Kim Mulkey said she hoped the two could become “ambassadors for peace.” Koval left the program afterwards.
In September, FIFA listed a Russian team for its boys’ Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan, which marked the first time a Russian team has competed in a FIFA tournament since the full-scale invasion began in 2022. In response, Ukraine called for a boycott. The International Olympic Committee has also withdrawn its recommendation to ban Russian teams, as Russian officials welcomed the decisions.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has been advocating for Russia to return to global football, saying, “We have to [look at reinstating Russia], definitely, because this ban has not achieved anything. It has just created ‍more frustration and hatred.”
Restrictions have also loosened across a variety of other sports for both Belarusian and Russian athletes, and in the future, many more restrictions will likely be lifted. Some in Europe understand the danger of this, and nine European nations have asked the European Union to drop financial support for international sports bodies, such as the IOC.
“For me, this is a very painful and unacceptable situation,” said Ukrainian Olympic athlete Yuliya Yelistratova. “I cannot see Russian and Belarusian athletes as simply ordinary competitors when Russia continues its war against Ukraine.”
“This is how Russian soft power in global sport works. It allows those who are open supporters, and even those who remain silent, in tennis, soccer, athletics and beyond, to continue competing in the West and retain support from their own organizations, fans and even some in the media,” Todos said. “This, in turn, normalizes the presence of Russia and Russians in the sporting narratives of those groups as well.”
For the IOC, the justification is that athletes shouldn’t pay the price for the actions of their government. But in Ukraine, hundreds of athletes have been killed in action or in Russian strikes, and they will never compete again. So to many Ukrainians, there is no justification for allowing Belarusian and Russian athletes to compete while Ukrainian athletes continue to die.
“Removing a flag from a uniform does not remove an athlete’s connection to the state,” said Yelistratova. “Many elite Russian athletes are connected to the state sports system, receive its support, or have ties to state or security structures. Their international victories can then be used by Russia to create an image of normality and international prestige.”
She added, “For me, saying ‘I am neutral’ is not enough. I would want to see not simply the absence of a flag, but a real break with the state and its sporting system. A public condemnation of the war, no state funding or ties to state sporting institutions, and an independent life and training outside the Russian system.”
The Kremlin uses international sporting success to improve Russia’s image abroad. Allowing Russian athletes to compete again gives Moscow an opportunity to present itself as a normal participant in international affairs despite its war in Ukraine.
“When I see Russian sports gradually returning to the international stage, I cannot help thinking about the role that money and political influence play in this,” Yelistratova added.
In late September, Russia bombed one of Ukraine’s biggest football stadiums in Kharkiv, as nearly 90 stadiums have been damaged or destroyed since the full-scale invasion. While Russia destroys Ukrainian sporting facilities and kills its athletes, Russian competitors are gradually being allowed to return to international competitions, sometimes under their national flag.
Ukrainians never asked for this war, and they were never given a choice. But allowing Russian and Belarusian athletes back onto the international stage is a choice.
David Kirichenko is a freelance journalist covering Eastern Europe. He can be found on the social media platform X @DVKirichenko.

title: Netanyahu: Magal's 'monkey' remark on Eisenkot inappropriate, but Likud voters face daily insults
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned Channel 14 presenter Yinon Magal for calling Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot a "monkey" and accused the opposition of failing to condemn similar insults against Likud voters during an interview with Radio North on Sunday."That is a highly inappropriate remark, and I condemn it," Netanyahu said, referring to Magal's comments about the former IDF chief of staff.However, the prime minister also criticized what he described as a double standard in the treatment of his political supporters, calling on Eisenkot to condemn derogatory remarks directed at Likud voters."I would be happy if Gadi Eisenkot condemned all the remarks by Gali Albin and others about Likud supporters being chimpanzees and baboons. It is inappropriate.”Magal made the comments during a Saturday evening broadcast of Channel 14's political talk show The Patriots, accusing Eisenkot of serving as a figurehead for an Ashkenazi political elite. He also claimed that Eisenkot's campaign manager, Ronen Manelis, was directing him behind the scenes.Netanyahu criticizes insults against Likud votersEisenkot responded to Magal's remarks by condemning the language and suggesting someone else was behind the presenter's comments, without identifying them.Asked about the resurgence of ethnic divisions in Israeli political discourse, Netanyahu acknowledged that such rhetoric remained prevalent, while arguing that it was disproportionately directed at his supporters."We haven't escaped it, even though Yinon said something [Saturday] that he should not have said. But every day I hear the condescension, patronizing attitude, and contempt toward Likud voters, who are called monkeys, baboons, and chimpanzees.""I wish this were a one-time phenomenon. It happens every day, and almost all of it is directed at Likud voters," he added.Netanyahu then turned to accusations directed at him personally, criticizing Eisenkot for what he described as a failure to condemn the use of the word "traitor" against the prime minister."Every single day, they accuse me, the prime minister of Israel, who has dedicated his life to the country, risked his life for the country, and continues to dedicate his life to the country, and they call me a traitor," Netanyahu said.The prime minister argued that such rhetoric should have disappeared from Israeli political discourse following the 1995 assassination of prime minister Yitzhak Rabin."I stood at demonstrations even before Rabin's assassination and said that he was not a traitor, that he was mistaken. But I am called a traitor on an hourly basis. Does Gadi condemn that? Gadi Eisenkot not only fails to condemn it, he personally uses it against me," Netanyahu said.Ben-Gvir defends Magal, rejects racism accusationsBen-Gvir came to Magal's defense in a post on X on Sunday, arguing that the presenter's remarks had been taken out of context and that accusations of racism against him were unfounded."I have known Yinon Magal for a long time. We have had quite a few conversations, both professional and personal, and I can say unequivocally: Trying to portray him as a racist and a bigot is simply ridiculous," Ben-Gvir wrote.The national security minister recalled that Magal had given him a platform early in his political career, at a time when other media outlets were unwilling to do so.את ינון מגל אני מכיר לא מהיום. היו לנו לא מעט שיחות, מקצועיות ואישיות, ואני יכול לומר בצורה ברורה: לנסות להלביש עליו תדמית של גזען וחשוך זה פשוט מצחיק. ינון היה בין הבודדים והראשונים שפתחו לי בזמנו את המיקרופון בזמן שאחרים סגרו אותו בפניי. וכן הוא יודע מצויין שאני מזרחי גאה, אמא משכונת הכורדים ואבא שגדל ליד שוק מחנה יהודה! לכולם ברור שינון השתמש בביטוי “קוף” בהקשר פוליטי, כשהכוונה לדבריו הייתה למועמד קש שמריצים אחרים. מכאן ועד להפוך את הדברים לאמירה גזענית נגד מזרחים - הוא סילוף מוחלט של הדברים. אני מזרחי, ומזרחי גאה! ואני האחרון שחושד בינון מגל שהוא רואה בי או במזרחים אחרים “קופים”. זה בדיוק כמו הניסיון להדביק את זה לראש הממשלה, ביבי מעולם לא פגע בי ובאיש על רקע עדתי. ישבתי אצלו בקבינט המצומצם במשך שנתיים וחצי, ומעולם לא נאמרה ממנו אמירה או יחס על רקע עדתי. אז לכל מי שממהר להדביק לינון תוויות ולתקוף את ביבי, כדאי לעצור, להקשיב למה שנאמר באמת ולהסתכל במראה. לא כל אמירה היא גזענות. ינון, אל תיתן לרעש להשתיק אותך.— איתמר בן גביר (@itamarbengvir) October 18, 2026"Yinon was among the few and the first to give me a microphone back then, when others shut me out. And he knows very well that I am a proud Mizrahi, with a mother from the Kurdish Quarter and a father who grew up near Mahane Yehuda Market!"Ben-Gvir maintained that Magal's use of the word "monkey" was intended as a political characterization of Eisenkot rather than an ethnic insult."It is clear to everyone that Yinon used the term 'monkey' in a political context, meaning, according to him, a puppet candidate being promoted by others. To turn that into a racist statement against Mizrahim is a complete distortion of what was said.""I am Mizrahi, and proudly so! And I am the last person who would suspect Yinon Magal of seeing me or other Mizrahim as 'monkeys.'"Ben-Gvir also defended Netanyahu against accusations of ethnic prejudice, citing his experience working alongside the prime minister."It is exactly like the attempt to pin this on the prime minister. Bibi has never mistreated me or anyone else on ethnic grounds. I sat with him in the inner cabinet for two and a half years, and he never made a remark or displayed an attitude based on ethnicity."The minister called on those criticizing Magal and Netanyahu to reconsider their interpretation of the presenter's remarks."So, to everyone rushing to label Yinon and attack Bibi, you should stop, listen to what was actually said, and look in the mirror. Not every remark is racism."He concluded with a message of encouragement to Magal: "Yinon, don't let the noise silence you."

title: Oyebanji targets industrialisation, SMEs to drive Ekiti growth
body: …Governor plans agro-processing, cheaper transport, 24-hour airport operations By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has said his administration will prioritise industrialisation, small business development and productivity in his second term to transform infrastructure investments into jobs, local manufacturing and economic growth. Oyebanji said the government would expand support for small-scale entrepreneurs, strengthen agricultural value chains, attract private investors and introduce alternative transportation systems powered by compressed natural gas (CNG) and electricity to reduce operating costs. The governor, who spoke in an interview on his second-term agenda, said the next phase of his administration would focus on ensuring that infrastructure developed during his first term translated into tangible economic benefits for residents. According to him, his administration invested substantially in roads, electricity, agricultural infrastructure and other critical facilities during its first term, providing a foundation for increased production and economic activities. He said the state had constructed roads linking communities, improved township roads and developed farm roads, adding that nearly 400 kilometres of roads would have been completed by the end of 2026. Oyebanji, however, stressed that infrastructure development would continue alongside efforts to promote industries, expand businesses and improve the state’s economic fortunes. He identified welders, tailors, hairdressers, barbers and other small-scale entrepreneurs as key beneficiaries of the proposed economic expansion, saying access to affordable financing would help them grow their businesses and create employment. The governor also emphasised the need to strengthen agricultural production and establish reliable markets for farmers, arguing that locally produced commodities must be processed within the state to generate greater economic value. On attracting private investment, Oyebanji said his administration was improving the business environment through reforms in land administration, taxation and regulatory processes. He said the government was establishing a one-stop shop to enable prospective investors to obtain relevant information, approvals and services without unnecessary bureaucratic delays. Oyebanji maintained that the government’s primary responsibility was to create an enabling environment for private capital rather than assume responsibility for establishing and operating industries itself. On transportation, the governor said his administration was testing a pilot mass transit scheme to determine its effectiveness before expanding government investment in the sector. He explained that the initiative was not intended to displace existing commercial transport operators but to introduce fair competition and provide residents with more affordable alternatives. Oyebanji identified CNG-powered and electric vehicles as important components of the state’s long-term strategy to reduce transportation costs, noting that petrol-dependent operations continued to impose significant financial burdens on drivers and passengers. He said discussions were ongoing with a company expected to introduce the initiative, which would extend beyond cars to include tricycles and motorcycles. On aviation, Oyebanji said his administration was working to enable the state’s airport to operate round the clock, rather than close at 6 p.m. or face restrictions during adverse weather conditions. He disclosed that an Instrument Landing System (ILS) had been installed and was undergoing assessment by a certification team, while a contract had been awarded for airport lighting infrastructure required to support night operations. The governor also announced plans to commission a privately developed fuel depot at the airport, explaining that the facility would allow aircraft to refuel in Ekiti and make flight operations more convenient. He said improved aviation facilities, agricultural investments and better road connectivity would support the state’s broader economic development strategy. Speaking on his priorities, Oyebanji said: “Our next major focus, therefore, is industrialisation and support for small businesses. That is the only way we can deepen our shared prosperity agenda. “Our farmers must also be able to produce at scale and have reliable off-takers who can purchase their produce and supply it to companies that will add value through processing. “The responsibility of government is to create an enabling environment for investors to come in, establish businesses and create jobs. “If the pilot scheme succeeds, the government will invest in transportation by procuring more vehicles that can compete with existing operators. I do not want to drive transport operators out of business. “I am not in government to inflict hardship on anybody. I understand the challenges these operators face, and I will not introduce policies merely to win applause from some people at the expense of others.” The post Oyebanji targets industrialisation, SMEs to drive Ekiti growth appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 2027: HPM targets six million votes for Hashim in North-West
body: The Hashim Progressive Movement (HPM) has set a target of at least six million votes for Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, across Nigeria’s North-West region in the 2027 general election. Hon. Aminu Aminu, HPM coordinator and Accord’s senatorial candidate for Jigawa Central, announced the target, saying the movement was mobilising supporters across the seven states of Jigawa, Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara. “We will prove he is our own in this region and the face of the New North,” Aminu said, describing the campaign as an effort to demonstrate Hashim’s connection with the region and his appeal as a presidential candidate with a national outlook. “This is a homecoming. For decades, the North has searched for a leader who understands its people and their challenges while offering a national vision for all Nigerians. We believe Dr Gbenga Hashim represents that possibility,” he said. Aminu said HPM’s mobilisation strategy would involve ward-to-ward and door-to-door engagement, with youth and women mobilisers working alongside Accord’s legislative candidates to strengthen the party’s presidential campaign. The movement plans to link its presidential mobilisation efforts with Accord’s senatorial and House of Representatives candidates to improve coordination and expand grassroots engagement across the region. “We are connecting presidential hope to grassroots reality,” Aminu said. He added that the movement believed voters were seeking practical solutions to insecurity and economic hardship, issues on which Hashim had continued to outline policy proposals. The six-million-vote figure represents HPM’s stated target for the North-West ahead of the 2027 general election. title: Iran, Pakistan FMs stress diplomacy amid regional tensions
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held a phone call Sunday with Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Mohammad Ishaq Dar, to discuss bilateral relations, regional developments and diplomatic efforts.
The Pakistani foreign minnistry issued a statement on Sunday, saying that Araghchi and Ishaq Dar discussed in a phone call regional issues and stressed the importance of dialogue and diplomacy..
Araghchi is in Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

title: Abu Dhabi Police confiscate more than 9,000 e-scooters in last 10 months
body: Police in Abu Dhabi have seized 9,237 e-scooters in the past 10 months across the emirate. The e-scooters were confiscated as part of a crackdown on breaches of the rules that govern their use on public roads, between vehicles, and in areas where they are forbidden. Police posted on Facebook that they had clamped down on “electric scooters violating traffic rules and regulations during 2026, as a result of their use on public roads, between vehicles, and on paths not designated for them, posing a danger to the safety of their users and road users”. “One of the most dangerous behaviours among electric scooter drivers is driving without paying attention to traffic, not wearing a helmet, and not wearing safety gear, which increases the likelihood of traffic accidents that may result in serious injuries or deaths,” police said on Sunday. Earlier this year, The National reported that data from the Ministry of Interior revealed a 97 per cent increase in major e-scooter accidents in 2025 compared with the previous year – a jump from 61 to 120. Alongside these figures, Al Wathba Insurance and RoadSafetyUAE conducted an e-scooter perception study and found that 93 per cent of UAE residents witness e-scooter riders behaving unsafely or recklessly, while 90 per cent personally feel unsafe because of the way e-scooters are used. Where can you ride an e-scooter in Abu Dhabi? E-scooters can only be used in areas designated by the Integrated Transport Centre in the capital. These are: Internal roads with speed limits less than 40kph. Lanes shared by pedestrians and cyclists. Cycle lanes designated for cyclists and e-scooter riders. You cannot ride e-scooters in three main areas. These are: Highways with a speed limit of 60kph or higher. Public roads and motorways. Pedestrian lanes.

title: Road projects: Uba Sani pays ₦2bn in compensation to 865 property owners
body: —Zaria, Sabon Gari, Giwa homeowners benefit -Receives ADC heavyweights into APC in Kaduna By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA –THE Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani has paid ₦2 billion in compensation to 865 property owners affected by township road projects in Zaria, Sabon Gari and Giwa. This makes the total sum the Uba Sani administration has paid so far to over ₦6.85 billion in direct compensation to citizens affected by public works — putting people at the centre of infrastructure. The Governor handed over the cheques at Unguwan Iya, Zaria, in the presence of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Abbas Tajudeen; Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas; former Governor Ramalan Yero, and other senior officials. The payout reflects the administration’s policy of compensating residents before demolition — a clear break from the past, when infrastructure projects often displaced people without redress. With this arrangement, affected property owners along the township road corridors can be relocated or compensated without loss, allowing construction to proceed without delay. This follows the administration’s earlier compensation exercises, including ₦2.85 billion disbursed in February 2026 for road projects across the state, and ₦2 billion paid in July 2026 to about 1,000 victims of the Rigasa-Tudun Wada flood and erosion control project. Speaking after receiving his cheque, one of the beneficiaries from Zaria, Malam Ibrahim Ahmed, said: “For the first time, government paid us before bringing down our properties. We can now find alternative accommodation without suffering. We thank Governor Uba Sani for remembering the common man.” Another beneficiary from Sabon Gari, Hajiya Fatima Suleiman, said “We were afraid when we heard the road would pass through our houses. But today we have received our compensation in full. This is true leadership — development with human face.” Traditional rulers, community leaders and political party leaders described the event as a validation of the link between leadership and compassion. In what some attendees described as “political tsunami”, the event also witnessed a massive defection as Governor Uba Sani received a wave of heavyweights and their thousands of followers into the All Progressives Congress (APC). Leading the defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) were political bigwigs Bashir Sa’idu, Senator Audu Kwari, Hon. Mohammed Sani Bello Mainan Zazzau, Hon. Jafaru Sani, Hon. Mukhtar Hazo, Hon. Bala Alwa’u, Hon. Nasiru Abdullahi Maikano, Hon. Lawal Buba, Hon. Ephraim Iliyasu and others. The defectors cited the Governor’s inclusive leadership, visible infrastructure delivery and people-centred compensation policy as reasons for abandoning the ADC for the APC. The development, according to observers, further consolidates the APC’s dominance in Kaduna North senatorial zone ahead of the 2027 general elections. title: US Resumes Intelligence Sharing With Ukraine, Zelensky Says
body:
The US has resumed sharing military and security intelligence with Ukraine after suspending data exchanges for a “some period of time,” President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Oct. 18.
Speaking during an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” as reported by Bloomberg , the president confirmed that intelligence pipelines had been restored following operational friction with Washington .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Zelensky also expressed hope that bilateral negotiations with American officials could take place within the coming week.
The temporary suspension of intelligence flows materialized amid sharp disagreements between Washington and Kyiv over battlefield targeting rules and prospective ceasefire mechanisms.
On Oct. 15, The Washington Post reported that US intelligence officials warned Ukraine that Washington would immediately halt intelligence sharing if Ukrainian forces continued long-range strikes against Russian oil refineries and petrochemical facilities.
The warning was formally conveyed to Ukraine’s embassy in Washington amid disputes surrounding an “energy ceasefire” unilaterally declared by US President Donald Trump .
The Trump administration had previously cautioned that it could suspend intelligence cooperation and block European purchases of American weapons earmarked for Ukraine if Kyiv refused to halt deep interdiction strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
While American sources cited by The Washington Post maintained that intelligence sharing was never completely dismantled, they acknowledged that specific data feeds had been restricted.
Prior to the restoration, Zelensky disclosed that Ukrainian defense forces received no advance warnings from Western partners regarding Russian ballistic missile launches toward Kyiv for two consecutive nights, during which kinetic impacts damaged critical capital energy installations and knocked out municipal power and water grids.
Zelensky’s confirmation that intelligence sharing has resumed comes as Ukrainian and American officials work to arrange direct bilateral consultations.
On Friday, Oct. 16, National Security and Defense Council Secretary Rustem Umerov held consultations with US special envoy Jared Kushner to discuss a timetable and format for upcoming in-person meetings .
Zelensky affirmed that Kyiv remains prepared for direct discussions with White House representatives to explore verifiable mechanisms for a reciprocal energy armistice to protect civilian utility networks ahead of winter.
The restoration of intelligence sharing also coincides with public scrutiny over related technological restrictions affecting Ukrainian defense capabilities, including artificial speed limitations placed on commercial Starlink terminals and Ukraine’s lack of access to the Pentagon-contracted Starshield satellite network .
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Vance says may run for president in 2028
body:
NEW YORK, October 18. /TASS/. US Vice President JD Vance has not ruled out running for President of the United States in 2028.
"Of course there's a chance," Vance said, adding he still has to think about this in more detail.
In June, US President Donald Trump, in an interview with Fortune magazine, declined to talk about his possible successor, who should continue the "America First" policy if he wins the 2028 elections. The American media has repeatedly written about Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vance as the main Republican candidates able to run for president in two years.

title: Sani, CJN: Healthy Judicial Personnel Vital to Justice Delivery
body: John Shiklam in Kaduna Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, has said the wellbeing of judicial officers and staff is vital to the effective administration of justice. He stated this in Kaduna on Saturday at the opening ceremony of the 32nd Annual Judiciary Sports Competition organised by the National Sports Association of Judiciary (NASAJ). Represented by the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, James Kanyip, Sani said sports provided judicial personnel an opportunity to stay fit, build professional relationships and promote teamwork. “The strength of our courts rests not only on laws, procedures, precedents and facilities, but on the competence, integrity and well-being of the people who serve in the courts,” Sani said. The governor said the values promoted through sports were equally important in the courtroom. “This competition gives judicial personnel a valuable opportunity to promote physical fitness, build professional relationships and enjoy healthy recreation. “It also reinforces values that matter in the courtroom as much as on the field. Fairness, respect for rules of law, discipline, teamwork and regards and respect for others,” he said. Sani described the judiciary as central to Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, saying the courts play vital roles in interpreting the law, resolving disputes, protecting rights and upholding the constitutional order. He commended the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere Ekun, for her attention to the welfare of judicial personnel. The governor said hosting the competition in Kaduna demonstrated the state’s commitment to cooperation among public institutions. He urged participants to compete with determination, respect the rules and honour one another. Speaking while declaring the event opened, the CJN, Justice Kekere-Ekun, described sports as vital to the wellbeing and effectiveness of judicial personnel. Represented by the Kaduna State Chief Judge, Justice Mohammed Tukur Muazu, the CJN said sports could promote physical fitness, relieve stress and improve the balance required for effective performance. She said: “The effectiveness of judicial institutions depends, in part, on the well-being of the men and women who serve within them.” According to her, the demanding responsibilities of judicial officers and staff required concentration, diligence, patience and sustained commitment. “Equally important, sporting activities encourage teamwork, discipline, perseverance and respect for rules. “These values are as relevant on the field of play as they are in the discharge of our respective professional responsibilities,” the CJN said. She commended NASAJ for sustaining the annual competition, saying it had created an opportunity for judicial officers and staff from across the country to interact, renew friendships and strengthen fellowship. She also expressed appreciation to the Kaduna State Government for hosting the competition. The CJN urged the participating teams to compete with commitment, fairness and respect for their opponents. Ealier in his welcome address, President of NASAJ, Comrade Noah Sunday, commended the CJN for the unwavering support and encouragement of sporting activities within the Nigerian judiciary.

title: Gender Ministry convenes stakeholders to review national action plan to combat human trafficking
body: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has convened a Technical Working Group (TWG) meeting to review and support the development of a new National Plan of Action (NPA) to combat human trafficking in Ghana. The meeting, organised through the Ministry’s Human Trafficking Secretariat, brought together key stakeholders to assess progress, identify gaps and discuss strategies to strengthen the country’s response to trafficking. Discussions focused on the availability and classification of trafficking data, resource mobilisation and funding for anti-trafficking interventions, as well as measures to improve monitoring and data collection systems. Participants also highlighted the need for stronger coordination among relevant institutions and partners to ensure the effective implementation of anti-trafficking measures. The meeting underscored the importance of reliable data in supporting evidence-based planning, tracking progress and providing a clearer picture of the resources committed by government institutions and development partners to combat human trafficking. Speaking on behalf of the Minister, Director of the Human Trafficking Secretariat, Abena Annobea Asare, stressed the importance of stakeholder collaboration in developing a practical and effective National Plan of Action. She called on all partners to maintain their commitment to addressing identified gaps and strengthening efforts to prevent human trafficking, protect victims and support the prosecution of offenders. The Ministry said it would continue to work with relevant stakeholders to advance the development of the new National Plan of Action and strengthen coordinated efforts towards eliminating human trafficking in Ghana.

title: Yagbonwura Cultural and Eco-Tourism Experience to showcase Savannah Region’s heritage and investment potential
body: As part of activities marking the 6th Inter Tourism Expo Accra (INTTA) 2026, the Yagbonwura Cultural and Eco-Tourism Experience will take participants on a journey through the Savannah Region on 25–26 October 2026, promoting tourism, cultural exchange, commerce and investment opportunities. The initiative seeks to bridge the geographical and economic divide between northern and southern Ghana by connecting people, businesses, investors and tourism stakeholders through the country’s rich cultural heritage and natural attractions. The experience will showcase key destinations, including Damongo, Mole National Park, Larabanga and Bole—the President of Ghana’s hometown-, highlighting the region’s cultural traditions, historic landmarks, wildlife and hospitality potential. From the historic Larabanga Mosque to the wildlife attractions of Mole National Park, the Savannah Region offers significant opportunities for heritage tourism, eco-tourism, hospitality, agribusiness and community-based enterprise development. Beyond sightseeing, the initiative aims to stimulate domestic tourism, encourage business partnerships and attract investment into tourism infrastructure, accommodation, transport, local food production, crafts and cultural experiences. Speaking on the economic importance of the initiative, Mr Emmanuel Treku, Executive Chairman of INTTA, stated: “Tourism is more than sightseeing; it is a powerful economic tool for connecting communities, creating jobs, stimulating local businesses and attracting investment. Through the Yagbonwura Cultural and Eco-Tourism Experience, we want to demonstrate that northern Ghana is not only rich in culture and natural attractions but also offers significant opportunities for tourism development, hospitality, agribusiness and commerce. Visiting Bole, the President’s hometown, is particularly significant because it provides an opportunity to spotlight the economic potential of the community and the wider Savannah Region. We want participants to experience these destinations firsthand, engage with local businesses and identify opportunities for investment and partnership. Our vision is to use tourism to bridge the gap between northern and southern Ghana, ensuring that the benefits of tourism, trade and investment reach communities across the country. When we travel across Ghana, we build cultural understanding, expand business relationships and create opportunities for shared prosperity.” The initiative also supports Ghana’s broader economic development ambitions by promoting tourism as a catalyst for employment, entrepreneurship and the 24-Hour Economy agenda. By connecting tourism destinations with investors, hospitality operators, agribusinesses and local enterprises, INTTA seeks to encourage a more inclusive tourism economy in which communities across Ghana can benefit from increased visitor spending and commercial partnerships. The Yagbonwura experience therefore represents more than a sightseeing excursion. It is an invitation to discover northern Ghana’s potential, strengthen national integration and create lasting connections between culture, commerce and investment. Ghana’s tourism future must embrace every region, connect every community and create opportunities for all. title: UN Security Council can be involved in creating conditions for dialogue in Gulf — Lavrov
body:
MANAMA /Kingdom of Bahrain/, October 18. /TASS/. The Russian Concept of Collective Security in the Persian Gulf is aimed at creating conditions for dialogue between countries, and if interested, permanent members of the UN Security Council can be involved to support the process, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said at a ministerial meeting of the Russia-Gulf Arab Cooperation Council (GCC) Strategic Dialogue.
"We consider the updated Concept of Ensuring Collective Security in the Gulf zone as our contribution, you are familiar with it. This document in its previous editions has been discussed for decades with representatives of the political, scientific, and expert circles of the countries of the Cooperation Council. And we proceed from the fact that it is necessary to give the coastal states themselves the decisive say in determining ways to ensure the safe development of this entire most important strategic region of the world," he said.
"Our concept is aimed at creating conditions for direct dialogue between the countries, the Gulf coast countries, and their neighbors, such as Iraq and Jordan. As you know, we propose to involve non-regional players in creating such conditions, including the leadership of the League of Arab States, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, and, if you are interested, the permanent members of the UN Security Council to support this process.".

title: 2027: Ondo targets one million votes for Tinubu — Oke
body: By Dayo Johnson, Akure A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo State, Chief Olusola Oke, SAN, has expressed confidence that the state will deliver more than one million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Oke spoke at the weekend in Akure during the inauguration of the Ondo State APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Committees. He said the one million votes target pledged by Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and other party leaders was achievable, citing what he described as the impact of Tinubu’s administration across the country . According to him, the effects of the President’s policies and development initiatives are being felt across the 36 states, including Ondo, and Nigerians would reward him with their votes in 2027. “Ondo State will ensure we return massive votes for the President in 2027. We will deliver well over one million votes as promised,” he said. Oke cited the Ore-Ondo Road, Akure-Benin Road and Akure-Ekiti Road as examples of federal infrastructure projects through which residents could feel the impact of Tinubu’s administration. “Asiwaju is revolutionising Nigeria,” he said. The APC chieftain also expressed optimism about the country’s economic outlook, claiming that the economy, which he said had been on the brink, was now on the path to recovery. He cited the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank and other international institutions as having acknowledged the country’s economic progress. “The IMF, World Bank and other international agencies cannot be wrong. This is a generational service the President is rendering to the nation,” he said. Oke assured the party leadership that members would be mobilised across the 18 local government areas of Ondo State ahead of the 2027 elections. The inauguration was attended by Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa; his deputy, Dr Olayide Adelami; Chief Pius Akinyelure; and Senators Nimbe Farunkanmi and Tayo Alasoadura. Others included the state APC chairman, Hon. Kolawole Babatunde, members of the Ondo State House of Assembly, members of the State Executive Council and other party leaders. title: Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial: Artists, locations, dates and what to know
body: Art installations are set to take over public spaces across Abu Dhabi and Al Ain as the second Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial returns this month. Organised by the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, the exhibition brings together 21 artists and collectives from the UAE and abroad, with monumental, interactive and multi-sensory works exploring home, collective memory and community. From the participating artists to where to find their work, here is what to know. When is the Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial? The biennial opens in Al Ain on October 23, followed by Abu Dhabi on November 15. The exhibition runs across both cities until February 15, 2027. Where will the artworks be? In Abu Dhabi, installations will be displayed at Mina Zayed (MiZa) , Souq Al Mina, Hidd Al Saadiyat and Saadiyat Cultural District , where works will occupy the park between Zayed National Museum and Louvre Abu Dhabi . The programme will also extend to selected locations across Al Ain, although specific sites have yet to be announced. Details of which artworks will appear at each location have also not been released. Which artists are taking part? The line-up includes UAE artists Khalid Al Banna, Roudhah Al Mazrouei and Shama Al Hamed, alongside international names such as Ibrahim Mahama, Laure Prouvost, Yinka Shonibare and Akram Zaatari. Also participating are Asuncion Molinos Gordo, blaxTARLINES, Celeste Boursier-Mougenot, Elena del Rivero, Ivan Argote, Jean-Marie Appriou, Kapwani Kiwanga and Marinella Senatore. Completing the roster are M'barek Bouhchichi, Mercedes Azpilicueta, Nari Ward, Reena Saini Kallat, Serge Attukwei Clottey and Vica Pacheco. What is this year’s theme? Artistic director Elvira Dyangani Ose leads the art event under the theme Home: A Glossary for a Communal Sense of Place. The exhibition approaches home as an evolving, shared human experience, exploring how people’s relationships with places are shaped by community, memory and everyday encounters. Artists will respond to the settings in which their works appear, drawing on research and engaging with surrounding communities. What can visitors expect? The biennial will bring contemporary art into public and cultural spaces, with installations exploring urban landscapes, material culture and civic participation. Visitors can expect a mix of large-scale, interactive and multisensory works designed to encourage engagement with both the art and its surroundings. Details of individual installations, visiting hours, ticketing and accompanying events are still to be announced.

title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
body: France awoke to scenes of widespread damage on Sunday after a day of riots and demonstrations, with shopfronts shattered, burnt out cars, charred bikes, and piles of glass and debris on the pavements of Paris. Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful. They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools. Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings. Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas. In Paris, protesters clashed with riot police, who turned tear gas and water cannon on the crowds. During the day, some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles. At least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups. Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons. Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram. In Lille, a McDonalds was set on fire, police said, and an Apple store in the city was broken into and looted. More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured in the unrest on Saturday, France’s interior ministry said. Around 1,500 shops and retailers were also damaged in the disturbances, the Retail and Trade Federation said. On Sunday morning in Paris, residents surveyed the aftermath, which included the smashed glass frontages of designer stores including Ralph Lauren, Gucci and Versace. Shopkeepers were out early with brooms, picking up large shards of glass as they began the clean-up. Rubbish trucks worked their way down some of the larger streets to clear some of the debris. Many shops were daubed with graffiti, some reading “tax the rich” and “eat the rich.” The BBC visited a clothes shop close to the Place de la République which had been ransacked, with piles of clothes and furniture scattered across the shop floor. The shop’s distraught owner told the BBC he saw looters on the CCTV who were in the shop for just over an hour and a half, and that during that time he saw no police in the process. The owner – who asked not to be identified – told the BBC he did not believe any of those who robbed the shop were genuine protesters against school conditions or the cost of living. He said the looters were taking advantage of the demonstrations. Close to the Place de la République, a BBC reporter visited the Good Vibes bakery, whose glass front was completely shattered, and the Nicolas wine store, where every bottle was either stolen or smashed, leaving smell of alcohol lingering in the street. CCTV footage shown on France’s Channel 2 shows groups of teenagers, mostly wearing masks, in a shop selling mobile phones helping themselves to items from the shelves. Student protests in France have seen hundreds of thousands take to the streets since they began late last month. Protesters have been demanding additional investment in their schools, criticising the lack of teachers and staff, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings. France’s Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that while demonstrating was a fundamental right, there were “outrages” committed by “several thousand far-left individuals” who were determined to target public buildings and confront the police. Later, they were joined by “delinquents who looted and ransacked numerous businesses in several cities in France”, he said. In the city of Lyon, Mayor Grégory Doucet said the burning of the city’s tourist office was “a tragedy”, telling French outlet BFMTV that “it breaks our hearts because it’s a very iconic, well-known historic building”. Local police said “hostile individuals” prevented firefighters from safely tackling the blaze. Fire crews also battled a fire at Limoges town hall, which caused part of the building to collapse. Local officials said the town hall was “largely lost.” “A wild horde” had “deliberately” set fire to the 143-year-old building, said Maurice Barate, the prefect for the Haute-Vienne department. Elsewhere, a young man “had his hand blown off” by a small explosive in Saint-Étienne, the south-eastern city’s Mayor Régis Juanico said on social media. “Such a tragedy should never have happened,” he said. France’s interior ministry said Saturday’s protests involved “targeted acts of violence” from “hooded individuals” in places, including parts of the capital and also in Marseille, Rennes, Toulouse, and the western city of Angers. Damage to buildings was reported across France, including in Grenoble, Avignon, Pau, Montpellier and Valence.

title: Iran's parliament approves Mehrdad Akhlaghi as defense minister after predecessor killed by Israel
body: Iran's parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi as defense minister on Sunday, ending months of interim leadership at the ministry and placing a former defense sector veteran in charge of the country's defense production and procurement apparatus.Akhlaghi replaces Majid Ebn al-Reza, who took over in an interim capacity after then Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh was killed by US-Israeli strikes in February.Akhlaghi has spent decades in Iran's defense industry and has held senior roles in its aerospace and missile sectors. He is subject to US and EU sanctions over his work in Iran's defense sector.In a program presented to lawmakers, Akhlaghi pledged to rebuild the country's military-industrial infrastructure, accelerate the development of defense technologies and expand cooperation with private-sector companies."If the American enemy makes another miscalculation, the response of the valiant Iranian people and the fighters of Islam will be surprising and extensive," he said, adding that Tehran had taken necessary measures to counter the potential use by the US of its "mother of all bombs" against Iran.US planning to use MOAB against IranCNN reported this week that the US has developed strike plans ​that could include using ‌the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, also known ​as the "mother of ​all bombs," against Iranian energy ⁠infrastructure and nuclear sites ​if President Donald Trump ​orders renewed combat operations.The weapon is one of the largest ‌non-nuclear ⁠bombs in the US arsenal."The US president should focus on ensuring his forces are withdrawn safely from our region. If he drops a single bomb, he will have to see how many of his troops end up being carried out of the region in a horizontal position," Akhlaghi said.

title: Martinez starts for Man Utd after outburst
body: Lisandro Martinez was named in Manchester United’s starting line-up to face Leeds on Sunday despite his controversial remarks about the struggling club’s hierarchy. Argentina defender Martinez took aim at United’s powerbrokers following their 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday. Martinez claimed United boss Michael Carrick had been left with an under-strength squad. The centre-back criticised technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he had “100 percent” expected more investment during the summer transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season. It is understood Martinez, who issued an apology on Thursday, has been fined for his outburst. Carrick confirmed during a pre-match press conference on Friday that Martinez would be in his squad for their Premier League match at bitter rivals Leeds. And he was true to his word as Martinez was selected in a United team looking to win for just the third time in 10 games this term. United have gone five matches without a victory in all competitions and are languishing in 14th place in the Premier League. A defeat at Leeds would heap more pressure on Carrick ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Como. The post Martinez starts for Man Utd after outburst appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: I don’t want my son to lose Medicine and Surgery admission — Abia pastor cries out
body: …330 UTME score, no N500,000 to secure admission By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — For Rev. Enyinnaya Nwabuko, a rural pastor in one of the foremost Pentecostal churches who has spent nearly two decades preaching the gospel, one prayer now weighs heavily on his heart: that poverty will not destroy his son’s dream of becoming a medical doctor. His son, Marvelous Nwabuko, has secured provisional admission to study Medicine and Surgery at Abia State University (ABSU), Uturu, after scoring an impressive 330 in the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME). But the family’s joy is threatened by a financial hurdle. With nearly ₦500,000 needed to pay the acceptance fee and other initial charges within two weeks, the indigent cleric is appealing to the Abia State Government, philanthropists, corporate organisations and other well-meaning Nigerians to help save his son’s admission. “I don’t want my son to lose his admission because of poverty. That is why I am crying out for help,” the distressed father told Vanguard. A father of three, Nwabuko hails from Umuelem Amakanma in Umuahia South Local Government Area but ministers at a local church, whose name is withheld, in Etorue Oloko, a rural community in Ikwuano LGA. For years, he and his wife have laboured in God’s vineyard, feeding the flock and serving their community despite their modest means. Now, the family faces a test of their faith and needs urgent intervention to avert a looming disappointment. Marvelous’s academic journey makes the prospect of losing the admission particularly painful. Last year, he sat for the UTME for the first time and scored an outstanding 340. However, he was denied admission because he was underage. Undeterred, Marvelous, who will turn 17 on November 10, returned to the JAMB examination hall in 2026, scored 330 and earned another opportunity to pursue his medical ambition. His Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) results were equally impressive, with three A1s and six B3s, giving him nine credits in one sitting. Yet, despite his academic brilliance, the young scholar may be unable to cross the threshold of university education simply because his parents cannot raise the required fees on time. “Since he got the admission letter last Friday, the two weeks allowed for payment have started counting. I have approached some people for assistance, but so far, it has been promises,” the father lamented. “I am afraid that if help does not come quickly, he may lose this opportunity. My desire is to give my son the best as a father, but my present financial situation is a challenge.” For Rev. Nwabuko, the appeal goes beyond securing admission. It is a plea to protect the future of a child whose hard work has earned him a place in medical school. He acknowledged that the financial demands of studying Medicine and Surgery extend far beyond acceptance fees and initial charges but said he was determined not to allow his economic circumstances to extinguish his son’s ambition. Vanguard checks revealed that, apart from the initial ₦500,000 needed for the acceptance fee, school fees and other charges, another ₦500,000 would be required for books and upkeep. “My greatest desire is to give my children a future. I may not have the money, but I want my son to study his dream course, which he has also worked so hard for,” he said. Marvelous, who dreams of specialising in cardiology, told Vanguard he remained hopeful that his ambition would become a reality. “I have faith in God that my dream will come true,” he enthused. For now, that dream rests partly on the generosity and intervention of public-spirited people willing to give a brilliant young Nigerian a chance. A donation towards his education could mean more than paying a university bill; it could help preserve years of hard work and open the door to a future that financial hardship threatens to shut. title: Fire at Volyn enterprise contained after Russian attack
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said this on Facebook .
“A private enterprise in the Kamin-Kashyrskyi district caught fire again as a result of an enemy strike,” the statement said.
Firefighters have contained the blaze. Efforts to fully extinguish it are ongoing. Due to the threat of further attacks, the work had to be suspended several times.
SES specialists tested the air. No concentrations of hazardous substances exceeding permissible levels were detected outside the enterprise.
No casualties have been reported, according to preliminary information.
