title: Bauchi agency CEO, 4 children die in road accident
body: Alhaji Ibrahim Ladan Duguri, the Executive Secretary of the Bauchi State Health Contributory Management Agency (BASHCMA), has lost his life alongside those of four of his children in an accident at Yalwan Duguri in Alkaleri Local Government Area of the State. Governor Bala Mohammed, who confirmed the tragedy, expressed profound sorrow and deep grief. The governor described the death of Alhaji Ibrahim Ladan Duguri as a monumental loss to Bauchi, particularly the health sector, “where he distinguished himself through dedication, commitment, and an unwavering passion for improving access to healthcare services for the people”. In his condolence message signed by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Mukhtar Gidado, the governor equally saddened by the tragic circumstances surrounding the incident and extends his heartfelt sympathy to the immediate family of the deceased, the Duguri Emirate Council, friends, associates, colleagues, and the entire people of Bauchi over the loss. Mining Marshals deny involvement in operation linked to miners’ deaths Corruption turning Nigerian courts to ‘market stalls’ – Retired Justice Augie He also prayed for the full recovery, strength, and comfort of Suleiman, one the deceased’s son who reportedly survived the accident . Mohammed said, “As Executive Secretary of BASHCMA, the deceased played an important role in advancing the state’s health contributory management system and supporting efforts to make healthcare more accessible to the people, especially the less privileged. His dedication was also evident in his contributions to the state’s medical team during pilgrimage exercises in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where his commitment to the health and well-being of pilgrims was widely valued. “Beyond his professional accomplishments, Alhaji Ibrahim Ladan Duguri was a close personal friend, and classmate of Governor Bala Mohammed. His death, therefore, represents not only the loss of a valued public servant but also the painful departure of a beloved family member and trusted companion whose life was marked by service, loyalty, and dedication to humanity.” He acknowledged that no words can adequately express the pain and anguish of the bereaved family at this difficult moment. Mohammed prayed that Almighty Allah, in His infinite Mercy, would forgive the shortcomings of the deceased, accept their good deeds, and grant Alhaji Ibrahim Ladan Duguri and his beloved children eternal rest in Aljannatul Firdaus. The governor called on all well-meaning citizens of Bauchi to remember the bereaved family in their prayers and to offer them the necessary compassion, and solidarity during this moment of profound grief. The funeral prayer for the deceased will be conducted at the palace of the District Head of Yalwan Duguri by 11:00am, on Sunday.

title: Ukrainian forces strike Russian drone launch site near Donetsk
body:
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces reported this on Facebook .
"In particular, a site used for the storage, preparation and launch of attack UAVs was hit near Donetsk. This reduces the enemy's ability to attack Ukrainian territory and civilian infrastructure with various types of drones," the statement said.
In addition, Ukrainian troops struck a repair base for motor vehicles and armored combat vehicles belonging to Russia's South Group of Forces near the settlement of Sukhodilsk in the Luhansk region.
"The strike complicates the repair of damaged equipment and its return to combat units on the front line," the General Staff said.
A concentration of personnel from one of the Russian army's units was also hit near the settlement of Dubove in the Donetsk region.
The General Staff stressed that operations against key enemy military targets were continuing.

title: One Injured As Five-Storey Building Partially Collapses In Abuja
body: One worker sustained minor injuries after a five-storey building under construction partially collapsed on Durban Street, Wuse II, Abuja, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has said. The incident adds to a series of building collapses reported in the Federal Capital Territory in recent months, including a three-storey building collapse in Wuse Zone 4 in September and another in Durumi 3 in May that claimed five lives. NEMA said its Abuja Operations Office received an alert about Saturday’s incident at approximately 6:30 pm on October 17, 2026, prompting the activation of relevant emergency response agencies. In a statement issued by its Press Unit, the agency said the FCT Fire Service was among the stakeholders mobilised, while its AYA Emergency Response Ambulance Bay team was deployed to coordinate search and rescue operations. The agency said no life was lost in the incident and confirmed that the injured worker was evacuated to a nearby hospital for medical attention. In September, a three-storey building collapsed in Wuse Zone 4 , hours after officials of the FCT Administration’s Department of Development Control had sealed the property and directed occupants to vacate it. The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the building had earlier been marked and sealed, while rescue operations were launched at the scene. In August, two residents were rescued after part of a one-storey residential building comprising six blocks of flats collapsed in Kubwa 2/2. The victims were taken to Kubwa General Hospital in stable condition. Earlier in May, a three-storey building under construction collapsed in Durumi 3 , near Gudu Market, killing five people. Fifteen people were pulled from the rubble, with nine rescued alive and one reported to be in critical condition. Following the incident, FCT Minister Nyesom Wike ordered a full-scale investigation and warned developers to comply with building standards and allow government officials to inspect construction sites. The post One Injured As Five-Storey Building Partially Collapses In Abuja appeared first on Channels Television .

title: All 46 NDC aspirants pass vetting ahead of Bono East regional elections
body: All 46 aspirants seeking various leadership positions in the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Bono East Regional executive elections have successfully passed vetting, clearing the way for the party’s regional polls scheduled for November this year. The aspirants, who had earlier submitted their nominations online, completed the in-person filing and vetting process on Wednesday. The exercise was overseen by the Vetting Committee, chaired by Nuru Hamidan, who also serves as Deputy Chief Executive Officer of STC. No one disqualified Speaking to Joy News after the exercise, Mr Hamidan said the process had been smooth and transparent, with all aspirants deemed qualified to contest. “The nomination exercise was peaceful. All 46 aspirants recorded on the committee’s dashboard completed the in-person filing process and went through the vetting successfully. They were deemed qualified, and no one was disqualified,” Mr Hamidan said. He added that the committee had encountered no challenges during the exercise and expressed hope that the aspirants would comply with the party’s electoral guidelines to ensure a peaceful election in November. “I hope that the aspirants will comply with the party’s electoral guidelines to ensure the election is peaceful,” he said. Aspirants express confidence With vetting complete, the aspirants are turning their attention to the campaign trail. One of the key contenders is the incumbent Regional Treasurer, Gapson Raphael Kofi, who is seeking to become Regional Secretary. Mr Kofi expressed confidence in his chances of winning, citing his track record of integrity and truthfulness. “My track record as someone with integrity and truthfulness puts me in a strong position to be elected as the party’s Regional Secretary,” he said. Outgoing secretary praises party’s decision The outgoing Regional Secretary, Adaebsa Isaac, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer of the GRATIS Foundation, is not seeking re-election. He commended the party’s decision to exempt current executives occupying government positions from contesting. According to him, the move would create opportunities to groom new leaders and allow party members who are not in government to dedicate more time to party activities. “Those occupying government positions currently are too busy to do the party’s work, and as a result, the party structure is getting weak,” Mr Isaac said. “There’s a need to groom others and pave the way for people who are not in government and have time to work for the party.” Call for clean campaigns The incumbent Regional Communications Officer, Sulemana Mohammed Mustapha, has urged delegates to ensure that the campaign is free from insults and personal attacks. He called on delegates to vote against aspirants who engage in such behaviour. “There’s a need for the delegates to stage clean campaigns devoid of insults. I urge delegates to punish such individuals by voting against them on election day,” Mr Mustapha said. He added that his communication experience and expertise were what the party needed to communicate the government’s policies effectively and retain power in 2028. What’s next? The NDC Bono East Regional executive elections will be held in Techiman in November this year. With all 46 aspirants cleared to contest, the party is preparing for an internal election that will shape its regional leadership ahead of the next general election.

title: Corruption turning Nigerian courts to ‘market stalls’ – Retired Justice Augie
body: A retired justice of the Supreme Court, Amina Adamu Augie, has warned that corruption within Nigeria’s judiciary and legal profession is eroding public confidence in the administration of justice and transforming the courts from institutions of impartiality into what she described as “market stalls.” Speaking in Abuja during the 40th anniversary celebration of the Nigerian Law School Class of 1986, popularly known as the Centennial Class, Augie said corrupt practices involving judges, lawyers and court officials had weakened the credibility of the justice system and damaged the public’s perception of the legal profession. The retired justice called for practitioners found guilty of misconduct to be punished, regardless of their seniority, influence or professional standing. Augie, who taught at the Nigerian Law School before beginning her judicial career, identified corruption, political interference, inadequate funding and delays in the administration of justice as some of the most serious challenges facing Nigeria’s judiciary. Wase mobilises stakeholders to tackle insecurity Makinde: Nigeria’s main challenge Is Poverty, not Religion “The third, which I will not dress up, is corruption. Where it exists on the Bench, at the Bar, or in the Registry, it poisons everything by turning the one place that a citizen should find impartiality into one more market stall,” she said. She nevertheless cautioned against the blanket condemnation of the judiciary, stressing that the majority of judges and lawyers remained honest, hardworking and poorly remunerated. According to her, the justice system must be designed in a way that protects judicial officers and other legal practitioners from undue pressure and temptation, rather than exposing them to conditions that make misconduct easier. Augie expressed particular concern about the conduct of some senior members of the legal profession, saying their actions had contributed substantially to the decline in public trust in the courts and the wider justice system. “Have we kept faith with them? In part, YES, in part, NO. Public trust has paid the price. The public today is quick to believe the worst of lawyers, and sorry to say, not always without cause,” she said. “When a few senior members of the profession have been found to traffic in the corruption of justice, the damage is not to them alone; it stains the gown we all wear.” She said rebuilding confidence in the legal system would require more than public relations campaigns or efforts to improve the image of the judiciary. In her view, the profession must demonstrate a willingness to discipline its members openly and fairly, without being intimidated by their status. “Restoring that trust is not a matter of better public relations. It is a matter of conduct and a profession willing to discipline its own, without fear or favor, no matter how senior the offender may be in the legal profession,” she said. The retired justice reminded lawyers that their foremost duty was to the court and the administration of justice, not merely to the clients who retained them. She said professional responsibility demanded honesty, candour, respect for judicial authority and commitment to the rule of law. Augie urged lawyers to reject attempts to manipulate court proceedings, manufacture or distort evidence, delay cases unnecessarily or secure favourable judgments through improper influence. She also warned that corruption could not be addressed in isolation from the broader conditions under which the judiciary operates. Inadequate funding, she said, posed a serious threat to judicial independence because a court that depended on the executive for basic infrastructure and operational needs could not be regarded as completely autonomous. “A Judiciary that must beg the executive for a Courtroom roof, vehicles, or even the Judges’ entitlements is not fully free; financial autonomy for the Courts is not a perk for Justices and Judges, but a guarantee for litigants,” she said. Augie further criticised the delays and high costs that continue to make litigation inaccessible to many Nigerians. She described delay as the “chronic disease” of the country’s justice system and said it had weakened public confidence in the courts. Drawing on her experience at the Supreme Court, she said the apex court was burdened by an excessive number of appeals, including disputes that should ordinarily have been resolved at lower levels of the judicial system. She recalled an appeal concerning the burning of 12 goats that eventually reached the Supreme Court, despite the enormous workload already confronting the court. According to her, constitutional amendments were needed to narrow the categories of cases that could be taken to the apex court. Such reforms, she said, would enable Supreme Court justices to focus on matters involving significant constitutional, legal and national questions. Augie also condemned the repeated failure of government authorities to comply with court orders. She cited the prolonged detention of former National Security Adviser Sambo Dasuki and Islamic Movement leader Ibrahim El-Zakzaky, despite judicial directives ordering their release. She said the disobedience of court orders by public officials weakened the authority of the judiciary and sent a dangerous message that compliance with the law was optional for those in power. Reflecting on the development of Nigeria’s justice system over the past four decades, Augie acknowledged that progress had been made, particularly since the country’s return to democratic rule in 1999. However, she expressed disappointment that justice remained slow, expensive and beyond the reach of many citizens. She referred to Nigeria’s ranking of 120th out of 143 countries in the 2025 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index, describing the position as an uncomfortable indication of the country’s institutional weaknesses and the continuing challenges facing its justice system. Augie called for comprehensive reforms to strengthen judicial independence, improve access to justice, modernise case management, reduce delays and restore ethical standards across the legal profession. She urged members of the Class of 1986, many of whom now hold senior positions in the judiciary, government and legal profession, to use their influence to defend the rule of law and rebuild public confidence in the courts. “If Governments obey the Courts, if its Judgments are enforced, if justice comes within a reasonable time and within reach of the poor, if the profession upholds its integrity and disciplines its own, Nigeria would be better positioned to secure its future”, she said.

title: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid launches latest Arab Hope Makers initiative with Dh1 million prize
body: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai , has launched the seventh edition of the Arab Hope Makers initiative, celebrating philanthropists across the region who dedicate their efforts to improving communities. The initiative, the largest of its kind in the Arab world, recognises individuals, volunteer groups and non-profit organisations driving change through charitable, social and humanitarian work. Applications are open at arabhopemakers.com, with the winner receiving a prize of Dh1 million ($272,000). "Nurturing hope is a triumph for life itself," said Sheikh Mohammed . "The hope we cultivate today will yield prosperity, peace and safety in people's lives tomorrow." The UAE will "always remain a nation of good deeds and optimism, inspiring positive change across the region and the world", said Sheikh Mohammed. Mohammed Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Secretary General of Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives, said the initiative has contributed significantly to humanitarian action and volunteering across the Arab world since its launch in 2017. More than 335,000 participants have taken part in six iterations. Mohammed bin Rashid launches search for 2026 Arab Hope Makers, says UAE will remain nation of good deeds, optimism #WamNews https://t.co/bNnKXHqvvK pic.twitter.com/JOTJ0aT7rj — WAM English (@WAMNEWS_ENG) October 18, 2026 "The initiative shines a light on the great aspects of our Arab societies and the potential and talents dedicated to sincerely improving people's lives," Mr Al Gergawi said. The most recent edition crowned Fouzia Mahmoudi from Morocco as the 2025 Arab Hope Maker after her foundation, Operation Smile, performed more than 19,000 surgeries on children born with cleft lips and palates. The two other finalists, Hend Alhajri from Kuwait and Abderrahmane Rais from Morocco, were also awarded Dh1 million each, bringing the total prize pool for the sixth edition to Dh3 million ($817,000). Ms Alhajri founded Fatima House, a refuge for orphaned children in Tanzania, while Mr Rais launched a humanitarian initiative supporting widows and women in need across Morocco. Operating under MBRGI, the initiative is open to applicants from across the Arab world and globally whose projects address community development, alleviate suffering or tackle local challenges on a voluntary, non-profit basis.

title: Ogun FRSC Commander is dead
body: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), RS2.2 Ogun State Sector Commander, Oludare Ogunjobi, is dead. A statement by the Command’s spokesman, Afolabi Odunsi, confirmed his death on Sunday, saying he passed away after a brief illness. The statement reads “His passing is a great loss to the Corps, his colleagues, and the entire road safety community. He will be remembered for his service, leadership, commitment to road safety administration, and dedication to the mandate of the Federal Road Safety Corps. “During his time in service, he contributed to the Corps’ efforts towards promoting safer roads, enhancing public enlightenment, strengthening stakeholder engagement, and improving compliance with traffic regulations. Mining Marshals deny involvement in operation linked to miners’ deaths Bagudu: Tinubu’s reforms yielding results “His demise is deeply regretted, and the Command extends its heartfelt condolences to his family, loved ones, colleagues, and associates during this difficult period.” According to him, further details regarding funeral arrangements will be communicated as appropriate. “May God grant his soul eternal rest and give his family, the Corps, and all those affected by his passing the strength to bear this irreparable loss,” he said.

title: Zelensky: Russia Hit Energy Grid 76 Times Since Ceasefire Call
body:
Russian forces have carried out 76 targeted strikes against Ukraine’s power grid and oil-and-gas infrastructure since US President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” one week ago, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Oct. 18.
In a public address reviewing weekly and overnight Russian aerial bombardments, Zelensky reported that Moscow has systematically expanded attacks on civil life-support networks rather than de-escalating, demonstrating that economic concessions and sanctions relief fail to curb the Kremlin’s war effort.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Since the American president announced an energy ceasefire a week ago , Russia has deliberately struck Ukrainian energy and the oil and gas sector 76 times,” Zelensky stated.
Zelensky confirmed that overnight into Sunday, Russian strikes hit electrical substations across the Odesa, Khmelnytskyi, Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr regions, cutting electricity to tens of thousands of households.
“Tens of thousands of families remain without power. Power engineers and repair crews are working virtually around the clock on restoration,” Zelensky said.
Alongside utility targets, Russian munitions engaged residential neighborhoods and commercial enterprises across several provinces overnight and early Sunday morning, killing two people and injuring 12 others, including two children.
“At night, the Russians also struck residential buildings in our regions. As of now, 12 people are known to be injured, including two children. Two people were killed,” Zelensky stated, extending condolences to the victims’ families.
On Sunday morning, a separate Russian strike targeted an agricultural enterprise in the western Volyn region, prompting local emergency services and civil defense personnel to deploy to the scene to assess damage.
Detailing the scale of Russian aerial operations over the preceding seven days, Zelensky reported that Russian forces deployed nearly 2,700 strike drones , 1,700 guided aerial bombs (KABs), and 66 missiles against Ukrainian territory, with the majority of missile systems consisting of high-speed ballistic weapons.
“In total over the past week, the Russians launched nearly 2,700 strike drones, 1,700 aerial bombs, and 66 missiles against Ukraine, the majority of which were ballistic,” Zelensky stated. “The main targets of these strikes are specifically energy; the Russians are trying to create a blackout.”
The president addressed policymakers in Washington directly, asserting that Moscow treats diplomatic accommodations – such as the White House’s executive waiver of statutory sanctions under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 and the bilateral commercial diesel agreement—not as incentives for peace, but as validation that its military strategy is yielding economic rewards.
“America must see that Russia is not making reciprocal steps in response to the lifting of sanctions or agreements,” Zelensky emphasized. “On the contrary, they perceive every signal of an opportunity to earn revenue as proof that their bet on war is working and that they can continue fighting.”
Zelensky reiterated that the war persists due to the Kremlin’s uncompromising posture rather than Ukraine’s legitimate defense of its sovereign territory, urging allied nations to increase economic and military deterrence.
“It is precisely because of this position of Russia that the war continues, and not because Ukraine is righteously defending itself,” Zelensky said. “It is precisely Russia that must be pressured so that peace has a chance.”
The presidential address follows a week of mounting diplomatic tension between Kyiv and Washington over the administration’s foreign policy approach toward Moscow.
On Oct. 11, Trump announced an immediate bilateral “energy ceasefire” on Truth Social, asserting that both Russia and Ukraine had agreed to suspend strikes against energy installations. However, operational mechanisms were never formalized, and Russian forces sustained heavy standoff bombardments against Ukrainian utility networks throughout the week.
The friction deepened after Trump signed an executive order on Friday, Oct. 16, invoking Section 115 of the Graham Act to waive mandatory 500 percent tariffs on Russian imports and 100 percent duties targeting global purchasers of Russian energy, just 48 hours before their statutory implementation date.
On Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterized the executive waiver as a 60-day pause to analyze the global and domestic economic fallout of tariffs and secondary sanctions, citing foreign partner dependencies such as India’s reliance on Russian crude.
Rubio also defended a separate bilateral commercial pact allowing Moscow to deliver refined Russian diesel onto global markets to mitigate fuel price inflation exacerbated by armed conflict in the Middle East .
White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers concurrently argued that enforcing statutory Graham Act sanctions at this juncture would impede American diplomatic efforts to broker a durable peace settlement, asserting that keeping the measures in reserve provides executive negotiating leverage.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Presidential aide: A prosperous nation can’t be built in 3 years
body: Tope Fasua, Special Adviser to the President on Economic Affairs, (Vice President’s Office), has said a prosperous nation cannot be built within three or four years. Speaking with NAN on the sidelines of the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Thailand, Fasua said Nigerians will begin to feel greater benefits of ongoing economic reforms as it consolidates recent gains in inflation, foreign reserves, economic growth and investment. Nigeria’s investment engagements in Thailand showcased 65 transactions and secured more than six billion dollars in private capital commitments. Fasua said the government was determined to sustain the reforms while introducing social protection measures to cushion the effects of economic hardship on vulnerable citizens. Nigerian courts must stop becoming ‘market stalls’ – Retired Justice Augie JUST IN: Ogun FRSC Commander is dead He said Nigeria’s inflation rate had declined to about 14.63 per cent in September. “I am optimistic that the downward trend will continue towards the 10 per cent range in the coming months, barring unforeseen circumstances. Positive economic indicators have improved Nigeria’s standing with the international investment community.” “What we have seen here is a very good reception towards Nigeria because they see that the macro-economy is doing extremely well,” he said. Fasua listed declining inflation, easing interest rates, improved foreign reserves and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth among the indicators suggesting that the economy was moving in the right direction. He also cited developments in the capital market, noting that the market had attracted investments estimated at N133 trillion, equivalent to about 100 billion dollars. Fasua, however, acknowledged concerns that improvements in macroeconomic indicators were yet to translate into corresponding relief for many households. “The micro-economy can only stand on the macro-economy. If you do not fix the macro, you can not do anything with the micro,” he said. He likened economic reforms to laying a solid foundation for a building, adding that sustainable improvements in household welfare required a stable macroeconomic environment. “President Bola Tinubu has indicated that the period of economic sacrifice is approaching its end, with the government now focusing on consolidating the gains of the reforms,” Fasua said. He acknowledged that rising fuel prices continued to exert pressure on households and businesses, but maintained that several sectors were recording positive developments. He listed real estate, oil and gas, entertainment and electronic commerce among sectors showing encouraging performance. Fasua said the government would resist any move to reverse the reforms, describing the current period as an inappropriate time to abandon the policies. On measures to address hardship, Fasua said the Federal Government was developing a social protection package targeting the most vulnerable members of society. He said that the initiative would prioritise people who were elderly, children and persons living with conditions that limited their ability to support themselves. “We are not very much a big fan of just collecting money and giving people money. It is better to teach people how to fish than to just give them fish,” he said. He, however, said that direct cash assistance remained necessary for vulnerable citizens who required immediate support. Fasua said the government was working on documentation to enable it to identify eligible beneficiaries and provide assistance directly to them. Fasua also urged the media to play a constructive role in communicating economic developments, noting that accurate information and public awareness are critical to national development. “Building a prosperous country requires sustained effort, cooperation and patience. Meaningful development can not be achieved within two, three or four years. We have only one country, and we all have to come together. Development is not a walk in the park,” he said. (NAN)

title: Assisi Girls SHS launches 70th anniversary as Joyce Bawah Mogtari, stakeholders champion girl-child education
body: Hundreds of alumnae, traditional authorities, educators, and students converged on the campus of St. Francis of Assisi Girls’ Senior High School in Jirapa on Saturday, October 17, to mark the institution’s 67th birthday, launch its upcoming 70th anniversary celebrations, and hold its annual Speech and Prize Giving Day. The Franciscan Old Girls Association (FOGA) homecoming drew old students from across Ghana and Nigeria, celebrating decades of educational excellence while spotlighting urgent infrastructural bottlenecks facing the Catholic girls’ institution. The multi-event celebration, held under the theme “67 Years of Nurturing Leaders and Inspiring Excellence: Time to Retrace Our Steps”, served as both a celebration of institutional milestones and an appeal to address systemic overcrowding, teacher shortages, and resource deficits. Delivering the keynote address as Special Guest of Honour, Special Aide and Presidential Adviser to the President of Ghana, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, urged students to recognise the immense potential of girls’ education and draw inspiration from groundbreaking women in leadership. Reflecting on her own time as a student on the Jirapa campus, Mogtari recounted how transferring to the school helped rebuild her academic path and formed the bedrock of her legal and political career. “I return to this great school not merely as your Special Guest of Honour, but as a proud daughter of this institution. I mean, who would have imagined all those years ago that one day, I, Joyce Bawah, would return here as a senior lawyer with expertise in maritime law, founder of a law firm, an entrepreneur, and Senior Presidential Adviser and Special Aide to the President of the Republic of Ghana?” she said. Mogtari conveyed warm felicitations from President John Dramani Mahama, emphasising his administration’s commitment to advancing educational access for young women. Pointing to national and global strides in female representation, she cited Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang as living proof that glass ceilings can be shattered. “For the first time since independence, and nearly 70 years after Ghana’s independence, we now have a female Vice President: Her Excellency Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang. Her story tells every girl in Ghana that no ambition is too great simply because she is female. If Ghana can have its first female Vice President, then surely, the curtain draws closer to us electing our first female President,” she stressed. Addressing the gathering on the state of the school, the Headmistress of St. Francis of Assisi Girls SHS, Anastasia Kaarawo, detailed the school’s academic achievements alongside severe infrastructural distress. Kaarawo highlighted that the institution, which began in September 1959 with just 12 girls and two teachers, has grown into a Category A institution with an active student population of 1,341. She reported an 88% overall pass rate in the 2025 WASSCE, with candidates currently awaiting the results of the 510 candidates who sat the 2026 examination. However, the headmistress lamented that exponential enrolment growth has overwhelmed existing facilities. “If you go to the dormitories, it is overcrowded. Every available space, like the box rooms and laundries, has been converted into dormitories. In the classrooms right now, the first years who are reporting do not have furniture to sit on. They are sitting on benches, and the benches are not even enough for them,” Kaarawo revealed. She listed critical shortfalls including deficits in toilet facilities, staff accommodation, science and home economics practical equipment, textbooks for the new curriculum, and teacher shortages in Chemistry, Physics, Biology, and Integrated Science. Kaarawo also shared a harrowing logistical challenge, recounting an incident where a school pickup conveying the body of a deceased security personnel caught fire in the Jirapa market square, forcing authorities to transfer the remains into an aboboyaa (motorized tricycle). She appealed to government, FOGA, and corporate bodies to assist in roofing and completing an ongoing chapel project, as well as providing logistical and classroom support. Reinforcing the school administration’s call, Former National President of FOGA, Fati Bodua Seidu—who delivered an address on behalf of current FOGA National President, Amina Abugdanpoka Kaguah—emphasized that alumnae affection for their alma mater must manifest in practical intervention. “All but one of our dormitories were built decades ago, but today accommodate almost three times the number of students they were originally intended to house. Some of our girls have had to sleep on the floor, on damaged or inadequate mattresses, and in spaces crowded between old bed frames. That should concern all of us here. And this is why FOGA has decided that our affection for this school cannot exist only in memories; it must translate into action,” Seidu stated. Seidu charged the students to complement the investments made by parents and teachers with personal discipline and academic rigor. “A new dormitory alone will not make you successful. A new classroom will not study for you. A comfortable bed cannot write your examinations. Confidence is not arrogance; ambition is not something for which a woman should apologize; excellence is not reserved for somebody else,” she told the student body. Chairing the event, the Paramount Chief of the Jirapa Traditional Area, Naa Dinaa Donglabong Ganaa III, commended the founding Franciscan Missionaries of Mary (FMM) and traditional ancestors for establishing the premier girls’ secondary school in northern Ghana. Naa Ganaa III challenged FOGA and development partners to evolve from sporadic reunion gatherings into an active institutional development network providing structured scholarships, internships, and mentorship. “Retracing our steps must not mean walking backwards. It means returning to our roots so that we can move forward with a clearer sense of purpose. FOGA must be more than a name, a membership list, or an organization that gathers only for anniversaries and homecomings. It must become a living network of opportunity,” the Paramount Chief stated. Awards were presented to outstanding students and staff across various disciplines, with the Managing Director of MyTURN Ltd and Lesken Enterprise presenting awards of tablets and, on behalf of the Dr. Kenneth Aneweneh Foundation, sponsored prizes for 15 students, cash rewards for awardees, and hosting a celebratory homecoming dinner.

title: Tensions over Headscarves, Israel Test Ankara-Baku Ties
body:
The normally close ties between Turkey and Azerbaijan have come under strain, fuelled by a dispute over Baku’s restrictions on the Islamic headscarf in schools and disagreements over Israel.
Public tensions have become evident in what has traditionally been a very close relationship between two nations which share a common language and whose bond is characterised by the slogan: One nation, two states.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Although the rhetoric has remained restrained at the top, senior officials have been more outspoken in their reactions.
On Monday, Oktay Saral, chief adviser to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, shed his normal diplomatic reserve to denounce as “unacceptable” Azerbaijan’s move to change school uniform regulations, banning anything that conflicts with the normal uniform or the secular principles of education.
“Wearing a headscarf ... is a requirement of faith!” he wrote on X.
“We expect Azerbaijan to reverse this mistake as soon as possible.”
The following day, the ruling Yeni Azerbaijan Party (YAP) hit back with a sharply worded statement denouncing Saral and MPs from Erdogan’s AKP for their “populist and irresponsible statements”.
“The recent disinformation campaign targeting Azerbaijan has become increasingly aggressive, systematic, and openly slanderous,” it said.
The confrontation reflected sharp differences between Azerbaijan -- one of the most secular states in the Muslim world -- and the Islamo-conservative leadership in Ankara.
But it also highlighted tensions over the growing rapprochement between Azerbaijan and Israel since Baku’s 2020 Karabakh war with arch-foe Armenia, when the Israelis supplied them with drones and other weaponry.
Turkey’s ties with Israel, by contrast, could hardly be worse, with Erdogan accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza and Ankara regularly releasing images of top-level talks with the leaders of Hamas, the Palestinian Islamist movement whose October 2023 attacks on Israel sparked its war in Gaza.
Turkey’s pro-government media has held little back, with the Yeni Safak daily denouncing the headscarf regulations as a gesture towards Israel.
“We firmly reject attempts to deliberately distort Azerbaijani-Israeli relations, portray these ties as supposedly exceptional, and use this as a basis for making political accusations against Azerbaijan,” the country’s ruling party said.
The sharp response underscores Azerbaijan’s emergence as a regional middle power.
It is more willing to push back against Turkey as Ankara seeks to project influence from the Black Sea, increasingly ensnared by the Russia-Ukraine war, and an ever-more volatile Middle East.
“The changing geopolitical order in the greater Eurasia has enabled Azerbaijan to pursue a more pragmatic foreign policy,” said Fuad Shahbazov, an independent political analyst, indicating that meant Baku now “categorically resists the attempts of external actors, even its ally Turkey.”
But on Friday, Kursad Zorlu, deputy head of Erdogan’s AKP, said the two sides knew how to tackle problems “within the family” in what appeared to be a tacit call for online restraint.
At a regional summit in Baku on Thursday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hailed “the unshakable bond ... between our leaders” despite being tested “in very difficult times”.
Observers agree the two nations share too much to risk a rupture.
“The sometimes-tense relations with Moscow and the Iran war happening next door mean that Baku cannot afford to alienate an otherwise good partner,” Ivan Klyszcz of the Estonia-based International Centre for Defence and Security (ICDS) told AFP.
“Moreover, energy cooperation, ongoing well before the current spat, is too important for both parties,” he stressed.
“For Turkey, Azerbaijan is an essential gate for Central Asia, a region ... seen by Ankara as strategic.”
Paradoxically, Baku seems to hold the cards, despite the fact its population is ten times smaller than that of its ally.
“The litmus test of the Baku-Ankara axis will depend on the latter’s further attitude and commitment to quickly get back on diplomatic tracks to handle this crisis,” Shahbazov told AFP.
“Azerbaijan possesses energy leverage and access to the Central Asian region, giving it leverage over Turkey,” he said.
And this is a crucial asset, given Ankara’s ambition to maintain its role as a transit hub between Europe and Asia.
On Friday, Baku said it had issued an “international arrest warrant” for a Turkish journalist working for the Sanliurfa Olay daily. According to prosecutors, Celal Ciftci called for a “coup d’état” in Azerbaijan and promoted “religious extremism”.

title: Five Dead, 10 Rescued In Ibadan Tanker Crash
body: Five people have been killed and 10 others rescued after a tanker loaded with 45,000 litres of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) lost control and crashed into four vehicles along the Ojoo–Iwo Road Expressway in Ibadan, Oyo State. The accident occurred around Aduloju Bus Stop on Saturday, October 17, 2026. The Oyo State Fire Service said in a statement that it received a distress call about the incident at 11:42 am and immediately deployed a response team to the scene. According to the agency, the tanker, with registration number B14R316XB (Abuja), somersaulted and crashed into a Nissan Micra with registration number AGG669XK (Oyo), before colliding with three other vehicles whose registration numbers were yet to be identified. The fire service said five victims were recovered dead and handed over to police officers from the Kajorepo Divisional Police Headquarters, while 10 others were rescued alive. It added that its personnel sprayed the accident scene to prevent a fire outbreak, given the volume of fuel carried by the tanker. Preliminary investigations by the agency indicated that brake failure caused the accident. Officials of the Oyo State Fire Service, the Oyo State Road Traffic Management Authority (OYRTMA) and the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) were at the scene to support the emergency response. The OYRTMA team was led by its General Manager, Ayoade Adeoye, while the FRSC team was led by DRS S. Boladale of the Moniya Unit Command. The post Five Dead, 10 Rescued In Ibadan Tanker Crash appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Sweden conducts first Patriot live firing in Crete ahead of planned mission to protect NATO’s Ukraine aid hub in Poland
body: The Air Defense Regiment, Lv 6, carried out the firing on Wednesday during Exercise Spartan Arrow. The exercise tested the unit’s ability to move, deploy and engage a target alongside allied forces. “Today, together with our allies, we have tested and demonstrated a complete operational capability, from moving and deploying our resources to conducting a live engagement,” said Swedish Air Force Chief Maj. Gen. Jonas Wikman. “It is an important milestone for Swedish air defense and a concrete example of how we are strengthening our shared capability within NATO.” More than 100 Swedish personnel are participating in Spartan Arrow at the NATO Missile Firing Installation. Sweden is attending the annual German air-defense exercise for the first time. The training runs for several weeks and includes complex combat scenarios under realistic conditions. Sweden operates Patriot under the national designation Luftvärnssystem 103. “By exercising with allies, we verify our interoperability and ability to operate in an integrated manner within NATO,” said Col. Sofia Westermark, commander of the Air Defense Regiment. “Swedish air-defense units are ready to take an active role in the defense of NATO.” The Swedish government announced its intention to deploy the Patriot unit on October 6. The force will operate under NATO Air Command, protecting the Polish hub used to move support into Ukraine. Sweden is also contributing Gripen fighters from October to NATO’s Integrated Air and Missile Defense and the protection of the hub. The government said this was the second Swedish fighter contribution to NATO’s operation protecting the site. “For the second time, Sweden is participating with Gripen fighter jets in support of NATO’s operation to protect NATO’s logistics hub in Poland,” said Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. “Sweden will also, starting December, provide the Patriot air defence system.” The government cited repeated violations of allied airspace and Russian attempts to disrupt support for Ukraine as reasons for the contribution. It said the deployment would also strengthen NATO’s deterrence and defense. “In light of Russia’s recent attempts to undermine our support to Ukraine, I cannot overstate the importance of the Swedish contribution,” said Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard. “The purpose behind the Swedish contribution is to ensure that military and civilian support reaches Ukraine.” Westermark described the Crete firing as confirmation that Sweden’s expanding air-defense capability was working in practice. She credited the regiment’s personnel with delivering that progress. “Swedish air defense is undergoing rapid expansion in a number of areas, and we have never been more at the forefront than we are today,” she said. “Today’s live firing is confirmation that the rapid growth in capability is working, and it is doing so thanks to the personnel’s expertise and commitment.”

title: Russian attack sets warehouse building on fire, damages homes in Lviv region
body:
According to Ukrinform, Maksym Kozytskyi, head of the Lviv Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram .
"At around 11:20, our air defense shot down an enemy drone over Malekhiv. A logistics complex was damaged. A warehouse building is on fire," Kozytskyi said.
According to him, firefighters and other emergency services are working at the scene.
"According to updated information, at around 10:30, debris from an enemy drone damaged two residential buildings in Murovane," Kozytskyi added.
No casualties have been reported so far.
Later, Kozytskyi reported that rescuers had extinguished the fire in a warehouse building at a logistics center in Malekhiv, Lviv region.
"The fire in the warehouse building at the logistics complex in Malekhiv has been extinguished. I thank our firefighters for their prompt response," Kozytskyi said.

title: ECOWAS, AES agree to build cooperation framework at Dakar meeting, after 2025 split
body: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) have agreed on ground rules for life after the split. At a foundational meeting of Ministers in Dakar, Senegal, the two blocs resolved to build a cooperation framework to govern diplomatic relations, economic ties, development and other mutual priority areas. Thematic working groups will now hold technical consultations, with expert advice shaping the final framework. Both sides say the interests of their citizens should remain paramount. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, all under military-led governments, announced their withdrawal from ECOWAS in January 2024, accusing the bloc of being influenced by foreign powers and failing to support their fight against terrorism. The three had already formed the AES confederation. Their exit took effect in January 2025, leaving ECOWAS without three of its fifteen members and raising questions over trade, free movement and regional security. Following the split, ECOWAS shifted its strategy from forcing the AES to return to the bloc to finding practical ways to coexist and to protect travel, trade and security for millions of citizens. The Dakar dialogue led by ECOWAS Council of Ministers chair, Sheikh Niang, and the AES steering committee chair, Karamoko Jean-Marie Traore, marked the first time both sides sat formally since the January 2025 split. The agreement or framework aims to largely preserve visa-free movement and the flow of goods.

title: Petros Kousoulos Claims Giorgos Mazonakis Died Poor After Inner Circle Took His Money
body: Petros Kousoulos has sparked fresh debate after claiming that popular Greek singer Giorgos Mazonakis died poor, with people in his close circle allegedly benefiting from his earnings. What Kousoulos Said About Mazonakis’s Money Responding on X to a user who asked what happened to the money Mazonakis earned during his successful career, Kousoulos wrote: “His ‘mates’ and the good environment that surrounded him were eating it.” The comment followed earlier remarks on his television programme in which he stated that Mazonakis had died poor and that a businessman had paid for the heating oil at his home. Circumstances of Giorgos Mazonakis’s Death Giorgos Mazonakis died on 9 September 2026 after suffering a cardiac arrest during a visit to a private clinic in Kolonaki. His death was confirmed at Elpis Hospital. The circumstances of the incident were investigated. Family Dispute and Inheritance Questions The singer’s financial situation had already been in the public eye. Since 2024 he had been involved in a dispute with his sister, Vaso Mazonaki, over company activities and property, including a home in Mykonos. Reports after his death indicated that no will was found. This has intensified questions about the true size of his estate and how any remaining assets should be handled. Kousoulos’s statements direct attention toward individuals who were close to the artist. These remain allegations and have not been supported by evidence in the original post. title: SERAP Sues INEC Over ₦126.46bn Electoral Funds
body: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has sued the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over its failure to account for more than ₦126.46 billion appropriated for electoral operations and allegedly diverted, lost, mismanaged or otherwise unaccounted for. The funds were earmarked for the procurement of ballot boxes, electoral devices and materials, sensitive materials, result sheets, vehicles and accreditation devices, as well as audit and consultancy services, digital archiving and other goods and services required for the conduct and administration of elections. According to SERAP, the allegations are contained in the 2023 audited report of the Auditor-General of the Federation, published on August 7, 2026. The findings cover transactions between January and December 2022 and, in some cases, extend to December 31, 2023. In the suit, numbered FHC/ABJ/CS/2507/2026 and filed last week at the Federal High Court in Abuja, SERAP is seeking an order of mandamus compelling INEC to disclose detailed information on the expenditure, utilisation and disbursement of the funds. The organisation is also asking the court to compel the commission to provide a full financial and documentary account of the money, including the amounts released and paid, the beneficiaries of payments, the contractors involved and their beneficial owners. “Electoral resources are public resources. INEC must be able to account for every naira, demonstrate that it was lawfully spent and show that it served the purposes for which it was appropriated,” SERAP argued. The organisation said the allegations were particularly concerning given INEC’s constitutional responsibility and the fact that the funds were meant to support the administration of Nigeria’s electoral system. “With the 2027 general elections approaching, transparency and accountability in the management of these funds are essential to safeguarding public confidence in the electoral process and ensuring that resources intended to support credible elections are properly utilised,” it said. SERAP further argued that the Auditor-General’s findings suggested possible violations of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, national anti-corruption laws and Nigeria’s obligations under the United Nations Convention against Corruption. In the suit filed on behalf of the organisation by its lawyers, Kolawole Oluwadare, Kehinde Oyewumi and Andrew Nwankwo, SERAP said citizens were entitled to know how funds entrusted to INEC for the conduct of elections had been spent. “Democracy requires an informed citizenry. That principle is directly relevant to public expenditure by an electoral management body: citizens are entitled to know how resources entrusted to INEC for the conduct of elections have been used,” the suit stated. Citing the Auditor-General’s report, SERAP said INEC “irregularly paid” more than ₦112 billion (₦112,155,597,845) for ballot boxes, electoral devices, items and materials without competitive bidding or a Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) Certificate of No Objection. According to the organisation, the Auditor-General found no evidence that the items had been procured and raised concerns that the contracts were awarded to companies whose competence, experience, capacity, addresses and factory locations were unknown. The report also raised the possibility that the money had been diverted and recommended its recovery, SERAP said. The organisation further cited an alleged payment of more than ₦1.05 billion (₦1,058,925,000) for Toyota Prado TXL 2021-model vehicles without advertisement, competitive bidding, bid evaluation or a BPP Certificate of No Objection. The Auditor-General reportedly expressed concern that the funds might have been lost and the contracts inflated. SERAP also said INEC paid more than ₦3.13 billion (₦3,136,806,050) to four contractors for ballot guides, sensitive materials and result sheets before the contracts were awarded, with no evidence of payment. The Auditor-General reportedly raised concerns that the money might have been diverted and called for its recovery and remittance to the treasury. Another finding involved more than ₦9.24 billion (₦9,245,965,502.60) paid for 22 contracts covering similar goods and services. According to SERAP, the contracts were split to circumvent procurement procedures and awarded on the same day. The Auditor-General reportedly warned that the money might have been lost and that payments could have been made for items not supplied. The suit also cited payments of more than ₦129 million (₦129,375,000) to 19 accounting firms for financial audit services without evidence of utilisation, requests or expenditure by the consultants. SERAP said the Auditor-General raised concerns that the money might have been diverted and recommended its recovery and remittance to the treasury. On accreditation devices, the organisation cited a payment of more than ₦504 million (₦504,492,641) allegedly made without due procurement procedures. It said the Auditor-General noted that the APG had expired before the security licence key was delivered and that the software was valid for only four months, raising questions about economy and value for money. The report also flagged more than ₦235 million (₦235,103,000) allegedly paid to unqualified contractors for sleeping mats and digital archiving. According to SERAP, the Auditor-General questioned the contractors’ eligibility and capacity and raised concerns that the funds might have been lost. SERAP is asking the court to compel INEC to provide documentary and physical evidence that the more than ₦112 billion identified as irregularly paid was used to procure the relevant electoral materials, and to account for the materials’ current location and status. The organisation is also seeking an order preventing the disposal, transfer, destruction, write-off or other handling of electoral equipment, materials and public assets covered by the Auditor-General’s findings in a manner that could frustrate transparency and accountability. It wants the names of contractors, companies, suppliers and consultants who allegedly received the funds irregularly, as well as INEC officials and other public officials who authorised, processed or facilitated the transactions or benefited from them, to be made public. SERAP said Nigerians were entitled to know whether the contracted goods and services were supplied, whether payments corresponded with deliveries and whether contracts were deliberately split to circumvent procurement requirements. The organisation cited Section 15(5) of the Constitution, which requires the state to abolish corrupt practices and abuse of power, and Section 13, which places a responsibility on public institutions to observe and apply the provisions of Chapter Two of the Constitution. It also relied on Nigeria’s obligations under the UN Convention against Corruption, which requires preventive anti-corruption policies and transparent public procurement and financial management. SERAP further cited Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, which protect citizens’ rights to participate in public affairs. The post SERAP Sues INEC Over ₦126.46bn Electoral Funds appeared first on Channels Television .

title: How Often Do Car Parts Need to Be Replaced?
body:
How often do car parts need to be replaced depends on the type of component, mileage, vehicle age, driving conditions, and manufacturer recommendations.
There is no single interval for every part. Brake pads may be replaced according to wear, while timing belts usually follow a specific mileage or time interval.
Owners searching for kia spare parts sharjah , hyundai spare parts sharjah , or infiniti spare parts sharjah should match parts with the exact model, engine specification, and manufacturer requirements. Al-Miyar offers replacement parts matched to different vehicle specifications.
How Often Do Car Parts Need to Be Replaced?
Every component experiences different stress. Some parts wear through friction, while others deteriorate because of heat, vibration, contamination, or age. As a result, car parts replacement intervals vary significantly.
Driving conditions also affect car parts replacement schedule. Heavy traffic, short trips, dusty roads, extreme temperatures, towing, and heavy loads can increase wear.
This provides a more realistic way to determine how often to replace car parts.
Which Car Parts Usually Need More Attention?
Some components need regular inspection because they experience continuous wear or affect vehicle control. Understanding when to replace car parts is particularly important for brakes and tires.
Brake components directly affect stopping performance. Brake pads become thinner through friction, but their service life varies with driving habits, traffic, vehicle weight, road conditions, and brake-system design.
Brake rotors may also require replacement when excessively worn, damaged, or below the manufacturer's specified thickness. Inspection is more useful than relying only on mileage. Tires Tire replacement cannot be determined by mileage alone. Tread depth, uneven wear, cracks, age, damage, and handling changes can indicate that a tire needs attention. Incorrect pressure and poor wheel alignment can accelerate uneven wear. Regular inspection helps maintain traction and handling. Engine Oil and Filters Engine oil becomes contaminated and may lose protective properties. Oil-change intervals depend on the vehicle, engine, oil specification, driving conditions, and manufacturer recommendations. Oil filters are commonly replaced during an oil service. Al-Miyar offers parts for different vehicle models. Parts With Longer but More Important Replacement Intervals Some components remain in service longer, but their specified intervals are important. Timing Belts
A timing belt synchronizes important engine components and may fail without an obvious warning. Replacement is generally based on the manufacturer's mileage or time interval. On some engines, failure can cause significant engine damage. The car parts replacement schedule should account for both mileage and age when specified. Batteries A battery gradually loses its ability to hold a charge. Climate, driving patterns, electrical demand, battery type, and vehicle usage affect its useful life. Slow cranking, dimming electrical systems, or starting difficulties may indicate that testing is needed. Unlike a timing belt, a battery does not have one universal replacement point. Spark Plugs Spark plugs are essential to petrol-engine combustion, but service intervals vary by engine and plug type. Worn plugs can contribute to rough running, difficult starting, reduced fuel efficiency, or misfires. The vehicle-specific maintenance schedule is more reliable than a generic mileage figure.
How Driving Conditions Change Replacement Timing Two vehicles with identical mileage can have different maintenance requirements. A vehicle driven on open roads may experience different wear from one driven the same distance in congested traffic. Severe conditions include: 1. Frequent short journeys 2. Heavy stop-and-go traffic 3. Extreme temperatures 4. Dusty or poorly surfaced roads 5. Heavy towing or loads 6. Long periods of inactivity Therefore, how often to replace car parts should be considered alongside actual vehicle use. Urban braking can increase brake wear, while dusty roads may require more frequent air-filter inspections. A Practical Replacement Schedule There is no universal schedule, but this framework identifies key items to monitor.
This table is a general framework, not a substitute for the maintenance schedule for a specific vehicle. When Should You Replace a Part Before It Fails? Waiting for complete failure is not always appropriate, particularly for braking, steering, suspension, tires, and engine timing components. The useful question is whether the part still operates within its required limits. Replacing a brake pad at its specified wear limit is different from waiting until all friction material disappears. Similarly, replacing a timing belt at its scheduled interval is different from waiting for failure. Understanding how often should car parts be replaced can help address wear before it becomes a larger mechanical problem. The Maintenance Schedule Is a Starting Point, Not the Whole Story A manufacturer's schedule provides a baseline for a specific vehicle and powertrain, but actual component condition also matters. Drivers should notice unusual sounds, vibrations, warning lights, fluid leaks, braking changes, starting difficulties, or handling changes. Regular inspections can identify developing problems before they result in expensive repairs. A vehicle-specific maintenance plan is the clearest reference for "how often do car parts need to be replaced", while inspections help account for actual wear and changing driving conditions. Maintenance records are also useful for tracking time- and mileage-based services. For owners asking how often do car parts need to be replaced, the most reliable approach combines manufacturer recommendations, mileage and age, and the actual condition of each component. Not sure whether a part is due for replacement or simply needs inspection? Start with the vehicle's maintenance schedule, then have the component's actual condition checked before deciding to replace it. Conclusion There is no universal answer to how often do car parts need to be replaced because components have different service requirements. Brake pads and tires depend heavily on wear and driving conditions, while timing belts and spark plugs generally follow vehicle-specific intervals. The practical approach is to combine the manufacturer's schedule with regular inspections and attention to warning signs. This helps owners address worn components before complete failure.

title: Low pressure system may affect Oman from Wednesday
body:
MUSCAT: Satellite imagery and weather analyses of the National Multi-Hazard Early Warning Centre (NMHEWC) have shown the presence of a tropical depression presently located southwest of the Arabian Sea at 59.0°E longitude and 7.7°N latitude. Wind speed around the centre of the weather system is estimated at 17-27 knots (31-50 km/h). The NMHEWC forecast indicates that the tropical depression will move westward and northwestward towards the Horn of Africa with no direct impacts on the Sultanate of Oman over the next five days. However, there is a chance of high and medium-level cloud formation which may lead to scattered rainfall over parts of the Dhofar and Al Wusta governorates starting Wednesday. The NMHEWC is closely monitoring the weather condition around the clock. The Civil Aviation Authority urges the public to follow its weather bulletins and reports. — ONA

title: Ukraine Drone Attack Kills One, Sets Two Russian Oil Refineries Ablaze
body: A “massive” Ukrainian drone attack overnight killed one person, wounded five others and set two oil refineries ablaze in the Russian city of Saint Petersburg, its governor said Sunday. “One person was killed and five others hurt and hospitalised following a massive attack carried out by Ukrainian Nazi military drones,” governor Alexandre Beglov said. He added firefighters were battling blazes at the Saint Petersburg oil terminal site, also hit in June, the Ruchi oil depot and industrial warehouses in the Kolpino district south of the city. Beglov added several residential buildings had been hit, as well as two houses. “Air defence systems are in operation,” he wrote on Telegram. Smoke rises above the city following an air attack on the oil terminal in Saint Petersburg on October 18, 2026, amid the ongoing Russian-Ukrainian conflict. (Photo by AFP) City authorities said the attack also disrupted flights at Saint Petersburg’s main airport, one of the country’s busiest, which was restricting operations “for safety reasons”, Beglov said. The strikes came after Ukraine’s leader Volodymyr Zelensky said this week Kyiv would resume hitting Russian refineries, after an “energy ceasefire” announced by US President Donald Trump failed to materialise. Zelensky insisted he was standing up for his war-torn country in the face of unrelenting Russian attacks, including on energy infrastructure, as support from the United States slumped. The governor of the Leningrad region surrounding Saint Petersburg, Alexander Drozdenko, said 145 drones had been shot down and said around 20,000 people were without electricity following the drone raid. “A large-scale UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) attack continues to be repelled,” Drozdenko wrote on Telegram. A police car is parked in front of a burning oil terminal following an air attack in Saint Petersburg on October 18, 2026, amid the ongoing Russian-Ukrainian conflict. (Photo by AFP) Saint Petersburg and the surrounding region are home to major oil infrastructure. Ukraine has specifically targeted the sector over recent months in retaliation for Russian bombings. TASS news agency said the attack was the largest on the region since the start of the war in February 2022. A June 6 attack saw 144 drones shot down, according to officials. Russia’s defence ministry said overall 1,015 Ukrainian drones were neutralised Saturday night in around 15 regions in Russia’s south and west, including the capital, Moscow. The Russian VK social network said the attack targeted one of its data centres in the region but that the site was working as normal. Trump, who has repeatedly criticised Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and oil depots, signed an executive order on Friday to waive sanctions and tariffs targeting Moscow’s energy revenues. The move, which came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine in the fifth year of its war, drew criticism in both Europe and the United States. title: Iran prepared devastating plan for any new military adventure
body:

title: Anthropic consults law firms to set fair negotiation norms before AI agents start cutting deals
body:
Anthropic is figuring out how AI agents could negotiate on behalf of users. According to the Financial Times , the company is consulting with law firms to develop fair negotiation norms for AI agents that would haggle over prices, resolve complaints, or improve contract offers. Anthropic has already shown in experiments that stronger models negotiate better deals, which could widen societal inequality.
This isn't new territory. Anthropic is already hiring Conceptual Reasoning Fellows , specifically lawyers. The fellows will spend four months testing Claude on judgment-heavy questions in law, philosophy, cognitive science, economics, and political science for $100,000 to $167,000.
The push traces back to a data problem. In math and code, improving AI models is relatively easy because verifiable data is plentiful or easy to generate. In the humanities, that data doesn't exist, partly because right and wrong answers are rarely clear-cut. Anthropic needs experts who can build test cases and evaluations to make Claude stronger in these areas. Justin Curl , a member of technical staff researching law, institutions, and AI at Anthropic, argues that in law it's "notoriously hard to define quality." Ad Ad

title: Three men jailed for 158 years each for murdering Australian and US surfers in Mexico
body: A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each. The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial. The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico. The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers’ mother, told the courtroom that her sons’ murders had taken “the future we had imagined with them”. The convicted killers’ full names were not given for legal reasons, meaning they were only identified as Jesús Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús. In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, Jesús Gerardo (alias “El Kekas”), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery. The court heard that the bodies of the victims were found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads. At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in the beach town of Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings. Ensenada has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico. The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers – all in their early 30s – had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time. Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them. Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

title: Trump Using 60-Day Pause to Review Russia Sanctions, Rubio Says
body:
US President Donald Trump will use a period of up to 60 days to evaluate the economic fallout of statutory sanctions against Russia and tariffs on nations purchasing Russian energy, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday, Oct. 17.
Speaking to reporters prior to departing for Uzbekistan, as reported by Reuters , Rubio characterized the administration’s executive waiver of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 as an analytical pause rather than a permanent abandonment of statutory penalties.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy,” Rubio said, emphasizing that the economic restrictions would affect numerous foreign partners beyond Russia itself.
Rubio specifically cited India , an important strategic partner of the US, observing that while New Delhi has diversified its energy sources, it remains substantially reliant on Russian crude oil imports.
The secretary of state noted that simultaneous geopolitical crises have intensified pressure on international energy markets, highlighting the compound effects of the armed conflict involving the US and Iran alongside recurring strikes by Yemen’s Houthi movement against Saudi Arabian infrastructure.
“These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they’re having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices” but on wider economies as well, Rubio explained.
Rubio also mounted a defense of the administration’s separate bilateral arrangement with Moscow to facilitate deliveries of refined Russian diesel fuel onto international markets.
“That diesel fuel was going to be sold one way or the other. The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get,” Rubio stated, arguing that the transaction aims to stabilize benchmark fuel prices that spiked following Middle Eastern shipping disruptions and refinery damage.
According to the secretary of state, pairing the commercial fuel agreement with the suspension of Graham Act penalties reflects the intricate diplomatic challenges of managing concurrent conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East .
The 60-day analytical timeframe outlined by Rubio provides operational context for the executive order signed by Trump on Friday, Oct. 16 , which waived mandatory trade duties and secondary sanctions just 48 hours before their statutory implementation date on Sunday, Oct. 18.
In issuing the suspension, the White House invoked Section 115 of the Graham Act, which authorizes presidential waivers upon submitting a certification to Congress affirming that such deferrals advance US national interests.
White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers defended the move , asserting that immediate enforcement of the statute would impede ongoing diplomatic efforts to broker a durable peace agreement between Ukraine and Russia.
Rogers stressed that the statute equips the president with negotiating leverage and noted that the executive branch retains authority to invoke the suspended measures at any point if national security dictates.
The waived statutory provisions represent some of the most stringent trade restrictions approved by Congress, including a mandatory 500 percent tariff on all Russian-origin imports alongside 100 percent duties targeting the five largest global purchasers of Russian crude oil and natural gas, such as China and India.
The law also mandates punitive trade actions against third countries facilitating petroleum sanctions evasion and secondary actions targeting Moscow’s maritime “shadow fleet.”
The administration’s decision to defer the penalties has provoked sharp criticism from Ukrainian officials and lawmakers in Washington.
President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the executive order on Saturday, characterizing the waiver alongside the commercial diesel agreement as a grave strategic miscalculation that directly benefits the Russian military.
Zelensky cautioned that offering unilateral economic accommodations to Moscow signals that attacks against Ukrainian civilian power networks will carry no economic consequence.
On Capitol Hill, where the Graham Act passed with overwhelming bipartisan support – including an 86–11 vote in the Senate – lawmakers across both parties criticized the postponement.
Republican Senator Thom Tillis called the executive order “more than irresponsible,” while Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Elizabeth Warren accused the White House of disregarding the statutory intent of Congress to offer unwarranted concessions to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
However, with both the House of Representatives and the Senate adjourned for the pre-election recess until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, congressional leaders remain procedurally constrained from advancing counter-legislation or joint resolutions of disapproval until post-election legislative sessions convene in Washington.

title: ‘Record’ 855 People Arrested Over Paris Protest Violence – Police
body: Police in Paris said Sunday they had arrested a “record” 855 people over protest violence in the capital the day before, with the prosecutor’s office saying more than 500 were being held in custody. The capital, and many other French cities, on Saturday experienced clashes between police and protesters, multiple street blazes and widespread looting. Paris’s deputy mayor Lamia El Aaraje said the capital had been hit by “a level of violence that I believe we had never seen before”. French gendarmes patrol by a broken frontage windows of a shop a day after riot and looting following a nationwide protest against the “high cost of living”, in Lyon central-eastern France on October 18, 2026. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP) The Paris prosecutor’s office said that, of those in custody, 346 were adults and 171 were minors, for a total of 517. It added that the numbers were provisional and could change. “Arrests took place throughout the night and up to 6:00 am (0400 GMT) this morning,” the office said. Most of the arrests were for receiving stolen goods, association with intent to commit violence, and vandalism, it said.
