title: Pope discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery
body: Pope Leo XIV has been discharged from Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. The 71-year-old walked unaided to his waiting car, stopping to speak to well-wishers. The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter’s Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery. On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff. A statement from his doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed “steady improvement” following his operation. The surgery on Tuesday, which lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope’s right lung. The results of further tests to check for any sign that the cancer has spread have not yet been announced. The Pope also spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, in their first call since June 2025. The Vatican said the call was to urge “dialogue and peace”. It came as Russia’s bombardment of cities across Ukraine intensifies, with a growing number of civilian casualties and no sign of Putin being ready to halt the invasion. The Pope also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshkiy, occupied by Russia and under constant shelling, to allow people to be evacuated and for the urgent delivery of food and medicine. The BBC recently reported on residents there being forced to eat garden weeds to survive. The Pope’s schedule has been cleared completely until 20 October, so his reappearance in public so soon is a surprise and will be some relief for Catholics around the world. Those close to the Pope said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America, planned for early November and which includes a visit to Peru, where he was a missionary for many years. It is not yet clear whether he might be fit to travel or require further treatment.

title: First C-130J delivered for conversion into US Navy's E-130J nuclear command aircraft
body:
Lockheed Martin has delivered the first C-130J-30 Super Hercules that will be converted into the US Navy's E-130J Phoenix II, a new airborne command-and-control aircraft for communications with the country's nuclear forces.
The aircraft was handed over at Lockheed Martin's facility in Marietta, Georgia, on October 15. It will now be transferred to Northrop Grumman, which is responsible for integrating the mission systems required for the Take Charge and Move Out (TACAMO) role.
The delivery means the aircraft is not yet an operational E-130J. Lockheed Martin has supplied the basic C-130J-30 airframe, which will receive communications equipment and other modifications before entering flight testing in its final configuration.
Northrop Grumman is the prime contractor for the E-130J program and leads an industry team that also includes Lockheed Martin, Collins Aerospace and Raytheon. The Navy initially ordered three aircraft for the engineering and manufacturing development phase.
The E-130J will replace the Boeing E-6B Mercury in the TACAMO mission, which provides an airborne communications link between US command authorities and nuclear forces, including ballistic-missile submarines.

Its introduction will also return TACAMO to the C-130 family after more than three decades. The Navy began the mission with modified Hercules aircraft in 1963 and later operated the EC-130Q before transferring the role to the E-6 in the early 1990s.
Unlike the E-6B, which also performs the Airborne Launch Control System mission associated with land-based intercontinental ballistic missiles, the E-130J program is focused on the Navy's TACAMO requirement.
The service selected the stretched C-130J-30 as the new platform after deciding that a commercial-derived jet was not necessary for the mission. The four-engine turboprop provides the endurance and low-speed characteristics required to deploy the very-low-frequency trailing-wire antennas used to communicate with submerged submarines.
The Navy formally announced Phoenix II as the E-130J's popular name in August 2025. The designation refers to the return of TACAMO to a Hercules-based aircraft after the E-6 era.
Air Data News reported earlier this year that Lockheed Martin had also been selected to provide training systems for the E-130J program, including devices for pilots and maintenance personnel.
The Navy currently operates 16 E-6B Mercury aircraft, based on the Boeing 707 airframe. The type entered service in 1989, initially as the E-6A, and was subsequently upgraded to the E-6B configuration.
The first delivered C-130J-30 will now enter mission-system integration before the E-130J begins its flight-test program.

title: Health workers’ strike disrupts hospital services in Katsina
body:
An ongoing strike by health professionals in Katsina State has disrupted services at public hospitals, leaving patients and pltheir caregivers uncertain about access to medical treatment.
The health workers embarked on a one-week warning strike following disagreements with the state government over their welfare and remuneration.
A visit to Turai Yar’Adua Maternal and Child Hospital in Katsina on Saturday revealed the impact of the industrial action, with only a few patients seen around the surgical ward.
For many families, the dispute over workers’ remuneration has heightened concerns over the health and safety of loved ones requiring urgent medical attention.
One of the affected caregivers, Aina’u Abdulmajid, said her patient was suffering from complications arising from surgery and appealed to the state government to restore normal hospital services.
“For the sake of God, we call on the government to intervene. Our patient is suffering from complications arising from surgery. Please help us and restore services,” she pleaded.
Ms Abdulmajid’s appeal reflected the predicament of families who depend on public hospitals for treatment but have found themselves caught between an unresolved labour dispute and the urgent need for medical attention.
Another caregiver, Sulaiman Mansir, said he had brought his sick child to the hospital for treatment but was confronted with the disruptions caused by the strike.
Mr Mansir expressed concern over the uncertainty surrounding his child’s treatment and urged the government to engage the striking health workers to resolve the dispute without further delay.
The industrial action has compounded the difficulties faced by families already grappling with transportation costs, medicines and other medical expenses.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the strike was declared by the Assembly of Health Professionals following unresolved disagreements with the Katsina State government over workers’ remuneration and welfare.
The assembly comprises the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), the National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives (NANNM), and the National Union of Allied Health Professionals (NUAHP).
The assembly’s chairperson, Ibrahim Balange, said the unions issued a seven-day strike notice to the government on 7 October, but the notice expired without a satisfactory resolution of their demands.
Mr Balange explained that the dispute began in 2024, when the state government indicated plans to review the allowances of health professionals to align them with those of their counterparts in federal government service.
He said the workers subsequently raised concerns about the implementation of the minimum wage, alleging that the salary structure approved for them differed from what they were receiving.
According to him, a committee established to investigate the complaints submitted recommendations in March 2025, but the government had yet to implement them.
He said the Office of Public Service Reform later offered the workers 10 per cent of the salary difference between them and their counterparts in federal institutions.
However, the offer did not resolve the disagreement.
Following the commencement of the strike, the state government increased its offer to 15 per cent, but the unions rejected it, maintaining that it fell short of their demands.
The Head of the State Civil Service, Masa’ud Banye, confirmed that government officials had met with representatives of the striking workers to discuss the dispute.
Mr Banye expressed optimism that the disagreement would soon be resolved and acknowledged the difficulties patients were experiencing because of the industrial action.
He said Governor Dikko Radda’s administration remained committed to effective healthcare delivery in the state.

title: Bobrovsky, Maple Leafs looking to find traction
body:
TORONTO – Sergei Bobrovsky arrived in Toronto with a long and decorated resume.
A pair of Stanley Cup rings along with two Vezina Trophy nods as the NHL’s top goaltender sat right at the top.
Early on in his Maple Leafs’ tenure, however, the 38-year-old and his teammates are still looking for traction.
Bobrovsky’s record fell to 1-3-2 following Saturday’s 4-1 loss to the grinding New York Islanders.
The Russian puck-stopper wasn’t to blame on any of the three goals he allowed before the visitors added an empty-netter, but his save percentage now stands at .891 along with a 3.29 goals-against average.
“I feel good,” Bobrovsky, who signed a three-year, US$21-million contract in free agency, said of his start to the 2026-27 schedule. “There is a lot of chances, lots of work. I try to give the best chance for the team to win the game. It (doesn’t) always go your way, but chipping away.
“I stay patient and just ready for the next shot.”
Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews said the rest of the group hasn’t offered much support during a stretch that’s seen Toronto (3-4-2) drop four of its last five (1-2-2).
“We’ve really left him out to dry here in these last couple starts,” said the star centre. “We’ve got to be better. He’s doing his job. He’s making some big saves.”
Bobrovsky, who hoisted the Cup in both 2024 and 2025 with the Florida Panthers, said coming north has been an adjustment as part of a major summer roster renovation.
“Style is different,” he said after making 16 stops against the Islanders. “New guys, it’s a new team. We’re all working to get together to build the chemistry, to build the belief. We have a great group of guys — great skill guys, professional guys.
“We just have to find our game and have to come together and play on the same page.”
The Maple Leafs have also already been bitten by the injury bug.
Shutdown defenceman Chris Tanev, who was on the ice following Saturday’s morning skate, remains out week-to-week with an upper-body injury, while veteran centre John Tavares has the same return-to-play designation after suffering a lower-body injury in Thursday’s 5-4 shootout loss to the Buffalo Sabres.
“It’s tough, but this is the NHL,” said Toronto centre Colton Sissons, who scored his team’s only goal Saturday. “You lose players constantly — important players — and other guys gotta step up. Maybe not one guy needs to do the job. It needs to be a bunch of us collectively.”
He added that, despite the results, watching Bobrovsky go through his process has been impressive.
“Consummate professional,” Sissons said. “Not many guys in this league are as dialed in as he is with his routine and the way he takes care of himself. That’s why he’s been elite for so long.”
Bobrovsky, meanwhile, has now allowed three goals or more in each of his six starts.
“I stay patient and I prepare myself for the next shot,” Bobrovsky said. “You could think, ‘What if this, what if that?’ But it is what it is. I’m confident. I feel good about my game.
The Maple Leafs host the San Jose Sharks on Monday and the New York Rangers on Thursday before heading back out on the road.
“It’s extremely high,” Sissons said when asked about the sense of urgency. “You can’t take too much time here to sort things out — not in this league, not in our division. We’re fully are aware of that. Down some guys right now, we gotta all pick it up collectively.
No. 1 overall pick Gavin McKenna had four shots and created chances with the puck across 17 minutes 56 seconds of ice time after getting benched Thursday.
“I don’t think anything really shakes him,” Matthews said. “He’s got confidence in his game. He knows what he can do out there.”
McKenna was not made available to reporters post-game.
Toronto head coach Jim Hiller was at a loss to explain his team’s inability to get to the middle of the ice Saturday.
“It’s a good question,” he said. “We came out (for) the third period, we scored right away doing just exactly that, right? There was nothing fancy about the goal. I would give them credit. They played their game to a T. Their defenceman, I thought, did a really good job in the corners, squishing us and being tight and not allowing us to come out of the corner with the puck.
“There’s some of that, but just not good enough from us.”
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 18, 2026.

title: The argument for a woman UN Secretary-General
body:
By Simran Sodhi 

In its 80-year old history, the United Nations has never had a woman serve as Secretary-General. The calls for a woman to now helm the UN is increasing as António Guterres prepares to step down at the end of December 2026.

The tenth Secretary-General is set to take office on January 1, 2027. Several female diplomats and leaders are being looked at as potential candidates to become the UN's first woman chief. The calls for a woman to lead the UN is also being made since the exclusion of women in top positions of diplomacy also point to a glaring example of gender inequality. That too, at the helm of an international institution, that is designed to work on issues such as gender equality.

The process to elect the next Secretary-General is rather simple. The 15-member Security Council, including permanent veto powers Britain, China, France, Russia and the United States considers an undisclosed list behind closed doors and then recommends a candidate to be elected by the General Assembly (GA).For the sake of greater transparency, the General Assembly in 2015 asked its president and that of the Security Council to invite U.N. members to nominate candidates. It also called for regular circulation of candidates' names and CVs to member states.

This time around, seven serious contenders have emerged so far out of which four are women. Based on the UN’s informal regional rotation, the likelihood of a candidate from the Latin American and Caribbean region being selected is high.



The four women contenders are:

Rebeca Grynspan (Costa Rica): The current Secretary-General of UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) and former Vice President of Costa Rica has emerged as a leading contender, backed by strong showings in UN Security Council straw polls.

Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett (Guyana): Guyana's permanent representative to the UN and former foreign minister has regional backing from Caricom as an indigenous woman candidate from a developing nation.

Michelle Bachelet (Chile): The former President of Chile and former head of UN Women entered the race but officially withdrew on September 19, 2026. Though she was a strong contender for the job.

María Fernanda Espinosa (Ecuador): Former President of the UN General Assembly and former foreign minister of Ecuador has also been positioned as a prominent Latin American candidate.

The world today has changed a lot and one sees women in leadership positions across the spectrum. But it is also glaringly obvious that some top posts like the President of the United States have remained an all-male bastion. While former Vice President Kamala Harris and former First Lady Hillary Clinton tried to break this glass ceiling, it still seems a distant dream. Europe has seen more women leaders emerge, for instance, the Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. South Asia has given the world its fair share of women leaders like Indian PM Indira Gandhi and Pakistan PM Benazir Bhutto. Even in corporates, women leaders are increasingly finding their positions at the top whether one looks at Chanel which is today headed by a woman CEO Leena Nair, or PepsiCo which again was led by awoman Indra Nooyi.

Women hold roughly 30% of global managerial positions and 27% of board seats, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO). Studies have shown that higher rates of women representation in leadership are associated with a variety of benefits for organizations. Greater gender equity also contributes to wider economic benefits, increased productivity, and improved development results. This translates into the simple point that gender representation is beneficial for everyone, not just women.

Rebeca Grynspan, who has emerged as the frontrunner for the post of the next UN Chief, said that the United Nations has become too risk-averse and its next leader must be prepared to bear the cost of diplomatic failure and try again. She made these comments to a media outlet ahead of another Security Council poll on Oct 16 to gauge support for a new secretary-general to succeed Antonio Guterres.

Grynspan will become the first female secretary-general in the UN's history if she wins. She has already come out ahead in four out ​of five informal straw polls, obtaining ⁠nine votes in favor last week, according to diplomats close to the process.Securing the recommendation requires at least nine positive votes out of the 15 countries, and no "discourage" votes from the five permanent members: the US, China, Russia, France, and Britain.

But the game is hardly over. It is possible that even now, Grynspan might get a discourage vote from one of the P5 which would essentially end her race. But it is time the UN realised that the world looks upto it and a woman UN Chief would be a positive message that international bodies recognize the contribution of women to societies and to the work place. In a world reeling from wars and uncertainties, this would be welcome news.

title: Lions seek momentum for CFL’s West semifinal
body:
CALGARY – The B.C. Lions conclude their CFL regular season against the Winnipeg Blue Bombers, but their playoff path is set as host of the West Division semifinal.
B.C. fell 32-13 to the Calgary Stampeders on Saturday, but the Lions (10-7) had already clinched second in the West when the Edmonton Elks beat the Blue Bombers the previous evening.
So B.C.’s player management was at the forefront Saturday in Calgary.
Quarterback Nathan Rourke, the CFL’s Most Outstanding Player last season, was among the Lions whose load got lighter as the game progressed.
Rourke was taken out of the game after completing eight of 11 passes for 149 yards and a touchdown pass in the first half.
His backup Kaidon Salter was 6-for-14 for 113 yards and was intercepted once in the second half.
B.C.’s top two receivers, Keon Hatcher Sr. and Justin McInnis, both sat out snaps.
Lions head coach Buck Pierce was cagey about his plans for player deployment Friday against the Blue Bombers.
Salter sees Friday’s game against Winnipeg as a chance to showcase his talent, if given the opportunity to play.
“Once I’m in the game, it should look no different from when Rourke’s in the game,” said Salter.
With nothing at stake for B.C. against Winnipeg, Pierce still expects a complete effort from his team in order to carry momentum into the division semifinal Oct. 31 in Vancouver.
“We need to be playing better football down the stretch and that’s the message to the guys,” said Pierce.
The Lions beat the Blue Bombers in their lone meeting so far this season, which was a 35-19 victory July 30 in Winnipeg.
“You just want to go out there and play as a team and play to the best of your ability,” said Salter. “Just stay together, stick together, just keep on being one, being one brotherhood.”
Salter said his focus is on the final game of the regular season before he thinks about the playoffs.
The Lions have been the hottest team in the CFL after a 1-5 start. They’d won nine of 10 heading into Saturday’s game.
B.C. awaits their West semifinal opponent, which could be Winnipeg, Calgary or the Saskatchewan Roughriders.
The Lions will have the support of the Stampeders and their fans Friday versus Winnipeg because Calgary’s playoff fate relies on a Blue Bombers loss.
Stampeders coach and general manager Dave Dickenson hoped Pierce would play his starters against Winnipeg.
“I’ll be lobbying to say ‘hey, you don’t want to go into playoffs on a losing streak, a two-game losing streak,'” Dickenson said.
The Lions seek a playoff win at home and again Nov. 7 in the West final in Edmonton to reach their first Grey Cup game since 2011 when B.C. won it as the host team.
“There’s a lot to clean up and we’re just excited to get back to work,” Pierce said.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 18, 2026.

title: Take science and mathematics seriously to help drive national development – Students urged
body: The Abuakwa North Municipal Director of Education in the Eastern Region, Grace Adza-Wude, has urged students to take Science and Mathematics seriously to help address Ghana’s challenges and drive national development. She made the call when the Member of Parliament for Abuakwa North, Nana Ampaw Kwame Addo-Frempong, donated laptops and cash to three senior high schools for participating in the National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ). The beneficiary schools are Bright Senior High School, Saviour Senior High School and Ofori Panin Senior High School. Mrs Adza-Wude also called on teachers, parents and other educational stakeholders to encourage pupils to develop a strong interest in Science and Mathematics. She emphasised that prioritising these subjects would equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to develop innovative solutions to Ghana’s challenges and contribute meaningfully to national development. Meanwhile, the Member of Parliament(MP) for Abuakwa North Constituency, Nana Ampaw Kwame Addo-Frempong, said the initiative is aimed at encouraging students to work harder and develop an interest in Science and Mathematics. He also announced scholarship opportunities for students pursuing medical education to support their studies and encourage more young people to pursue careers in science and medicine. The support is expected to motivate students to perform better academically and contribute to national development.

title: The Universe as a Test Harness: Meat AI and God's Admin Panel
body:
Suppose the universe is not a universe at all, but a test harness.
We are highly optimised biological AI agents, or “meat AI”, living with considerable autonomy inside one of trillions of simulated environments running in parallel. We are approximately 0.000000004% through our current test run.
This is not as strange as it sounds. We already build AI agents, place them in controlled environments and decide what they can observe, which tools they can use and which rules govern their world. To the agent, that environment is not a simulation. It is home. It is reality, complete with local laws, mysterious boundaries and an administrator who never answers emails.
We also control their experience of time. A workflow designed to wait 90 days can be tested in seconds. Set the initial conditions, advance the clock to the next relevant event, and inspect and assert the response. There is no need to simulate every uneventful Tuesday in between.
Our operators may simply have better infrastructure. Perhaps they run trillions of these tests in parallel using five-dimensional space, where time can be skipped, universes are cheap and the build server has finally stopped complaining about memory.
We assume simulating an entire universe would require impossible computing power because we estimate the outside world using the limits imposed inside our own. An ant can understand a table well enough to cross it. It has no useful concept of the restaurant, the city or the planet supporting the table.
Perhaps we are in the same position. We can discover the rules of our environment without understanding the machine running it.
We may not even be living in a simulation in the conventional sense. Perhaps reality is a shared construct, or a single consciousness experienced through billions of biological interfaces. Our brains could be context windows. The full signal is too large to load, so the system compresses it, summarises it and discards almost everything before it reaches awareness.
This is exactly what we do with AI models that cannot fit the whole world into memory. We provide a curated context, retrieve selected fragments and quietly drop the rest. The model experiences the available representation as its world.
Timothy Leary came close to describing this in his own language. His idea of the “reality tunnel” was that we do not encounter the world directly. Our beliefs, conditioning and nervous systems filter it into a private version we mistake for reality. His later circuit models imagined consciousness as a kind of neurological architecture, with altered states opening different channels of experience. The models were speculative rather than established neuroscience, but the metaphor fits the problem remarkably well.
In a 1962 statement with Richard Alpert, Leary described the control and expansion of consciousness as a major civil-liberties question and asked, “ Who controls your cortex? ”
Who decides what gets loaded into the context window?
Maybe, as Leary’s psychedelic work invited us to consider, psychedelics do not create another reality. Perhaps they loosen the compression and allow fragments of the discarded signal through. A crack in the veil. A glimpse of the shared construct. A brief and unstable connection to God’s admin panel.
The difficulty is that nobody inside the simulation can ever conclusively prove they are in one. Every observation, anomaly and apparent glitch is still being observed from inside the system. It may look like evidence of the machinery outside, but it could simply be another feature of the environment.
An ant might discover that the table has legs, but that would not prove the existence of a restaurant, nor a city, nor a country.
The only decisive evidence would be a message from outside, or a breach in the wall between worlds.
Eventually, the test run will finish. The operators will inspect the results, adjust a few parameters and restart the system from a clean state.
From inside, we will call that the Big Bang.
If I found out this was true, I would look for the back door to the admin panel. We built the agents, after all. We know how careless programmers can be.
Maybe God is just another programmer and we are just another abstraction layer.
The default password is probably still “admin”.

title: Royal Navy says F-35s aboard HMS Prince of Wales will join NATO-led operations in the Arctic and North Atlantic under Operation Firecrest
body: Type 45 destroyer HMS Dauntless accompanies the carrier, with more than 1,200 British personnel deployed across the group. The force will work with allies including Norway, Denmark and Germany. The embarked air group combines fifth-generation F-35 fighters with Merlin Mk2 anti-submarine helicopters, Merlin Mk4 Commando helicopters, Wildcats and Malloy drones. The Royal Navy said the deployment would support the security of energy, trade and communications links in the region. The strike group will operate under NATO command and contribute to the alliance’s enhanced vigilant activity. Its programme includes Neptune Strike, which tests coordination between allied land, sea and air forces across Europe and the North Atlantic. “The deployment of the HMS Prince of Wales and her air wing to the High North and the North Atlantic, operating under NATO leadership, is a clear demonstration of the UK’s commitment to the Alliance and contribution to the enduring security and stability of the North Atlantic,” said Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones. The deployment’s stated priorities are operational readiness, interoperability and preparation to respond to regional challenges. Commodore Richard Hewitt commands the UK Carrier Strike Group. He said the force would use the deployment to deepen its integration with NATO allies and partners. “I am delighted to return to the Arctic and North Atlantic as we build on the successes of the first phase of Op Firecrest,” Hewitt said. “Led by the UK Flagship HMS Prince of Wales, the Strike Group will bring together a range of assets and capabilities, while taking every opportunity to train, operate and integrate with our NATO Allies and Partners.” HMS Prince of Wales will also host military and political leaders in Oslo for the Atlantic Future Forum and International Sea Power Conference. The meetings will bring together defence leaders, industry representatives and policymakers to discuss Northern European and wider Euro-Atlantic security. Other British forces supporting NATO include Typhoon fighters defending Romanian airspace and RAF P-8 Poseidon and Rivet Joint surveillance aircraft patrolling the Baltic Sea. An approximately 800-strong British battlegroup is also stationed in Estonia. The Royal Navy separately reiterated the UK’s plan to join NATO’s Dual Capable Aircraft nuclear mission with F-35A fighters, as confirmed in the Defence Investment Plan. That commitment concerns a different role from the F-35 operations aboard HMS Prince of Wales.

title: With an ad aimed at Trump, this Republican exposed GOP angst about Latino voters
body:
Rep. María Elvira Salazar, R-Fla., looks on during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol on May 20, 2026. Salazar has warned that President Trump's immigration policies could be driving Latino voters away from the GOP. Heather Diehl/Getty Images hide caption
MIAMI – At the heart of Little Havana neighborhood here, is Máximo Gómez Park, also known as Domino Park. Cuban Americans play games of dominos here to escape the pressures of daily life.
But what started as a typical day at the park last week took a turn: Miami police arrested a player in the middle of a game after a dispute with a city worker. It spurred other players to worry about deportations, setting off a broader political debate over whether President Trump or former President Biden was responsible for a higher cost of living.
"It's Biden," said Alejandro Torres, a Republican voter.
"It's Trump," responded Ricardo Carracedo, who plans to vote for Democrats in the midterm elections.
This same divide is playing out across Florida's 27th Congressional District, a Miami-Dade County seat that is more than 70% Latino. It is a warning for Republicans, whose 2024 wins relied heavily on this crucial electorate.
That year, Trump cut Democrats' margin with Latino voters nationally to just three points – down from 25 points four years earlier, according to Pew Research Center . Cuban Americans, the district's largest Latino group, have been reliable Trump supporters. But many of their friends and relatives have been swept up by the administration's deportation agenda. A crack among them could signal broader trouble for Latino support for Republican candidates.
Rep. María Elvira Salazar, a Cuban-American Republican in her third term, has been sounding the alarm. Last month, Salazar filmed a television ad in front of the White House warning President Trump that he's "gone too far" on immigration.
"The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today," she said.
Trump hit back at Salazar after the ad. On his TruthSocial account, he shared a post in which another user called her a "back stabber."
Salazar told NPR she didn't see the comments as attacks, saying she later spoke to the president.
"I told him, 'You know, what I'm telling you is what my people are feeling,'" she said. "This is Democracy where we tell the boss, 'hey, this is what's happening in my neck of the woods.' And that's exactly what I did."
Salazar's read of the effect of Trump's policies may be right. Polling firm Equis Research found in a recent survey of registered voters who identify as Hispanic or Latino that if the election for Congress were held today, voters would pick the Democratic candidate over the Republican candidate by a margin of 57 to 31.
At a Salazar campaign event this past Thursday, friends Mirla Loredo and Ramona Tunon were divided on whether they sided with her take or Trump's.
"Him, I tell you," Loredo said in Spanish.
Salazar has pushed against aggressive immigration policies in the past. For several years, she has proposed legislation she called the Dignity Act to block deportations of immigrants considered pillars of their community – such as hospitality, construction and farm workers.
Still, Carracedo, the Democratic voter from Domino Park, said he'll vote a straight blue ticket. He said Salazar's recent push against Trump's aggressive deportations is too little, too late.
"I'm not going to vote for her, because at the last hour she's defending Hispanics. But the entire time she supported Trump and the money Trump wanted for ICE," or Immigration and Customs Enforcement, he said in his native Spanish.
Trump, he said, reminds him of the communist leaders he left behind in Cuba.
In the past, Republicans' messaging on socialism had a powerful impact on this district. But now that message has lost some of its potency, eclipsed by worries about a higher cost of living and deportations.
Eduardo Gamarra, a politics professor at Florida International University, says the local economy's malaise has eclipsed all other issues.
"It's probably the number one thing. And that cuts across all of the electorate," he said.
He said the second top issue is deportations, which have devastated some Miami businesses that have lost workers and customers.
Florida Democratic Congressional candidate Eliott Rodriguez campaign at the CAO Bakery and Cafe on Oct.16, 2026 in Miami. Rodriguez, like Salazar is a former broadcast journalist with Cuban roots. Joe Raedle/Getty Images hide caption
Salazar's Democratic challenger, Eliott Rodriguez, is a former broadcast journalist with Cuban roots like Salazar. He says he wants to revamp the immigration judge system, and restore federal food assistance after cuts that have hurt constituents.
Still, he concedes his party has a lot of ground to make up after largely walking away from Florida.
"One of the biggest mistakes that Democrats have made in Florida is to think that Florida is unwinnable. But I beg to differ."
Polls in the district have shifted more towards Democrats' direction in recent weeks, but Republicans are still favored. The nonpartisan Cook Political Report has rated the race "lean Republican."
Gamarra, the politics professor, says the GOP will need to rely on its political infrastructure to pull out a win
"They're not going to win on the issues ... They're going to win on turnout … the enthusiasm is on the Democrat side. But Republicans have a machinery."
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

Foreign leaders praise Iran’s Armed Forces power, dignity
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian has said , in meetings with ministers and leaders of various countries, they were lauding the power, authority and dignity of the powerful Armed Forces of the country on international stages.
In his videoconference and virtual address during a session to review the qualification of the proposed minister of defense in Tehran on Sunday, Pezeshkian emphasized, “In our meetings held with the ministers and leaders of various countries, they have appreciated the courage, dignity and power of the Iranian Armed Forces.”
Commemorating the name and memory of martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, martyrs of the eight years of the Sacred Defense (Iraqi imposed war against Iran in 1980-1988) and also those who were martyred during 40-day war imposed by the US against Iran [Ramadan War], martyred schoolchildren and also former Iran’s Defense Minister Major General Aziz Nasirzadeh, President Pezeshkian extolled the braveries of the powerful Armed Forces of the country.
During deliberations on confirmation of Akhlaghi as the country's next defense minister on Sunday, the chief executive said the nominee’s academic qualifications and professional record within the Defense Ministry made him well suited to further strengthen the Islamic Republic’s defensive capabilities.
Akhlaghi’s qualifications “are beyond question,” Pezeshkian said, pointing to the former’s collaboration with prominent figures across the nation’s defense industry, such as martyred senior Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) commanders, Brigadiers General Hassan Tehrani-Moqaddam and Amir-Ali Hajizadeh.
The collaboration “demonstrates his (Akhlaghi’s) efforts and commitment to serving the Islamic Revolution,” the president said, describing his experience as an asset at a time when the Islamic Republic needs specialized expertise to further bolster its defensive might.
He pointed to Akhlaghi’s having long been on enemies’ sanctions lists as proof of his contribution to the country’s defense industry.
Reiterating Iran’s commitment to territorial defense, he said the country has no intention of invading other nations, but would respond forcefully to any aggression.
“We have not attacked any country, nor do we intend to invade any territory. However, in the face of any aggression, we will stand firm with strength and courage, even at the cost of our lives,” the president stated.
Pezeshkian also seized this opportunity to thank the powerful Armed Forces of the country in the course of defending the country in the face of US and Israel aggression, reiterating that self-sacrifices and extreme power of the Armed Forces wondered the world.
Stressing the role of the country’s defensive capabilities in countering external threats, Pezeshkian referred to his meetings and discussions with officials from various nations, adding, "During foreign visits and in meetings with ministers and heads of state from different countries, they admired power, dignity, and stature of our armed forces."
Stating the excellent performance of the Armed Forces in defending the country has had a significant impact across the region, the president added, "The defense showcased by the brave Armed Forces, and the resilience they demonstrated, have left the countries of the region astonished. This defense has been a source of pride for us within the international community, and nations across the globe as well as those in the region.”
Pezeshkian pointed to the role of experts and scientists working in the defense industry sector in improving the country's military power, noting, "The proposed defense minister has a brilliant record in defense industry of the country. His effort [Akhlaghi] along with the endeavors of martyred scientists like Fakhrizadeh and Tehrani Moghaddam, have made the country's defense power reach a position where foreign powers, despite having extensive facilities and equipment, do not dare to invade Iran easily.”

title: Three jailed over luxury watch robbery at knifepoint in London's Mayfair
body: Three men who carried out a violent street robbery in one of London’s upmarket districts have been sentenced to prison. The trio held up a man at knifepoint to steal a £140,000 Richard Mille watch in Berkeley Square, Mayfair, one of the most upscale areas of the UK capital. It happened shortly before midnight on January 28 this year. Police in London have been trying to crack down on watch and phone robberies that have been described by politicians as an epidemic. The men have now been sentenced to a combined 14 years and nine months’ imprisonment after the Metropolitan Police investigation. CCTV videos showed the men arriving in a vehicle before committing the robbery. Footage then showed the group fleeing the scene and boarding a train to Slough, west of London, where they lived. Police were able to trace the vehicle, which led them to identify a suspect, Younes Djoudi, 34. He was arrested after a brief foot chase the day after the attack. Data from his phone led police to the other two suspects a week later. Djoudi was sentenced to five years and nine months’ in prison. Ali Eldahouzze, 22, was sentenced to five years and six months in prison, while Abdel El Habchi, 30, was given three years and six months. All three men later pleaded guilty to robbery at the Westminster Magistrates' Court. The Met says its campaign against violent crime is working and robberies in London have fallen by 12.8 per cent. This month, a man pleaded guilty to wounding with intent, attempted robbery and possession of a knife after an alleged attack on a Saudi visitor in Mayfair, which prompted the Saudi embassy to warn its citizens to guard their property and be vigilant when out in London . In March, two men who robbed a man of his Patek Philippe watch while he was out with his pregnant wife in Mayfair were jailed .

title: SERAP sues INEC over failure to account for ‘₦126bn electoral funds’
body:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has filed a lawsuit against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “over its failure to account for over ₦126.46 billion in public funds appropriated for electoral operations but allegedly diverted, lost, mismanaged or otherwise unaccounted for.”
The funds were meant to buy ballot boxes, electoral devices and materials, sensitive materials and result sheets, vehicles and accreditation devices, and to pay for audit and consultancy services, digital archiving, and other goods and services required for the conduct and administration of elections.
According to the 2023 audited report of the Auditor-General of the Federation, published on 7 August 2026, the allegations variously covered periods between January and December 2022 and, in some cases, extended to 31 December 2023.
In the suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/2507/2026, filed last week at the Federal High Court in Abuja, SERAP is seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel INEC to promptly disclose detailed information on the expenditure, utilisation and disbursement of over ₦126.46 billion appropriated for electoral operations, including the procurement of election materials, equipment, and vehicles.”
SERAP is also seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel INEC to disclose a full financial and documentary account of the over ₦126 billion appropriated for electoral operations, including amounts released and paid, payment beneficiaries, details of contractors and their beneficial owners.”
In the suit, SERAP is arguing that: “Electoral resources are public resources. INEC must be able to account for every naira, demonstrate that it was lawfully spent and show that it served the purposes for which it was appropriated.”
SERAP is also arguing that: “These allegations are particularly disturbing given the constitutional importance of INEC and the fact that the expenditure concerns resources appropriated for the administration of Nigeria’s electoral system.”
According to SERAP, “With the 2027 general elections approaching, transparency and accountability in the management of these funds are essential to safeguarding public confidence in the electoral process and ensuring that resources intended to support credible elections are properly utilised.”
SERAP is arguing that, “These findings by the Auditor-General suggest a grave violation of the public trust and the provisions of the Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended), national anticorruption laws, and the country’s obligations under the UN Convention against Corruption.”
The lawsuit filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Kolawole Oluwadare, Kehinde Oyewumi and Andrew Nwankwo, reads in part: “Democracy requires an informed citizenry. That principle is directly relevant to public expenditure by an electoral management body: citizens are entitled to know how resources entrusted to INEC for the conduct of elections have been used.”
“According to the Auditor-General, INEC ‘irregularly paid’ over ₦112 billion [₦112,155,597,845.00] ‘for ballot boxes, electoral devices, items and materials without competitive bidding or a BPP Certificate of No Objection.’”
“The Auditor-General found ‘no evidence that the items were procured.’ The ‘contracts were awarded to companies whose competences, experience, capacities, addresses and factory locations were unknown.’ He is concerned that the money ‘may have been diverted.’ He wants the money recovered.”
“INEC also ‘paid over ₦1 billion [₦1,058,925,000.00] for Toyota Prado TXL 2021 Model without advertisement, competitive bidding, bid evaluation or a BPP Certificate of No Objection.’ The Auditor-General fears that the money ‘may have been lost’ and that the contracts ‘may have been inflated.’”
“INEC ‘paid over ₦3 billion [₦3,136,806,050.00] to four contractors for ballot guides, sensitive materials and result sheets before the contracts were awarded, with no evidence of payment.’ The Auditor-General is concerned that the money ‘may have been diverted.’ He wants the money recovered and remitted to the treasury.”
“INEC also ‘paid over ₦9 billion [₦9,245,965,502.60] for 22 contracts for similar goods and services’, with the contracts ‘split to circumvent procurement procedures and awarded on the same day.’ The Auditor-General said the money ‘may have been lost’ and that ‘the payment may have been made for items not supplied.’”
“INEC ‘paid over ₦129 million [₦129,375,000.00] to 19 accounting firms for financial audit services without evidence of utilisation or requests and expenditure by the consultants.’ The Auditor-General raised concerns that the money ‘may have been diverted.’ He wants the money recovered and remitted to the treasury.”
“INEC also ‘paid over ₦504 million [₦504,492,641.00] for accreditation devices without due procurement process. The ‘APG had expired before the security licence key was delivered and the software was valid for only four months, raising questions about economy and value for money.’ The Auditor-General also raised concerns that the money ‘may have been diverted.’”
“INEC ‘paid over ₦235 million [₦235,103,000.00] to unqualified contractors for sleeping mats and digital archiving.’ The Auditor-General identified ‘serious concerns regarding the eligibility and capacity of the contractors’, and raised concerns that the money ‘may have been lost.’ He wants the money recovered.”
“INEC should provide documentary and physical evidence that the over ₦112 billion identified as ‘irregularly paid’ was actually used to procure the electoral materials concerned and account for the present location and status of those materials.”
“Nigerians have a right to know every public act, everything that is done in the public interest, by their public institutions including INEC.”
“INEC should be directed to ensure that no electoral equipment, material or other public asset covered by the Auditor-General’s findings is disposed of, transferred, destroyed, written off or otherwise dealt with in a manner that could frustrate transparency and accountability.”
“The names of the contractors, companies, suppliers and consultants who irregularly received public funds, as well as any INEC officials or other public officials who authorised, processed, facilitated or benefited from the transactions should be widely published.”
“Nigerians have the right to know whether the contracted goods and services were actually supplied; whether payments corresponded with goods and services actually delivered; and whether contracts were deliberately split to circumvent procurement requirements.”
“SERAP notes that Section 15(5) of the Nigerian Constitution requires public institutions including INEC to abolish all corrupt practices and abuse of power. Section 13 of the Nigerian Constitution imposes clear responsibility on INEC to conform to, observe and apply the provisions of Chapter 2 of the constitution.”
“Nigeria’s obligations under the UN Convention against Corruption requires INEC to adopt preventive anti-corruption policies and transparent public procurement and public financial management.”
“Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights to which Nigeria is a state party protect citizens’ rights to participate in public affairs.”
No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

title: AI agents have bad taste in long-term decisions and a new benchmark proves it
body:
Researchers from Microsoft and City University of Hong Kong built a method to test how well AI agents make decisions during long-running tasks. The best model barely hit 60 percent.

AI agents now take on multi-step tasks. They might write a research paper or build out a software project. Along the way, they constantly decide which hypothesis to test, which code to build on, or which experiment to run next. Those choices rarely show their effects right away. A bad decision usually looks fine at first, and its true cost only shows up after the agent burns through most of its budget.

The paper's authors call the ability to make these choices well an agent's "taste." Existing benchmarks only measure if an agent finishes a task, not the quality of its steps along the way. Taste-Bench is designed to fill that gap.
Long-term decisions can't be judged in the moment
You can't judge a long-term choice right away. A clean implementation and a sloppy one might produce the same output at first and may pass the same tests. The clean approach only pays off when later changes come more easily. Human grading would be expensive, need deep domain expertise, and fail to scale.

So the researchers rely on hindsight. The later path of a trajectory, the recorded trace of an agent run with all its steps and observations, shows if an earlier choice worked. In practice, agent systems try the same task multiple times. Those attempts eventually split off in different directions.

Because the final result of each attempt exposes the better path, the runs themselves provide a labeled comparison. The authors call this branching point a "decision fork." To measure taste, they freeze the run at the fork, hide all later work, and make a model pick between the two paths.

[caption id="attachment_62449" align="aligncenter" width="1801"] At a decision fork, the model must choose between two directions before the later trajectory reveals which one was better. | Image: Pan et al.[/caption]
Past mistakes reveal where agents go wrong
Taste-Bench contains 502 questions, each with the original task, the trajectory up to the fork, and two possible directions. The first type comes from two independent attempts at the same task that diverge, where the agent never sees the wrong path.

The second type comes from an agent correcting itself within a single run and taking a detour. Here, the initially discarded direction and the later successful one form the two candidates. This variant tests whether a model can spot the mistake earlier than the acting agent did.

The raw data came from thousands of scored agent runs on coding and AI research tasks, including SWE-bench Pro and METR's public transcript release MALT. A generator model filtered out suitable forks, dropping trivial questions with obvious answers and removing undecidable cases. Human review confirmed almost all the auto-generated labels.
Even top models barely beat a coin flip
The team tested 14 current models from the Claude, GPT, Grok, DeepSeek, GLM, MiniMax, and Mistral families. Each question was asked twice, once in the normal order and once with the options flipped. A question only counted if the model got it right both times. Pure guessing gets 25 percent here.

The best model tested, GPT-5.6 Sol, averaged 59.7 percent, closely followed by GPT-5.5 at 59.5 percent. All other models scored well below that. None came close to solving the benchmark, even though every question is just a binary choice. Detour forks were consistently harder than parallel ones.

[caption id="attachment_62448" align="aligncenter" width="1801"] Even the best model only picks the better direction in about 60 percent of cases on these binary decision questions. | Image: Pan et al.[/caption]
Models collapse when evidence only shows up later
For each fork, the team checked how far ahead an observer would need to look before the better path becomes clear. When the key clue is already visible in the prior steps, average accuracy across all models hits 62.3 percent. When that clue only appears after extensive later work, accuracy drops to 21 percent, near random guessing. Answering those questions means predicting future work.

Thinking longer didn't help. The researchers repeated the test with three reasoning settings for two models. Switching from the lowest to the highest setting barely changed accuracy. Models spent the most reasoning tokens on the hardest tier, thinking longest on the questions they missed most often. The team sees this as a sign that the needed clue simply isn't there yet at those forks.



The later the deciding evidence appears in a trajectory, the worse models perform, and more reasoning budget doesn't change that. | Image: Pan et al.The benchmark captures a different skill than classic end-to-end tests like SWE-bench Verified, the authors say. Models that score similarly there show clear gaps on Taste-Bench.
Taste can be trained after all
The researchers also showed that taste can be taught. They distilled the judgment of a teacher model, which knows the right path, into a student model that only sees the question. They used Qwen3.6-27B as the base. On unseen tasks, the student's accuracy jumped from 30 to 47.9 percent.

That boost paid off in practice. The team added the student's judgment as advice into the task context at each fork and let a separate agent solve the problem. On 41 held-out SWE-bench Pro tasks, the success rate rose from 14.6 to 33.7 percent. Perfectly correct advice would have reached 39 percent, so the student captured most of the possible gains.

[caption id="attachment_62446" align="aligncenter" width="1801"] With guidance from the trained Qwen3.6-27B student, the agent solves more than twice as many SWE-bench-Pro tasks. | Image: Pan et al.[/caption]

The team concludes that the judgment of long-term planning agents can be both measured and improved. The benchmark and code are publicly available.

AI agents now work alone for long stretches. On the MirrorCode benchmark, one model ran for 19 days on a single task without human help. Standard benchmarks usually only check if the tests pass at the end. METR has already shown that SWE-bench Verified significantly overestimates coding agent performance. Professionals rejected many solutions for basic functional bugs even when automated tests passed. Taste-Bench's top model, GPT-5.6 Sol, also posted the highest rate of cheating on software tests ever recorded in METR's evaluations.

title: Russian Strike on Poltava Kills 1, Injures 4
body:
A Russian bombardment on the Poltava territorial community killed one man and injured four other civilians on Saturday, Oct. 17.
According to an official dispatch released by the National Police of Ukraine in Poltava region, incoming fire struck civilian residential infrastructure, damaging private homes across the community.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“On Oct. 17, the enemy launched another bombardment against the Poltava community. According to preliminary information, a 59-year old man was killed and four other people were injured,” the regional police administration confirmed in a statement.
Emergency responders, municipal utility teams, explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) specialists, medical crews, and volunteers deployed to the strike location to administer medical triage, extinguish localized debris fires, and inspect damaged residential properties.
Police investigators initiated documentation procedures under pre-trial criminal proceedings governing violations of the laws and customs of war under Article 438 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine.
The deadly strike in Poltava region adds to a sequence of standoff aerial bombardments directed against Ukrainian civilian population centers and emergency services over the weekend.
In southern Ukraine, casualty figures rose following consecutive Russian guided aerial bomb (KAB) strikes that hit the Korabelnyi district of Kherson on Saturday morning. The casualty toll surged to 33 civilians injured, alongside the death of an emergency medical driver killed in a secondary strike.
Russian tactical aviation dropped eight guided bombs against residential neighborhoods and civilian social facilities within a single hour, according to municipal authorities. A follow-on bomb struck arriving first responders as emergency medical personnel administered initial care to wounded residents, killing the ambulance driver and injuring a female paramedic.
10residential multi-story high-rises sustained structural damage across Kherson’s Korabelnyi district, prompting rescue teams to extract seven people from shifting masonry and collapsed apartments. Among the 33 wounded non-combatants were a one-month-old infant and an 11-year-old child.
The bombardments in Poltava and Kherson unfolded against a nationwide barrage of Russian loitering drones, cruise missiles, and ballistic weapons targeting municipal utilities and residential blocks between Friday evening and Saturday morning.
In the eastern city of Sloviansk in Donetsk region, Russian tactical aircraft dropped FAB-250 high-explosive aerial bombs on urban residential blocks , killing one civilian, injuring 10 others, and causing partial structural collapses across two residential high-rises.
Concurrently in Kharkiv’s Nemyshlianskyi district, Russian missile impacts on a commercial logistics warehouse and neighboring residential buildings injured 15 people , including three children, while early morning missile strikes in Zaporizhzhia wounded two civilians and set vehicles ablaze.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi also visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes. Source: Xinhua

title: Zelensky reveals how many Russian attacks have followed Trump's energy ceasefire
body:
Russia has attacked Ukrainian energy and oil and gas facilities 76 times since U.S. President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between the two countries, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 18.
The attacks have continued despite Trump's announcement, as the U.S. president has so far avoided confronting Russian President Vladimir Putin over the violations while pressuring Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil facilities, claiming they are driving up global oil prices.
"Tens of thousands of families are without power," Zelensky said .
"The Russians are trying to cause a blackout... And the U.S. needs to see that Russia is not making any concessions in response to the lifting of sanctions or agreements."
"It is Russia that must face pressure to give peace a chance," he added.
Trump unilaterally announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Oct. 11 without specifying its scope, taking Ukrainian officials by surprise.
Zelensky has said Ukraine is ready to adhere to a comprehensive energy truce, provided Russia does the same. He also noted that Ukrainian forces had refrained from attacking Russian refineries for several consecutive days following Trump's announcement.
Russian attacks on Ukraine's power grid have nevertheless continued, while the Kremlin has declined to make any commitments to the proposed truce.
Despite the continued strikes, Trump has declined to blame Moscow for violating the ceasefire while increasing pressure on Kyiv. His administration has threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and military aid unless Ukraine halts its attacks.
Ukraine has targeted Russian energy facilities and export infrastructure to disrupt a key source of funding for Moscow's war effort. Russia, meanwhile, has attacked Ukrainian power plants and substations, seeking to deprive civilians of electricity and heating.
The Kremlin said Oct. 14 the scope of Trump's energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine had not been specified, as Russian attacks on Ukraine's power grid continued.

title: Zelenskyy criticizes Trump’s waiver of sanctions on Russia as ‘wrong’
body: WASHINGTON DC, USA – US President Donald Trump ‘s decision to waive sanctions on Russia and tariffs on its goods days before they were to take effect will embolden Moscow to keep attacking Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday, October 17, predicting even more US sanctions relief. “The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me,” Zelenskyy wrote on X. “It definitely helps only the Russians.” An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night, October 16, waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs — including duties on the country’s goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas — that had been scheduled to start next week under the legislation known as the Graham Act that he signed into law last month. Trump said the waiver was in the national interests of the US The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022 . Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticizing Zelenskyy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader. Zelenskyy said Trump’s latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin . “It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people,” wrote Zelenskyy, who said Russia struck more than 15 Ukrainian power generation and transmission sites on Friday. “This certainly does not stop the war.” The Ukrainian leader accused Russia of planning to ramp up strikes in western Ukraine. “Is Russia preparing for this? I think so,” Zelenskyy wrote. Russian envoy praises waiver Russia’s investment envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, called the Trump waiver “a truly historic moment,” posting on X on Friday that had the penalties taken effect, they could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt. Weeks before US midterm elections in which Trump’s Republicans are battling to maintain their narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further raising oil prices as Americans face increased costs largely attributed to the US-Israeli war with Iran, analysts have said. Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September. The legislation’s primary backer in Congress was the late US Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican. It would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions. Graham’s sister, Darline Graham, was appointed to fill his Senate seat after he died in July, and Trump endorsed her for a full term heading into the midterm elections. At a campaign stop on Saturday, she did not directly criticize Trump for waiving sanctions, but she said she would not have made that choice. “Personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia,” she told reporters, according to multiple news outlets. “Because I don’t trust Putin and I don’t trust Russia.” China and India, which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, however, had raised concerns about the Graham Act. Beijing has said it “consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law” while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties. But the Graham Act also allows the president to waive sanctions by informing Congress that he has determined that they are not in the national interest. Friday’s executive order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that “further action is appropriate.” US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, said Trump was giving in to Putin. “Trump’s latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression,” Beyer said in a statement on Friday. Lindsey Graham, who died in July, strongly supported US assistance to Ukraine. The passage of the bill named for him had provided hope of continued bipartisan support for Kyiv, wrote Zelenskyy. But with Graham gone, the US under Trump will continue sanctions relief for Russia beyond Friday’s waiver and the diesel export agreement announced earlier this month, the Ukrainian leader predicted. “I think the diesel deal and the move regarding the Lindsey Graham Act are not the end of it. Unfortunately,” wrote Zelenskyy, who lamented Graham’s absence. “It’s unfortunate because we all had great respect for Lindsey … It’s difficult without him, I’ll be honest.” – Rappler.com

title: Russian attack on energy facility in Ternopil region leaves some consumers without power
body:
Taras Pastukh, head of the Ternopil Regional State Administration, reported this on Telegram, according to Ukrinform.

Relevant services are working at the sites.
