body: Kuni Tyessi in Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) is set to rescue thousands of Nigerian graduates who have been unable to participate in the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme for years because of discrepancies between their Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) records and National Identification Number (NIN). Speaking yesterday while receiving a delegation from Veritas University, Abuja, led by its Vice-Chancellor, Rev. Fr. Professor Hyacinth Ichoku, the JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, said the examination body was set to introduce a service to align the biodata of the affected candidates. Aina said the initiative was part of measures by the examination body to remove administrative bottlenecks that had left graduates stranded despite completing their university education. According to him, the new NIN alignment service would enable eligible candidates to update their biodata to match their official identity records, potentially clearing a major obstacle preventing affected graduates from proceeding to NYSC. He said the board had identified cases of graduates who completed their studies four or five years ago but remained unable to participate in the national service scheme because their personal details in JAMB’s records did not match those registered with the National Identity Management Commission. The registrar estimated that thousands of candidates could be affected, describing the initiative as part of his administration’s commitment to reducing the difficulties students and graduates encounter while dealing with the board. “I am pleased to announce that today we will be formally launching an NIN alignment service that will allow candidates to change their biodata to match their official identity and that will unlock the possibility of NYSC for thousands of people,” he said. Aina, who described his mission at JAMB as one of building trust and reducing trauma, said the board was leveraging technology to resolve problems that had previously prevented candidates from accessing its services. He added that candidates who had lost access to their registered email addresses or telephone numbers could now make changes and regularise their relationship with the board, unlike in the past when such situations could prevent them from carrying out transactions. The registrar also urged universities to cooperate with JAMB in regularising admissions, warning that candidates admitted outside the board’s Central Admissions Processing System remained a particularly difficult challenge. He said such candidates might have completed their studies but could still face recognition and documentation problems because their admissions were not processed through the approved central system. Beyond the planned NIN alignment service, Aina disclosed that JAMB was considering incorporating life skills and critical-thinking assessments into the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) to give universities a broader basis for selecting candidates. He said the proposed reform was intended to move admission decisions beyond academic performance alone and recognise candidates with practical abilities, sound reasoning and other competencies essential for success in higher education. According to him, the board had established a committee to examine how the additional assessment components could be integrated into the UTME. Aina argued that candidates who had already been assessed in their subject knowledge at the ordinary-level stage might not need to be evaluated solely on the same basis during the admission process. He said the proposed approach would give universities greater flexibility to identify applicants whose critical-thinking and life-skills performance demonstrated their suitability for particular courses, even where their conventional UTME scores fell slightly below the institutions’ usual cut-off marks. “We should be able to find institutions that will say our cut-off for this course is 200, but we will take 190 if you score over 80 per cent in the critical-thinking and life-skills component of the examination,” he said. The registrar noted that some candidates might not be outstanding academic performers under conventional assessment methods but could possess other abilities that made them worthy of admission consideration. He said the proposed reform would promote a more inclusive admission process by recognising candidates’ all-round capabilities rather than relying exclusively on their academic performance on examination day. The initiative, he added, would require collaboration between JAMB and tertiary institutions to ensure that the proposed assessment components served as useful tools for admission decisions. Aina, however, expressed concern over candidates admitted into tertiary institutions outside the central admissions system, saying the board had yet to find a solution for many who had completed their programmes but were not recognised in its records. He described the situation as a serious challenge, noting that the consequences of administrative decisions in the admission process could affect the future of young Nigerians. “The responsibility entrusted to you is a big one. It is not just one person that you tell to go away and come back; it is a life that can be destroyed by the work that you do,” he said. He urged university administrators to work closely with JAMB to ensure that admissions were properly processed and documented, thereby preventing students from encountering difficulties years after graduation. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Veritas University, Rev. Fr. Professor Ichoku, congratulated Aina on his appointment and pledged the institution’s cooperation with the examination body.

title: Oyebanji Makes First Appointment, Re-appoints SSG, COS, CPS
body: Wale Igbintade Ekiti State Governor, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, has approved the re-appointment of Prof. Habibat Adubiaro as Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Mr. Oyeniyi Adebayo as Chief of Staff, and Mr. Olayinka Oyebode as Chief Press Secretary (CPS), following his inauguration for a second term in office on Friday. The appointments, which take immediate effect, are the first made by the governor since his inauguration. Prof. Adubiaro, a Professor of Chemistry and seasoned administrator, holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry from the University of Ibadan. She obtained her master’s degree and PhD from the University of Ado-Ekiti, now Ekiti State University, Ado-Ekiti, in 2004 and 2010, respectively. She began her professional career at the defunct Oodua Textile Industry, Ado-Ekiti, in 1995, shortly after completing her National Youth Service. In 1999, she joined the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, where she spent several years teaching and advancing through the academic ranks. In February 2013, she joined the Federal University Oye-Ekiti as a Lecturer in the Department of Industrial Chemistry. Her academic career culminated in her promotion to the rank of Professor of Chemistry, officially announced in January 2025, with effect from October 1, 2022. Her research interests include food chemistry and organic synthesis, particularly the chemical composition, nutritional properties and functional characteristics of plant-derived food materials. Prof. Adubiaro has a longstanding record of public service in Ekiti State. She previously served as Special Adviser on Women Affairs to the Ekiti State Governor between 2003 and 2004 before her appointment as Secretary to the State Government by Governor Oyebanji on October 16, 2022. As SSG, she played a central coordinating role in the state administration, bringing her experience in governance, institutional administration and policy implementation to bear on government operations. Mr Adebayo, the re-appointed Chief of Staff to the Governor, hails from Usi-Ekiti in Ido/Osi Local Government Area of Ekiti State. A former banker and financial management expert, he combines academic training in Forest Resources Management and Agricultural Economics with advanced business education and extensive experience in banking, corporate management and public service. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Forest Resources Management and a Master of Science degree in Agricultural Economics from the University of Ibadan. He subsequently obtained a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, United States. He has also attended executive programmes at Harvard Business School, INSEAD and the Kellogg School of Management. Adebayo began his professional career at Arthur Andersen, where he gained experience in accounting, auditing and financial consultancy across various industries. He later worked with Merrill Lynch Private Wealth Management Group in Los Angeles, United States, gaining experience in investment management and wealth advisory services. He subsequently built a career in commercial banking, serving in various leadership and specialist roles at Wema Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA), First City Monument Bank (FCMB) and the defunct Enterprise Bank, where he served as Executive Director. In November 2022, Adebayo joined the Oyebanji administration as Special Adviser on Budget, Economic Planning and Performance Management. He was appointed Commissioner for Budget, Economic Planning and Performance Management in August 2023, contributing to budgeting, economic planning, fiscal coordination, development planning and performance monitoring. On December 31, 2024, Governor Oyebanji appointed him Chief of Staff, effective January 2, 2025. In that capacity, he supported the coordination of executive administration, facilitated engagement between the Governor’s Office and other government institutions, and helped drive the implementation of government priorities. Mr. Oyebode, the re-appointed Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, has extensive experience in journalism, media management and strategic communication. A graduate of English and Literary Studies from the then Ondo State University, Ado-Ekiti, (now Ekiti State University, Ado-Ekiti), Oyebode holds a master’s degree in Peace and Security Studies from the same institution. He is also an alumnus of the International Journalism Institute, Berlin, Germany, and the Austria Study Centre for Peace and Conflict Resolution (ASPR), Schlaining, Austria. He began his journalism career with the Post Express newspaper, Apapa, Lagos, in 1996. He subsequently worked with The Punch and The Nation newspapers, where he rose to the position of Assistant Editor (Politics). Oyebode joined the Ekiti State Government in December 2010 as Special Assistant on Media to the Governor. He was appointed Chief Press Secretary in June 2011 and served in that capacity until the end of the first administration of former Governor Kayode Fayemi in October 2014. Between 2015 and 2018, he served as Special Adviser on Media to the Minister of Mines and Steel Development. He later returned to Ekiti State as Chief Press Secretary to the Governor from October 2018 to October 2022. On October 16, 2022, Governor Oyebanji re-appointed him Chief Press Secretary. In 2023, he was additionally appointed Special Adviser on Media and Strategy, combining the two responsibilities until the end of the administration’s first term on October 15, 2026. Governor Oyebanji congratulated the appointees on their re-appointments and urged them to deploy their wealth of experience, professional expertise and institutional knowledge towards effective service delivery and the continued development of Ekiti State.

title: Air defenses down 95 drones over Leningrad Region — governor
body:
ST. PETERSBURG, October 18. /TASS/. Russian air defense forces have shot down 95 drones over the Leningrad Region, Governor Alexander Drozdenko reported on Friday on his Telegram channel.
"The response to a large-scale drone attack is ongoing. As of now, 95 enemy UAVs have been shot down over the Leningrad Region. Debris has fallen on a private house near the town of Kirovsk and on an apartment building in Vsevolozhsk," Drozdenko wrote.
The governor also reported power outages caused by drone debris hitting power lines.

title: COAS Visits Borno as Parents Lament Children’s 155 Days in Captivity
body: The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant-General Waidi Shuaibu, arrived in Maiduguri, Borno State capital yesterday, amid heightened tensions and a looming protest by the parents of 78 school children who were abducted in May. The high-stakes visit comes as the parents shelved a planned journey to the nation’s capital, where they had threatened to occupy the streets outside the Presidential Villa in Abuja until President Bola Tinubu personally addressed their plight. The postponement comes as the families grapple with crippling poverty, a lack of transport fares, and the struggle to leave behind food for their remaining dependants. The children were abducted on May 15, 2026, from the Mussa and Lassa communities – the same day school teachers and students were kidnapped in Oyo State. While the Oyo victims have since been rescued, the Borno parents say they have been left to grieve in isolation. “We were surprised by the level of seriousness accorded to the Oyo children, thinking that the same would be extended to our children. Unfortunately, we were left alone to grieve,” lamented Ishaku Suya, Chairman of the Association of the Abducted Children’s Parents. Suya noted that no top security chief had visited the affected communities since the tragic incident occurred. The parents are now looking to the Chief of Army’s current visit to Borno as a turning point, urging him to personally inspect Mussa and Lassa just as military leadership did following the Oyo abduction. The pressure from the families coincides with increased legislative interest and recent executive interventions. Earlier this week, Borno State Governor Babagana Zulum held a closed-door meeting with President Tinubu in Abuja to discuss the fate of the captive children. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Zulum reassured the public of the federal government’s unwavering commitment to securing their release. President Tinubu subsequently directed all heads of security agencies to launch rescue operations nationwide. Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, stated on October 15 that the president gave explicit instructions to leave no terrorist or bandit camp standing in Nigeria, while ensuring a secure environment ahead of the upcoming elections. During his arrival in Maiduguri at approximately 11a.m. yesterday, Lt-Gen Shuaibu immediately went to work. Following a closed-door meeting with senior officers of Operation Hadin Kai at the Maimalari Cantonment, the COAS addressed the troops, charging them to guarantee a security-free breach during the 2027 electoral process and emphasizing the critical need for inter-agency synergy. Reminding the soldiers of recent increases in their salaries and logistical backing from the federal government, the COAS stated, “To whom much is given, much is expected. You’ve been motivated in this fight against insurgency. As we go towards the elections, you must continue to provide the enabling environment… for it to be a hit-free exercise.” He later paid a courtesy call on Governor Zulum.

title: Stallion Group Challenges Court Judgment, Files Appeal and Stay of Execution
body: Stallion Group has filed an appeal against the judgment delivered by the Federal High Court, Lagos, on October 16, 2026 in Suit No. FHC/L/CS/2074/2023: UBA Plc and Ors v. Stallion Nigeria Limited & Others. The judgment arose from a commercial dispute initiated by UBA Plc in 2023. A statement by Abdulsalam Gaffar Olatokunbo said Stallion Group respectfully but firmly disagrees with the decision, adding that having reviewed the judgment with its legal advisers, it considered that there are strong grounds for appellate review and is determined to pursue its rights through the courts. The Group noted that a Notice of Appeal has been filed at the Court of Appeal and stay of execution of the judgment pending the hearing and determination of the appeal. It added that it would pursue the appeal vigorously and will continue to respect the judicial process. The Group said it has confidence in the appellate courts and their ability to consider the issues raised in the appeal. “The Group’s operations continue. We ask our employees, customers, business partners and other stakeholders to rely on verified information and not on speculation or sensational reports about a matter that is now before the appellate court,” the stressed.

title: Egypt's North Coast: Where to go on the Mediterranean and what's coming next
body: Ask Sherif Fathy where Egypt's next big holiday destination lies and he points north to the Mediterranean. “It’s what we call ‘sun and fun’,” the Egyptian Minister of Tourism and Antiquities says with a smile. "That coast has huge investments going on now, and it will be the summer destination of the Mediterranean for the coming decades," Fathy tells The National on the sidelines of World Travel and Tourism Council’s Global Summit in Malta last week. "The growth is big.” That extends to national figures, as Fathy says Egypt had welcomed about 14.4 million international tourists in 2026 by the end of September, despite regional tension slowing growth. "We expect to end the year with 20 million." Much of that runs through Cairo. The Grand Egyptian Museum , which opened in November 2025, is now "the jewel of the crown", Fathy says. "Everybody is trying to reroute his trip, start or end his trip in Cairo." It welcomed about four million visitors between its opening and the end of August, and Fathy expects that figure to reach five million a year. Yet the coastline running west from Alexandria towards Libya, known to Egyptians as the Sahel, has long been where Cairo families escape the summer heat. Now it is being sold to the wider world, and Fathy says the numbers prove demand is there. For example, charter flights into El Alamein, he says, grew by 540 per cent last year and by a further 50 per cent this summer. The growth "could have been more, but we didn't have enough rooms," he adds. That shortage is being tackled, however. "The properties being built there are extremely luxurious," Fathy says, and he expects the beach clubs and nightlife to be a big part of the draw. Is it a good fit for UAE travellers? "Definitely," he says, describing UAE families who book the same hotels year after year and "come and enjoy it every summer". Here is where to go along the coast, heading west. Getting there Most visitors fly in. El Alamein's airport is one of three serving the coast, and Fathy says it will soon be enlarged, along with the airport at Marsa Matrouh further west. This summer, Alamein International was served by 15 airlines, including Etihad and flydubai alongside Saudia, Flynas and Air Cairo, although many routes are seasonal. Alexandria's Borg El Arab airport is the other main gateway, and the city makes an easy first or last night. By road, New Alamein is about 250km from Cairo, which is under a three-hour drive. It’s worth noting that locals place everything by its kilometre marker along the coastal road, so you will hear a resort described as being at "Km 126". El Alamein and New Alamein Best for: summer festivals and Second World War history The coast's main hub begins around Marina El Alamein at Km 100. Officials expect about 300,000 visitors to Alamein in 2026, up from about 170,000 last year. New Alamein was planned as a year-round city, with an opera house, universities and residential districts alongside its beaches. In summer, it fills with concerts and festivals. This year's Yalla Sahel drew Gulf visitors to shows by Egyptian and Arab stars such as Amr Diab and Elissa. The town is better known for the Second World War battles fought here in 1942. El Alamein Military Museum displays weapons and uniforms from the campaign. Nearby, the El Alamein War Cemetery holds the graves of thousands of Commonwealth soldiers and a German cemetery commemorates those who died in the battle. Sidi Abdel Rahman and Marassi Best for: luxury resorts and beach clubs Between Km 124 and Km 144, on the International Coastal Road, Sidi Abdel Rahman is the coast's upscale heart, with high-end resorts, beaches and a busy entertainment scene. Marassi, at Km 126, is one of the best-known names on the coast, with several beaches, world-class hotels, residential villages, an 18-hole golf course and the first water park in Egypt’s North Coast. A little further west, Ghazala Bay is quieter, private and exclusive, while El Dabaa offers calmer beaches with soft white sand and turquoise water. Much of this stretch is gated resort communities, so check day access beforehand. Ras El Hekma Best for: what's coming next, with a UAE connection The biggest change on the coast is being built with Emirati investment. Abu Dhabi's ADQ appointed Modon Holding as master developer of Ras El Hekma in 2024, on a site of more than 170 million square metres. The first district, Wadi Yemm, will be anchored by a lighthouse and a 10,000-seat amphitheatre. It includes a Montage hotel with about 200 rooms and suites, plus 96 branded villas. Beach club brand Nammos has also unveiled plans for a Cycladic-inspired resort, beach club and 72 one- to four-bedroom branded residences, plus a penthouse and retail village. None of it is open yet. As of July, the project was in full construction with completion dates scheduled for 2028, so for now Ras El Hekma is one to watch rather than book. Beyond it, Sidi Heneish has wide, largely untouched beaches and is starting to attract luxury developers. Marsa Matrouh Best for: hidden coves and Bedouin culture Further west, Marsa Matrouh is a city rather than a resort strip. Fathy points to the Bedouin experience as one of the coast's draws. The real attraction is the water. Ageeba Beach is a cove tucked between two hills and reached by a flight of steps. Cleopatra's Bath is a pool inside a rock cave where the waves break. Legend says the queen bathed there. Lagoon Beach, with its pearl-white sand and clear water, suits families. For a break from the sea, the Rommel Museum, opened in 1977 in memory of German field marshal Erwin Rommel, holds Second World War artefacts. Side trip: Siwa Best for: desert landscapes and ecotourism The coast itself is about “sun and fun”, Fathy says, but "it can be combined with ecotourism in Siwa". The oasis lies well inland – close to the Libyan border – and is a long drive from the coast. It’s worth the effort, however, as it’s a leading ecotourism destination for the country, famed for its mud-brick architecture, natural landscapes and distinctive Berber culture . Visit the old Shali fortress, a medieval citadel uniquely built from a salt-and-mud material called kershef. Or see the salt lakes, a network of saline pools and natural springs, which are said to be healing and glow in vivid colours. Elsewhere, the Temple of the Oracle, built in the 6 th century BC, is linked in legend to Alexander the Great.

title: At Golden Jubilee Anniversary, CAN Honours Gowon, Obasanjo, Jonathan, Osinbajo, Oluremi Tinubu
body: . Church must be voice of IDPs, attacked farmers, says Okoh Kuni Tyessi in Abuja The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) yesterday honoured former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon (rtd.), former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Goodluck Jonathan; former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, and the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, at its 50th anniversary thanksgiving service in Abuja. This is just as the President of the association, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, has declared that the Church cannot afford to be silent while vulnerable Nigerians suffer, charging it to speak boldly against injustice, insecurity and corruption. The ceremony, held yesterday, was part of the activities marking CAN’s golden jubilee. Senator Tinubu was conferred with the Christian Icon Award, while Gowon, Obasanjo, Jonathan and Osinbajo received the Pillar of Faith Award for their contributions to the Christian community and national development. Other recipients included Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume; Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio; Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Dr Benjamin Kalu, Governors Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta, Monday Okpebholo of Edo and Seyi Makinde of Oyo State. Speaking after receiving her award, Senator Tinubu thanked Okoh, describing the honour as a call to deeper service. “I want you to know that this award is a call to greater work in service to God and humanity,” she said. She said 50 years of CAN was a significant milestone and urged sustenance of unity among denominations. She said the anniversary theme, “Walking Together in Faith”, reflects God’s call for oneness, citing John 17:21-22 and Ephesians 4:4-6, and prayed that CAN blocs would continue to work together for the Church and Nigeria. She urged CAN to remain focused on preparing believers for the second coming of Jesus Christ. In his address, Okoh said CAN’s 50-year journey attests to God’s faithfulness and the foresight of founders who in August 1976 created a united platform for Christians. He noted that Nigeria remained the only African country where diverse Christian traditions were united under one ecumenical umbrella CCN, CPFN/PFN, OAIC, TEKAN/ECWA and others, despite early suspicion, prejudice and marginalisation which successive leaders had worked to overcome. He urged Christians to guard that unity and shun divisive social media exchanges, stressing CAN belonged to all Christians. Okoh said in 50 years CAN had spoken on religious freedom, justice, good governance, corruption, insecurity and humanitarian service, but must now be more informed, courageous and evidence-based. He charged the Church to defend vulnerable Nigerians, IDPs, out-of-school children, jobless youths, farmers who were unable to access farmlands due to insecurity, women facing violence and trafficking victims. Okoh, said the gospel itself makes indifference impossible. “The gospel makes it impossible to remain indifferent to the living conditions of the vulnerable. Faith must find practical expression in compassion, service and advocacy. The Church must speak!” he added. He listed those the Church must defend to also include communities destroyed by environmental degradation. “The church must speak!” he declared, but warned interventions must be anchored on truth and credible evidence, not rumours or partisan politics. He advocated “critical collaboration” with government: “Collaborate where common good requires it, challenge where justice requires challenge, commend where government does well and warn where government fails, while maintaining the church’s independence.” Okoh urged stronger institutional capacity for research, advocacy, environmental protection, climate resilience and ethical technology. He called on leaders to govern responsibly, respect the Constitution and account for public resources, and on the Church to “pray for Nigeria, pray for those in government, speak for Nigeria, serve Nigeria, build Nigeria and heal Nigeria.”

title: Atiku is a True Pan-Nigerian Leader, Deserves 2027 Electoral Victory, Says ADC
body: • Accuses Tinubu’s administration of sectionalism and divisive politics Chuks Okocha in Abuja The Presidential Campaign Council of African Democratic Congress (ADC-PCC) has described its presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as a true Pan-Nigerian leader and a detribalised statesman deserving of victory in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. The Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, stated this in Abuja at the weekend while receiving the leadership of the Grassroots Mobilisation Network (GMN), led by its National Coordinator, Sadiq Abubakar Adamu Lwafu, during a visit to his office. Speaking during the visit, Lwafu said the organisation was embarking on a nationwide mobilisation campaign to rally Nigerians across the country behind Atiku’s presidential ambition and ensure the defeat of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 election. He noted that the Tinubu’s administration had subjected Nigerians to severe economic hardship, worsening insecurity and what he described as an increasingly authoritarian political environment. “President Tinubu’s administration has made life so difficult for Nigerians. The hardship is too much. Nigerians are now living in fear of insecurity. It appears that governance has collapsed, as a group of greedy politicians have ganged up against the poor, and democracy has been abused and replaced with an authoritarian regime,” Lwafu said. He warned that Nigeria was drifting towards the path of failure like come African countries where, in his view, democratic institutions had been weakened and political power increasingly concentrated. “The only man who can rescue Nigeria is Atiku Abubakar, and we are on a mission to ensure that the APC is thrown out of power through the ballot box next year,” he added. Lwafu described the ADC as a credible platform bringing together experienced politicians, patriotic Nigerians and leaders committed to national development. “ADC is the only platform with great minds and patriotic leaders. Look at our National Chairman, David Mark; Look at Atiku Abubakar, Rotimi Amaechi, Tunde Ogbeha, Rauf Aregbesola, Kashim Imam, Senator Austin Akobundu, Senator Aminu Tambuwal, Emeka Ihedioha, Ralph Nwosu, Dele Momodu, Dino Melaye and others. “These are not jokers like what we have in the APC. Look at the characters in the APC and compare: propagandists, deceitful, pretenders and certificate forgers,” he said. Responding, Ologbondiyan commended the GMN leadership for its commitment to national development and grassroots mobilisation, insisting that the difference between Atiku and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was evident in their respective approaches to national leadership and political inclusion. According to him, Atiku represents a unifying national figure whose political relationships and personal outlook transcend ethnic, religious and regional boundaries. “In the last three years, Tinubu has shown clannishness in governance. His appointments, his policies, his body language—everything screams sectionalism and exclusion. “Atiku Abubakar, on the other hand, is a natural Nigerian devoid of ethnic, religious or sectional inclination. He is a leader for all tribes and regions “, Ologbondiyan said. He argued that Atiku’s family, business and political relationships reflected the diversity of Nigeria and demonstrated his capacity to unite people across the country’s multiple ethnic and religious identities. “Check the people around him over the years. Take a close look at his immediate family, his businesses and his political associates. Atiku represents Nigeria and Nigeria is in him. “He is married across the Niger, his children represent our diversity, and his associates cut across every tribe and religion. That is the definition of a Pan-Nigerian leader,” he said. Ologbondiyan also accused the APC of exploiting Nigeria’s ethnic and religious differences for political advantage rather than promoting national unity and addressing the welfare of citizens. “The APC has so much capitalised on our fault lines to divide the country. “They don’t care about the welfare of the people as far as they can remain in power. ” They are not concerned about our unity but about winning elections against the peace and harmony of the nation,” he further alleged. He also accused the ruling party of deploying divisive political strategies to retain power, expressing confidence that Nigerians would reject such an approach at the next general election. “No government in the history of our country has ever used divisive means to hold on to power more than the APC. But Nigerians are wiser now and ready to kick them out through the ballot,” he said. The ADC-PCC Director maintained that the administration’s alleged sectional approach had failed to translate into improved governance or better living conditions for Nigerians. He argued that the government could not justify its approach to national leadership without delivering tangible results to the people. Ologbondiyan said Atiku’s record, policy proposals and commitment to economic recovery positioned him as the best suited candidate to address the country’s current challenges.

title: FG to Move against Schools over Arbitrary Increase in WAEC Fees
body: Funmi Ogundare The Federal Ministry of Education is taking steps to check schools that arbitrarily increased the 2027 May/June examination fees, the new Head of National Office of the West African Examinations Council (WAEC), Nigeria, Suleiman Danlami Kum, has said. Kum succeeded Dr. Amos Dangut, who was appointed as the new Registrar/Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of WAEC. Speaking with reporters during an inspection of the conduct of the ongoing 2026 West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) for Private Candidates, Second Series, yesterday, Kum said the council was aware that some schools had been charging candidates more than the examination fee ahead of the May/June examination. He, however, clarified that WAEC had yet to release the entries for the forthcoming May/June examination, adding that the Federal Ministry of Education was taking steps to address the issue. “We know in the past that schools have been charging more than the examination fee. But I want to tell you that the Federal Minister of Education is not just sitting down. We thank God for the Minister of Education we have. I want to assure you that something is being done by the Federal Ministry of Education now to check those schools that are increasing these examination fees arbitrarily,” he said. Kum disclosed that more than 56,000 candidates registered for the 2026 WASSCE for Private Candidates, Second Series, nationwide, including about 272 walk-in candidates who registered to sit specific papers after the main registration window had closed. He said that more than 22,000 candidates in Lagos were participating in the examination. He explained that the walk-in arrangement allows candidates who wish to remedy deficiencies in particular subjects to register before the relevant paper is taken and sit the examination on the scheduled day. Kum expressed satisfaction over the conduct of the examination, describing computer-based testing (CBT) as an effective approach to improving examination integrity and reducing malpractice. According to him, WAEC began implementing computer-based examinations in 2024 and has continued to improve the process since its introduction. He said candidates were searched before entering examination halls to prevent them from taking unauthorised materials into the centres, adding that male candidates were searched by male officials and female candidates by female officials. He explained that the screening was intended to prevent malpractice rather than set traps for candidates who might inadvertently carry prohibited materials into the examination hall. “CBT has come to stay,” he said. He added that the CBT approach had made the conduct of examinations more seamless and helped reduce examination malpractice. He reaffirmed the council’s commitment to maintaining examination integrity and introducing innovations to improve its operations. He urged candidates preparing for their examinations to study diligently and make use of WAEC past questions and answers.

title: Declare Hunger a National Emergency, Obi Tells FG, Raises Alarm over Nigeria’s Worsening Hunger Crisis
body: Chuks Okocha in Abuja The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr. Peter Obi, has asked the federal government to declare a national emergency on hunger. Obi made the call in an X post at the weekend to mark World Food Day, saying no Nigerian deserved to go to bed hungry. The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) estimates that about 36 million Nigerians would face acute hunger this year. The former Anambra State governor said Nigeria’s hunger crisis had worsened, with the country ranking 117th out of 125 countries, compared with 109th in 2023, when the current administration took office. While the figure is correct, the 2026 Global Hunger Index (GHI), which Obi cited, ranked Nigeria 117th out of 122 countries. Although 136 countries were assessed for the report, only 122 had sufficient data to calculate hunger scores and determine rankings. Obi said the hunger situation was troubling given Nigeria’s vast arable land, noting that about 60 percent remained uncultivated and provided hideouts for non-state actors. He said hunger, poverty and insecurity continued to affect millions of families despite the country’s agricultural potential. “On World Food Day, the message is clear: Nigerians deserve a country where no family goes to bed hungry, farmers can work without fear, and poverty and insecurity are confronted with urgency and compassion,” he said. The former Anambra State governor said if elected president, his administration would prioritise security and provide farmers with targeted grants, subsidies and other forms of support to boost agricultural production. He said farmers must be able to return to their farms and work in peace and dignity. Obi added that he joined rural women across Nigeria on Friday to mark International Rural Women’s Day, noting that their contributions to food production underscored the need to address hunger as a national emergency.

title: EU: Nigeria’s Poor Population May Be World’s Largest, Commits €45m Aid
body: • Announces € 20m support package for Nigerian armed forces to combat terrorism Linus Aleke in Abuja The European Union (EU) Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, has said Nigeria probably has the highest number of people living below the poverty threshold globally, describing poverty as one of the country’s biggest challenges. This is as it also announced € 20 million in support for the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the European Peace Facility, as part of coordinated efforts to combat terrorism and restore peace to troubled areas across the country. The envoy spoke in Abuja at the weekend at the 2026 International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, where he called for sustained efforts by the federal government, development partners and other stakeholders to address the country’s poverty crisis. “Today, Nigeria is probably the country in the world with the highest number of people living under the poverty threshold,” he said. Mignot also disclosed that the European Union had committed nearly €45million in humanitarian assistance to Nigeria in 2026, particularly to support conflict-affected and crisis-prone areas. He described poverty as a major concern for Nigeria’s international partners, stressing that it required urgent attention and sustained commitment in the years ahead. Mignot cited figures indicating that 133 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty in 2022, adding that estimates from different sources suggested the situation had worsened since then. He said the EU’s humanitarian assistance was being provided through the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, with particular attention to communities affected by conflict and other crises. “Through the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, ECO, the European Union has committed again this year almost 45 million euros for humanitarian assistance in Nigeria, particularly in conflict-affected and crisis-prone areas”. According to him, the EU is working with the Nigerian government, humanitarian organisations, development partners and local communities to ensure that emergency assistance is linked to long-term resilience and sustainable solutions. He explained that humanitarian interventions address immediate needs, while poverty reduction programmes focus on creating lasting pathways out of poverty. Speaking on the theme of the event, United for Peace and Human Rights, Safe Homes for All, the ambassador said meaningful poverty reduction was impossible without peace, security, dignity and respect for human rights. He added that households unable to meet their basic needs could hardly feel secure or fully enjoy their fundamental rights. Mignot acknowledged the federal government’s efforts to tackle poverty through social investment programmes, targeted cash transfers, livelihood support and measures to strengthen social protection systems. He listed the National Social Safety Net Programme, the Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus, and the Renewed Hope Social Protection Programme among the initiatives aimed at supporting vulnerable Nigerians. He also highlighted the Household Prosperity and Empowerment Social Protection Project, supported through Nigeria’s partnership with the World Bank, saying the initiative was expected to improve assistance to vulnerable households and strengthen their resilience. The envoy said the EU was complementing these efforts through its Supporting Sustainable Social Protection Systems in Nigeria programme, which works with government institutions and implementing partners, including UNICEF, GIZ, the International Labour Organisation, ActionAid and Oxfam. He disclosed that the programme covered Abia, Benue, Oyo, Sokoto, Kebbi, Adamawa and Borno states. According to him, the intervention focuses on strengthening social protection policies, expanding social registers to identify more poor and vulnerable households, and improving data systems for planning and resource allocation. Mignot said multidimensional poverty assessments helped governments identify overlapping deprivations in education, healthcare, nutrition and living standards, enabling them to target interventions more effectively. He added that the EU had supported the review of Nigeria’s National Social Protection Policy, as well as the development of state social protection policies and a Social Protection Bill. In related development, the EU also announced € 20 million in support for the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the European Peace Facility, as part of coordinated efforts to combat terrorism and restore peace to troubled areas across the country. Ambassador Mignot announced the support package during a working visit to the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), at his office at Ship House, Abuja. According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the meeting with General Musa also provided an opportunity for both parties to discuss critical bilateral defence agreements, including a review of security co-operation between Nigeria and the EU. Speaking during the visit, Ambassador Mignot commended the minister for his efforts to improve the country’s security situation. He also used the opportunity to invite him to a meeting of defence ministers scheduled to take place in Brussels later in the year. Ambassador Mignot disclosed that an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details of the delivery. He further commended the recent conference of past and serving commanders of the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF), which was attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission. For his part, General Musa expressed gratitude to the EU for its consistent support for Nigeria. He assured the Ambassador of the president’s commitment to ensuring the safety of Nigerians and promoting the country’s development. He explained that relative peace was gradually returning to the country as a result of the commendable efforts of the Armed Forces and other security agencies. However, he noted that kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities remained persistent challenges that the authorities were working to address. In this regard, he said Nigeria was expecting the delivery of ten attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other critical military equipment, with the support of the President. The Minister explained that the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, on which more than 50 million people depend for their livelihoods, remained a potential source of instability. He stressed that denying terrorists access to their strongholds on the islands of Lake Chad remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) Programme, the Minister emphasised that the initiative should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel.

title: MKO: The Story of An Unlikely Hero of Democracy
body: Confession: I despised Gen Sani Abacha with the same intensity Obidients hate President Bola Tinubu. I thought I had overcome the ill-feeling after 28 years. Alas, I watched ‘MKO’ — the documentary on Bashorun Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola currently showing in film houses across Nigeria — and my emotions went haywire again. It brought back painful recollections of military rule and sickening memories of Abacha, the military head of state who chastised Nigeria with scorpions. Media repression and assassinations were the hallmarks of the Abacha regime. It was horror all over again. My emotions swung from nostalgia to despair, from anger to resentment. Three things hit me instantly from the documentary. One, the incredible transformation of Abiola from an establishment person to, as it were, an activist for democracy — like a prince becoming a rebel. Two, the key role Abacha played in the June 12 annulment crisis and how he became the ultimate beneficiary. Three, the place of America in the logjam and the unending suspicion that it played a role in sustaining the annulment and even in the death of Abiola. I went away with a few lessons, chief of which is that life is not black and white. Hardline positions might seem principled and desirable, but pragmatism as an option should always be on the table in playing national politics. Abiola was a friend of power. I remember when he declared his presidential bid ahead of the 1993 election, one well-respected activist said: “President Babangida wants to hand over to one of his friends.” The impression was that he would never have come out without assurances from the powers that be. And, indeed, he did seek and get assurances, according to the man himself. He had been a government insider from the 1970s, when he was in the telecoms equipment business and got huge public contracts. He subsequently went into politics in 1979 and was believed to have supported at least one military coup. As a friend of power, he was quite circumspect in his ways. But in ‘MKO’, we see a transformed Abiola as soon as the election he won in 1993 was about to be truncated. Various historical clips show a defiant Abiola taking on the establishment — the military establishment. After declaring himself president on the eve of the first anniversary of the election in 1994, he was arrested for alleged treason. His aide called the BBC and Abiola went live on air announcing he had been arrested. The BBC anchor asked him why he was still able to speak and Abiola quipped: “They have come to arrest me, not my mouth!” That made me laugh. He was taken to court, denied bail and thrown into the typical Nigerian police cell — a rat hole, dirty and tatty. Abiola could not believe this was happening to him. He was not only regarded as the richest Nigerian at the time but also as an international figure and now effectively the president-elect of the largest black nation, even though his mandate was crushed by the military. Asked, in one of the clips, if he had any regrets, he said: “Any sacrifice is in order if it will bring democracy, peace and prosperity to Nigeria.” That was an amazing statement for a man who had all the comforts of life and did not really have to be a politician or become president. He was the Alhaji Aliko Dangote of that era. Can you imagine Dangote being clamped into a dingy cell for winning an election and claiming his mandate? And, yes, we can say Abiola is the hero of the democracy we enjoy today — though I am aware some characters are still praying for military rule, either because they were born yesterday or are suffering from bitterness-induced and desperation-stirred amnesia. If Abiola had accepted the annulment of June 12 as the “will of God” as we normally do in Nigeria — hiding behind religion — the military would probably have remained in power in civilian cloak, as the case has been with President Teodoro Obiang of Equatorial Guinea since 1979. The trend was for dictators to transition to “democracy” and the transmute to “elected” life presidents. Abacha was on that path in 1998. By standing his ground and refusing to take the easy way out, Abiola complicated the situation. The military authorities could not believe it. They obviously thought a few days in detention would break him and make him renounce his mandate. Why would he swap a waterbed for a six-by-six mattress in a police cell? Why would he swap his private jet for a Black Maria? Why would he swap the bosoms of his harem of wives for an anticlimactic romance with mosquitoes? Yet, Abiola courageously fought on until his suspicious death in detention on July 7, 1998 — a month after Abacha suddenly died also under cloudy circumstances. Abiola had refused to give up the mandate after four years in detention. But for Abiola, maybe we would also not have power rotation today. Between 1960 and 1999, the north dominated the exercise of executive power at the centre, save for the six months of Maj-Gen JT Aguiyi-Ironsi in 1966, the three years and seven months of Gen Olusegun Obasanjo from 1976 to 1979, and the three months of Chief Ernest Shonekan in 1993. Abiola, a southerner, had won the June 12 election fair and square but was denied for no good reason. It was only fair and just, the core northern elite reasoned, that power be conceded to the south in 1999 following Abiola’s sacrifice. Today, there’s a gentleman’s understanding to rotate political power, even if it is not legally binding. The Yoruba also have Abiola to thank for showing them the pragmatic pathway to power. In the First Republic, the core Yoruba elite, led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo, pursued an alternative political strategy that did not sufficiently overcome the electoral arithmetic. The three biggest power blocs in Nigeria, the tripod on which the federation was founded, are the Hausa-Fulani, the Igbo and the Yoruba. The Hausa-Fulani, after winning federal power in 1960 and 1979, allied with the Igbo to run government. Awolowo was an outsider. He preferred to be in opposition. He tried to work with the northern minorities to get power. It did not work. The numbers are clearly with the tripod blocs. In 1979, Abiola chose to work with the Hausa-Fulani and was demonised in Yoruba politics and called a “traitor” like Chief SL Akintola in the First Republic. But he was busy building bridges, even when he felt rejected at some point. He was finally elected president in 1993, getting half of the northern votes, and defeating a northerner in Kano, Borno, Jigawa and Yobe, etc. Obasanjo and Tinubu later became presidents through similar alignments with the core north, an idea Abiola had to suffer for. As I pointed out in my new book, ‘Winning Formula’, being competitive in two out of the tripod blocs has consistently produced winners of the presidential elections since 1999. Abiola saw this ages ago. One major revelation in ‘MKO’, for me, is what Brig Halilu Akilu said happened after Babangida decided to step aside in August 1993 and hand over to an interim government to organise a fresh election. Actually, Babangida had announced that all service chiefs would retire with him. Akilu, the former intelligence chief who hardly grants interviews, said Babangida and Abacha had a stormy meeting on the eve of departure. Akilu said Abacha insisted he would not retire, and Babangida wished him luck serving under Shonekan. I was hearing this bit for the first time. It somehow aligns with Babangida’s claim in his autobiography about the central role of Abacha in the power game. ‘MKO’ also opened my eyes to the ambivalent role of US President Bill Clinton in the saga. Just as supporters of some politicians today believe President Donald Trump will come and remove Tinubu as president, we were all stupidly expecting Clinton to arrest Babangida and Abacha over the June 12 annulment. It was pure fantasy. What ‘MKO’ has done is to put the pieces together: whatever the Americans said about democracy, their economic interests — particularly our “sweet” crude oil — appeared to take precedence when the chips were down. So much for the defence of democracy. I do not know if America killed Abacha and Abiola, but their deaths essentially ended the impasse. Ose Oyamendan, the Nigerian-American filmmaker based mainly in Los Angeles, wrote and directed ‘MKO’. He was my senior at the mass communication department, University of Lagos. He played an important role in kick-starting my journalism career when he gave me a note to Mr Mumini Alao, then editor of Complete Football magazine, for me to undergo my internship at Nigeria’s most prestigious sports publishing outfit. After fleeing from Nigeria to the US in the crazy days of Abacha, Oyamendan transitioned fully from print journalism to filmmaking, even earning a master of fine arts (MFA) degree in film, television and digital filmmaking from the University of Southern California. I recommend ‘MKO’ — which credits Mark Jonathan Harris, three-time Academy Award winner, as executive producer — to anyone who is interested in our political history. It fills a big gap and puts contemporary developments in context for those who genuinely want to see the bigger picture of our politics. I could not believe the calibre of people Oyamendan, who also serves as the narrator, was able to interview. Many of them are now dead; some look very young. The interviews were recorded over 10 years ago. Lest I forget, Amb Babagana Kingibe, Abiola’s running mate who was accused of jumping ship, said he actually watched him draw his last breath that fateful day. Damn! AND FOUR OTHER THINGS… SUICIDE JOKE I have always believed that the most insensitive politician in Nigeria today is Senate President Godswill Akpabio and he has never given me a reason to rethink my conclusion. The other day, he made a cynical joke on a motion to “allow the poor breathe” in view of the prevailing economic hardship. His latest show of insensitivity is on suicide — strongly linked to depression and other forms of mental health challenges. Akpabio is opposing a bill to decriminalise attempted suicide, joking: “If you attempt suicide, you better succeed. If you don’t succeed, we will send you to prison.” Akpabio urgently needs an education on mental health. He has turned a big issue into a joke. Sad. KID YOU NOT In case you missed it, the trial of Alhaji Yahaya Bello, former Kogi governor, continued on Thursday with a bureau de change (BDC) operator testifying at an FCT high court in Abuja. Mallam Jamilu Abdullahi, the 19th prosecution witness in the N110.4 billion alleged fraud trial, said he received N1.4 billion from Alhaji Abba Adaudu, Bello’s associate, between December 15, 2021 and February 21, 2022 and converted it to dollars. He also gave details of the payment of the school fees of Bello’s kids. As we were told by the EFCC before, the payments were for several years ahead. I just imagine what N1.4 billion could have done for school libraries and laboratories in Kogi state. Depressing. ROLLER COASTAL Mr Dave Umahi, minister of works, initially announced that President Bola Tinubu had directed that part of the Lagos-Calabar coastal highway be routed through the existing East-West Road from Ondo into Edo state. Umahi called it “a wonderful engineering decision” in his usual flamboyant language. He subsequently clarified that the original coastal highway project remained intact. The explanations and clarifications have left more questions than answers. Was there a proper engineering survey? Was there an environmental impact assessment? How come the federal government is only now discovering the impact of “climate change” and “flooding challenges” on the project? Messy. NO COMMENTS Vice-President Kashim Shettima was brutally witty at the inauguration of the APC presidential campaign council on Wednesday. “Atiku Abubakar, I will still respect him and call him a former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar,” he said, in response to Atiku’s newfound love of calling the president by his first name. “I will not follow suit with (Babachir) Lawal and call him Kachalla. No.” Kachalla is a leadership title now being used for bandit commanders. Shettima continued: “Atiku Abubakar, who [is contesting] for the presidency for the eighth time, is no Abraham Lincoln. He is more of [Raila] Odinga.” The late Odinga ran for Kenya’s presidency five times without success. Ouch!

title: Stampeders win and await playoff fate
body:
CALGARY – The Calgary Stampeders didn’t know if they were done for the year after their regular-season finale in the CFL.
They avoided elimination from playoff contention with a 32-13 victory over the visiting B.C. Lions on Saturday, but will spend a few days in football limbo during a season-ending bye week awaiting the outcome of next Friday’s game between the Lions and Winnipeg Blue Bombers (8-9) to know their fate.
Calgary (9-9) needs the team they just beat to defeat the Blue Bombers, which would vault the Stampeders into the post-season picture.
It’s an awkward head space for Stampeder coaches and players to be in as they have zero influence over their playoff chances now, and must depend on a divisional rival to do them a favour.
“It’s a little awkward,” concurred Calgary’s quarterback Vernon Adams Jr. “We could have helped ourselves out earlier in the year. You can’t go back on it. It is what it is. We’re just going to sit back and see what happens.”
The Edmonton Elks (13-4) secured first in the West Division with Friday’s win over the Blue Bombers, which also allowed the Lions (10-7) to clinch second.
The Elks will host the division final Nov. 7 with the victor advancing to the Grey Cup game in Calgary on Nov. 15.
The Lions host the division semifinal Oct. 31 with their opponent still to be determined.
The defending Grey Cup champion Roughriders (9-8) can finish no worse than fourth in the West after beating the Montreal Alouettes 16-12 earlier Saturday.
Saskatchewan’s win meant Calgary had to beat the Lions to avoid elimination.
The fourth seed will cross over to meet the Toronto Argonauts in the East Division semifinal. The third seed heads to Vancouver to face the Lions in the West semifinal.
Calgary could conceivably finish third, fourth, or out-of-the-playoffs fifth in the division, but the Lions prevailing Friday is the key to the Stampeders continuing to play this season.
The Blue Bombers went 2-1 against the Stampeders this season, and would thus finish higher in the event of a tie.
“We know the West, it’s always tight and it’s a really good division man, really good teams,” Adams said. “It just sucks that so many close games we lost early on in the season that could have gone a different way, a play here and play there. Just can’t do anything about the past.
Nine wins was enough to make the CFL’s playoff cutline for almost three decades until 2025, when 10-8 was the cutoff. The Stampeders in 2023 were a playoff team at 6-12.
Head coach and general manager Dave Dickenson says the bye week will resemble most, with a few days off before reconvening.
“We’re going to keep working,” Dickenson stated. “We’ll just do a lot of individual stuff, drill work, compete periods, situational football.
“We know we’re going to play, I believe, B.C. or Toronto, so we know it. We’ll keep working and lock in those two opponents. If we get our opportunity, let’s take advantage of it.”
As the Lions began resting more of their starters in Saturday’s game — quarterback Nathan Rourke played just the first half — Calgary took over the game with Adams throwing his first touchdown pass of the game in the fourth quarter.
The game was interrupted for a couple minutes early in the fourth quarter when a pair of rabbits ran amok on the McMahon Stadium turf.
Kicker Rene Paredes intends to retire after a 15-year career, all with the Stampeders, and didn’t know if he’d played his last game in the red and white in a new scenario for the veteran.
“I don’t think I’ve seen it in 15 years,” Paredes said. “We took care of our job. We got to nine and nine and all we can do is just wait until next week. Hopefully we have a shot at playoffs. This team could make a push. If it is my last game, I’m good with it.”
The 41-year-old kicked field goals from 24, 22, 29 and 32 yards, but missed a 57-yard attempt Saturday.
Quincy Vaughn scored a pair of short-yardage touchdowns and Ajou Ajou caught a touchdown pass for Calgary. Adams threw for 324 yards and was intercepted once.
Rourke went 8-for-11 in passing for 149 yards and one touchdown pass in the first half. His backup Kaidon Salter went 6-for-14 in passing for 113 yards and one interception in the second half
Justin McInnis caught a touchdown pass for B.C. Sean Whyte kicked field goals from 48 and 26, but missed from 46.
Saturday’s kickoff was held under sun and a temperature of 16 C, but winds gusted to 53 kilometres per hour out of the west before diminishing during the game.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 17, 2026.

title: Ukrainian drone activity near Zaporozhye NPP, Energodar persists despite ceasefire
body:
MELITOPOL, October 18. /TASS/. The situation at the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) and in the city of Energodar remains tense, with Ukrainian drone activity persisting despite a local ceasefire around the Zaporozhye Thermal Power Plant, Director of Communications of the ZNPP, Evgenia Yashina, told TASS.
"Regarding drone activity, I must unfortunately state that the situation around the plant and its satellite city, Energodar, remains tense. Unmanned aerial vehicle activity persists. As for the situation at the plant itself, it remains tense but under control. Personnel continue to monitor all safety parameters around the clock," Yashina said.
On October 15, Rosatom Director General Alexey Likhachev announced an IAEA-mediated local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine near the Zaporozhye Thermal Power Plant. The pause is required to repair equipment that transmits electricity to the Zaporozhye NPP from the "Ferrosplavnaya-1" high-voltage line, which runs from the Ukrainian-controlled right bank of the Dnieper River. Parts of this equipment were damaged by Ukrainian shelling. Its restoration will secure the nuclear plant's power supply and reduce the risk of future blackouts.

title: Horvat leads Islanders past Maple Leafs 4-1
body:
TORONTO – Bo Horvat scored the winner and added an assist as the New York Islanders cruised past the Toronto Maple Leafs 4-1 on Saturday night.
Simon Holmstrom with two, including one into the empty net, and Anthony Duclair had the other goals for New York (4-3-1). Ilya Sorokin made 28 saves.
Colton Sissons replied for Toronto (3-4-2). Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 16 shots for the Maple Leafs, who have dropped three straight games, and four of their last five.
The Islanders jumped out to a 1-0 lead at 8:18 of the first period when Duclair took a pass in the slot and changed the angle before firing through a partial screen on Bobrovsky.
Coming off a hat trick in Thursday’s 5-4 home shootout loss to the Buffalo Sabres, Maple Leafs winger Kirill Marchenko had a couple of chances that Sorokin turned aside in the second.
No. 1 overall pick Gavin McKenna, who was benched for the second half of Thursday’s contest, had an opportunity to tie things late in the period on a partial breakaway, but fired high and wide. The Islanders raced the other way, with Horvat eventually beating Bobrovsky at 18:33 to double the visitors’ lead.
Sissons got Toronto — which topped New York 2-1 at Scotiabank Arena on Sept. 30 — within one at 3:54 on a tipped shot through traffic, but Holmstrom restored the two-goal lead at 14:08 off a Horvat setup before firing into the empty net with just over two minutes remaining in regulation.
Islanders: Matias Maccelli left the game in the first and didn’t return with an apparent lower-body injury. The winger, who spent last season with Toronto, stepped on the stick of defenceman Darren Raddysh and fell awkwardly.
Maple Leafs: The club announced veteran centre John Tavares is out week-to-week with a lower-body injury suffered Thursday. The 36-year-old has two goals and five assists in seven games this season.
New York killed off a delay-of-game penalty after defenceman Matthew Schaefer fired the puck over the glass midway through the third period with his team up 2-1.
Schaefer, who won last season’s Calder Trophy as NHL rookie of the year and has yet to score this season, remains one goal shy from tying Tim Connolly for the most by a teenager in franchise history with 24. Bryan Trottier tops the list with 32.
Islanders: Host the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday.
Maple Leafs: Host the San Jose Sharks on Monday.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 17, 2026.

title: Iranian fishermen scramble for loot from sunken container ship after explosion
body: The Persian Gulf coast in Iran became the scene of unusual activity this week as local fishermen abandoned their traditional fishing nets and headed into the waters of the Strait of Hormuz in small motorboats and rescue dinghies with one clear goal: to collect valuable cargo floating on the water's surface.According to a report by The Telegraph, a massive shipment containing hundreds of brand-new iPhones, luxury French perfumes, and other consumer goods spilled into the sea following the sinking of the container ship "GFS Pride" on October 14.Videos circulating on social media show dozens of local fishermen navigating between semi-submerged containers while pulling boxes directly from the waves, with one small boat even seen attempting to tow a fully loaded giant shipping container.Authorities in Singapore, where the vessel is flagged, confirmed that the ship sank following a fire that broke out on deck, but all 21 crew members were evacuated unharmed.Conversely, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claimed that the vessel strayed into an "unauthorized and dangerous" lane and struck a naval mine, which sank it along with more than 2,500 containers on board. This is the third vessel to sink in the area since the outbreak of hostilities in late February.Iranians recover new iPhones floating in Strait of Hormuz  https://t.co/V2IakWuW4b https://t.co/WGy6rj9eGP— The Telegraph (@Telegraph) October 16, 2026Surge of hostile IRGC activity in the Strait of HormuzThis incident occurs against the backdrop of a sharp surge in hostile IRGC activity surrounding the strategic strait.Last Friday, Iranian armed forces spokesman Gen. Mohammad Akraminia clarified that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon a full withdrawal of United States forces from the region, threatening that Iranian forces would forcibly expel American troops if they remained.According to him, foreign presence in the area undermines maritime security, and he urged shipowners to utilize only corridors supervised by the Iranian military to ensure their safety.Maritime and land warfare in the region continues unabated. The Iranian Navy reported closely monitoring a fire that broke out aboard an oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman after it attempted to cross a "prohibited zone" while turning off its tracking systems.On the other side of the Arabian Peninsula, the Houthi movement in Yemen tightened its siege on the city of Taiz, while the Saudi-led coalition announced it successfully intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles and drones launched toward Riyadh and Red Sea ports.

title: Greek Restaurants in Dubai’s 2026 Michelin Guide
body: Dubai’s Greek dining scene is represented in the 2026 Michelin Guide, with two restaurants showcasing Hellenic cuisine in a city facing renewed scrutiny over its prestigious restaurant rankings. The latest edition of the guide has attracted controversy after several closed restaurants retained their Michelin stars, prompting questions about how the organisation evaluates establishments during a difficult period for Dubai’s hospitality industry. While the debate has centred on restaurants awarded stars despite being closed, Greek cuisine continues to feature in the emirate’s high-end dining landscape. Two Greek Restaurants Feature in Michelin’s Dubai Guide The Estiatorio Milos and Avli by Tashas are the two restaurants listed under Greek cuisine in the Michelin Guide’s Dubai selection. Estiatorio Milos Estiatorio Milos: Greek Seafood at the Heart of Dubai Located at Atlantis The Royal on Palm Jumeirah, Estiatorio Milos brings a contemporary interpretation of Greek dining to one of Dubai’s most prominent luxury hospitality destinations. The restaurant highlights the flavours of Greece, with seafood, fresh ingredients and traditional Hellenic dishes at the centre of its menu. Michelin praises its Greek offerings, including tomato and aged feta salad, alongside a selection of Greek wines. The restaurant combines Mediterranean culinary traditions with an upscale dining experience aimed at international visitors and Dubai residents. Avli by Tashas: A Taste of Greece Avli by Tashas is the second Greek restaurant appearing in Michelin’s Dubai guide. Its inclusion reflects the continued presence of Greek cuisine in the emirate’s competitive restaurant market, where international culinary traditions compete for the attention of residents and visitors. However, neither Estiatorio Milos nor Avli by Tashas holds a Michelin star in the 2026 Dubai Guide . Both appear in Michelin’s Greek cuisine category, which is distinct from its list of starred restaurants. Michelin Faces Questions Over Closed Restaurants The wider controversy surrounding the 2026 guide centres on establishments that retained their distinctions despite being closed. Michelin has defended the decision, explaining that the restaurants’ distinctions remain based on previous inspections and that its inspectors will reassess them when they reopen. The guide’s fifth Dubai edition, unveiled in October, features 122 restaurants across 38 cuisine types. It also recognises restaurants that have continued to develop their culinary offerings despite challenging conditions for the hospitality sector. For Greek cuisine, the inclusion of Milos and Avli demonstrates that Hellenic dining remains part of Dubai’s international food scene. The post Greek Restaurants in Dubai’s 2026 Michelin Guide appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Israeli TV host calls Gadi Eisenkot a 'monkey', alleges behind-the-scenes control
body: Yinon Magal, host of "The Patriots" on Channel 14, called Yashar party chairman and former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot a "monkey" on Saturday evening, claiming that Ashkenazi Jews were controlling him behind the scenes. The remarks, made during an episode of the political talk show, prompted a sharp response from Eisenkot, who suggested that someone else was behind Magal's comments.During the discussion, Magal said, "He's a monkey, he's a monkey. Are you impressed by the fact that he's Mizrahi?" He later added, "They put a monkey there, and behind him all the elitist Ashkenazim are running him."Magal also singled out Eisenkot's campaign manager, Ronen Manelis, claiming that he controlled Eisenkot and told him what to say. Addressing another panelist, Magal added, "They gave you a Moroccan prime minister, as if we don't see the reality. It's the emperor's new clothes."'The problem is not Yinon Magal,' Eisenkot says in responseEisenkot condemned the remarks, saying, "Yinon Magal said I'm a monkey being controlled by Ashkenazim, so I have nothing to say in response to something this low."He went on to suggest that Magal was acting on behalf of someone else, though he did not identify the person. "The problem is not Yinon Magal, but the man standing behind Yinon Magal."ינון מגל אמר שאני קוף שמופעל על ידי אשכנזים, אז אין לי מה לענות לתת רמה הזו- הבעיה היא לא ינון מגל אלא האיש שעומד מאחורי ינון מגל. אנחנו נביא לשינוי במדינה, את תופעת המגליזם והברדוגיזם אנחנו נעביר מהחיים שלנו ונביא למדינה טובה יותר. https://t.co/NRAMZLWorP— Gadi Eisenkot - גדי איזנקוט (@gadi_eisenkot) October 17, 2026Eisenkot also pledged to bring political change, adding, "We will bring change to the country. We will remove the phenomenon of Magal-ism ... from our lives and bring about a better country."

title: Massive Ukrainian drone attack hit oil facility, bridge, and data centers in St. Petersburg
body:
Editor's note: This story has been updated to include additional details.
Ukrainian forces struck an oil terminal, a data center, and a bridge in a large-scale overnight attack on St. Petersburg on Oct. 18, Russian officials and media reported.
Ukrainian drones hit the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal and a data center belonging to Russia's largest social media platform VK, formerly known as VKontakte .
VK confirmed that a drone had attacked its data center, saying its services remained operational. However, users reported disruptions across the social network and its affiliated platforms, according to Downdetector, a service that tracks online outages.
Russian e-commerce giant Ozon reported a drone attack on one of its logistics centers.
"We evacuated all employees, and no one was injured. A fire broke out, and emergency services are working at the scene," the company wrote on Telegram.
Ozon said some orders may be canceled as deliveries are rerouted to other logistics centers. The company is one of Russia's largest e-commerce platforms and a major rival of Wildberries, often dubbed "Russia's Amazon."
Aleksandr Drozdenko, governor of Leningrad Oblast, said 127 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the region. Drone debris damaged four cars in a parking lot, while fires were reported at several locations.
St. Petersburg Governor Alexander Beglov confirmed the attack, reporting fires at the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchyi oil depot, and industrial warehouses in the Kolpinsky District. According to Beglov, one person was killed and five others injured, while 12 apartment buildings and two houses were damaged.
Russian state media later reported that the number of injured has risen to 10 people, citing the Leningrad Oblast Health Committee.
The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the targets or the extent of the damage at the time of publication.
Ukrainian monitoring channels Exilenova+ and Supernova+ reported that the "massive" drone attack began at 2:50 a.m. local time.
Eyewitness footage shared by St. Petersburg residents appeared to show Ukrainian drones flying over the city as Russian air defense systems operated.
Large explosions lit up the night sky in the city of 5.6 million people, located 850 kilometers (530 miles) north of the Ukrainian border.
Numerous videos appeared to show the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal engulfed in flames. Located in the city's port, the facility is one of Russia's largest fuel storage and export facilities.
It receives and ships petroleum products by river, rail, and road, with a reported annual throughput of 12.5 million tons.
Ukrainian drone manufacturer Fire Point claimed that its FP-1 attack drone was used to strike the terminal.
The strike comes after U.S. President Donald Trump's attempted energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine failed to prevent attacks on energy infrastructure.
Russian independent media outlet Astra also reported that a power substation was hit during the attack. Blackouts and low water pressure were reported in the region, and an apartment building was damaged, according to the outlet.
The strike on VKontakte's data center marks the latest attack on Russian internet infrastructure. Ukrainian forces have struck multiple Yandex data centers in recent weeks, following President Volodymyr Zelensky's promise that Ukraine would "respond in kind" to Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centers.
Ukraine has repeatedly targeted St. Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, several times during the full-scale war. On July 4, Ukrainian forces struck and damaged the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal in an overnight attack.
Asked about Ukraine's latest attacks on St. Petersburg, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov sought to downplay their impact, telling reporters that Ukrainian strikes on Russia were incapable of "changing the course of events."
As Moscow intensifies its attacks on Ukrainian civilian and energy infrastructure, Kyiv has continued to hit sites deep in Russia . Swarm attacks by Ukrainian drones have disrupted air traffic around Moscow and damaged data centers in the capital region in recent days.

title: British, French and German troops to hold exercises in Poland simulating postwar deployment to Ukraine
body:
This was reported by The Times , according to Ukrinform.
According to the publication, at least 1,500 military personnel from these countries will take part in the exercises . They will practice the movement of troops and the delivery of necessary resources, including food and fuel.
The exercises are intended to prepare European forces for a potential post-war mission in Ukraine, where the presence of peacekeepers could serve as a deterrent to Russia. The decision to hold these exercises was agreed upon at the “Coalition of the Willing” summit in July.
British Defense Minister Wes Streeting stated that the exercises will help prepare for supporting Ukraine after hostilities end.
“Next month, thousands of service members will take part in large-scale exercises in Poland to ensure we are ready to support the military training and post-war reconstruction that Ukraine will need,” he said.
Streeting emphasized that Ukraine is on the front lines of the fight for freedom, and that European countries must join forces to ensure peace and counter Russian aggression.
A source in the defense ministry told The Times that the military will practice a scenario in which “multinational forces are stationed together in a single territory.”
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk supported this move, calling the presence of French and British troops “crucial.”
According to the publication, the Polish official also noted that the exercises will strengthen the positions of leading European military powers in confronting the Russian threat.
As reported by Ukrinform , Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated in July that the first exercises of the Coalition of the Willing, involving British and French troops, would take place this fall in Poland.

title: ‘We voted for a reset, not equalization’ – Senyo Hosi on EC appointments
body: Convenor of the One Ghana Movement and policy analyst Senyo Hosi has described President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC) as one of his biggest disappointments with the administration. President Mahama appointed Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission. Ms Agbenyo previously served as an NDC manifesto spokesperson and as Director of Legal Affairs for the party’s Women’s Wing.
