Her appointment has drawn criticism from the New Patriotic Party (NPP), which has called for it to be withdrawn. Mr Kwakye Ofosu has defended the appointments, arguing that a reset could include balancing state institutions he considers to have been unevenly constituted under the previous administration. The debate has centred on how the EC’s leadership appointments may affect perceptions of the commission’s political neutrality and independence. Mr Hosi said the appointment raised concerns about the perceived independence of the electoral management body, particularly given Ms Agbenyo’s previous role as a spokesperson for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) manifesto. He stressed that his criticism was not driven by hostility towards the President, whom he said he liked and respected. “Having said that, this is one of two disappointments I have in the Mahama presidency. I like and I love Mahama. I have to be clear about that,” he said. “Because of the tone of the governance that we saw, this is one of my biggest disappointments. Honestly.” Mr Hosi said his objection was not about Ms Agbenyo’s professional ability, but about the need to protect the EC’s independence and public confidence in its neutrality. “The woman’s competence is not the problem. No, it isn’t. Because that’s not being a matter. Article 46 is about the independence of our electoral commissions,” he said. He argued that independence must not only be guaranteed in law but must also be evident in how the institution is constituted and perceived by the public. “The condition of independence is not just a legal position. It’s something that must be manifestly seen to be delivered,” he said. Mr Hosi also rejected the argument by Minister of State in charge of Government Communications Felix Kwakye Ofosu that a reset of state institutions could involve balancing what the government considers to be a lopsided structure. “Felix, we voted for a reset. We didn’t vote for equalization. We didn’t vote for tilting,” he said. While acknowledging the demands of Mr Kwakye Ofosu’s role, Mr Hosi urged the government to consider how the appointment could affect confidence in the electoral commission. He spoke on TV3. He said the administration’s commitment to governance reform made the decision particularly disappointing to him.

title: Trump vows ‘very good decision’ on anti-Russian sanctions
body:
WASHINGTON, October 18. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump has stated that he intends to make a "very good decision" regarding anti-Russian sanctions, one that will benefit the entire world.
"A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out. It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, according to the White House press pool.
Earlier on Saturday, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Trump set a 60-day window to evaluate the potential consequences of imposing sanctions on Russia, as well as the associated tariffs on other nations, including the impact on both the U.S. and global economies. According to Rubio, this additional analysis is prompted by the current volatility in global energy markets.
Previously, Trump signed an executive order suspending the application of the anti-Russian measures stipulated by the new law, pending further instructions from the president or the secretary of state. On September 18, Trump signed a bill passed by Congress that mandates tougher sanctions against Russia’s top political and military leadership, as well as state-owned enterprises. The legislation includes provisions for a 500% increase in tariffs on imports from Russia, and a 100% increase on imports from countries that are major purchasers of Russian energy. Under the terms of the law, the U.S. administration may opt not to implement these measures if it deems them contrary to the national interests of the United States.

title: Sam George unveils plan to connect 48 government data registries for AI-driven planning
body: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George, has said the government is developing a national data exchange hub to connect 48 data registries across public institutions, as part of efforts to improve national planning and ensure development projects are driven by evidence rather than political considerations. He says the initiative will allow government institutions to share and analyse information across sectors, helping policymakers identify communities’ most pressing needs and allocate resources more effectively. Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum, Mr. George explained that the project forms part of the government’s broader plan to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into public administration. “The finance minister should be able to write a budget that is not driven by sentiments and political rhetoric, but that’s driven by hardcore data at the click of a button,” he said. According to the minister, development decisions are sometimes influenced by political promises and demands from communities rather than a comprehensive assessment of their actual needs. Sam George He explained that politicians campaigning in communities may promise roads or other infrastructure without necessarily having the data to establish whether those projects should take priority over other pressing concerns. Using a hypothetical example, Mr. George said a community might demand a road when available health data could reveal that maternal mortality in the area is 12 per cent higher than the national average. In such circumstances, he argued, investing in a maternity ward or hospital might have a greater impact on the lives of residents. “The reality is, if you took the data sets that were being generated from different registries, for example, the health sector, you’d realise that maternal mortality in that community was 12% higher than the national average,” he explained. “It then meant that the real concern and need of that community, even though they may need a road, the primary thing that will make the lives of those people better would have been a maternity ward or a hospital in there.” The Ningo-Prampram MP believes that access to integrated data will enable government officials to assess competing development priorities more objectively, rather than relying primarily on requests made during political campaigns. “I think that where we should get to as a country is that our interventions in communities must be driven by hardcore empirical evidence,” he stressed. He questioned why decisions about public investments should be influenced primarily by political visibility or the preferences of influential individuals when data could provide a clearer understanding of what communities actually need. “What’s reporting in the hospital? What’s happening to the pass rate in that community?” he asked. “Do we need to invest in that community, not because a chief or an opinion leader thinks that this is a fanciful project they want, or because a politician thinks that this is something that will be visible enough for votes, but what actually makes the lives of the people better?” Connecting government data through AI The minister explained that the proposed data exchange hub is intended to address the fragmentation of information currently held by different public institutions. He said although government agencies generate substantial amounts of data, much of the information remains in separate systems, making it difficult to analyse the country’s development needs comprehensively. The proposed hub will seek to connect 48 registries, allowing information from different sectors to be brought together for analysis and decision-making. “To be able to crunch those numbers, the various data sets, you need a data exchange hub we’re working on to have our 48 registries seamlessly interconnect,” he explained. The initiative is expected to work alongside the government’s proposed national AI compute centre, which will provide the computing infrastructure needed to process large volumes of information. The communications minister said the government has committed US$250 million towards the first phase of the AI compute centre, which it intends to develop with capacity to serve Ghana and other African countries. He believes the two projects could complement each other by making government data more accessible for analysis while providing the technological capacity to identify patterns, assess development needs and support policy decisions. The minister also identified agriculture as another area where the combination of data and artificial intelligence could improve government interventions. He explained that satellite imagery and weather information could be analysed to support agricultural extension services, improve weather predictions and help farmers make better decisions. Beyond development planning, Mr. George said the wider adoption of AI and integrated digital systems could also simplify how citizens access government services. He cited efforts to standardise government forms and improve the delivery of electronic services as part of the ministry’s broader digital transformation agenda. The minister did not specify when the data exchange hub would become fully operational or provide a separate cost estimate for the project. For Mr. George, the ultimate objective is to build a public administration system that understands the needs of citizens and responds to them using reliable information. He believes the successful integration of government data and artificial intelligence could help Ghana move towards more transparent, efficient and responsive public service delivery. “A harmonised system that works for the benefit of the Ghanaian people,” he said, describing his vision of Ghana’s AI-powered future. “I want to leave this ministry with a legacy that we’ve left a digitally inclusive and data-driven economy.” The role of artificial intelligence in improving governance, economic productivity and public service delivery will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?” The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel , will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George; Economist and Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr. Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons. It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m.

title: Parliament must not be a spectator in BRICS decision – Hassan Ayariga
body: The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has called on Parliament to scrutinise the government’s proposed move to join BRICS, warning against excluding elected representatives from major national decisions. In a press statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Dr Ayariga urged the Speaker of Parliament, the Majority and Minority leadership, and all Members of Parliament to demand a comprehensive briefing from the Minister for Foreign Affairs on the proposed partnership. “Parliament must demand a comprehensive briefing from the Minister for Foreign Affairs concerning the proposed BRICS partnership,” he stated. He said the government should present the economic justification, anticipated benefits, potential risks, financial implications and legal obligations associated with Ghana’s proposed participation for parliamentary consideration. According to him, the decision has implications for the country’s economic and political future and should not proceed without adequate scrutiny. Ayariga raises constitutional concerns Dr Ayariga said any arrangement that qualifies as a treaty, agreement or convention under Article 75 of the 1992 Constitution must follow the applicable constitutional ratification procedures. He added that even if parliamentary ratification is not legally required, the significance of the proposed partnership warrants parliamentary debate and public scrutiny. The APC leader also rejected the argument that an electoral victory gives a government unlimited authority to make major national decisions without wider consultation. “We must reject the dangerous notion that once a party wins an election, it acquires unlimited authority to make every major national decision without national debate and collective decision. A President is elected to lead the people to govern themselves, not to dictate to the people,” he stated. Five demands to government Dr Ayariga outlined five measures he wants the government to take before proceeding with the proposed BRICS arrangement. He called for the publication of a comprehensive policy document explaining the objectives, benefits, risks and obligations of participation. He also urged the government to present the proposal to Parliament for debate and any constitutionally required approval, while engaging political parties, civil society organisations, economic experts and business associations in a transparent national consultation. The APC leader further demanded that the government obtain and disclose the relevant constitutional and legal assessment and guarantee that any arrangement would protect Ghana’s economic independence and national sovereignty. ‘Ghana belongs to Ghanaians’ Dr Ayariga said the country’s sovereignty and democratic institutions must remain central to decisions affecting its future. “The Constitution is supreme. Our sovereignty is not negotiable. Our democracy must be protected. Our Parliament must be respected. And our people must never be treated as spectators in decisions that could shape their economic and political future,” he stated. He added: “Ghana is not for sale. Ghana is not the property of any government, President or party. Ghana belongs to Ghanaians. And no matter who occupies the presidency, the Constitution must remain supreme.” Background to Ghana’s BRICS bid The government announced its intention to pursue BRICS membership on October 6, 2026, with Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa saying Cabinet had approved a decision to formally apply to join the bloc. The Minority in Parliament has also called for an urgent briefing on the proposal, demanding greater disclosure of its geopolitical implications and significance for Ghana’s national interests. The calls for parliamentary scrutiny come as the government seeks to broaden Ghana’s international partnerships through engagement with emerging economies.

title: Trump takes 60 days to assess impact of potential sanctions against Russia — Rubio
body:
WASHINGTON, October 18. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump intends to use a 60-day window to evaluate how potential sanctions against Russia and related tariffs on other nations could affect the US and global economies, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters.
"The problem is these sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries, India, for example, and others. And so, I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy," Rubio said.
The secretary of state noted that the additional analysis is prompted by tensions in global energy markets. He highlighted that energy supplies are facing pressures from the situation involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and strikes on energy infrastructure during the Russia-Ukraine conflict, all of which drive global energy prices.
Rubio also pointed to India, which, he said, is "voluntarily diversifying their energy portfolio" but still imports "substantial amount of energy from Russia because it is hard to pivot everything from one day to the next."
"But they [India] are also an important ally and partner of the United States," he remarked, emphasizing that Washington must weigh these factors to find the optimal mix of sanctions and tariffs.

title: Japan Motors MD Salem Kalmoni named CIMG Marketing Man of the Year
body: The Managing Director of Japan Motors, Salem Kalmoni, has been named Marketing Man of the Year at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards organised by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG). The award was presented at a ceremony at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, 2026, as part of the institute’s annual recognition of outstanding achievements in marketing. According to the official 2025 award winners’ list, Mr Kalmoni received the top individual honour in recognition of his contribution to marketing and business leadership. The CIMG Awards also recognised professionals across different areas of the marketing industry. Abena Amoah, Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange, was named Marketing Woman of the Year. Mavis Frimpong, Head of Corporate Communications, Marketing and Brands at Consolidated Bank Ghana Limited, received the Marketing Practitioner of the Year award, while Thomasina Tetey, Import Sales Manager at MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company, was named Marketing Student of the Year. The CIMG Annual National Marketing Performance Awards recognise individuals and organisations for their achievements in marketing and their contributions to business development in Ghana. The annual ceremony brings together professionals and organisations to celebrate marketing performance and highlight the role of marketing in organisational growth and engagement with consumers.

title: Russia's Battlegroup Center destroys Ukrainian unit of about 2,000 troops in Dobropolye
body:
DONETSK, October 18. /TASS/. A Ukrainian military unit numbering around 2,000 troops has been destroyed in Dobropolye after the entire force became trapped in the city, TASS reported on Sunday, citing the reconnaissance chief of the 110th Brigade of Russia's Battlegroup Center, who goes by the call sign "Udav" (Boa).
"The unit consisted of about 2,000 personnel. As of now, it has been completely destroyed," the reconnaissance chief said.
According to the serviceman, the initial Ukrainian force in Dobropolye did not exceed 1,300 troops. The Ukrainian command later reinforced the unit, only to effectively abandon them after they were encircled.

title: Kromberg and Schubert electrical wiring plant in Lutsk halts operations following Russian attack
body:
A Kromberg & Schubert electrical wiring plant in the city of Lutsk halted operations due to Russian attacks on the facility, the company announced on Oct. 17.
"The business has stopped!" said the company's Ukrainian division in a social media post. "Our absolute priority is the safety, life and health of each of the employees. We are currently assessing the current circumstances and coordinating all further steps."
The Lutsk facility in northwestern Ukraine, which manufactures wiring systems for BMW, Audi, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and Skoda vehicles, was attacked by Russian drones on Oct. 16.
Kromberg & Schubert, a German-owned corporation, established its Ukrainian division in 2005 and had 5,500 workers at its Lutsk plant as of May 2025, according to its website .
The company said it will notify employees when they can return to work, though it did not give an estimate of how long that may take.
Though far from the front lines, Lutsk has been a target for Russian strikes since the full-scale invasion began in 2022.
On Oct. 14, Russian drones killed six people and injured 10 others in Lutsk. A large-scale fire broke out in the 'Eurogroup' warehouse as a result of the Russian attack, killing five people at the scene and injuring a sixth person so severely that they succumbed in hospital, regional governor Roman Romaniuk said .
Throughout the war, Moscow has struck foreign-owned businesses operating in Ukraine. On Sept. 3, a Coca-Cola facility outside of Kyiv was damaged in Russian attacks, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed was "a clear Russian signal to America."

title: Greece explains why it is not supplying Patriot missiles to Ukraine
body:
Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis made this statement at a press conference following the European Council meeting in Brussels, while responding to a question about the possible transfer of interceptor missiles for Patriot systems to Ukraine, according to Ukrinform.
“You know we have supported Ukraine with significant anti-aircraft capabilities from our stockpiles. At the same time, I want be very, very honest: we will do the best that we can to support Ukraine, without compromising the defence posture of Greece,” Mitsotakis replied.
He added that Greece is also located in a challenging geopolitical region and has other obligations.
As reported by Ukrinform, The Telegraph wrote that Greece and Spain have interceptor missiles for Patriot systems in their stockpiles that are nearing the end of their service life and could strengthen Ukraine’s air defense. However, they refused to transfer them to Ukraine.
During a briefing in Brussels, President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that European countries have a sufficient number of PAC-2 and PAC-3 anti-ballistic missiles to meet Ukraine’s minimum needs this winter.

title: Ukraine currently lacks access to Starshield military communications system — Rubio
body:
WASHINGTON, October 18. /TASS/. Ukraine does not currently have access to the Starshield satellite communications system, and the matter is under discussion, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday.
"Starlink is a commercial product and it's regulated and handled as a commercial product. Starshield is a defense product, a military product, and as I said, I mean that that is something that we have and the United States military uses. It's not at this moment available to Ukraine, and that's under conversation. It's under discussion right now of how they would want to use it," he told reporters before flying to Uzbekistan.
According to the secretary of state, Ukraine "asked for access to it in order to conduct deep strikes inside Russia." "They do not have access to it at this moment," he emphasized.

title: NY announces game ownership bill requiring ownership rather than licensing
body:
New York joins Pennsylvania in protecting gamers.
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .
Rep. Ritchie Torres of New York's 15th congressional district has introduced the Power To The Players Act . This new legislation aims to protect consumers by directing the FTC to establish regulations on game ownership to curb anti-consumer business practices. "Under the bill, buying a video game would give the consumer ownership of the game rather than a license to play it," the release says. "Games with online functionality would also be required to provide an offline mode before the servers supporting them are shut down."
Games having an expiration date despite being more expensive than ever has been scrutinized by players all over the world, along with aggressive monetization schemes within the games themselves. Rep. Ritchie Torres isn’t the first to fight for gamers, as Pennsylvania state senator John Kane also recently introduced the Protect Our Games Act , requiring publishers to provide an offline mode, community servers, or a 25% minimum refund. Players want to be able to enjoy their games even if the publisher decides to stop supporting the game, but Sony doesn’t think the players own their games and that they have the right to pull the rug from under them. Sony’s lawyers even recently said in a defense in an ongoing class action lawsuit that clicking on the “purchase” button would obviously not lead the consumer to think that they were acquiring a durable right to use the game instead of a revocable license; basically a one-time rent fee that Sony could take away at any moment that benefits them.
One of the most prominent recent examples of players not owning their games came in 2024 with The Crew , an online-only racing game that Ubisoft shut down for server upkeep, making it unplayable even for those who had recently purchased it. Ubisoft had not provided a way for community servers to be set up, nor an offline mode, since even the single-player campaign depended on a connection to Ubisoft’s servers. Another is the notorious yearly sports games released by EA, 2K, and Sony, with NBA 2K25 specifically being cited by Rep. Torres in his announcement of the Power to the Players Act ; NBA 2K25 is being pulled from digital storefronts, with the online servers being shut down only two years after release, leaving players unable to use a main feature of the game they purchased, and new players unable to purchase the game at all. Overwatch 2’s release also killed the first Overwatch game, replacing it outright instead of the first game becoming a purchasable and separately playable game.
The Crew’s shutdown prompted the Stop Killing Games movement, demanding that publishers leave the games functional after discontinuation in the form of an offline mode, peer-to-peer patching, and the ability to host community servers. The movement also pushes back against the industry standard of selling games as revocable licenses rather than outright ownership of the copy. Concrete definitions and details of the bill have yet to be released, but it aims to require publishers to provide an offline mode before shutting down servers and actual consumer ownership instead of a license that can be taken away, potentially satisfying the demands of the movement. We don’t know whether the right to transfer that Rep. Torres mentions is mandatory for digital purchases, but it will likely be relevant for physical copies. It is also important for the bill to strictly define what ownership is and what rights the owners have over their copy.
One popular phrase against these practices is “If buying isn’t owning, piracy isn’t stealing,” pushing strongly against these revocable licenses that the companies want you to purchase. Piracy is often touted as a better experience by players, as it removes DRM that often slows games down and provides a permanent copy that the publishers cannot modify to be dysfunctional; many players say they would be more glad to purchase the game if it were actually a better experience. It is still yet to be known how well the bill will execute its aims, but this is a big step towards correcting the direction the gaming industry is currently on.

title: Russia sees Europe’s need for Russian fuel — deputy premier
body:
MOSCOW, October 17. /TASS/. Russia sees continued interest in Russian fuel from European consumers, including amid calls in Germany to resume purchases of Russian gas, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said in an interview to Marina Kim on the Soloviev Live television.
"Recently, we have seen more and more politicians and countries saying that it was a mistake to stop purchases of Russian gas or Russian oil, or petroleum products," he said. "The countries that still benefit from exemptions are calling for these exemptions to be extended. In other words, we see interest in Russian energy resources."

title: John Kiriakou Makes His Case to Be US Ambassador to Greece
body: “I’m your guy”: Ex-CIA officer John Kiriakou makes his case to be US ambassador to Greece The Greek American whistleblower is pushing back on reports that called his bid “half-joking”. Former CIA officer and whistleblower John Kiriakou is making a bid to become the next US ambassador to Greece, and he is pushing back on suggestions that he isn’t serious. My pitch to be US ambassador to Greece made it into the country’s biggest newspapers! A little confused why they say I made the pitch “half-joking”? https://t.co/ZDI6VWzBbO pic.twitter.com/PWM4eKymt1 — John Kiriakou (@JohnKiriakou) October 17, 2026 After Kathimerini described the bid as “half-joking”, Kiriakou responded on X: “My pitch to be US ambassador to Greece made it into the country’s biggest newspapers! A little confused why they say I made the pitch ‘half-joking’?” The ambassadorship became vacant after Kimberly Guilfoyle left the post following allegations of misconduct. Career diplomat Josh Huck is now leading the US Embassy in Athens as chargé d’affaires ad interim. “Athens like the back of his hand” Kiriakou put his name forward on X on 15 October, appealing directly to President Donald Trump. “Folks, the Greek ambassadorship is open. President Trump, I know you love a dark horse candidate. Especially one who has been unjustly persecuted by the Obama DOJ,” he wrote. “If you want someone who knows Athens like the back of his hand from hunting terrorists, I’m your guy.” He set out his case in more detail on his podcast, John Kiriakou’s Briefing Room , pointing to his Greek heritage and years of experience in the country. “I don’t know what my chances are, but I would like to throw my hat in the ring here to be ambassador to Greece,” he said. He argued that Greece deserved a US ambassador who knew its culture and people and was committed to transparency. Kiriakou acknowledged that he would need a presidential pardon to take up the post. “Mr President, if you are looking for a bold, unexpected choice that’s gonna distract people from the midterm elections, I’m the guy,” he said. From Athens station to whistleblower Kiriakou, 62, worked for the CIA from 1990 to 2004. From 1998 to 2000 he was a counterterrorism operations officer based at the US Embassy in Athens. He later served on the staff of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee from 2009 to May 2011. He became one of America’s best-known whistleblowers after publicly disclosing details of the CIA’s use of waterboarding in interrogations. He was later jailed for disclosing the identities of two CIA officers. He recounted his intelligence career in his book The Reluctant Spy: My Secret Life in the CIA’s War on Terror . Sources: John Kiriakou on X; Kathimerini The post John Kiriakou Makes His Case to Be US Ambassador to Greece appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: MyJoyOnline wins CIMG Online News Portal of the Year award 2025
body: MyJoyOnline.com has been named Marketing-Oriented Online News Portal of the Year for 2025 at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards organised by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG). The award was presented at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, 2026, in recognition of the portal’s commitment to quality journalism, public service and impactful storytelling. In its citation, CIMG commended the portal for delivering timely Ghanaian news and public-interest coverage to digital audiences. “Myjoyonline.com has helped Multimedia Ghana Limited bring timely Ghanaian news and public-interest coverage to digital audiences,” the citation read. It added that cross-platform publishing and audience measurement help the portal reach audiences through the channels they use daily. CIMG singled out the portal’s coverage of critical national issues, including its Poisoned for Gold investigation, as an example of journalism that promotes public awareness and accountability. “Through your 24-hour newsroom operations, responsive audience engagement, and compelling coverage of critical national issues, including Poisoned for Gold, you continue to strengthen public awareness, promote accountability, and advance national discourse,” the citation stated. The institute also praised MyJoyOnline.com for amplifying the voices of underserved communities and recognising individuals whose contributions might otherwise go unnoticed. It highlighted initiatives such as the Joy Impact Makers Awards, saying the portal’s commitment to community-centred journalism demonstrated the media’s potential to shape society and support positive change. “Your sustained commitment to community-centred journalism and the recognition of unsung heroes exemplify the transformative power of the media in shaping society and driving positive change,” the citation read. CIMG assessors also commended the portal’s approach to digital publishing, which combines news reporting, video and online engagement to serve different audience groups. “Our assessors described the cross-platform publishing as impressive with news and everyday information speaking to varied audience segments. Its blend of reporting, video and online conversation demonstrates the value of a responsive news service,” the citation stated. MyJoyOnline.com is the digital news platform of the Multimedia Group, providing news, analysis and multimedia content to audiences in Ghana and abroad. Its induction into the CIMG Hall of Fame earlier in 2026, alongside the latest award, adds to its recognition within Ghana’s media and marketing industry.

title: A Serres Sheepfold Hides Far More Than Cannabis
body: Police arrested a sheepfold owner in northern Greece after officers found cannabis plants growing beside hundreds of suspected Serres antiquities, from bronze coins and arrowheads to lamps and figurines. Officers from the Hellenic Police drug squad of the Serres Crime Investigation Sub-directorate made the arrest on Friday, 16 October. The man faces charges under Greece’s drug laws and its laws protecting antiquities and cultural heritage. Initially, police stopped the man and found two packages of raw cannabis weighing 9.8 grams on him. A search of his sheepfold, in the wider Serres area, followed. There, officers found seven cannabis plants, between 1.3 and 2 metres tall, growing in pots. They uprooted and seized the plants, along with six packages weighing 86 grams, 1.69 kilograms of cannabis plant material and a precision scale. Inside the Serres antiquities haul In the same building, police seized 214 bronze coins, 42 bronze arrowheads and 28 lead sling bullets. Investigators also recovered 21 bronze bracelets plus part of another, 19 lamps and 17 figurines or figurine fragments. Next on the list came 16 bronze rings, 11 bronze pendants and 10 clay perfume vessels. Eight clay vessels, among them a cup, drinking cups known as skyphoi and a small amphora, as well as 26 other objects, complete the Serres antiquities. An archaeologist from the Ephorate of Antiquities made a first assessment. In that view, the Serres antiquities fall under the protective provisions of Greece’s antiquities law. Police seized a further 90 coins, 74 metal objects and 10 silver coins, as well as eight fragments of copper slag and six of silver slag. Those items will now go for further examination. Cannabis at a second property Later, a search of a house the man used turned up four more packages of raw cannabis weighing 489.8 grams. Officers also found a second precision scale there. Following the arrest, police took the man before the Serres public prosecutor. His case then went to an investigating magistrate. Authorities have not named the suspect or given his age. Nor have they said where the Serres antiquities came from or how long he kept them. Looting has troubled the region before. In March 2025, the Culture Ministry suspended a night guard at the local ephorate over his alleged role in a looting network. That same month, police broke up antiquities smuggling rings across northern Greece , arresting 23 suspects. Source: Kathimerini The post A Serres Sheepfold Hides Far More Than Cannabis appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Ghana must protect national interest in pursuit of BRICS membership – Hassan Ayariga
body: The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has cautioned Ghana against exchanging one form of economic dependency for another as the government pursues membership of the BRICS economic bloc. In a press statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Ayariga said he was not opposed to Ghana establishing strategic relationships with BRICS countries but insisted that such partnerships must protect the country’s national interests, constitutional governance and democratic accountability. He argued that any move to join the bloc must deliver tangible benefits for Ghanaian citizens and businesses rather than create new forms of economic dependence. “For decades, African countries have struggled with economic dependency, foreign control of strategic resources, unequal trade relationships and limited industrial development. We must not repeat the mistakes of the past,” he said. “If Ghana seeks to join BRICS to diversify its international relationships, that objective must translate into tangible benefits for Ghanaian citizens and businesses.” Hassan Ayariga said Ghana’s gold, oil, minerals, agricultural resources and strategic infrastructure must be managed in ways that support national development. He criticised the continued export of raw materials with limited local processing, arguing that Ghana must strengthen its industrial capacity and retain more value from its natural resources. “We cannot continue exporting our raw materials cheaply, importing finished products at enormous costs and allowing foreign interests to dominate strategic sectors of our economy,” he stated. He said Ghana’s approach to international partnerships should be guided by the same principles, regardless of whether potential partners come from Europe, America, Asia or the Middle East. “Whether our partners come from Europe, America, Asia, the Middle East or elsewhere, the guiding principle must remain the same: Ghana first. Ghanaians first. National interest first,” he said. “International cooperation must strengthen our sovereignty, not weaken it.” The APC leader also called for clarity on the terms and implications of Ghana’s proposed BRICS membership. He questioned the economic and diplomatic obligations the country might assume, the level of influence it could exercise within the grouping and the practical benefits for ordinary Ghanaians. “What exactly does Ghana stand to gain? What obligations will Ghana assume? What are the potential economic, political and diplomatic consequences? Will Ghana become a full member or merely a partner country?” he asked. He further questioned whether Ghana would have meaningful influence in decision-making or become a participant in a grouping dominated by larger economies. Hassan Ayariga said the government must also explain how the proposed partnership would benefit farmers, traders, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and other businesses. He maintained that such questions should be treated as matters of national interest rather than dismissed as political opposition. The government announced its intention to pursue BRICS membership on October 6, 2026, with Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa saying Cabinet had approved a decision to formally apply to join the bloc. The government has said the move is intended to diversify Ghana’s international partnerships and create opportunities for trade, investment and economic cooperation.

title: Greek Households Circle Seven Dates Before New Year
body: Greek households and pensioners can expect fuel subsidies, a rent rebate and a bigger heating allowance before the new year under a winter support plan the government is preparing as energy prices climb. With oil trading near US$110 a barrel and natural gas at levels last seen in the energy crisis, the government’s economic team wants enough fiscal room to keep support going all winter. The Ministry of National Economy and Finance sits at the centre of that team. Officials expect a demanding season because of high energy costs. Still, the dates remain provisional, and amounts may change. Key dates in the winter support plan November brings the first milestones. New subsidies for heating oil, diesel and unleaded petrol are due on 2 and 16 November, with amounts set to match market conditions at the time. On 30 November, more than €1.1 billion is due to reach households. That sum includes the rent rebate and a one-off €400 payment to pensioners over 65. Under the winter support plan, December then brings further fuel subsidy rounds on the 1st and the 15th of the month. Next, the heating allowance falls due on 23 December. Officials expect it to rise by 30 per cent. Higher 2027 pensions follow on 27 December. Based on current estimates, the increase could exceed the 2.8 per cent written into the 2027 budget . More help depends on Brussels At the same time, Athens awaits a decision from the European Commission on its request for extra fiscal space. A green light could open the way for new measures early in the new year. Options for widening the winter support plan include a new “cost-of-living cheque” for vulnerable households and families with children. Measures to hold down ferry ticket prices could also continue. In addition, the winter support plan may add one-off, income-tested payments. That way, help would go to those most in need. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis warned of a difficult winter on 14 October. He pointed to the 30 per cent rise in the heating allowance for 1.2 million households. Earlier, the government extended its fuel subsidy scheme to heating oil from 15 October, Greek City Times reported . Source: ERT News The post Greek Households Circle Seven Dates Before New Year appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Greece Returns to the Desert Where 89 Soldiers Fell
body: EL ALAMEIN, October 2026 — Greece honoured the 89 officers and soldiers of its 1st Brigade who fell in Egypt in 1942, as Deputy Defence Minister Thanasis Davakis attended the El Alamein anniversary ceremony on Saturday. Davakis represented the Greek government at the Greek Military Memorial of El Alamein, marking 84 years since the battle. The Ministry of National Defence sent him to pay tribute to Greeks who died fighting alongside the Allies against Nazism. A memorial service opened the El Alamein anniversary, followed by the traditional roll call of the dead. Davakis then laid a wreath at the memorial to the fallen. Greece’s ambassador to Egypt, Nikolaos Papageorgiou, attended, as did Cyprus’s ambassador, Elena Rafti, and Germany’s ambassador, Jürgen Schulz. Air Vice Marshal Konstantinos Bouzos, chief of staff of the Hellenic National Defence General Staff , represented the armed forces. Members of the Greek community, pupils from Greek schools in Egypt and scouts also took part. Davakis at the El Alamein anniversary In his El Alamein anniversary address, Davakis stressed the weight of the Greek fighters’ sacrifice in the Middle East. At the time, Greece itself lay under a triple occupation. “We stand here today with a feeling of deep reverence and national pride at this sacred spot in the Egyptian desert,” Davakis said. “At the sacred place where Greek virtue, the unbowed spirit and self-sacrifice met world history.” He described how the flame of Greek freedom passed to the Middle East. Volunteers from the Egyptian Greek community joined hundreds of officers and soldiers who crossed the sea despite great danger, he said. Greeks in the Allied front line Under Colonel Pafsanias Katsotas, the 1st Greek Brigade fought on the front line within the British Eighth Army, Davakis said. Greek naval and air force units also served there. Those forces were not mere observers, he said, but paid a heavy toll in blood for the freedom of Europe. The Second Battle of El Alamein ran from 23 October to early November 1942. It ended in an Allied victory over German and Italian forces in North Africa. Greek airmen also played a part. Last October, the Hellenic Air Force honoured Greek and British pilots who flew together in the desert. Earlier this year, Davakis also represented the government at the 85th anniversary of the Battle of Crete in Chania. Each El Alamein anniversary draws Greeks from across Egypt to the desert memorial. Source: Ta Nea The post Greece Returns to the Desert Where 89 Soldiers Fell appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Internet Café Players Never Stood a Chance, Police Say
body: Police have broken up a Thessaloniki gambling ring that allegedly rigged games at internet cafés in two northern Greek cities, arresting 20 people and putting its illegal gains at more than €1 million. Officers from the Hellenic Police Northern Greece Organised Crime Sub-directorate led the operation, with help from forensic investigators. The Thessaloniki gambling ring also operated in Kavala. Of the 20 people arrested, 18 are alleged members of the Thessaloniki gambling ring, including its leaders. The other two were players. Police also built a case against 14 more people. Depending on the individual, charges include membership of a criminal organisation, felony fraud, breaches of gaming laws, money laundering and personal data offences. How the Thessaloniki gambling ring worked Two leading members, aged 55 and 51, built a hierarchical group with distinct roles, investigators found. A months-long Financial Crimes Unit inquiry traced their activity back to at least 2013. The Thessaloniki gambling ring ran premises licensed as food and drink outlets, mostly internet cafés. Illegal games of chance ran there on special software. That software let the leaders set payouts and choose which players would win, bypassing the games’ random mechanism. As a result, players never knew their true chances of winning. To avoid detection, the cafés kept a separate room with controlled entry, while lookouts stood watch. Staff could also press a panic button that changed what the computer screens showed whenever they spotted police. Police said the 55-year-old allegedly held the central coordinating role, deciding how the shops ran, who joined and who did what. He also managed the profits and watched staff through CCTV cameras in the shops. A 68-year-old, one of his deputies, allegedly ran the staff, the cash flow, the daily takings, as well as technical support. Bank accounts belonging to a 51-year-old woman allegedly helped move and hide the money. Another deputy, aged 40, allegedly ran the software remotely, trained staff and, on the leader’s orders, could pick winning players. Money, straw men and seizures Some members allegedly posed as owners of the companies behind the shops. These straw men hid the real owners and helped the Thessaloniki gambling ring avoid tax and employer contributions, police said. Two of the leading members spent far more than their declared incomes, a parallel financial probe found. Takings also moved through specific people, bank accounts and betting accounts to disguise their origin. Given its activity since 2013, police estimate the total illegal gain of the Thessaloniki gambling ring at more than €1 million. Anti-money laundering authorities have frozen bank and betting accounts belonging to the leading members. Searches of homes, shops and vehicles turned up €61,460 and US$700 in cash, 11 gold sovereigns, jewellery and four cars. Officers also seized 28 mobile phones, 61 computer units, 21 cameras, 22 hard drives and handwritten notes. Following the arrests, police took the suspects before the prosecutor, who released the two players on an oral order. Illegal gambling remains a target for Greek authorities, and the Hellenic Gaming Commission regulates legal gaming. In March, police dismantled a separate network that allegedly made more than €16 million. Earlier, in February, the finance ministry was preparing a bill with jail terms of up to 10 years for illegal gambling. Source: Athens-Macedonian News Agency (AMNA) The post Internet Café Players Never Stood a Chance, Police Say appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Oregon governor Tina Kotek reacts to Silver Rail Elementary school shooting
body:
NPR's Joel Rose talks with Oregon Governor Tina Kotek about the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon.
JOEL ROSE, HOST: Just days after the attack on Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend Oregon, new details are emerging about the heroic efforts of bystanders to stop the shooter and about the victims, three children and a teacher who were killed in the attack. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) MIKE KRANTZ: The 5-year-old boy is identified at the request of his family as Rhoam Summer. ROSE: Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz, speaking at a press conference yesterday. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) KRANTZ: The teacher who was killed and has been identified is 25-year-old Megan Lambert of Bend. ROSE: A police spokesperson shared a statement from Lambert's family. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) UNIDENTIFIED SPOKESPERSON: Her goal was to be an educator and teach in the school district she loved growing up in. She loved Silver Rail. This was her dream job. Megan was compassionate and had a huge heart. She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs. She was an incredible sister, daughter, niece and granddaughter. ROSE: And we've learned more about the brave actions of bystanders that day. Again, Police Chief Krantz. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) KRANTZ: A teacher in the classroom threw her cell phone at the suspect and then tackled him and fought to take the firearm from him. She was not injured in that incident, but she almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed. ROSE: The attacker was followed into the school by a father of two students at Silver Rail. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) KRANTZ: He then went to the classroom where the struggle was underway and fired his weapon, striking the suspect multiple times. ROSE: Through it all, community members in Bend have been gathering to mourn and to remember the lives of those lost. UNIDENTIFIED GROUP: (Singing) Now I'm found (ph). ROSE: Oregon Public Broadcasting reporter Holly Bartholomew was at a vigil last night and talked with Matthew McCarthy, whose mother works at Silver Rail. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED NPR CONTENT) MATTHEW MCCARTHY: No one really expected it to happen here, but, like, at the same time, it was, like, you know, you always go to it with that thought, like, every morning. Like, my mom works at Silver Rail. She had that thought every day. ROSE: I want to bring in Oregon governor Tina Kotek now, a Democrat. Welcome to the program, Governor. TINA KOTEK: Thank you, Joel. ROSE: First of all, are there any updates you can provide about the investigation into this shooting? KOTEK: Not at the moment. The press conference yesterday was pretty extensive, and it's an ongoing investigation. And I really appreciate all the outpouring nationally of just well wishes and condolences coming from across the country and people just wanting to know how they can help. And we're still in that, you know, first 48 hours of just trying to understand it. And it's going to be a couple more days before we know all the details. ROSE: Are there any details you've learned about the other victims which might help us understand, you know, a little bit more about who they were? KOTEK: Not yet. Everyone is appropriately trying to respect their privacy. There hasn't been the announcements other than the ones you just spoke about. I did have a chance to talk to the mother of Megan Lambert, and obviously, they are heartbroken. Megan was an amazing teacher and volleyball coach loved in the community. And, you know, we have to remember that these events have so much ripple effect across the community, people knowing someone who knows someone or knowing them in all kinds of different contexts. This is such a big shock and pain in the community right now, and people are holding each other up and still just trying to make sense of it, if you even can. ROSE: Is there any more information you can give us about the shooter's motives? I know that's a question a lot of people are still asking. KOTEK: I think that's what you see in these situations. People want to know why. We don't have that kind of information. Remember, this was also a child. The shooter was 16 years old. And it's just - you know, we see these patterns, and people want to know what the situation is. It'll be days before we have more information about the background there. What I'm focused on right now is making sure the school district has what it needs, that the community has what it needs. This is a disaster, I mean, in the most fundamental sense of the word. And so everyone is trying to make sure there are mental health resources, that the immediate needs of some of the people who have been injured are being met. And this - here's what I know. I hear from other governors, you know, to be a governor, to get this phone call, it's the worst thing you want to have happen. But the outreach from both Republican and Democratic governors alike who have experienced these types of mass shooting incidents in their states, you know, offering advice - this is going to take time, and the thing is we just need to stick with the community who will have a long process of healing from this. ROSE: Governor Kotek, do you know how the shooter, who was 16 years old, got access to the firearm and ammunition? KOTEK: I do not have that information. We have - you know, we believe adults should be responsible. We don't know how the gun ended up with the 16-year-old. And - but it's a question everyone is asking. ROSE: Some outlets are saying that the gun was registered to the mother. Can you confirm that? KOTEK: I have seen that. I can't confirm that. I am letting law enforcement do their job and getting updates as they have them, but this - you know, it's an ongoing investigation, so I can't speak to that. ROSE: Oregon gun law does have some exceptions that allow minors to possess long guns if their gun is given to the minor by a parent or a guardian, for example, or with their consent. Do you plan to revisit that in the aftermath of this shooting? KOTEK: Well, I - you know, as governor, I've been a strong proponent of our gun violence prevention policies, and we've had success here in the state doing evidence-based, reasonable approaches to help people be safe with their firearms. Our law does say that if you are under 18 and have access to that gun, that's because your parent or guardian have given you that permission to have that gun. I think there'll be a lot of questions about that going forward. And I don't - to be honest, it's just too soon to jump into those conversations, but I know that people are going to want to have them. ROSE: One of the most remarkable things about this tragedy is that a community member with a gun was able to intervene and to kill the shooter. I wonder, has that changed anything about your thinking around gun laws? KOTEK: Well, I have - you know, you have to do - you have to praise the adults who jumped in. The individual who came into the school after witnessing the 16-year-old coming into the school, the teachers in the classroom fighting to protect the children - it is - and that's - it is both heroic, and you have to say, we shouldn't have to have that. And so, you know, when you have a gun involved, people are going to get hurt. And I know that, you know, the way people have responded in such quick thinking is why there wasn't more death or injury in this situation. And I want to, you know, praise the Bend-La Pine School District. They have - they've done the things they've needed to do. They had security locks on their doors. They, you know, have been training for these things. You hate to say, we have to train for them, but they were ready in - when it happened to keep as many kids safe as possible. I just want us to get to a place in this country where we don't have to be doing those trainings and those protocols. We just shouldn't have this happening in our schools. ROSE: You are up for reelection next month, and it is a fairly tight race between you and your Republican counterpart. Should gun control be a key issue, do you think, in this election? KOTEK: Oh, I don't think any of us should be politicizing this incident. I mean, this is - our job is the stand up for the community right now. And as you have seen across the country, after these events have happened and people have had a chance to think about it, there will be a discussion, probably next year. But right now, I'm focused on the community and making sure they have what they need. ROSE: You know, Silver Rail Elementary had just done a lockdown drill a few weeks ago. The school's doors were locked. Law enforcement was on the scene quickly. KOTEK: Yes. ROSE: You know, the teacher, the other bystanders who intervened - so this is a prepared school, a swift response. And yet, three children and a teacher still lost their lives. Briefly, is there anything else that you plan to do in Oregon to prevent tragedies like this from occurring? KOTEK: Well, no community should experience this, no parent. And we, as the adults, should continue to think about what we can do differently to keep our young people safe. They should be able to go to school, feel safe, be secure. And like I said, there will be plenty of conversation about the laws we do have on the books, things that we could be doing differently. And we need some space before we can get into that. But what I will say is that I've been proud of Oregon. We approached this in a reasonable, rational way, and that's what we will do going forward when the moments right. ROSE: Thank you. That is Oregon governor Tina Kotek, a Democrat. Thank you very much for joining me. KOTEK: Thank you, Joel. Copyright © 2026 NPR. All rights reserved. title: Air defense forces destroy 11 UAVs heading toward Moscow — city mayor
body:
MOSCOW, October 18. /TASS/. Air defense systems have destroyed 11 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that were heading toward Moscow, Mayor Sergey Sobyanin announced.
"The Defense Ministry’s air defense system has destroyed eleven UAVs that were heading toward Moscow. Emergency services personnel are working at the site where the debris fell," he wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: Multimedia Group wins Media Organisation of the Year award at the 2025 CIMG Awards
body: The Multimedia Group Limited has been named Marketing-Oriented Media Organisation of the Year for 2025 at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards organised by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG). The award was presented at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, 2026, in recognition of the Group’s use of radio, television and digital platforms to drive public engagement and audience participation. In its citation, CIMG praised the Group for turning audience attention into public conversation and participation, highlighting its JoyNews Impact Maker Awards and other audience-focused initiatives. “The Multimedia Group has used its radio, television and digital platforms to turn audience attention into public conversation and participation,” the citation read. It added that the Group’s initiatives demonstrated “the value of strong editorial brands supported by coordinated marketing”. The citation also highlighted the Group’s reported audience shares for 2025, putting television at 28 per cent, Accra radio at 46.9 per cent and Kumasi radio at 43.2 per cent. CIMG further noted the reach of the 2026 JoyNews Impact Maker Awards, which attracted about 2,000 attendees and 34 corporate participants. The institute said the Group’s marketing approach extended beyond broadcasting messages to creating platforms where audiences could gather, contribute and share experiences. “The marketing achievement extends beyond broadcasting a message. By giving your audience a reason to gather, contribute and share stories, the Group turns its media properties into platforms for participation,” the citation stated. It described the Impact Maker event as an example of how editorial trust could support experiences that deliver value to communities and partners. In its concluding remarks, CIMG commended the Group’s performance and its position in Ghana’s media industry. “Your continuous exploit in this arena sets you apart as a media house of choice,” the citation stated. The institute subsequently adjudged Multimedia Group Limited the Marketing-Oriented Media Organisation of the Year for 2025. The Multimedia Group operates radio, television and digital platforms in Ghana. Its brands include Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews, Adom FM, Hitz FM, Asempa FM, Luv FM, Nhyira FM and MyJoyOnline.com. The award recognises the Group’s marketing performance and its use of established media brands and audience-focused initiatives to strengthen public engagement.

title: Oil prices over $100 could affect war with Iran, leading to escalation before elections - analysis
body: High oil prices are going to be an issue over the next few weeks if they continue to stay above $100 a barrel. That is a clear challenge for the United States and also potentially for Israel in terms of keeping a lid on a renewed conflict with Iran prior to the elections in both countries.It is no secret that the looming elections have tended to change dynamics, estimations, and assessments about whether the conflict could start again.The high oil prices come during a decline in stock prices on Wall Street. This is amid concerns about AI companies and energy prices. That could tend to be a kind of triple threat affecting the US, and thus also affecting Israel.There has been a lot of messaging about how the Strait of Hormuz is open and the availability of alternative energy sources, but the question is whether or not the global market will accept these assertions.Recent videos show ships sinking in the Strait of Hormuz and all sorts of containers floating away as ships are in distress. This is not something that will boost global optimism regarding supply chains, and it always remains a question whether enough ships are transporting energy supplies.What will the Houthis do?It also leads to questions about what the Houthis might do. The Houthis could try to threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They could also encourage other Iranian proxies, such as those in Iraq, to continue attacks on Saudi oil and gas energy infrastructure.A mysterious explosion in Iraq on Saturday appears to have struck an Iranian proxy group. All this could continue to disrupt global trade.When there are attacks on pipelines or transit points in Saudi Arabia, for instance, it takes weeks to repair them. That creates disruption, and all those disruptions add up to the feeling in the global market that there is too much uncertainty.This kind of uncertainty will affect the US. It already appears to be affecting US policy regarding the Ukraine war and Russia, and this is the kind of thing that can lead to escalation in the Middle East or miscalculations in which something happens again with Iran.Iran continues to be blockaded, but it also tends to feel a bit confident about its next steps. Therefore, we are seeing a potential for escalation within the next week or two.Iran also knows there are elections in Israel and the US; therefore, Iran and its proxies may want to take advantage of this period.

title: Bell tower of Limoges town hall collapses after arson during riots
body:
PARIS, October 18. /TASS/. A bell tower has collapsed onto the roof of the town hall in Limoges, central France, after a fire broke out during riots, according to footage broadcast by the France 3 television channel.
The fire started after several groups of radicals broke into the building and set fire to rooms on the ground floor. They then torched several vehicles parked nearby, which later exploded.
Despite firefighters battling the blaze for an hour, the fire spread to the roof. An hour later, the flames engulfed the bell tower. Footage shows the burning structure toppling sideways and crashing through the central section of the roof. Firefighting operations are still underway.
"There are no words to condemn what happened - it is so vile. This is chaos for the country," Limoges Mayor Guillaume Guerin said. He claimed the rioters "came to kill," adding that this was "visible on security camera footage." The mayor pledged to file a formal complaint and ensure that all those responsible for destroying the historic building are punished.
The Limoges town hall, built in 1883 by architect Charles Alfred Leclerc, is a protected historic landmark.

title: Sudan reaffirms Abyei claim as new chief takes office
body: Sudan’s newly appointed head of the joint oversight committee for the disputed Abyei region has reaffirmed Khartoum’s claim to the territory while calling for regional cooperation to resolve the dispute with neighbouring South Sudan peacefully. Retired Major-General Al-Khair Abdullah Idris Abu Muridat made the remarks on Saturday after taking over from his predecessor, Hamid Mannan, at a handover ceremony in Khartoum overseen by Abdullah Yahya, a member of Sudan’s Transitional Sovereignty Council, the state news agency SUNA reported. Abu Muridat was appointed on September 23 by Sovereignty Council Chairman Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, replacing Mannan. He pledged to pursue a peaceful settlement that would spare Abyei’s communities further hardship and urged the region and neighbouring countries to cooperate in resolving the dispute in line with agreements signed by Sudan and South Sudan in 2011. He also pledged to serve all communities in the Abyei region without discrimination and promote stability. He called on the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) to protect local communities and fulfil its mandate. Abu Muridat described relations between Sudan and South Sudan as strong but reiterated Khartoum’s position that Abyei belongs to Sudan. The dispute also involves the interests of the Misseriya, predominantly Arab pastoralists who traditionally move through Abyei with their cattle, and the Ngok Dinka, the region’s principal resident community, which is largely aligned with South Sudan. Disagreements over whether the Misseriya tribe should be eligible to vote in a referendum on Abyei’s future have been a major obstacle to resolving the dispute. Before his appointment, Abu Muridat headed the intelligence department of Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) after being seconded to the force from the Sudanese army. Abyei, an oil-producing region claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan, has remained a source of tension since South Sudan gained independence in 2011. The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement provided for a referendum in which Abyei’s residents would decide whether the region should remain part of Sudan or join what became South Sudan. The vote has never taken place because the parties failed to agree on voter eligibility and other outstanding issues. Agreements signed in 2011 established interim administrative and security arrangements for Abyei, but its final status remains unresolved. The post Sudan reaffirms Abyei claim as new chief takes office appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: JoyNews’ #NoToGalamsey campaign wins CIMG New Media Campaign of the Year
body: JoyNews’ #NoToGalamsey campaign has been named New Media Campaign of the Year for 2025 at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards organised by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG). The award was presented at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, 2026, in recognition of the campaign’s use of digital platforms to extend the reach of its reporting on illegal mining and its effects on water bodies and communities. In its citation, CIMG said the campaign had used digital conversations to broaden public engagement with the issue. “JoyNews used digital conversation to widen the reach of its #NoToGalamsey campaign,” the citation read. “Social audio, podcasts and cross-platform storytelling gave audiences ways to engage with reporting on illegal mining and its effect on water and communities.” CIMG praised the campaign for bringing environmental concerns into everyday public discussion through journalism. “The campaign’s strength lies in using journalism to make an environmental crisis part of everyday public discussion,” the citation stated. The institute said the campaign brought scientific information, expert perspectives and citizen participation to audiences through social audio, podcasts and other digital channels. It also recognised the partnerships that helped amplify the campaign’s public-interest reporting. The judges highlighted the campaign’s scientific grounding and its collaboration with stakeholders, including experts, institutions and citizens. “The campaign linked public-interest journalism with participation by experts, institutions and citizens,” the citation noted. The recognition reflects the campaign’s use of multiple digital formats to sustain attention on illegal mining and its environmental and social consequences. In its concluding remarks, CIMG commended the campaign for its impact, describing it as a resounding success that impressed the evaluators. The citation ultimately conferred on JoyNews’ #NoToGalamsey the title of New Media Campaign of the Year for 2025. The #NoToGalamsey campaign has contributed to Ghana’s national conversation on illegal mining, highlighting its effects on the environment, communities and livelihoods. Through its radio, television and digital platforms, the Multimedia Group has used the campaign to raise awareness, scrutinise the response of duty-bearers and advocate action to protect the country’s natural resources. The CIMG recognition adds to the campaign’s profile as a public-interest media initiative focused on one of Ghana’s pressing environmental challenges.

title: Romanian F-16s down two jet-powered drones after airspace incursion
body:
Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two drones flying in Romanian national airspace, the country's Defense Ministry announced on Oct. 17.
The two drones were jet-powered, belonging to the Geran-family of attack drones frequently used by Russia to attack targets in Ukraine, according to Romania's Defense Ministry. The Ministry did not specify which nation the drones belonged to.
Initially, Romania's radar system detected a group of aerial targets flying around 120 kilometers (75 miles) east of Snake Island in the Black Sea . Romania then scrambled two F-16 fighter jets from its Borcea Air Base at 5:43 p.m. local time.
Two drones were shot down between 6:01 p.m. and 6:05 p.m. local time over Romanian national waters. The drones spent a total of five minutes maneuvering in the nation's airspace.
Geran drones are among some of the latest drones deployed by Russian forces in attacks on Ukraine. They are particularly difficult to engage , flying significantly higher and faster than any of Russia's older drone models, with a maximum speed of 600 km/h (370 mph).
Amid Ukraine's shortage of air-to-air missiles, F-16 jets are increasingly being used to shoot down Geran drones. Ukrainian warplanes are responsible for the downing of about 55-60% of all jet-powered drones launched by Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky told journalists on Oct. 17.
In recent months, Russian drones have flown into Romanian airspace multiple times, raising tension between Moscow and the NATO member state.
On Oct. 15, seven sailors were reported missing from one of two tanker ships that caught fire in Romania's Black Sea following drone incursions into the country's airspace.
Ten days prior, a cargo ship caught fire in the Black Sea off the Romanian coast after a Russian drone strike , killing two, injuring at least 11 more, and prompting a large search-and-rescue operation.
On Sept. 24, suspected Russian drones crashed in Romania and Moldova overnight amid a sustained mass drone and missile attack on Ukraine.
