title: Hassan Ayariga challenges Mahama over BRICS move, demands parliamentary consultation
body: The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has challenged President John Dramani Mahama over the government’s plan to pursue Ghana’s membership of BRICS, demanding parliamentary scrutiny and public consultation on the decision. In a statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Dr Ayariga questioned whether Cabinet could determine Ghana’s long-term international economic and geopolitical commitments without broader public and parliamentary engagement. “Who gave Cabinet the authority to decide for over 34 million Ghanaians without parliamentary and public consultation?” he asked. He argued that Ghana’s sovereignty rests with its citizens and that decisions with far-reaching implications for the country should be subjected to transparency, accountability and public participation. Hassan Ayariga cited Article 1(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which establishes that sovereignty resides in the people of Ghana. He said the President and Cabinet must exercise their authority in accordance with the Constitution and remain accountable to the people. “My question to President John Dramani Mahama is simple: Who has the authority to determine Ghana’s long-term international economic and geopolitical commitments? Can the President do so without the approval of Parliament and the Ghanaian people?” he asked. The APC leader maintained that democratic governance should extend beyond periodic elections to include consultation and participation in decisions affecting the country’s future. He said major political, economic, legal and social policies should reflect the will of the people and be implemented through the appropriate arms of government. Hassan Ayariga also invoked Article 75 of the Constitution, which provides for the President to execute treaties, agreements and conventions on behalf of Ghana, subject to ratification by Parliament. He urged President Mahama to present the BRICS matter to Parliament for deliberation and a decision on the way forward. “Mr President, you must therefore place this matter before Parliament for the deliberations and decision of Parliament and the people,” he said. He further called on the government to explain the proposed membership’s contents, implications and expected benefits before proceeding. “The contents, implications and benefits must be made clear to Ghanaians before membership,” he added. The government announced on October 6, 2026, that Cabinet had approved a decision to formally apply for Ghana to join BRICS, according to Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. BRICS is a grouping of major emerging economies that has expanded beyond its original members and seeks to strengthen cooperation among participating countries in areas including trade, investment and development. The government has presented the proposed engagement as an opportunity to broaden Ghana’s international partnerships and deepen economic cooperation with developing economies. The Minority in Parliament has also called for an urgent briefing on the decision, seeking disclosure of its geopolitical implications and potential effects on Ghana’s national interests. Hassan Ayariga’s latest intervention adds to calls for greater parliamentary scrutiny and public discussion as the government pursues its plan.

title: UK defence secretary calls for stronger defence industry and faster delivery of military capabilities during Washington talks
body: Streeting met U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth for talks on defence production, supply chains and Europe’s responsibilities within NATO. Both officials emphasised cooperation between allied industries as their countries rebuild military capacity. Streeting said Britain was undertaking its biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the end of the Cold War. He argued that the additional funding must support the right technologies and bring them into military use more quickly. “But to your point, it’s not just about investing more; it’s about investing in the right things and making sure that we’re pushing the frontier of defense innovation and translating that innovation into capability a lot more quickly,” Streeting said. He also called for a stronger British defence industrial base. Hegseth said rebuilding U.S. military production required contributions from allies and partners. He stressed the importance of dependable supply chains and said Britain was actively pursuing that objective. “We talk about an arsenal of freedom here in the States, [about] building that and ensuring that our domestic manufacturing, our industry, our production lines, [are] made in America [at] speed, scale, [and] made with partners,” Hegseth said. His remarks linked the expansion of American manufacturing with cooperation overseas. Hegseth raised “NATO 3.0”, a proposed rebalancing under which European countries would take primary responsibility for their conventional defence. That would allow the United States to reduce its troop presence in Europe and focus more on other regions, including the Pacific. Streeting agreed that European NATO members needed to become more self-reliant. He said Britain was stepping up willingly and credited President Donald Trump with pressing Europe to take its defence more seriously. The officials also stressed the continuing importance of the U.S.-UK alliance. Hegseth said the relationship needed to remain active in addressing current threats rather than rest on its history. Hegseth thanked Streeting for communications about recent threats to U.S. forces in the UK. These included a suspected Iran-backed terror plot and a security incident at RAF Fairford in September that prompted American bombers to return to the United States. The meeting was Streeting’s first visit to Washington since taking office in July. He said Britain and the United States would not stand aside from the security challenges facing them. “It’s fair to say, at this stage, it’s not clear whether freedom or tyranny will define the 21st century,” Streeting said. “What is clear is that the United Kingdom and the United States will not be bystanders in that struggle, and we’re determined to see freedom prevail.”

title: IRGC spox. lambasts Washington for "Mother of Bombs" threat
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 17 (MNA) – A spokesman for the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has slammed the US President Donald Trump for using the sacred term 'mother' for a bomb to threaten Iran.
In a message on Saturday, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebi said the future belongs to a nation that turns the enemies’ “biggest” threats into a subject of public humor.
Accoridng to the Press TV EN website, the statement comes amid reports that the US military has developed strike plans that could involve using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), also known as the “mother of all bombs,” against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if President Donald Trump orders a resumption of combat operations.
The potential use of the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal would mark a significant escalation in the war between Tehran and Washington.
However, officials familiar with military planning discussions say questions remain over whether the weapon would help achieve US strategic objectives.

title: World Bank recognizes Russia’s achievements, provides platform for cooperation — Deputy PM
body:
BANGKOK, October 18. /TASS/. The World Bank recognizes Russia’s digital achievements and provides a platform to share this expertise with developing economies, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk told TASS, following the autumn meetings of the IMF and World Bank.
Overchuk noted that "Russia possesses vast experience and knowledge and has much to offer countries of the Global South," particularly regarding "digital transformation in public administration."
"The World Bank acknowledges Russia’s achievements in this area, understands how vital Russian expertise is for developing economies, and provides us with an international platform to work directly with these nations," he emphasized.
On the sidelines of the meetings in Bangkok, Russia organized two packed working seminars with World Bank support. "One seminar focused on digital transformation in land and real estate administration and geospatial data systems. The other addressed digital public services and digital transformation in tax administration," Overchuk said.
He noted that these areas crucially impact the business climate, investment attractiveness, and socio-economic development in the Global South. "The World Bank prioritizes these issues, and Russia is a global leader in digital governance," Overchuk said, adding that Russia ranks eighth in the World Bank’s GovTech Maturity Index.
"By learning from our experience, developing nations are seeking closer cooperation with Russia, which aligns with our interests."
Overchuk also pointed out that the World Bank primarily focuses on supporting developing nations and the Global South, the vast majority of which are friendly to Russia. "These nations form the core audience at World Bank meetings. They come here seeking access to financing, global best practices, and knowledge to develop their economies," the deputy prime minister concluded.

title: Belgium-based ICGC pastor enstooled Amanonehene of Abotakyi
body: A 44-year-old Reverend Minister of the International Central Gospel Church (ICGC), Rev. Richard Tagoe, has been enstooled Amanonehene of Abotakyi in the Akuapem Traditional Area of the Eastern Region, with a pledge to mobilise diaspora support and attract investment for the town’s development. The businessman, who lives in Belgium, assumes the traditional title Nana Ohene Tagoe I. The Amanonehene title is intended to promote the welfare of indigenes living abroad and mobilise their support for development projects in the town. Following the traditional rites, Nana Ohene Tagoe I was carried shoulder-high and paraded through the principal streets of Abotakyi amid cheers, drumming and dancing. At a ceremony at the Abotakyi chief’s palace on October 12, Nana Ohene Tagoe swore an oath of allegiance to the town’s chief, Nana Kwame Sakyi Ababio II. The chief and elders said the traditional council introduced the Amanonehene title to strengthen relationships with indigenes and organisations outside Ghana and mobilise resources for local development. The Abotakyihene said Nana Ohene Tagoe was selected because of his previous support for the town and his willingness to help raise funds from the diaspora. “We decided to introduce such a title in the traditional area to help us mobilise the needed funds from the diaspora,” the chief said. He added that the new Amanonehene had been recommended by someone familiar with his generosity and contributions to the community. The chief also urged him to remain truthful in his efforts to solicit financial support for development initiatives. “I believe that as a reverend minister, you will be truthful in all your undertakings when soliciting for financial support from the diaspora for the development of the town,” he said. In an interview, Nana Ohene Tagoe I pledged to use his new position to promote infrastructure development and attract investors to Abotakyi. He said he intended to connect the town with business-minded people willing to invest in projects that could create employment and improve livelihoods. “I accept to be Amanonehene to bring in investors, business-minded people who will develop the town. I will help get the youth employed and reduce the unemployment and teenage pregnancy rate in town,” he said. His appointment is expected to strengthen the town’s engagement with its diaspora as traditional leaders seek support for development and economic opportunities for residents.

title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
body:
Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services.
According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab , this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.)
However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now The Verge reports that the provision has been removed.
“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement. “It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers.”

title: Ukrainian forces shell DPR settlements 13 times over past day
body:
DONETSK, October 18. /TASS/. Ukrainian forces have attacked the territory of the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) 13 times over the past 24 hours, the department for documenting Ukraine’s war crimes at the DPR head’s office and government reported on Friday.
"Thirteen armed attacks by Ukrainian formations have been recorded. No civilian casualties were reported today," the statement says. Meanwhile it became known that two civilians had been injured in Konstantinovka and Donetsk on October 12 and 15, respectively.
The shelling damaged three residential buildings, two civilian infrastructure facilities, a truck, and several cars. In total, Ukrainian troops fired 15 rounds of various ammunition into the DPR, the office added.

title: Iranian official meets Asian Cultural Heritage Union head
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – The deputy minister for Cultural Heritage met and held discussions with the president of the Asian Cultural Heritage Alliance (ACHA) on the sidelines of the alliance’s fourth meeting.
On Saturday, October 17, on the sidelines of the 4th meeting of the Asian Cultural Heritage Alliance (ACHA)—held in Hangzhou, China, from October 15 to 17 with a focus on the exchange of experiences among member states regarding the preservation of cultural and natural heritage—Ali Darabi met with Rao Chuan, Chair of the ACHA Council, Vice Minister of Culture and Tourism of China, and Head of the National Cultural Heritage Administration of China.
During this meeting, Rao Chuan expressed gratitude for Iran’s support regarding his chairmanship for this term and announced that the Asian Cultural Heritage Alliance has been approved by the Chinese government, elevated to the status of an international organization, and granted legal and diplomatic standing.

title: Over 500,000 people took to streets across France on October 17 — trade union
body:
PARIS, October 17. /TASS/. CGT, one of France’s largest trade unions, said that more than 500,000 people took to the streets across the country to protest against price growth and declining purchasing power.
"Over 500,000 people took part," BFMTV quoted the trade union as saying in a statement.
The figure was later officially confirmed by French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez. He said 100 rallies were held all across the country, with 550,000 people participating, including 110,000 in Paris.
In turn, student organization L'Union Etudiante estimates the number of participants at 800,000. In all, 1,700 rallies and marches were held all across France, the organization said.
The authorities have not yet published any official numbers.
French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the unrest and pledged to bring those responsible to justice.
"There is no place for violence in our republic. Those who took part in looting, attacked prefectures and shops, ransacked public facilities, including our mayor’s offices, will be prosecuted and punished," he wrote on the X social network.
The president also expressed his support to police forces.
A series of mass protests against rising fuel prices and the declining purchasing power of the population has been taking place all over France on October 17. In a number of cities, the protests have escalated into riots and clashes with police. By 1:00 p.m. GMT, some 400 people have been detained all over France, including over 160 in the capital.
According to French media reports, cases of looting were registered all across the country, including in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux, Lyon, Nice and other cities.
