title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
body:
Earlier this year, Mercedes’ AMG performance brand grabbed our attention with the GT four-door coupe, a souped-up sports sedan with three axial flux motors delivering over 1,150 horsepower. Well, now meet its beefier cousin, the 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV, an equally powerful, ultra-fast-charging electric people-hauler.
The AMG GT SUV (say that five times fast) marks the first time in the performance brand’s 59-year history that it has developed a full-size SUV entirely in-house from the ground up. Scheduled to hit the US next summer, the new EV is built on Merc’s high-performance AMG.EA architecture to combine sports-car handling with full-size SUV suburban practicality.
It will be available in three trims — GT 53, GT 55, and the flagship GT 63 — with the top model delivering 1,153hp via the same three axial flux motors powering the four-door coupe. That beats the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with Launch Control, which is sure to make for some awkward run-ins around Stuttgart.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_081.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_080.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_077.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_075.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_074.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_078.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_073.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_070.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_072.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_076.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
Thanks to an 800-volt architecture, the SUV supports blistering-fast charging speeds up to 710kW on the 128kWh battery (GT 63 / GT 55) and 600kW on the 106kWh battery (GT 53). Drivers can charge 10–80 percent in 12 minutes or gain up to 450km (around 280 miles) of WLTP range in just 10 minutes. The 128kWh battery trims will have an estimated max range of 435 miles.
That battery, by the way? It utilizes F1-inspired technology with specialized NCMA cathodes, silicon-containing anodes, and cylindrical cells. An electrically nonconductive oil flows directly around each individual cell for uniform thermal management, enabling continuous high-power delivery and long battery life. Mercedes has quietly been on the vanguard of battery technology for a while now, with the AMG GT SUV just the latest example. The 710kW charging speed, in particular, could give Mercedes another edge over Porsche’s 320kW speeds.
For a full-size SUV, the AMG GT sounds like it could handle like a vehicle half its size. Mercedes-AMG replaced the traditional mechanical roll bars with a newly developed suspension that uses active hydraulic elements to eliminate pitch and roll during acceleration, heavy braking, and cornering. Combined with three-stage air springs and standard six-degree active rear-axle steering, it purports to balance track precision with long-distance comfort.
But just because it’s a beefy lad doesn’t mean it’ll tip the scales. The AMG GT 63 SUV weighs in at 5,941lbs, making it slightly lighter than the Lotus Eletre R (6,007lbs) and Lucid Gravity (6,100lbs), and nearly identical to the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric (5,960lbs).
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_015.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_016.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_012.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_040.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_009.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_011.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_013.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_014.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_039.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
Silence is golden — except to a performance brand’s EV engineering team. That means piping in recorded sounds of real AMGs — in this case, the legendary AMG V8 and six-cylinder engines — to preserve the “emotional” AMG identity. Mercedes is proud that it’s using real engine sounds over synthetic EV tones, though some may disagree. The system even simulates mechanical gear shifts with paddle controls, offers adjustable sound profiles, and integrates physical seat vibrations — so you can still feel like there’s a real engine under that hood instead of a 78-liter frunk. The so-called AMGFORCE Sport+ drive program is offered as standard across all three trims of the Mercedes-AMG GT SUV.
Inside, you’ll find the MB.OS platform on your 14-inch display, with an army of AI agents from ChatGPT, Microsoft, and Google at your disposal to boss around. Use them to set navigation, discover random locations, do web searches, tell bad jokes, or whatever else people use AI for in their cars. Merc’s own onboard AI system can handle the physical stuff, like adjusting HVAC, changing drive modes, or fiddling with the lighting — all through voice commands.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26C0332_048.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
Beyond voice and navigation, the AMG GT SUV applies AI to high-performance track driving through something called the Predictive Performance Manager. Mercedes says the PPM uses track-mapping data to dynamically throttle or boost electric motor output depending on topography, conserving battery energy on downhill or technical winding sections so full power is available on steep inclines and long straights. That could also mean faster, more consistent overall lap times by eliminating battery overheating and power throttling during track driving — something an AMG lover would likely appreciate.
Mercedes didn’t release the official pricing yet, though we can expect something closer to its official launch.

title: 'Blows kept coming, I felt the aircraft going down': Flydubai captain on the cockpit battle to save his plane
body: Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar has spoken of the moment his co-pilot repeatedly struck him with an axe before sending their Boeing 737 plunging towards the Arabian Desert, with the intention of killing 172 people on board. In a world exclusive interview with The National from his hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, Capt Machchhar said the first officer sitting next to him for two hours had shown no sign of what Emirati prosecutors say was a “premeditated terrorist plot” to hijack the aircraft. Flydubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv plunged 17,000 feet in less than a minute when the first officer attacked Capt Machchhar and seized control of the plane. I tried to block the blows as much as I could. [I was] screaming for my colleagues. I fell face down in the cockpit Capt Smit Machchhar Capt Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for getting the cockpit door, locked from the inside, open and allowing the attack to be foiled. All of the 172 passengers and crew on board the September 30 flight survived. The first officer has been detained in the UAE and faces terrorism charges. The statements made in this interview reflect the interviewee’s recollection of events, based on his personal experience and his perception of them at the time they occurred. In his interview with The National at Zayed Military Hospital, Capt Machchhar revealed: He thought the first blow to his head was a falling piece of equipment, before more blows rained down on him The co-pilot – who prosecutors said was radicalised by online Islamist content and in a religious study centre in Australia – showed no sign of unusual behaviour Capt Machchhar does not know what sparked the first officer to seize the controls when Tel Aviv airport, which he planned to crash into, was more than an hour away He expects an airline industry security review may lead to changes, amid questions over the cockpit fire axe He thanked the UAE for his treatment and returning him to his family, saying: “I was told that, by the order of His Highness Sheikh Mohamed, the President of UAE has called you back home – I smiled for the first time.” Cockpit battle Narrating the hijacking to a media outlet for the first time, Capt Machchhar said he thought the blow to his head was from a cockpit panel that had collapsed. “The first time when I was hit … my thought was something's gone horribly wrong with the aircraft structure, which has fallen on my head,” he said. “It almost made me fall on my control column. In the next couple of seconds, when the hits kept on coming, [I realised] it's the other person who I thought was supposed to be on the team.” He recalled those initial moments, explaining: “My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts. And I tried to just block the blows as much as I could, because the blows were coming on the head.” Capt Machchhar suffered serious injuries to his head and arm, including defensive wounds from trying to stop the blows. “While the first few blows came in, my vision … it was so narrow. I lost a lot. I was just looking [at] outlines.” Capt Machchhar is not entirely clear how events unfolded nor the timeline. But he managed to open the cockpit after several attempts. He explained that every time he had to exert himself physically, he would lose blood and consciousness. Nosedive “Immediately, my hand went to the knob which opens the door," he said. "And [I was] screaming for my colleagues. I believe that was the first time when I lost consciousness. I fell face down in the cockpit.” He believes he regained consciousness as the attacker plunged the aircraft into a dive. Crew members and passengers began banging on the other side of the cockpit door. “The scariest thing that I heard and felt was the engines spooling down. When I say spooling down, it's the engine sound going from full blast to like … not what you want at that stage in the flight. And I felt the aircraft was steeply going down.” Capt Machchhar became emotional as he explained his instinct to survive. “At that point, I realised that you will not survive this," he explained. "And I was constantly looking for the door. I did go for it. I did push it … the next thing I remember was I was facedown, lying with, thank God, the cockpit door open. I was between the cockpit and the galley.” Chaos and commotion Capt Machchhar said there was “so much chaos and commotion” as he was hauled out of the cockpit. It was at that moment that passengers and crew seized the first officer. A pair of flydubai pilots who were travelling as passengers took control of the plane. “If I have to say how many people were trying to control the situation, I would say a million. I know it doesn't make sense, but, yeah, I would say a million people were trying to take over control,” he said. Flydubai pilot hailed a hero for averting disaster on Israel flight - in pictures He described the moment others came to his rescue as “magic”, saying: “The next thing I remember was [being] pulled out by one of the passengers. And then, soon after that, the senior cabin crew thankfully reached where I was and did his magic. And yeah, that's how I'm speaking to you today.” Recovering in his bed in Zayed Military Hospital, Capt Machchhar has been trying to piece together events in the two weeks since the failed terror plot. He remembers praying as the cabin crew chief and others, including dentist Shota Musaev, tried to stem the bleeding from his wounds. “There was heavy bleeding from his head and left hand,” Dr Musaev told The National last week . “He had very, very deep cuts and we needed many ice packets. But every time I opened the T-shirt to check the bleeding, it would bleed more. So I pressed not very hard and with ice. All through the 45 minutes I kept the pressure on.” Capt Machchhar was clearly emotional as he spoke. He said: “I prayed a lot. I thought about my son, my daughter, and prayed. That was the point where I would say I didn't give up.” He spoke frankly: “Did I give up? No. I can 100 per cent tell you I did not give up. But was I sure I was going to make it? No.” No suspicion of co-pilot Asked whether he suspected anything from his co-pilot's behaviour, he said he did not notice anything. “If there was something that could have hinted earlier on the ground or something, yes, of course, I would have acted. I would have spoken up. I would have questioned some things like that,” he explained. He described that morning as ordinary, saying it was the first time he had met the first officer. “It was a morning flight. So, yeah, there was some small talk, but there was not really like a deep conversation,” he said. Capt Machchhar added: “We avoid getting into deep conversations, especially during high-intensity or high-density airspace, especially nowadays with all the restrictions. Saudi is very high density.” "Nothing until that point would have caused me to think that: 'Hey, hold on, there's something off.'” There has been speculation about why the first officer attacked his colleague when the plane was an hour away from Tel Aviv airport, which prosecutors said he intended to crash into. “I won't say I've been thinking a lot about it, but yes, I did give it a thought. It makes no sense to me,” Capt Machchhar said. There was also much scrutiny over the presence of a cockpit axe, and how the co-pilot was radicalised. Asked whether aviation security will change as a result of the close call, Capt Machchhar said: “I think so. And for good." He added: “I won't blame it on anyone. You've got to learn from the event … I would just say: learn from whatever's happened and then make sure that this doesn't happen again, ever.” Capt Machchhar, who lives with his wife and children in the UAE, faces a long recovery but wants to return to the cockpit. “Did my love die for aviation? Not at all. Not at all,” he said with a smile. “I'm just glad that I was able to do my part.”

title: Europe Braces for a Winter Energy Crisis as Gas Reserves Run Low
body: After months of elevated energy prices, Europe can expect fuel costs to continue rising through the winter months as demand grows. Ongoing energy trade constraints and threats to energy infrastructure across the Middle East are expected to limit global energy supplies and continue to drive up prices, hitting consumers hard unless governments intervene.  The European Union EU is thought to have paid an additional 100 billion on oil and gas so far this year, prompting EU ministers to seek ways to manage the impact of high fuel prices. Since 2022, the extra costs of energy have surpassed 900 billion, even as total demand has fallen. The price of natural gas in Europe has more than doubled since the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli-led war in Iran. This winter could be the most challenging in terms of energy supplies and prices since the start of Russia's war on Ukraine and the subsequent sanctions on Russian energy.  Meanwhile, EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen has warned that the winter months could be challenging amid "very high" oil and gas prices, although he reassured consumers that no supply issues are expected. Jorgensen also proposed postponing the introduction of rules to reduce methane emissions on energy imports to help ease pressure on European energy markets.  Gas storage has fallen to its lowest level since 2022. In September, across Europe, gas storage stood at around 67 per cent full, compared with a seasonal average of around 80 per cent. Germany, which has the largest storage capacity in Europe, is roughly half full, and is expected to miss its official 80 per cent storage target this year.  Meanwhile, constrained supplies due to strict limits on energy trade through the Strait of Hormuz have sharply driven up energy prices. Oil prices increased by 65 per cent, diesel by 45 per cent, and jet fuel by 112 per cent between 25 September 2025 and 2026. This has led the European Commission to call for consumers to reduce their demand throughout the year to manage supplies.  As Europe heads into its high-demand winter months, there is no end to the war in Iran in sight. In addition, the El Nio weather cycle is expected to add an element of uncertainty to weather trends, which could further complicate the gas demand picture. Threats remain to fuel shipments traversing the Strait of Hormuz, as well as ongoing threats to energy infrastructure across the Middle East. Meanwhile, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and against pipelines continue to be a concern. Therefore, there are likely to be restrictions on global oil trade well into 2027.  The United States has focused on increasing oil and gas production to help alleviate some of the energy supply chain constraints, but this can only partly fill the gap. Atlantic and Pacific freight rates have returned to pre-Iran war levels, as a larger share of cargoes from the United States is heading to Europe rather than Asia, thereby reducing travel distances and increasing ship availability.  The independent LNG and shipping analyst Pratiksha Negi stated, "The growing share of Atlantic trade, combined with an increasing pool of prompt vessels, will continue to pressure freight rates I expect Europe to remain the principal destination for marginal U.S. LNG at the start of Q4 2026, given the significant storage deficit this season." Negi also highlighted the rise in newbuild deliveries, with roughly 55 new vessels delivered in the first seven months of the year and another 40-45 expected by the end of the year.  Across Europe, it is not only households that are concerned about their energy bills, as several industries prepare for fuel shortages. Higher fuel prices are driving up operating costs in factories and other facilities, which could lead companies to charge more for manufactured goods, as costs will once again shift to consumers. Meanwhile, companies that cannot secure or afford adequate fuel supplies may be forced to suspend operations in the winter, leading to job cuts.  A recent forecast by the Item Club suggested that in the United Kingdom, as many as 163,000 jobs could be lost in 2026 in relation to the war, mainly in manufacturing-heavy regions such as South Wales and the Humber region. As one of Europe's biggest gas consumers, the U.K. is highly exposed to trade restrictions, particularly because it has one of the lowest levels of domestic storage capacity, which means it relies heavily on pipeline imports from Europe and tankers from the U.S. and the Middle East. The CEO of British Gas owner Centrica, Chris O'Shea, said in August that Britain had "almost no gas in storage" for the coming winter.  Both households and businesses across Europe could be hit hard this winter by the continued constraints on oil and gas supplies and high energy prices. This could force consumers to ration their consumption and may prompt the European Commission and governments to intervene to ensure consumers have access to vital energy supplies.  By Felicity Bradstock for Oilprice.com

title: Texas Researchers Say Permian Wastewater Could Cool AI Data Centers
body:
Oil Prices Plunge 7% as U.S. and Iran Signal Room for Diplomacy
Canadian oil producer Strathcona Resources…
Haley Zaremba is an energy journalist and researcher with more than a decade of professional experience covering global energy systems, land and natural resources, and…
The artificial intelligence boom is placing a dangerous strain on the world’s water and energy resources. As hyperscalers build up resource-hungry data centers at a breakneck pace, demand projections for these finite resources are skyrocketing faster than policymakers can keep pace. But a new study from researchers at the University of Texas at Austin suggests that there may be a way to sustainably source water for data centers by using wastewater from the oil and gas industry.
The water and energy use of AI data centers is enormous and growing rapidly. Large data centers can directly consume as much as 5 million gallons of water per day, according to figures from the Environmental and Energy Study Institute . But hard numbers are hard to come by, as the tech sector operates under extreme opacity. And, what is more, new studies suggest that those figures may be greatly underestimating the real water usage of these operations.
Recent research from the University of Michigan contends that these water footprints should also account for the water usage of the energy being produced to power those data centers. A new paper calculates that when water used offsite is included in the water accounting of three large AI data centers planned for Michigan, the projects’ water footprint increases by a whopping 14 billion gallons.
“There has been much less attention to this indirect water usage, even though that oftentimes is significantly higher than the direct water usage and has impacts on watersheds and regional water resources,” Shaolei Ren, a professor at the University of California, Riverside, recently told Bloomberg.
Finding a way to limit the water usage of these projects, or make that usage more sustainable, is paramount. This is where new research from the University of Texas at Austin comes in. In a brand new paper published in the scientific journal Water Research , researchers model different proven ways of desalinating wastewater to gauge their energy efficiency for use in data center cooling processes, with the goal of reducing the sector’s pressure on finite freshwater resources. The scientists find that the most efficient method is reverse osmosis. However, it struggles with water saltier than seawater, which could pose a challenge for some wastewater resources.
In applications where reverse osmosis isn’t feasible, heating water into vapor and capturing the resulting freshwater is another viable approach, albeit a more energy-intensive one. Either way, neither approach is new, and that is the appeal. “We’re not waiting for a futuristic technology to come along and solve this problem for us,” Vaibhav Bahadur, who is a professor at the University of Texas’ Cockrell School of Engineering and one of the leaders of the research, was recently quoted by Interesting Engineering. Treatment isn’t free, but Bahadur says the cost would be a small fraction of a data center’s total energy footprint, even with the most energy-intensive option.
Using wastewater from the oil and gas sector would shrink data centers’ water footprint, and it would also solve a problem for the fossil fuel sector by closing a problematic resource loop. As big as the AI sector’s water needs are, the oil and gas sector’s water needs – and water waste – are even bigger. By Bahadur’s count , the Permian alone generates roughly 790 million gallons of wastewater a day, more than 150 times the 5 million gallons a large data center can consume.
“The Permian (Basin) puts out 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools per day, and right now this water is transported over long distances and injected underground. This is problematic in many ways including the risk of seismic activity,” said Bahadur, according to Interesting Engineering . “We’re also running out of space to bury that water, by as early as 2030. We need to find a way to use it, and cleaning it up for data centers is a great way to do that.”

title: SSPDF arrests eight over alleged child trafficking in Juba
body: South Sudan’s military says it has arrested eight suspects over alleged child abduction and trafficking in Juba, amid reports of 23 children missing from the Mangateen residential area. Maj. Gen. Lul Ruai Koang, spokesperson for the South Sudan People’s Defence Forces (SSPDF), said on Saturday that military intelligence personnel arrested the suspects during an operation targeting criminal activities in Souk Darfur, an area of Juba’s Mangateen neighbourhood. “These people were caught red-handed getting involved in the business of kidnapping, abducting and trafficking in children,” Koang told journalists at Giada Barracks in Juba. He said the suspects allegedly played different roles in the network, including enticing children, keeping them in safe houses and identifying potential buyers. Three of the suspects presented by the military are SSPDF personnel, while civilians are also among those arrested. Koang said authorities had received repeated reports of children disappearing from their homes and markets in Souk Darfur, also known as Darfur Market. The reports prompted military intelligence personnel to monitor the area and gather information from residents. One child, identified as Hakim, has been recovered and reunited with his family, while the military said eight other children had been traced to people suspected of holding them. Hakim’s father, Kuol, said his son went missing on September 15 while his parents were at work. When they returned home in the evening, they discovered that the child was missing and began searching the neighbourhood. “When we returned home in the evening, we found that my child was missing,” Kuol said, adding that other children told him Hakim had gone to a video hall with another boy. He said the family searched the area and later received information that Hakim had been taken to Mogiri, but they were unable to find him until security personnel intervened. Kuol said he intended to pursue the case through the courts to ensure justice for his son. He added that he had been taking Hakim for medical treatment since his recovery. “The stress I had when the child was kidnapped, I was not eating, and at night I could not sleep. I am very exhausted with this issue,” he said. Kuol also thanked the government and security personnel for their efforts to recover his son. Meanwhile, one of the suspects, identified as Ayella Dominic Onono Nelson, a minor, told journalists that he had delivered three children to a woman identified as Mary, allegedly acting on instructions from another suspect named Angok. “We started this operation in 2025,” Nelson said, alleging that Angok had instructed him to take a child named Atem to Mary’s home, where another child named Geng was also staying. Nelson said he had delivered three children in separate operations and received rewards in return. He alleged that he was given a bicycle for himself and his child after the first delivery, 400,000 South Sudanese pounds after the second delivery and 200,000 pounds after the third. He said he used some of the money to buy clothes. The SSPDF spokesman said the alleged trafficking network involved people from different communities, with some suspects accused of arranging the transfer of children to buyers in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area. He alleged that children were sold for millions of South Sudanese pounds in Juba, while transactions in Greater Pibor could involve livestock. According to the spokesperson, girls were allegedly sold for 15 million South Sudanese pounds in Juba, while boys fetched between 7 million and 9 million pounds. In Greater Pibor, boys were reportedly exchanged for between 45 and 50 cows, while girls were exchanged for between 30 and 45 cows, Koang said. The army spokesperson warned that child abduction and trafficking are no longer confined to areas traditionally associated with such incidents in Greater Jonglei, saying the activities had spread to residential areas of Juba. Koang said suspects with military backgrounds would remain under military jurisdiction for possible military trials, while civilian suspects would be handed over to the police for further legal proceedings. He appealed to parents and guardians to monitor their children’s movements and urged residents to report suspicious activities to security agencies. He also called on the public and media outlets to circulate photographs of missing children to help investigators trace them. Koang said investigations are continuing as authorities seek to recover the remaining missing children and establish the level of involvement of each suspect. Captain Achol Lazarus Garang, legal adviser to the SSPDF’s Military Intelligence, described child trafficking as a threat to families and communities across the country and urged residents to work together to combat the practice. “Human trafficking is a threat not only to one family, but to every family in Juba,” Garang said, appealing to parents and guardians to remain vigilant about their children’s safety. The post SSPDF arrests eight over alleged child trafficking in Juba appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Semiconductor market to remain solid ‘at least through next year,’ South Korea finance minister says
body:
The semiconductor boom will last at least through 2027, South Korean finance minister Lee Hyoung-Il said on Saturday.
"For now, our view is that we can sustain this growth at least through next year," Lee told CNBC on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. "That's because the gap between demand and supply for semiconductors is still very wide, and supply is still being expanded."
His comments come after semiconductor stocks fell sharply this week, hurt by investor concerns about interest rate hikes and rising competition from Chinese companies. South Korean chip stocks like SK Hynix and Seoul Semiconductor were part of the sell-off, along with U.S. giants like Nvidia .
Chip stocks' large weighting has fueled volatility in South Korea's stock market this year, Lee said. He attributed the market's wild swings to the semiconductor industry's larger share of the economy than in other countries. Despite the market swings, South Korea's economy is "solid," Lee said.
On Thursday, an opinion column in Maeil Business Newspaper , a prominent South Korean publication, urged the country's government to prepare for the coming slowdown in the artificial intelligence boom. The author said two experts expect a "flood of new supply" of semiconductors that will turn the memory market "into a red ocean" by 2029, according to a CNBC translation .
While South Korea's semiconductors may be driving volatility in its stock market, the industry has also fueled tax growth. Lee said the country expects to collect more taxes than initially projected this year.
South Korea will ultimately be in a stronger fiscal position because of the chip boom, he added.

title: G7 pledges 260 million euros to repair Chornobyl’s shield after Russia pierced it. Full repair will require 500 million euros by 2030, before corrosion sets in
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A Russian drone tore a hole in the shield over Chornobyl’s dead reactor. Now the G7 is paying to patch it. The Group of Seven nations plans to allocate 260 million euros ($292 million) to repair the New Safe Confinement at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant, First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal says on X. The confinement, a 35-story steel arch sealing the reactor that exploded in the 1986 disaster, was damaged by a Russian drone strike in February 2025. Full restoration will cost at least 500 million euros, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) estimates , so the G7 pledge covers just over half, leaving about 240 million euros still to raise. Shmyhal calls the decision an important step toward restoring nuclear safety at the plant, which the Russian strike had compromised. The money will go to priority work, including resealing the structure and restoring its ventilation system. “Thank you to France and personally to Minister Roland Lescure for leadership in mobilizing international support,” Shmyhal says, crediting France and the EBRD with co-chairing the effort. The night a drone pierced the sarcophagus The damage dates to 14 February 2025. A Russian drone carrying a high-explosive warhead punched a hole through the arch’s roof and ignited a fire in the cladding, breaching the structure’s seal and ventilation. The attack caused a 15 m² breach in the inner and outer cladding and damaged around 200 m² of panels. "It was a targeted Russian attack on the Chornobyl station with a drone that is an analog of the Iranian Shahed," Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said at that time. A bill only half-covered, and a 2030 deadline The G7 money closes only part of the gap. Partners must still raise roughly 240 million euros more, and Ukraine hopes to secure it at a donor conference in Paris co-chaired by Ukraine, France and the EBRD, Shmyhal says. The clock matters as much as the cost. The work must be finished by 2030 to limit corrosion and protect the arch’s 100-year design life, the EBRD says, turning a repair bill into a race against the rust the strike set loose. In 2024, Elon Musk promised to give away $1 million a day to a randomly selected registered voter in a swing state. That prompted legal challenges, raised questions about its legality, and drew lawsuits from two Arizona residents claiming the lottery was a fraud. Musk has now agreed to settle the two lawsuits filed in Austin, Texas, though the details of the settlement have not been made public.
The plaintiffs claim that when Musk announced the sweepstakes, he falsely claimed the prizes would be awarded randomly. Philadelphia’s District Attorney sued to stop the giveaway , claiming that Musk was running an illegal lottery. During a hearing, Chris Gober, a representative for Musk’s America PAC, told the judge that “The $1 million recipients are not chosen by chance … We know exactly who will be announced as the $1 million recipient today and tomorrow.”
That directly contradicted Musk’s claim that the drawings were random. The plaintiffs say they never would have signed the petition required to enter the giveaway if they had known it wasn’t random. They accused Musk and America PAC of using it as a ploy to obtain user data and said the petition “places no limitations on America PAC’s use of or sale of the personal data it collects, nor does it provide any additional information about the planned use of data.”

title: CICA’s Next Chapter in Asian Cooperation
body: At the October 15 summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku, Kazakhstan proposed a mechanism for preventive diplomacy to address disputes before they escalate. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said the mechanism would give each member state a role in decision-making and help translate political commitments into coordinated action. If adopted, the proposal could increase Astana’s influence among Asia’s larger powers by making its founding initiative more enduring. Influence Through an Asian Agenda Kazakhstan already coordinates CICA’s military-political dimension, working with Türkiye on military exchanges, training-center visits, and seminars that include mediation. Kazakhstan could draw on these exchanges when seeking members’ agreement on a mandate for preventive diplomacy. They provide experience of organizing cooperation in a politically sensitive field, although a standing role in addressing emerging disputes would require a separate political agreement defining what members authorize the mechanism to do. The Think Tank Forum offers another example of Kazakhstan’s influence over CICA’s institutional development. China initiated the Forum in 2014; its transformation into a permanent CICA advisory body followed in October 2021, when member states acted on Tokayev’s initiative. Azerbaijan hosted the first meeting outside China in September 2025, at which the handover to the Indian Council of World Affairs was announced; the latter now chairs the Forum for 2026–2027. Kazakhstan thus helped turn a Chinese initiative into a permanent CICA advisory body that Azerbaijani and Indian institutions subsequently helped sustain. China also contributes funding and seconded personnel to the Secretariat; Kazakhstan can build influence by securing agreement on standing arrangements through which other members pursue their priorities. At the Baku summit, Tokayev also proposed establishing a CICA Water Partnership to promote joint research, technology exchange, and water-saving measures. He suggested that Central Asian countries and Azerbaijan could jointly advance a proposal for an International Water Organization under the United Nations. These proposals could give Kazakhstan a role in shaping cooperation on water security within CICA and, through a joint regional initiative, at the UN. Kazakhstan’s Foundational Role in CICA’s Development Kazakhstan conceived CICA in 1992 and has led its institutional development, including the effort to transform it into a full-fledged international organization. The initiative has a constituency extending well beyond Central Asia. Fifteen states adopted CICA’s first founding declaration in 1999. With Laos’s accession at Baku, CICA now has 29 members, ranging from China, India, Pakistan, and Russia to Iran, Israel, and South Korea. The 2022 Astana summit launched CICA’s transformation into a full-fledged international organization. The Road Map endorsed by member states in 2023 specified reforms through which to pursue that transformation. The reforms cover the Charter, implementation of confidence-building measures, procedural rules, and the Secretariat’s organization. These changes affect CICA’s capacity to carry agreements forward between high-level meetings. Within CICA, the consensus rule makes collective agreement a condition both of institutional change and of policy coordination. Kazakhstan thus has an interest in the procedures through which future cooperation will be organized. Cambodia’s pre-summit ratification of the convention on the Secretariat’s privileges and immunities enables its entry into force on November 8. The convention provides the Secretariat with the legal capacity needed for its functions in states bound by the treaty, while protecting its official operations and personnel. Kazakhstan separately strengthened the Secretariat’s position by ratifying amendments to the Host Country Agreement in May 2025. Alongside these legal reforms, CICA is expanding its economic cooperation. The Finance Summit provides a forum for member states to cooperate on investment, development financing, and sustainable and digital finance. Tokayev proposed giving permanent status to the China-initiated Finance Summit at the 2022 Astana summit; members established it as a permanent CICA advisory body by adopting its regulations in September 2025 under Azerbaijan’s chairmanship. Its inaugural meeting, organized by the Astana International Financial Centre in September 2026, brought the arrangement into operation. The AIFC chairs the Finance Summit, with Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Finance as co-chair, giving Kazakhstan a continuing role in an institution developed through cooperation with other CICA members. Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan’s Institutional Partnership During its 2020–2024 chairmanship, with the Secretariat’s support, Kazakhstan prepared the initial Charter draft; Azerbaijan subsequently advanced negotiations over the text among member states. The draft declaration that senior officials approved for the Baku summit on October 14 welcomed progress on the Charter’s preparation. The Charter’s final provisions will determine the organization’s functions and the distribution of responsibilities among its organs. By preparing the text for discussion, Kazakhstan has already influenced those arrangements and given direction to the process, although the eventual agreement must accommodate other members’ positions. During Azerbaijan’s 2024–2026 chairmanship, members established the Women’s Council, adopted regulations for a permanent Finance Summit, and began operating a network of leading universities. The university network had been proposed by Tokayev, while Kazakhstan’s chairmanship had sought permanent status for the China-originated Finance Summit. These developments thus reproduce a recognizable division of trans-Caspian labor: Kazakhstan formulates institutional proposals, while Azerbaijan helps give them collective effect and develops priorities of its own. The university network is a case in point. Its 182 participating institutions come from thirteen member states; Azerbaijan’s ADA University chairs a coordination council that also includes universities from Kazakhstan, China, India, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. The network’s diplomatic value will depend on the exchanges and joint work its members undertake, while its organization already provides a practical means of maintaining cooperation across successive chairmanships. The Preventive-Diplomacy Proposal and Its Future The preventive-diplomacy proposal would carry this institutional approach into a more politically demanding field. The next question is whether members can agree on the mechanism’s mandate and their participation. Negotiators would need to determine who could initiate consultations, how the states concerned would consent, what work the mechanism could undertake, and what responsibilities participants would assume. Resolving these questions would determine whether members were willing to authorize a continuing diplomatic function beyond the professional exchanges CICA already conducts. Azerbaijan’s establishment of the Non-Aligned Movement’s Parliamentary Network in 2021 and Youth Organization in 2022, during its NAM chairmanship, exemplifies its wider experience in institutionalizing cooperation among governments with differing priorities. Azerbaijan’s CICA chairmanship, extended at Baku through 2028, provides scope to apply that experience to sustaining the transformation initiated under Kazakhstan’s 2020–2024 chairmanship while advancing Azerbaijan’s own role in shaping CICA’s development. The Middle Corridor offers a parallel field of bilateral cooperation; CICA’s broader membership gives the Kazakhstan–Azerbaijan institutional partnership a different diplomatic constituency. Within CICA, the synergy between Kazakhstan’s institutional initiatives and Azerbaijan’s multilateral executive experience strengthens their joint capacity to organize cooperation across Asia. At the Baku summit, Kazakhstan sought to convert its investment in CICA into a greater role in determining what Asian states undertake together. Azerbaijan’s complementary contribution helps sustain that effort, while Kazakhstan’s lasting influence depends on what other members agree to undertake through CICA and whether the resulting institutions continue to guide their cooperation.

title: Russian troops executed Ukrainian POWs in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, military says
body:
Russian forces are accused of executing Ukrainian prisoners of war (POWs) on the Huliaipole front in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, a Ukrainian military spokesperson told Ukrainska Pravda on Oct. 17.
Ukrainian forces intercepted radio communications between Russian soldiers as the alleged executions took place, according to Maksym Kravchuk, spokesperson for Ukraine's Southern Forces Group.
Kravchuk said Russian troops received orders to kill wounded Ukrainian soldiers, including instructions to "take them out immediately." The Russian soldiers reportedly carried out the orders, killing what Ukrainian officials believe were two unarmed POWs.
The incident occurred several days before the allegations were made public, although the exact date and location of the reported executions have not been disclosed.
The Russian soldiers are believed to belong to the 38th Separate Motorized Rifle Brigade, which is operating in the area. Kravchuk alleged that orders of this nature within the brigade are issued at the initiative of its commander, Colonel Valery Kazak.
The Ukrainian military said the intercepted communications and other relevant materials had been handed over to law enforcement authorities.
The execution of prisoners of war is prohibited under the Geneva Conventions and constitutes a war crime.
Russian forces have previously been accused of executing Ukrainian POWs in the Huliaipole sector. In November 2025 , five Ukrainian soldiers were reportedly captured and executed near the village of Zelenyi Hai, according to the Ukrainian battlefield monitoring group DeepState. Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office subsequently confirmed that five POWs had been shot by Russian forces.
According to figures released by Ukraine's Human Rights Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets in August 2026, Russian forces have executed at least 345 Ukrainian soldiers who surrendered since the beginning of the full-scale invasion.

title: Investors are buying up vast tracts of timberland across U.S. in one of market's longest-term bets
body:
When the economy and the market look shaky, gold and government bonds are the traditional places to park money. Lately, some investors have also been looking at something more rooted: timber.
The pitch is easy to like: a back-to-basics, natural asset that grows on its own, matures into a harvest and can be cashed in all while you use it to hunt, pitch a tent, or forage.
Institutions have been buying timberland at a rate of one million acres per year, according to Bank of America, and some financial advisors say individual investors, including younger Americans priced out of the housing market, are also taking a look at the asset class. But it is far from a rush, and investors who already own timberland caution that it may not be very profitable in the short term.
"Timber is a very low return investment. I have curtailed my investments," said Pat Dorn, founder of Anchor Investment Management, a fee-only advisory firm in Columbia, South Carolina, and a former chairman of the South Carolina Forestry Association. Dorn owns 2,500 acres of timberland in South Carolina's booming upstate region. Dorn said the problem is that right now more timber is being grown than is needed in a sluggish housing economy.
"Supply beats demand, and that causes flat prices. Timber is not an investment I would make currently," Dorn said.
Nationally, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' producer price index for logs, bolts, timber, pulpwood and wood chips ticked up in September, but prices have been mostly on the decline since summer 2022. This measures prices received by producers for those products, rather than timberland values or investment returns. Over the very long-term, prices have climbed substantially.
Financial institutions point to the asset class as one of interest specifically for the long-term investor.
Ken Shepard, head of specialty asset management at Bank of America Private Bank said that timberland is not a tactical asset class that can be easily entered or exited in response to short-term market conditions. "We view it as a strategic, long-term investment supported by several favorable secular trends, including the continued expansion of the timber industry in the U.S. South and growing demand for wood products beyond traditional construction uses," Shepard said.
For example, he said, demand for wood pellets used in bioenergy, while controversial , has increased significantly. In addition, timberland values are benefiting from strong demand from recreational and lifestyle buyers , providing support for land prices beyond the income generated from timber harvesting.
The National Council of Real Estate Investment Fiduciaries' Timberland Property Index, which tracks privately held U.S. timber properties owned at least partly on behalf of institutional investors, posted a total return of 0.95% in the second quarter of 2026, comprising 0.34% income and 0.61% appreciation.
Bank of America's 2026 outlook reported that the one-million-acre annual pace of buying is a three-year streak of dealmaking it expects to continue.
According to Bank of America, timber managers acquired 55% of all acres that changed hands in 2025 against just 15% sold. Institutions are playing the long game. Large timberland managers buy for pension funds and endowments that can wait decades, and that can make bets on a longer-term recovery in a currently slumping U.S. housing market that will be good for lumber pricing. But a private owner living through today's market sees things differently.
Dorn pointed out that timber companies buy less mature trees for pulpwood, which goes into paper towels or notebook paper, and those trees can take 12-14 years to mature. The chip-and-saw variety of trees take a little bit longer, while the big prize, timber cut for houses, can take 25 years. "That is where the top value is," he said.
According to Dorn, what landowners are paid for standing timber varies depending on what the trees are used for. Pine pulpwood consists of trees ground into paper and packaging, while pine sawtimber is made up of larger trees cut into lumber for homebuilding. Meanwhile, hardwood sawtimber, consists of oak and other big trees used in flooring, furniture and pallets. Each product feeds a different set of buyers, so one can climb while others fall.
South Carolina Forestry Commission data show statewide average pine pulpwood stumpage prices, what buyers pay landowners for standing timber, fell from $5.67 a ton in the third quarter of 2025 to $3.79 in the third quarter of 2026, a decline of about 33%. Pine sawtimber prices fell about 6% over the same period, from $22.78 to $21.47 a ton, while hardwood sawtimber prices rose about 40%, from $16.04 to $22.52.
Historically, pulpwood has been as high as $12 to $18 a ton, according to Dorn, and twenty years ago, soft timber was in the $35-$40 range. He said those prices could make a comeback if the housing market ever recovers, because pine sawtimber is cut into lumber for new homes, so its price tends to follow home building.
Strategically placed, timber may not be a bad investment, according to Dorn, though that would be because of the land itself more than the timber. "The return is in the land, not the timber," Dorn said.
He advises anyone thinking of investing in timberland to scout for prime parcels of land located outside growing metro areas that may be poised to pop as the local population keeps spreading. "If one hopes to buy land near growing metro areas and holds on to it, timber is a reasonable way to keep it earning something — a very low return — while you hold that land," he said.
Michael Martin, a timber owner in western New York and vice president of market strategy at brokerage firm TradingBlock , says timberland can be a good long-term investment but the reality of being an owner belies the romantic image of acres of untouched timberland. It is not as passive an investment class as it may seem to be.
Direct ownership is highly illiquid and comes with management costs, property taxes, harvesting expenses, exposure to local timber markets, and risks including wildfire, pests, disease and trespassers hunting or cutting trees.
And when it is time to harvest timber, you need to make sure you are getting the best deal. "If you simply go with a small local outfit without getting competing bids, you don't always know if you're getting the best price," Martin said.
He also said timber prices are very local and can impact whether it's a solid investment.
"I am constantly checking stumpage reports because timber prices are extremely local. An oak tree in western New York may have a completely different value from one in the Adirondacks," Martin said.
In addition, partial timbering every ten years or so has barely covered the property taxes. "At the end of the day, I barely break even," he added.
Some in local real estate and investing markets say younger buyers are curious, though firsthand evidence is hard to find.
"As a millennial and a realtor, I understand the appeal. I've thought about buying timberland myself," said Jake Kennedy, a Nashville-based realtor, noting that his generation has lived through the dot-com crash, the Great Recession, a pandemic, huge swings in housing and now inflation. "One lesson from all of that we have learned is that scarcity matters when it comes to places to park your money," Kennedy said, adding as examples that more IPOs can be announced or new crypto created.
"But you can't manufacture another 500 acres of land," Kennedy said. "Timber itself is a resource that takes decades to grow. And there is something reassuring about owning an asset that is tangible," he added. But he also cautioned that timber's durability doesn't mean profitability. Trees can be temperamental and subject to many variables.
The people Kennedy has spoken with see timberland as a relatively safe place to park money, he said, because demand for timber products isn't going away. "In the meantime, yes, hunting is a common activity while owners are waiting for the investment to grow and mature, literally," he said.
"I don't think my generation is suddenly giving up on houses and becoming timber barons. However, I do think we are a lot more interested in alternative places to store wealth than previous generations might have been," he added.
For many millennials, homeownership has become increasingly difficult due to elevated home prices, higher mortgage rates, and limited inventory in many markets. "As a result, some investors are looking for alternative ways to participate in real assets and potentially build equity without purchasing a home directly," said Nadeem Kassam, chief investment strategist at Marnoa Private Wealth Counsel.
Outside direct or institutional fund ownership, there are timber ETFs and timber-focused funds that provide exposure to a theme that is closely tied to long-term housing demand and construction activity, though they remain highly niche investments in an ETF market now valued in the trillions of dollars.
Kassam pointed to the iShares Global Timber & Forestry ETF ( WOOD ), with roughly $260 million in assets, and the Invesco MSCI Global Timber ETF ( CUT ), which has roughly $30 million in assets.
"The investment case is supported by persistent housing shortages across many parts of the U.S. and growing bipartisan support for policies aimed at increasing housing supply and improving affordability. If these efforts lead to increased homebuilding over time, demand for lumber and wood products could benefit," Kassam said.
But he noted that investors should understand that timber ETFs are not a direct investment in timberland. Neither ETF owns trees.
"Most own publicly traded companies involved in timber, forest products, wood manufacturing, and other parts of the housing value chain," Kassam said, explaining the advantage is liquidity and accessibility, but returns will be driven by more than just timber prices.
WOOD's largest holdings include Weyerhaeuser , a major timberland owner, alongside Brazilian pulp maker Suzano , Nine Dragons Paper and West Fraser Timber . CUT is weighted toward paper, packaging and materials makers such as Svenska Cellulosa, UPM, Stora Enso and Avery Dennison . WOOD has drawn about $73 million in net inflows over the past year, according to ETF Database.
"For investors who are priced out of the housing market, timber ETFs may offer a way to participate in the long-term housing and construction story through a diversified, liquid investment vehicle. The key is recognizing that you're buying exposure to businesses that benefit from housing-related demand, not a direct ownership stake in land or residential real estate," Kassam said.
Junyi Liu, professor of economics at Soka University of America, who studies international and development economics, said he is not seeing evidence of a boom, but that timberland does have some unusual characteristics as an alternative asset.
"Returns can come from biological growth, timber prices, and land appreciation, and owners sometimes have the option to delay harvesting when timber prices are unfavorable," Liu said. But for retail investors, Liu added, it is quite different from "the simple 'trees grow while you wait' investment story."

title: Georgia: Billionaire Ivanishvili meets ruling party leaders – what is known about their talks after silent video release
body: Ivanishvili Georgian Dream meeting On 17 October, a rare political event took place in Georgia . Bidzina Ivanishvili , founder and honorary chairman of the ruling Georgian Dream party, chaired a meeting of the party’s political council, followed by a meeting of the parliamentary majority, at the party’s central office. This was the first public appearance in several months by Ivanishvili, whom many consider Georgia’s “shadow” ruler. Yet it could hardly be called an “appearance”. Ivanishvili himself said nothing to journalists. The party’s press office released only silent footage of the meetings. What was discussed behind closed doors became known through three sources: Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze’ s briefing, the party’s written statement, and a brief comment by parliamentary majority leader Irakli Kirtskhalia . Kobakhidze emphasised that Ivanishvili had expressed “pain” over his former team-mates who are in prison. This likely refers primarily to former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili, who for many years was considered Bidzina Ivanishvili’s closest and most loyal ally but has now been convicted of large-scale corruption. However, in the party’s statement, this issue is presented in a different tone. It is stated that corruption problems within the team have been “fully and effectively” overcome. While the meetings were underway, citizens protested outside the building under the slogan “Georgia against Ivanishvili”. One of the banners read, “Supporting Georgian Dream = betraying the country”, while another said, “14 bloody years”, referring to the years Georgian Dream has been in power. 750,000 lari bribe and other new allegations against jailed former Georgian PM who turned against the government Two related issues are being debated in Georgian society: corruption in the Defence Ministry and the possible use of the law as a tool of political pressure Who joined the political council The only publicly announced decision from the meetings was to expand the political council. Parliamentary majority leader Irakli Kirtskhalia and Zurab Pataradze , head of the government of the Autonomous Republic of Ajara, joined the body. Footage released by the press office shows Ivanishvili entering the meeting, shaking hands with MPs and taking his seat. Irakli Kobakhidze, parliamentary speaker Shalva Papuashvili, Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze and Irakli Kirtskhalia sat beside him at the head table. Ministers were also present. According to Kobakhidze, both meetings addressed current domestic and foreign policy issues. The party statement referred to “political and economic processes” in the country. It also said time was devoted to initiatives and reforms recently announced by the government. The context behind Ivanishvili’s meetings with ruling party leaders Bidzina Ivanishvili rarely appears in public. He has been under US sanctions since 2024. His participation in party meetings on 17 October came amid an apparent crisis within the government. Former senior Georgian Dream officials have been arrested one after another on corruption charges. The most high-profile case involves former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili. In January 2026, he was sentenced to five years in prison under a plea agreement. In August, prosecutors brought a new bribery charge against him. Gharibashvili has been publishing letters from prison in which he accuses Irakli Kobakhidze and former Deputy Prime Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze . On August 27, Mamuka Mdinaradze resigned from his post and announced his departure from politics. He denied any connection to the letters. Another important factor in the context of Ivanishvili’s meeting with ruling party leaders is that the Constitutional Court is due to hear the authorities’ case seeking to ban opposition parties in just a few days. According to opposition representatives, hearings were scheduled for October 21, 22 and 23. In response, an alliance of nine opposition parties announced a rally in Tbilisi on 25 October under the slogan “Georgia without Ivanishvili. Georgia deserves better.” Georgia without an opposition? How ruling party moved to ban its opponents through constitutional lawsuit Ruling party Georgian Dream asks Constitutional Court to ban five opposition parties, four of which crossed the electoral threshold in parliamentary elections Gharibashvili is Ivanishvili’s “heartache” – and the statement about “overcoming difficulties” After the meetings at the ruling party’s office, journalists asked Irakli Kobakhidze whether the possibility of releasing former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili from prison had been discussed. Kobakhidze replied that there had not. According to him, Ivanishvili gave a general assessment of “the developments”. “For all of us, including, of course, first and foremost, Bidzina Ivanishvili, what happened is painful, when events unfold this way and former members of the team are serving sentences for specific crimes (…)” , Kobakhidze said. He added: “What happened is regrettable. It was, of course, something of a blow to the team.” Gharibashvili was sentenced to five years in prison in January 2026 following a plea agreement. In August, prosecutors brought a new charge against him. According to the prosecution, the former prime minister accepted 750,000 lari (about $290,000) in bribes. Gharibashvili’s lawyers say he denies the new charge. There is no mention of “heartache” in the party statement’s account of the same subject. According to the statement, Ivanishvili reviewed the corruption challenges the team had faced in the past and said that “as a result of the effective work of the prime minister, the government team and the security apparatus, these challenges have been fully and effectively overcome” . Conflict analyst’s view on clash between Georgia’s former and current prime ministers Conflict analyst Paata Zakareishvili comments on the clash between Georgia’s former and current prime ministers, Garibashvili and Kobakhidze. Kobakhidze: “Friendship is none of your business “ Kobakhidze said the team had also discussed Mamuka Mdinaradze, a former deputy prime minister who previously served as head of the State Security Service. Mdinaradze resigned from his post on August 27 and announced his departure from politics. At the time, he denied that his resignation was connected to Garibashvili’s letters published from prison. Kobakhidze declined to elaborate publicly. “Mamuka Mdinaradze has left politics” , he said, adding that he did not consider it appropriate to bring the issue to the fore in these circumstances. He said he remained in occasional contact with Mdinaradze. He did not give a direct answer when asked whether they were still friends. “Why are you asking about friendship? Friendship is none of your business” , he told journalists. Journalists also raised the issue of a controversial social media post by Georgian Dream party member Dito Samkharadze, who wrote that “rats” [informers] had been identified within the ruling party.” Kobakhidze was asked whether Samkharadze also meant Mdinaradze and whether legal proceedings against him were expected. “ I don’t know what you’re referring to ,” the prime minister replied. He said there was “no basis whatsoever” for such speculation. Parliamentary majority leader Kirtskhalia: “Ivanishvili spoke mostly about Kobakhidze “ Journalists asked Irakli Kirtskhalia to comment on growing public speculation that Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze could soon resign. According to him, Ivanishvili devoted more time to Kobakhidze than to anyone else, “ expressing support and praise, which the entire team, of course, shares ”. “ Ivanishvili said that the government is performing very well under Kobakhidze’s leadership, and that not only is there no reason for his resignation, but every day confirms that he is the best prime minister, ” Kirtskhalia said . He described the resignation rumours as gossip spread by the opposition. Opinion from Tbilisi: 'Everything is in place for Prime Minister Kobakhidze's resignation' Political analyst Gia Khukhashvili predicts that Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze could resign soon. Scandal over possible corruption in spending on the Patriarch’s funeral At a press briefing, Irakli Kobakhidze addressed the main political issue: allegations of possible corruption in spending on the Patriarch’s funeral. He said preliminary information from the Government Administration showed “no indication of any improper expenditure” . He also said a large portion of the allocated funds had been returned. In September, speaking on Rustavi 2, Kobakhidze provided specific figures : according to preliminary data, 722,000 lari (about $275,000) of the 3 million lari (about $1,100,000) allocated had been spent. The questions he answered concerned former Culture Minister Tika Rukhadze’s possible involvement in the alleged embezzlement. Kobakhidze said detailed information would be presented to the public in the near future. Asked whether investigative agencies should look into the matter, he replied: “First, we will present detailed information to you, and if any questions remain on this issue, let us discuss them together.” Millions spent on Patriarch’s funeral: scandal involving Georgia’s former culture minister Tinatin Rukhadze Why are calls being made to investigate the former minister? “Whatever they call us, we keep winning” – Kobakhidze on media restrictions Irakli Kobakhidze also commented on restrictions on the use of various words and expressions in the media adopted by the Communications Commission. On 9 October, Transparency International – Georgia reported that the Communications Commission had objected to expressions used by independent TV channels Formula and Pirveli. The commission compiled a list of 93 words and phrases that it banned from use, including “regime”, “oligarch” and “prime minister appointed by Ivanishvili”, according to TI. Fines for using words on the list were increased to 10,000 lari (nearly $4,000). Kobakhidze explained the decision as necessary to uphold the principle of objectivity. He said these rules had existed in legislation for years, but an enforcement mechanism had not previously been in place. News programmes are now required to maintain neutrality. That requirement does not apply to programmes expressing their hosts’ own views, Prime Minister said. “Nothing bothers us. We win elections and emerge victorious from every political confrontation. Whether they call us a regime or a dictatorship, we win either way” , Kobakhidze said. News in Georgia

title: Ukraine cannot be forced to surrender, says commander whose brigade destroyed 57,000 Russian targets, as US pressure and Russian missiles test its will
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ending the war by forcing Ukraine to capitulate is impossible, the commander of the 429th “Achilles” Unmanned Systems Brigade, Yurii Fedorenko, said in an interview with 24 Kanal. His statements came as Ukraine absorbed the fallout from the US-Russia diesel deal that saw its Starlink throttled and US intelligence lapse, a gap tied to a strike that killed three in Kyiv. Achilles is a volunteer unit formed in the first days of the full-scale invasion, built around aerial reconnaissance and drone strikes and credited with more than 57,000 strikes. Fedorenko, its commander, was named a Hero of Ukraine in January 2026. Fedorenko says he believes that there would be no “miraculous de-escalation,” and now argues that neither pressure from Washington nor Russian missiles can break the country’s will to fight for its liberty. Russia will keep terrorizing Ukrainians with ballistic missiles, jet drones and Shaheds, and no near-term shift in US policy will stop it, Fedorenko stresses, so Ukraine will keep defending itself and striking back. A lasting energy ceasefire, he added, will not hold. “Ukrainian society is ready to defend itself and to uphold its right to life by force,” he says, arguing that the Kremlin’s mouthpieces, and those working for third countries, have misjudged the mood in Ukraine. No measure, he insists, could force Ukraine to capitulate in the short term. Why the US election could swing the pendulum back Fedorenko sees the political balance shifting after the US vote. President Donald Trump will probably not hold the majority he once had, making it harder for him to take domestic decisions alone, he notes. Even foreign policy, a presidential prerogative, will have to reckon with that balance. If Trump must bargain with Democrats to pass domestic measures, that will shape the wider picture, Fedorenko argues. He stopped short of predicting impeachment, calling that the wrong framing, but cautioned that decisions already taken could be reviewed, challenged and overturned in the courts. “I am firmly convinced we will get through the difficulties dictated by circumstances, including those arising across the ocean,” he says. A cold shower for Europe that could help Ukraine The US turn toward Moscow has jolted Europe, in Fedorenko’s view. American threats to leave NATO or rewrite how it shares the burden landed on European leaders like a cold waterfall, he recounts, pushing each state to ask how it would stand if the US walked away and to treat the Russian threat as one standing at its own borders, no longer a problem confined to Ukraine. That alarm can work in Kyiv’s favor, drawing more weapons, defense financing and economic support from European partners, Fedorenko argues. The same logic drives the satellite question. Ukraine cannot build a Starlink alternative alone, lacking its own space program, so the answer is collective, with NATO states pooling launches into a shared network, he explains. Russia is taking the other path with its “Rassvet” system, much of it, in fact, built by China, and if Moscow and Beijing get there first, he warns, the fallout would reach far beyond Ukraine.
